column6: Tidal Vision is a vertically integrated company that has developed a proprietary process to extract chitosan from crustacean shells, a byproduct of the seafood industry. column5: AI-Native IT Service Management Platform
column6: Serval is an AI-powered IT Service Management (ITSM) platform designed to automate help desk functions for modern IT teams. Founded in April 2024 by CEO Jake Stauch and CTO Alex McLeod, the company aims to challenge legacy systems like ServiceNow by using AI agents to resolve IT issues. The founders, who previously worked together at Verkada as Director of Product and Director of Engineering respectively, identified pain points in traditional IT ticketing systems, which often act as simple task managers. Their experience building products for IT at Verkada inspired them to create a platform that doesn't just track tasks but completes them. The core of Serval's platform is its AI agent workforce, which can be deployed to handle help desk requests, manage application access, and automate workflows. A key feature is its natural language-to-code workflow builder, which allows IT administrators to create complex automations by describing them in plain English. The system can automate a wide range of tasks, including employee onboarding and offboarding, software access provisioning, password resets, and creating user groups. For employees, requests made in channels like Slack are intercepted by an AI agent that either routes the request to an appropriate automation for instant resolution or escalates it to a human technician if the task is outside its capabilities. The platform also integrates with knowledge bases like Notion, Google Drive, and Confluence to surface answers to common questions automatically. Serval operates in the enterprise service management market, targeting any organization that requires an ITSM solution. The business model is focused on providing a more efficient and less cumbersome alternative to established players. The company secured a seed funding round in April 2024 from investors including General Catalyst, First Round Capital, Box Group, and Alt Capital. Serval's long-term vision is to expand beyond IT into a universal workflow automation platform for other business functions such as security, HR, and legal. column5: Web based fleet solutions
column6: Radius, initially established as UK Fuels in 1990, has evolved from a UK-based fuel card provider into a global business services company. It was founded by Bill Holmes, who identified a market need for streamlined fuel expense management for businesses while working as a salesperson for Esso Petroleum. Armed with a biochemistry degree and sales experience, Holmes started the company in a small office above a hair salon in Holmes Chapel, Cheshire. The business was founded to simplify payments and fleet management for industrial clients. The company's growth has been propelled by a combination of organic expansion and a vigorous acquisition strategy. A significant milestone was the 2013 merger of over 20 European fuel card companies to form Radius Payment Solutions. This was followed by a strategic diversification into telematics with the launch of its Kinesis vehicle tracking solution in 2015 and subsequent expansion into the US market. Further acquisitions have broadened its portfolio into telecommunications, insurance, vehicle solutions, and electric vehicle (EV) charging. This includes the creation of the Radius Connect brand for its telecoms division and investments in EV charging infrastructure companies. Inflexion Private Equity made a minority investment in 2018, supporting this M&A-driven growth. As of October 2023, Bill Holmes transitioned from CEO to Executive Chairman. Radius operates on a business-to-business model, primarily serving small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) with fleet and connectivity needs. Its revenue is generated through a diverse portfolio of services. The core offering remains fuel cards, which help businesses manage fuel expenses efficiently. This is complemented by a suite of integrated services including vehicle telematics for tracking and performance monitoring, vehicle and asset insurance, and vehicle leasing and rental solutions. The company has also established a significant presence in the telecommunications sector, providing mobile, VoIP, and broadband solutions. Acknowledging the energy transition, Radius has expanded into EV solutions, offering charging points and payment networks. This multi-product strategy allows Radius to function as a comprehensive solutions provider for its clients' mobility and connectivity requirements, leveraging data to offer insights that help reduce costs and enhance security. column5: Merger of ten pharmaceutical companies developing drugs for sleep-wake disorders, neurological conditions and cancer
column6: Centessa Pharmaceuticals plc is a clinical-stage pharmaceutical company that has revolutionized traditional drug development through its unique asset-centric business model. Founded in 2020 through the strategic merger of ten specialized biotech companies, Centessa operates as a hub-and-spoke organization where each subsidiary maintains operational autonomy while benefiting from centralized resources and infrastructure.The company's core focus centers on developing potential best-in-class orexin receptor 2 (OX2R) agonists for treating sleep-wake disorders, including narcolepsy type 1 (NT1), narcolepsy type 2 (NT2), and idiopathic hypersomnia (IH). These oral therapies target excessive daytime sleepiness, impaired attention, cognitive deficits, and fatigue across neurological, neurodegenerative, and neuropsychiatric conditions. The company's lead orexin candidate, ORX750, is currently in Phase 2a clinical trials with data expected across all three sleep disorder indications in 2025.Additionally, Centessa maintains an early-stage immuno-oncology program built around its proprietary LockBody® technology platform, developed under the leadership of Dr. William Finlay. This platform focuses on engineered antibodies designed to improve cancer treatment outcomes.Centessa's business model revolves around advancing high-conviction therapeutic programs through regulatory approval and eventual commercialization. The company generates limited revenue from collaboration agreements and milestone payments. Primary funding comes from equity investments, debt financing, and strategic partnerships rather than product sales, as the company remains in clinical development stages.Each of Centessa's ten subsidiary companies operates with dedicated teams led by subject matter experts who maintain singular focus on their respective therapeutic programs. This structure enables rapid decision-making and specialized expertise while providing access to shared resources including regulatory affairs, manufacturing support, and capital allocation.The company serves the global pharmaceutical market, targeting healthcare providers and patients through traditional regulatory pathways in the United States and Europe. With headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and operations across the UK, Centessa aims to address significant unmet medical needs in sleep disorders and cancer treatment.Keywords: Orexin receptor agonists, sleep-wake disorders, narcolepsy, clinical-stage pharmaceutical, asset-centric model, LockBody technology, immuno-oncology, neuroscience, biotechnology, drug development.

column6: Silverfort delivers a unified identity security platform that provides comprehensive protection across on-premises, cloud, and hybrid environments for both human and non-human identities. Through its patented, agentless Runtime Access Protection (RAP) technology, Silverfort natively integrates with enterprise identity infrastructure without requiring proxies or system modifications. This integrated approach eliminates the dangerous visibility gaps and security weaknesses created by siloed point solutions. Key strategic moves, such as a top-tier partnership with Microsoft and the 2024 acquisition of cloud security firm Rezonate, have cemented Silverfort’s position as an end-to-end identity protection leader, extending its capabilities across the entire enterprise ecosystem from on-premises Active Directory to multi-cloud infrastructure.​Founded by veterans of Israel's elite Unit 8200, Silverfort has scaled into a global cybersecurity leader with dual headquarters in Tel Aviv and Boston, and over 1,000 enterprise customers, including Fortune 50 companies like UPS and Airbus. The company's significant market impact and technological innovation were recognized when Fast Company named it one of the World's Most Innovative Companies for 2025. column5: E-Mobility as a Service for commercial fleets.
column6: BillionElectric Mobility is an Indian e-Mobility-as-a-Service (eMaaS) provider, specializing in transitioning commercial fleets to zero-emission transport. Founded in 2016 by Kartikey Hariyani, and later joined by co-founders Mustafa Wajid and Sanjeev Kulkarni, the company focuses on decarbonizing India's mid-mile and long-haul trucking routes. Hariyani has over two decades of experience in electrical engineering and renewable energy, having previously founded TecSo Energy, a solar power and energy storage company. This background in sustainable energy infrastructure informs BillionElectric's integrated approach. The company's business model is centered on providing a comprehensive ecosystem that bundles electric vehicles, charging infrastructure, battery management, and AI-powered fleet management software into a single service. This model aims to remove the primary barriers to EV adoption for businesses, such as high upfront costs and a lack of charging infrastructure. BillionElectric serves a wide range of enterprise clients in sectors including e-commerce, pharmaceuticals, cement, steel, automotive, and logistics. The company's offerings are structured as end-to-end solutions that include the vehicles (ranging from 12T to 55T trucks and tarmac buses), charging access, route engineering, and maintenance support. BillionElectric's platform provides features like vehicle tracking with geofencing and immobilization technology. A key strategic advantage is its affiliation with CHARGE ZONE, one of India's largest high-speed EV charging networks, which facilitates the electrification of major freight corridors. This partnership ensures reliable charging access for its commercial fleets. The company entered the Indian market in June 2023 with a $10 million seed funding round, which was used to deploy electric tarmac buses at Bengaluru International Airport and develop its mid-mile heavy EV truck platform. By January 2026, BillionElectric secured an additional $25 million in a growth capital round to scale its commercial operations and expand its fleet. The company plans to deploy over 500 electric trucks in the 2026-27 fiscal year and has a pipeline for over 1,500 more in the next two to three years. column6: MedicubeX® is a Finnish start-up that has developed a unique self-service health kiosk, the eHealth Station™, and proprietary AI-driven analytics for the early, non-invasive detection and risk assessment of cardiovascular diseases (CVD) and Type 2 Diabetes (T2D).The eHealth Station is a certified medical system that integrates CE-marked medical devices and AI analytics into a single, automated platform. It provides immediate, personalized, highly accurate health insights without the need for trained on-site personnel, in just a few minutes.The Station measures all vital signs, including blood pressure, pulse, respiratory rate, SpO₂, temperature, and weight, along with additional critical health parameters such as a full ECG (with instant detection for over 20 arrhythmias). A revolutionary new solution is also being added to non-invasively diagnose heart valve abnormalities from the person's neck.The proprietary, patent-pending algorithm delivers the world’s most accurate risk analysis for CVD and T2D. It predicts an individual’s likelihood of a heart attack, stroke, heart failure, and peripheral artery disease - entirely non-invasively and without the need for blood tests or clinical staff. The solution delivers superior, highly accurate non-invasive CVD risk analysis, outperforming traditional blood-test gold standards.The eHealth Station is designed for maximal accessibility and efficiency. Its interactive, multilingual UI ensures a smooth, staff-free user experience, and the standalone unit's flexible deployment and integrated UV disinfection reduce manual maintenance. The core impact is making preventive care widely accessible and cost-efficient, overcoming traditional healthcare barriers. Furthermore, the solution features a scalable SaaS model with 24/7 support, seamless integration with existing EHR and telehealth platforms, and rapid deployment in less than a day.The MedicubeX eHealth Station is primarily a preventive healthcare platform. It serves as an autonomous tool for population screening, research, and occupational health initiatives, enabling the early and accessible identification of key health risks, such as those related to CVD and T2D. By automating data collection for pre-appointment checks and chronic disease monitoring, it supports the proactive management of existing conditions and helps prevent complications. Its deployment in public places makes basic health checks readily available to the public, shifting the healthcare focus from late diagnosis to proactive self-care and early risk detection.The Station also provides significant value to acute and emergency care through triage and automating routine measurements. This improves efficiency for healthcare providers by gathering standardized vital signs before a patient sees a clinician. The collected data helps identify the most acute patients upon arrival and bring them to care faster.The MedicubeX eHealth Station™ is already actively deployed and operating in five European countries: its home market of Finland, Germany, the UK, Estonia, and Latvia. Finland and Germany are emerging as key markets, with deployments in leading institutions such as the University Hospital of Frankfurt.In Finland, MedicubeX has secured major achievements in the last few months, including:- Winning a significant national-level public tender organized by Istekki Oy, a Finnish expert organization for ICT and welfare services, for the procurement of self-measurement stations, with an estimated value of €4 million.- Forming a strategic partnership with Terveystalo, a leading private healthcare provider in Finland, making them the exclusive private-sector partner to utilize the eHealth Station™ for occupational and preventive health services.Keywords: Digital Care Assessment, Medical Technology, Disease Prevention, eHealth Station™, Cardiovascular Risk Assessment, Diabetes Risk Assessment, Remote Consultations, Real-time Data, Automated Healthcare, AI-Driven Diagnostics.

column5: Develops AVC-Boosters to enhance NK cells, activate the immune system, and provide broad anti-tumor responses for cancer immunotherapy
column6: Avidicure is a Netherlands-based biotechnology firm, founded in 2022 by Govert Schouten and Robert Friesen, that is developing a new class of antibody therapies for oncology. The company launched in April 2025 with a significant $50 million (€44 million) seed financing round led by EQT Life Sciences, with participation from investors including Kurma Partners, BioGeneration Ventures, and others. The founding management team, which includes CEO Arthur Lahr, COO Dirk De Naeyer, CSO Robert Friesen, and CBO Govert Schouten, brings extensive experience from executive roles at successful European biotech companies like Crucell, Ablynx, and Kiadis. This collective expertise in drug discovery, development, and commercialization underpins the company's strategic direction. The team claims to have created their core technology entirely from scratch. Avidicure's core business revolves around its proprietary "AVC-Booster" platform, which engineers multifunctional, dual agonistic antibodies. These therapies are designed to activate and modulate immune cells directly within the tumor microenvironment, harnessing both the innate and adaptive immune systems to fight cancer. The business model is focused on the research and development of these novel drug candidates, with the goal of progressing them through clinical trials and ultimately to market. The company's technology is built on decades of expertise in antibody engineering, in-silico protein design, and immunology. The AVC-Booster product is engineered to be functional only when it engages with tumor cells, a feature called avidity engineering. This localized activation aims to stimulate a potent immune response directly at the cancer site, thereby enhancing efficacy while reducing the risk of systemic toxicity commonly associated with other immunotherapies. The platform's 'plug-and-play' design allows for the efficient development of multiple products targeting different cancer antigens. Avidicure's lead candidate, AVC-S-101, is a TROP2-targeting booster being developed for non-small cell lung cancer and other solid tumors. Preclinical data has shown that AVC-S-101 can improve tumor control in animal models and activate immune cells in human tumor samples. column5: Robotic-powered prosthetic knees for lower-limb amputees
column6: BionicM Inc. is a developer of powered prosthetic solutions for lower-limb amputees, founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the University of Tokyo. The company's creation stems from the doctoral research of its founder and CEO, Dr. Sun Xiaojun, who is himself an amputee. Sun lost his right leg to bone cancer at age nine and used crutches for 15 years before getting his first prosthesis, an experience that drove him to develop better solutions. After earning a master's degree and working as an engineer at Sony, he pursued a Ph.D. at the University of Tokyo, focusing on robotic prosthetic legs, which led to the founding of BionicM. The company's main business is the research, development, and commercialization of robotic prostheses. Its flagship product, the Bio Leg®, is a powered prosthetic knee that utilizes robotics and AI to replicate lost muscle strength, assisting with movements like walking and ascending stairs. This technology is designed to reduce the physical burden on users, enabling more natural and intuitive movement. The Bio Leg®, which weighs about six pounds and has a full-day battery life, has received FDA Class II registration and U.S. medical insurance coverage. The company is also developing a more affordable model, the Cybo Leg, and exploring features to collect biometric data to help clinicians guide gait training. BionicM operates on a business model that involves partnering with third-party socket manufacturers, which helps make its products more affordable than some competing devices. The company launched sales in China and Japan in 2021 and entered the U.S. market, the world's largest for prosthetics, in August 2024. To support its global expansion, BionicM established a U.S. subsidiary in Virginia and has raised approximately $12.7 million in total funding from investors including UTEC, JST, and Shinsei Corporate Investment. column5: AI-powered medical device for skin cancer pathways
column6: Skin Analytics is a British health-tech company, founded in 2012 by CEO Neil Daly, that is focused on improving the detection of skin cancer. Daly, originally from Australia, leveraged his background in physics and an MBA from London Business School to address the challenges in dermatological care, inspired by his father's experience with cancer and the prevalence of skin cancer in his home country. The company's core product is DERM, an acronym for Deep Ensemble for the Recognition of Malignancy. It is an AI-powered medical device that analyzes high-resolution, dermoscopic images of skin lesions to identify malignant, pre-malignant, and benign types. The technology is designed to be integrated into healthcare pathways to triage patients, helping to distinguish between urgent cases and benign conditions. This process allows for the quick discharge of patients without cancer, which frees up dermatologist capacity to focus on high-risk patients, reduces wait times, and addresses care backlogs. As of June 2025, the system had been used to assess over 170,000 NHS patients. Post-market surveillance showed that DERM correctly identified 97% of cancers with a negative predictive value of 99.8%. Skin Analytics primarily serves public health systems, most notably the UK's National Health Service (NHS), with which it has partnered since 2016 and is deployed at 26 sites. Its business model involves providing its AI platform to healthcare organizations to create more efficient patient pathways. The company also provides remote skin assessment services for private insurers like Bupa and Vitality. Skin Analytics has received significant funding, including a £15 million Series B round in April 2025 led by Intrepid Growth Partners, to support expansion into the US, European, and Australian markets. column5: AI-powered 3D vision for robots, helping manufacturers scale flexible automation across factories worldwide
column6: Inbolt, established in 2019 by co-founders Rudy Cohen, Albane Dersy, and Simon Bousquet, is a company focused on advancing robotic automation within the manufacturing sector. The founding team combines expertise from diverse backgrounds; Rudy Cohen has experience in robotics and computer vision from his time at MIT and various tech companies, Albane Dersy brings a background in industrial and manufacturing systems from Arts et Métiers and experience at industrial giants like Saint-Gobain, and Simon Bousquet contributes his knowledge in robotics and AI. This collective experience addresses a critical challenge in modern manufacturing: the high cost and rigidity of traditional automation systems that rely on fixed infrastructure.The company's core business revolves around its proprietary AI-powered robotic guidance technology, which enables industrial robots to operate in dynamic and unstructured environments. Inbolt develops and sells a hardware-agnostic software platform that integrates with 3D cameras to provide real-time, vision-based guidance for robots. This system allows robots to identify and locate parts with sub-millimeter precision, even on continuously moving assembly lines, a significant step forward in factory automation. The technology is designed to be a generalist solution, adapting to various applications without requiring extensive custom tuning, thereby reducing integration costs and deployment times. Inbolt's business model is centered on providing its technology to major industrial players, particularly in the automotive industry. Its client roster includes prominent manufacturers such as Stellantis, Renault, Toyota, and Ford, with deployments in over 50 factories across Europe, the United States, and Japan. The company's revenue is generated by selling its software and guidance systems to these large enterprises, helping them to automate complex tasks that were previously difficult or impossible to automate, such as screwdriving, welding, and quality inspection on moving lines. Having secured $20 million in funding from investors like SOSV, Exor, and MIG, Inbolt is positioned to expand its market presence and further develop its technology, setting a new benchmark for flexible robotics in manufacturing. Keywords: robotic guidance, manufacturing automation, computer vision, AI software, industrial robotics, automotive manufacturing, assembly line automation, 3D vision, flexible automation, GuideNOW

column5: Powered by the proprietary Impulse Printing™ technology, the company enables assembly of 3D microelectronics in a scalable and sustainable way
column6: FononTech B.V., based in Eindhoven, operates in the high-tech manufacturing sector, specializing in advanced printing technology. The company has developed a unique method for creating complex 3D interconnects and high-resolution patterns using a lithographic process. This process allows for the rapid transfer of intricate designs onto various substrates (the base material on which the pattern is printed) with micron-sized precision. FononTech's technology is particularly notable for its ability to perform local alignment between the pattern and the substrate through selective heating. This capability is enhanced by a flat heater plate and a stencil print process, which can produce larger features within the same machine. The company's innovative approach enables the printing of complete patterns all at once, opening up new possibilities for applications that were previously unattainable.The company serves a diverse range of clients, including research institutions, electronics manufacturers, and other high-tech industries that require precise and complex patterning capabilities. FononTech operates in the global market, with a focus on sectors that demand high-resolution and multi-layer printing solutions.FononTech's business model revolves around the sale and leasing of its advanced printing tools. The company offers a beta tool capable of printing down to micron-sized features, which will be available for delivery in Q2 2024. This tool features 256 individually controlled printing zones, enabling multi-layer printing and local substrate alignment. Additionally, FononTech provides a proto tool compatible with a wide range of materials, supported by a robotic arm for precise substrate handling.The company generates revenue through the sale of these advanced printing tools, as well as through service contracts for maintenance and support. By offering cutting-edge technology and comprehensive support, FononTech aims to establish itself as a leader in the high-tech printing market.Keywords: advanced printing, lithographic process, 3D interconnects, high-resolution patterns, selective heating, multi-layer printing, research institutions, electronics manufacturers, global market, robotic arm.

column5: Energy planning and management platform for commercial real estate
column6: Moca Energy provides a data-driven platform designed for the commercial real estate sector to streamline energy planning and management. The company's mission is to simplify energy and building planning, making it more accessible and actionable for clients such as real estate managers, asset managers, and sustainability advisors. Moca's platform uses existing energy data, along with building and lease information, to generate up-to-date energy plans without requiring physical site visits. This approach is positioned as a faster and more cost-effective alternative to traditional consultants. The core service revolves around creating clear roadmaps for clients to achieve their net-zero and energy efficiency targets. The platform aggregates a portfolio's building and energy data into a single location, offering a comprehensive view of performance and identifying areas for improvement. It continuously tracks building performance, highlighting abnormal energy usage to enable timely corrections. Key features include CRREM (Carbon Risk Real Estate Monitor) pathway analysis, which identifies when buildings might become stranded assets and suggests actionable solutions to maintain compliance and value. Furthermore, Moca facilitates tenant engagement, recognizing it as a cost-effective method for reducing energy consumption. The business model is centered on its software platform that provides remote audits, ongoing monitoring, and data analysis to help clients manage regulatory compliance (like EPC and BREEAM In-Use), future-proof assets, and reduce operational costs. By analyzing energy data against historical weather patterns and other information, Moca can diagnose energy waste and provide clear guidance on improvements, from operational changes to technology upgrades like solar PV or replacing gas heating. The platform keeps plans current by continuously updating for changes in technology and energy prices. column5: Programmable Ethernet switches optimizing AI data center connectivity for hyperscale efficiency
column6: Xsight Labs is a fabless semiconductor company pioneering the rearchitecture of cloud infrastructure through fully programmable Ethernet switching and data processing solutions. Founded in 2017 by former EZchip engineers with decades of experience in networking silicon, the company has built a world-class R&D organization focused on solving the fundamental bottlenecks of modern data center architecture. Operating with offices across Israel, Armenia, and the United States, Xsight Labs addresses the critical challenge of exponential bandwidth growth in hyperscale cloud environments while simultaneously reducing the power and thermal footprint that constrains current infrastructure scaling.The company's flagship product portfolio—comprising the X1 fully programmable Ethernet switch (25.6Tbps/12.8Tbps), the second-generation X2 switch (12.8Tbps at less than 200W power consumption, representing 40% lower power than competing solutions), and the E1 software-defined DPU (800Gbps with 64 ARM Neoverse N2 cores)—delivers unprecedented programmability combined with application-specific optimization. Each product incorporates advanced architectural innovations including fully shared buffer systems for wire-speed in-cast performance, X-PND™ elastic resource allocation engines, fine-grained intelligent queuing (X-IQ™), comprehensive in-field health monitoring (X-Mon), and cutting-edge 5-nanometer silicon technology fabricated by TSMC. Xsight Labs' commitment to open-source architecture and industry collaboration is evidenced by its recent initiative to open the instruction set architecture (XISA) of its X-Series switches, challenging decades of vendor lock-in and enabling a thriving ecosystem of developers and system integrators.​The company's customer base spans hyperscale cloud service providers, enterprise data centers, and next-generation AI infrastructure operators requiring best-in-class power efficiency, programmability, and performance for demanding distributed computing workloads. With a funding portfolio anchored by strategic investments from Intel, Microsoft, Xilinx, Valor Equity Partners, Atreides Management, and Fidelity Management & Research Company, Xsight Labs has established itself as a critical infrastructure innovator positioned to define the networking silicon paradigm for the AI era. column5: AI-powered contract lifecycle management and e-signature platform
column6: INHUBBER offers a business-to-business software-as-a-service (SaaS) contract lifecycle management (CLM) platform that utilizes artificial intelligence and blockchain technology. The company was founded in 2018 by Dr. Elena Mechik (CEO), Andre Sokolov (CTO), and Leonid Mechik (CFO). It originated as a research project at Humboldt University of Berlin. The platform is designed for businesses of all sizes, including small and medium-sized businesses, enterprises, and public institutions, serving industries such as retail, real estate, procurement, and logistics. Clients include organizations like the OECD, SHARP, and EDEKA. The business model is subscription-based, with pricing plans that include options for unlimited contracts and users. INHUBBER's core product is a cloud-based platform that centralizes contract management, allowing users to create, negotiate, e-sign, store, and monitor contracts. Key features include AI-driven document analysis for extracting critical data, identifying risks, and summarizing contracts. The AI was developed in collaboration with Humboldt University Berlin. The platform also offers legally binding digital signatures that support various file formats, including PDF, Word, Excel, and video files. Security is a major focus, with end-to-end encryption, two-factor authentication, blockchain-based audit trails, and hosting on ISO 27001-certified servers in Germany to ensure compliance with standards like GDPR and eIDAS. Additional functionalities include customizable workflows, automated reminders for deadlines, task management, role-based access control, and full-text search. The platform integrates with various other software, including Microsoft SharePoint, SAP, Google Workspace, and Salesforce. INHUBBER also contributes 1% of its revenue to a project aimed at mitigating climate change by reducing illegal logging, utilizing its blockchain technology to provide supply chain transparency for timber. column6: Sdui provides a digital operating system for the education sector, specifically targeting K-12 schools and daycare centers. The company was established in Koblenz, Germany, in February 2018 by Daniel Zacharias and Jan Micha Kroll. The initial idea originated from their own experience as high school students in 2015, when they sought a way to be digitally notified about class cancellations. This led to a project for the "Jugend forscht" (Youth Research) competition, which eventually evolved into the company after they finished school. Zacharias, who serves as CEO, taught himself to code using online resources and gained early entrepreneurial experience by building an online shop. Kroll was identified as the technical talent, having developed his first app at the age of seven. Their journey included an unsuccessful appearance on the German investment show "Die Höhle der Löwen" in 2020. The company's business model is centered on providing a GDPR-compliant, cloud-based software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform to educational institutions, including individual schools, districts, and government bodies. Sdui has established itself as a significant player in the European EdTech market, serving approximately 22,000 institutions across more than 70 countries. The firm generates revenue by simplifying administrative and organizational tasks for educators, parents, and students. Strategic growth has been fueled by substantial funding rounds, including a Series A extension to €25 million in February 2023 and a significant growth investment led by Bain Capital in July 2025. Sdui has also pursued an inorganic growth strategy through acquisitions, such as purchasing the Spanish company Additio, and FoxEducation from GoStudent in July 2024, which brought the brands SchoolFox, KidsFox, and TeamFox into its portfolio. Sdui's platform functions as a central hub designed to streamline school operations. Key features include a news feed for digital parent letters, secure chat functions as a compliant alternative to consumer messaging apps, video conferencing, and a cloud for sharing documents. The system integrates timetables from existing school management software and offers digital class registers, absence management, and survey tools. A notable feature is the automatic translation of content into numerous languages, aimed at overcoming communication barriers for families with migration backgrounds. The platform is designed for ease of use across all devices without requiring prior digital expertise and can be integrated with a school's existing digital infrastructure, such as websites and bus schedules. In late 2024, Navitas announced plans for a new 60-acre manufacturing campus with an initial capacity of 1.5 GW, projected to expand to 10 GW by 2025. The company has received multiple rounds of funding, including a $5 million Series A round in 2023, to fuel its expansion. column5: Upcycled PET for circular food packaging
column6: Formaspack is a Spanish manufacturer of food-grade recycled polyethylene terephthalate (rPET) packaging that has pioneered the concept of "upcycling" in the plastics industry. Founded in 1995 and headquartered in Cantabria, the company operates a fully integrated circular ecosystem that transforms post-consumer plastic waste—from beverage bottles to food trays—into premium packaging materials that meet the stringent food-contact standards of the European Food Safety Authority and the U.S. FDA. Rather than degenerating materials through traditional recycling, Formaspack's proprietary decontamination and solid-state polycondensation technology restores the molecular properties of recycled PET to virgin-equivalent quality, enabling infinite material cycles without quality degradation.The company serves food industry manufacturers, beverage producers, and retailers across Europe who face regulatory pressure (EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation, PPWR 2023/2006) to incorporate recycled content while maintaining food safety integrity. Formaspack's competitive advantage lies in its vertical integration: from collection and sorting, through decontamination and pellet production, to sheet extrusion and thermoforming, the company controls every step, ensuring traceability and compliance. The business model is B2B transactional, with revenue generated from the sale of customized rPET sheets and finished containers. By 2024, Formaspack had achieved €100+ million in annual revenue with production capacity exceeding 75,000 tonnes of rPET annually, operating with approximately 200 skilled employees and backed by strategic investment from Tresmares Capital (Banco Santander-affiliated).In 2024, Formaspack formalized its operations into Formaspack Upcycling Group, consolidating three subsidiaries (Recopolymers, OMT Recycling Project, and Formas y Envases) to optimize resource allocation and strengthen its position as Europe's leading advocate for PET upcycling. The company's commitment to decarbonization includes €1M+ annual investments in renewable energy infrastructure, with 2,000+ solar panels installed across production facilities. This model—transforming waste into equivalent-value material while reducing carbon emissions and supporting European circular economy targets—represents the future of sustainable packaging manufacturing.Keywords: recycled PET, food-grade packaging, upcycling, circular economy, decontamination technology, beverage packaging, food safety, thermoforming, EFSA compliance, sustainability, rPET sheet, packaging waste, family business, Spanish manufacturing, waste-to-product

column6: GoCab is a mobility fintech company that provides ethical financing and vehicle ownership opportunities for gig-economy workers, primarily in Africa. Founded in 2024 by former investment bankers Azamat Sultan and Hendrick Ketchemen, the company aims to address the limited access to financial services and asset ownership for drivers and delivery couriers. Sultan, from Tajikistan, and Ketchemen, from Cameroon, leveraged their expertise in structured finance and emerging markets to create a business model that transforms capital into a tool for social mobility and financial inclusion. The company's core offering is a drive-to-own model, which allows drivers to acquire cars and motorbikes through flexible leasing and ownership plans. GoCab purchases vehicles in bulk, primarily from China, and sells them to drivers who make daily payments deducted automatically from their earnings over a fixed term, typically three years. This model includes maintenance and insurance, providing a comprehensive solution for drivers who often lack access to traditional bank financing. GoCab operates in five countries, including Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal, and Morocco, and has expanded into the Middle East and Latin America. By early 2026, GoCab had generated over $17 million in Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) within 18 months of operation and employed over 120 people. In February 2026, the company announced a significant funding round of $45 million, consisting of $15 million in equity and $30 million in debt. The equity round was co-led by E3 Capital and JANNGO Capital, with participation from KawiSafi Ventures and Cur8 Capital. This funding is intended to scale operations, expand into new cities, increase the share of electric vehicles (EVs) in its fleet, and deploy AI-driven solutions for credit scoring, fleet optimization, and risk management. A core part of GoCab's strategy is the transition to electric mobility to reduce emissions and lower operating costs for drivers. The company also offers a comprehensive membership app that includes a digital wallet, debit card, and buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) options for fuel and phones. column5: Pesticide-free vegetables via patented, soilless farming technology
column6: Eeki Foods, legally known as Eeki Automations Pvt Ltd, is an agritech company founded in 2018 by IIT Bombay alumni Abhay Singh and Amit Kumar. The founders, after brief stints in business development, product design, and IoT, were driven by the need to address global challenges like food security and climate change. They began their research in March 2018 on a small rooftop farm in Kota, Rajasthan, before establishing their first R&D farm in January 2020. The company's name, 'Eeki', is derived from the Japanese concept of 'Ikigai', reflecting a philosophy of a healthy and purposeful life. The core of Eeki Foods' operation is its patented growing chambers which enable the cultivation of produce without any growing medium like soil or coco-peat. This technology, a form of aeroponics and hydroponics, involves suspending plant roots in the air within these chambers and nourishing them with a nutrient-rich mist. This method significantly reduces the risk of medium-borne diseases. The system is powered by IoT technology, allowing for remote monitoring and control of climate conditions such as temperature, humidity, and nutrient levels, which makes the process less dependent on manual labor and enables year-round cultivation regardless of seasonal changes. The technology claims to use 80-90% less water than traditional farming while producing significantly higher yields. The farms are also designed to be energy self-sufficient, utilizing solar power. Eeki Foods operates on an asset-light business model, partnering with landowners and other investors who provide land and capital to set up the farms. Eeki then manages the complete operations, from cultivation and harvesting to selling the produce to B2B clients, providing a source of income for its partners. The company initially focused on growing tomatoes and has since expanded to crops like cucumbers, green chilies, musk melon, and eggplants. The produce is sold at prices competitive with local markets ('mandi rates'). Financially, the company has shown significant growth, reporting revenues of ₹29-30 crore in FY23 and projecting ₹63-65 crore for FY24. Eeki Foods has attracted substantial investment through multiple funding rounds, including a $6.5 million Series A round in April 2022 led by General Catalyst, and a $7 million round in mid-2025 led by Sixth Sense Ventures. These funds are aimed at scaling operations across India, including states like Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Tamil Nadu, and even expanding internationally to the Middle East. column5: Bodd is an Australian technology company that has developed 3D body scanning technology which captures ultra rich body data, enabling brands to deliver highly personalised consumer experiences
column6: Bodd is an Australian data and technology firm founded in 2013 by CEO Rob Fisher and CTO Dave McLaughlin. The company has engineered a 3D body scanning technology designed to capture extensive human body data for creating personalized consumer experiences. Development of the core technology began in 2016 and involved several years of research in collaboration with prominent Australian academic institutions, including Swinburne University of Technology and RMIT.  The firm's primary product is a self-service 3D body scanner that completes a non-obtrusive scan in approximately 60 seconds. This process captures over 300 data points, creating a detailed digital avatar of the user. The collected data includes precise body measurements, contours, Body Mass Index (BMI), and body fat percentage, which are compiled into a 'body passport' that consumers can consent to share with brands. The scanners themselves are manufactured in Australia through a strategic partnership with Bosch Australia Manufacturing Solutions (BAMS), which also supports distribution and in-field technical service.  Bodd operates on a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) business model, charging clients on a per-scan basis rather than requiring an upfront capital outlay for the hardware. This approach provides a recurring revenue stream tied to the usage of the deployed scanners. The company serves a diverse client base across several industries, including apparel, health and fitness, military, and corporate uniforms. For the apparel industry, the technology addresses the significant costs associated with returns due to incorrect sizing by providing accurate size recommendations. In the wellness and health sectors, the data can be used for personalized product recommendations and tracking health metrics.  The company has achieved significant milestones, including securing approximately $8 million in total funding from sources like an Angel round in December 2022 and grants from the Advanced Manufacturing Growth Centre. This capital is being used to fuel expansion into North American and European markets. Bodd has already established a customer base in Australia, New Zealand, and Southeast Asia, and is conducting trials with major retailers and wellness brands in North America. The company was also named Company of the Year at the 2022 Pause Awards. column5: Nurses' Workflow App for Dementia Care
column6: Momo Medical, a Dutch health-tech company founded in 2017, provides a monitoring system to enhance patient safety and caregiver efficiency in nursing homes. The company was established by Menno Gravemaker and Ide Swager, both alumni of TU Delft with backgrounds in Electrical Engineering. Gravemaker's personal experience with his grandmother in a nursing home highlighted the technological gaps and the immense pressure on caregivers, inspiring the venture. He observed the staff's challenges, particularly during night shifts, which motivated the development of a solution to ease their workload. The founders initially focused on preventing pressure ulcers but pivoted in early 2020 to a broader application within nursing homes after recognizing a more significant need. The company's core offering is the Momo BedSense system, which operates on a business-to-business subscription model. This system includes a patented, internet-connected sensor plate placed under a resident's mattress, a companion app for caregivers, and a dedicated communication network. The sensor is designed to be non-intrusive and monitors micro and macro movements, including breathing and heart rate, to provide real-time insights. These insights help caregivers know if a resident is in or out of bed, is restless, or has been in one position for too long, which helps prevent pressure sores and cramps. A key feature is the ability to predict a potential bed exit up to 70 seconds in advance, allowing for proactive fall prevention. The system aims to reduce false alarms, which are common with older sensor technologies. The Momo App synthesizes this data into a clear overview for the entire care team, enabling them to prioritize attention on residents who need it most. This shift from routine physical checks to person-centered, data-driven care results in improved sleep for residents and a reduced workload for staff, with one study indicating time savings of 4.5 hours per day for a 90-resident home. The company reports significant outcomes for its clients, including a reduction in fall incidents. Momo Medical serves nursing homes primarily in the Netherlands and has expanded into North America and Belgium. column6: Positioned at the forefront of India's clean energy transition, NEWEN SYSTEMS PRIVATE LIMITED provides critical infrastructure for energy storage and management. The company was founded in 2020 by Nitin Sharma and Nitesh Bhutada, who spun the BESS (Battery Energy Storage System) division out of Raychem RPG. Headquartered in Vadodara, Gujarat, Newen Systems operates with a mission to address the intermittency of renewable energy sources and to support grid stability across the nation.The firm's core business revolves around manufacturing and supplying advanced power electronics, including Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), bi-directional inverters, microgrid controllers, and DC-DC converters. Its product line serves a diverse client base, including utilities, industries, and clean energy developers, with both "Front-of-the-Meter" (utility-scale) and "Behind-the-Meter" (commercial and industrial) applications. A key element of its strategy is a technology and manufacturing partnership with Dynapower, a U.S.-based leader in power conversion systems. This collaboration allows Newen to produce globally recognized technology locally, aligning with the 'Made-in-India' initiative. Revenue is generated through the sale of these systems and providing comprehensive services such as system integration, modeling, simulation, and design. The company reported a revenue of ₹54.1 Crore for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2024.Newen Systems' offerings are engineered to be battery-technology agnostic, although they typically utilize Lithium-Ion batteries. Their portfolio features bi-directional inverters ranging from 100 kW to 5.3 MW and DC-DC converters from 250 kW to 1000 kW. A unique selling point is the native integration of their Power Conversion Systems (PCS) with their in-house Energy Management System (NEEMS), which provides functionalities like black start capability and seamless transition between grid-tied and off-grid modes. The company has established India's first gigawatt-scale PCS manufacturing facility in Vadodara, which is currently undergoing expansion from 2GW to a 4.5 GW annual capacity. The firm also provides solutions for the green hydrogen sector and e-mobility infrastructure, having launched India's first green hydrogen project in 2023 and a 'Way-Point Charging' concept for EVs in the Himalayas.Since its inception, Newen has achieved significant milestones, including securing its first 1 GW PCS manufacturing line in 2020, obtaining ISO 9001 certification in 2021, and accumulating a firm order book of over 500 MW by 2022. Beyond immediate savings, Collo continuously spots process faults—mis-timed valves, subpar CIP cycles, drifting setpoints—so teams can fix root causes. column5: Multi-Cloud Starts at the Edge
column6: IO River, accessible at ioriver.io, is a cutting-edge technology startup that focuses on enhancing the reliability, performance, and cost-efficiency of online services. The company operates in the edge computing market, which involves processing data closer to where it is generated rather than relying solely on centralized data centers. This approach helps in reducing latency (the delay before a transfer of data begins following an instruction), improving speed, and ensuring more consistent performance.IO River serves a diverse range of clients, including businesses that rely heavily on online services and need robust, scalable, and secure solutions. These clients could range from e-commerce platforms to streaming services and any other online service providers that require high uptime and optimal performance.The core offering of IO River is its "Virtual Edge" platform, which unifies multiple edge platforms into a single, cohesive environment. This platform integrates various Content Delivery Networks (CDNs) and provides a unified layer of security, traffic control, and serverless compute services. Essentially, it helps businesses manage their online traffic more efficiently by monitoring and rerouting it to avoid outages and performance issues. The company guarantees a 99.999% uptime, ensuring that services remain available almost all the time.IO River's business model is based on providing these integrated services to its clients, who pay for the enhanced performance, security, and reliability that the platform offers. The company makes money through subscription fees or usage-based pricing, depending on the specific needs and scale of the client's operations.In summary, IO River is revolutionizing the edge computing space by making it more accessible and efficient for businesses. By offering a unified platform that bridges multiple edge services, the company helps its clients achieve consistent and optimal performance worldwide.Keywords: Edge Computing, Virtual Edge, CDN Integration, Traffic Control, Serverless Compute, Security, Uptime Guarantee, Performance Optimization, Online Services, Data Processing.

column5: Healthy Eating At Work, Made Easy
column6: Foorban operates as a food-tech platform in Italy, focused on enhancing workplace well-being through smart and healthy meal solutions. The company was established in Milan in 2016 by Marco Mottolese, Stefano Cavaleri, and Riccardo Pozzoli. The founders identified a personal need for high-quality, convenient, and healthy food options during a busy workday and aimed to transform the corporate lunch break. Marco Mottolese, the CEO, holds a degree in economics and has a background in the food tech, retail, and hospitality sectors. Stefano Cavaleri's experience is in marketing and finance, while Riccardo Pozzoli brought knowledge of American food trends and digital business to the venture. Initially launched with a direct-to-consumer (B2C) food delivery model for lunch, Foorban controlled the entire process from cooking in a central kitchen to delivery via its own fleet. Recognizing a significant opportunity in the corporate market, the company pivoted to a business-to-business-to-consumer (B2B2C) model in February 2021. This strategic shift involved discontinuing the direct delivery service to individuals and focusing entirely on providing corporate solutions. This move proved successful, allowing the company to expand its services across Lombardy, Turin, and Rome. Foorban's core offering is the "Foorban Fridge," a smart refrigerator installed in client company offices, providing employees with 24/7 access to healthy meals and snacks. Employees can use a dedicated app to view the weekly rotating menu—designed by a chef and a nutritionist—and purchase ready-to-eat dishes. The menus are diverse, catering to various dietary needs including vegetarian, vegan, and traditional Italian options, all inspired by Harvard's healthy eating plate model. The business generates revenue by providing these comprehensive food services to corporate clients, ranging from small businesses to large corporations like EY, Fineco, ITA Airways, and Hewlett-Packard. Beyond the smart fridges, Foorban's portfolio includes super-automatic coffee machines, water dispensers, smart catering for events, daily breakfasts, and fresh fruit delivery. The company also offers corporate wellness programs, such as nutrition workshops. The company has shown consistent growth, reporting revenues of 8 million euros in 2024 and reaching financial break-even. Foorban has secured several funding rounds, including a €2 million investment in January 2025 to fuel expansion across Italy, develop its smart fridge technology, and open new logistics hubs. Sustainability is a central element of its operations, utilizing compostable or recyclable packaging and partnering with organizations like Banco Alimentare and Too Good To Go to donate unsold meals. column5: Wearable autonomous driving system for visually impaired individuals
column6: .lumen is a Romanian research and development startup founded in 2020 by Cornel Amariei, with Gabriel Chindriș and Mihai Ivașcu as co-founders. Amariei's personal connection to the challenges of disability, growing up in a family where both parents and his sister have disabilities, inspired the company's mission. Before .lumen, Amariei was the Head of Innovation at Continental Automotive Systems. The company develops assistive technology for the 40 million blind people worldwide, a number expected to grow significantly. Its flagship product is the .lumen Glasses, a headset designed to replicate and expand upon the capabilities of a guide dog, addressing the significant gap between the number of visually impaired individuals and the approximately 28,000 guide dogs available globally. The technology leverages concepts from autonomous driving and robotics, scaled down into a wearable device. The system uses AI, sensors, and cameras to create a 3D map of the environment, understand surroundings, and compute safe walking paths over 100 times per second without needing an internet connection. It communicates with the user through a patented haptic and auditory feedback system, essentially "pulling" the user's head to guide them around obstacles and toward destinations. .lumen operates on a B2C model, planning to sell the device directly to users and through healthcare providers. A limited-series launch is planned for late 2024, with entry into the US market anticipated in late 2025. The company aims to sell 10,000 units by the end of 2026. In July 2024, the startup secured €5 million in funding, including €4 million from the European Innovation Council and Venture to Future Fund, and €1 million from private investors via SeedBlink, to support its strategic roadmap. The core technology, called Pedestrian Autonomous Driving (PAD) AI, also has potential applications in other markets like delivery robotics and outdoor augmented reality. column5: Insect farming technology for upcycling organic by-products
column6: Reploid Group AG is a biotechnology company headquartered in Wels, Austria, that specializes in insect farming technology to upcycle organic waste. Founded in 2019 by Philip Pauer, who serves as CEO, the company utilizes the larvae of the Black Soldier Fly (BSF) to convert organic by-products from the food and feed industry into valuable resources. This process yields high-quality proteins, fats, and organic fertilizers. The company's business model is centered around a decentralized network of container-based, modular insect rearing facilities called "ReFarmUnits". Reploid partners with agricultural and food industry clients, offering an end-to-end solution that includes sourcing local organic waste, operating the ReFarmUnits, and marketing the final products. This approach helps clients reduce their ecological footprint and disposal costs while creating a circular economy by reintroducing nutrients back into the value chain. The company employs AI-supported big data analysis to optimize biological processes and enhance resource efficiency. Reploid was formed from the merger of three European BSF producers: madebymade, Nutrifly, and Insektianer. A significant milestone occurred in July 2025, when the company was listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange's "Direct Market Plus", an unusual step for a company only a few years after its founding. In August 2025, the German food giant Premium Food Group (formerly Tönnies) became a strategic partner and shareholder, aiming to utilize Reploid's technology for its own food production by-products. The company has received approvals to establish its ReFarmUnits in Germany, with plans for further expansion in Austria, Switzerland, Italy, the Czech Republic, and France. column6: Reality Defender is a cybersecurity company founded in 2021 that provides a deepfake and AI-generated media detection platform for enterprise, government, and institutional clients. For example, it offers a Zoom plugin that analyzes participants' video and audio feeds in real-time to identify signs of synthetic manipulation. Reality Defender's business model is primarily subscription-based, offering different tiers based on usage and features to generate recurring revenue. Reality Defender serves a diverse client base that includes financial institutions, government agencies, media organizations, and technology platforms. Notable clients and partners include Visa, Microsoft, NATO, and NBCUniversal. The firm has attracted significant investment from backers such as Illuminate Financial, Booz Allen Ventures, IBM Ventures, Accenture, and DCVC, securing a total of $33 million in its Series A funding round by October 2024. column5: Open-source inference engine for scaling AI models cheaper and faster
column6: Inferact is an artificial intelligence infrastructure company founded by the creators and core maintainers of vLLM, the world's most widely adopted open-source large language model inference engine. Originating from UC Berkeley's Sky Computing Lab in 2023, vLLM has grown to become the de facto standard for deploying AI models at scale, with over 60,000 GitHub stars, a global community of 2,000+ contributors, and adoption by major technology companies including Meta, Google, Character.AI, Amazon, and the broader AI industry. vLLM addresses a fundamental problem: as large language models have grown exponentially in size and capability, running them efficiently in production has become a critical bottleneck. The company's core innovation, PagedAttention, dynamically optimizes GPU memory allocation, enabling significant reductions in inference costs and latency while maintaining model quality—allowing enterprises to serve more users on fewer servers.Inferact's dual mission combines open-source stewardship with commercial innovation. The company commits to maintaining vLLM as an independent, vendor-neutral project under the PyTorch Foundation governance, continuously advancing the engine with support for emerging model architectures (mixture-of-experts, multimodal, agentic AI), expanding hardware coverage (NVIDIA, AMD, Google TPU, AWS Neuron, Intel, and custom accelerators), and pushing performance boundaries through distributed inference, speculative decoding, and disaggregated serving. Simultaneously, Inferact is building a commercial platform—a managed inference service that abstracts away operational complexity. This enterprise offering provides serverless model deployment, observability and monitoring, troubleshooting tools, disaster recovery, and multi-tenant scaling on Kubernetes, enabling engineering teams to focus on AI applications rather than infrastructure.The company's positioning at the intersection of model providers, hardware vendors, and enterprises creates a unique ecosystem advantage: deep technical relationships with both sides of the AI stack, the ability to influence industry standards, and a user base that depends on vLLM's performance and reliability. Inferact's founding team—including CEO Simon Mo (PhD student and original vLLM creator), co-founders Woosuk Kwon, Kaichao You, Roger Wang, Joseph Gonzalez (UC Berkeley faculty), and Ion Stoica (Databricks co-founder and Sky Computing Lab director)—brings 15+ years of collective experience building infrastructure companies that transformed entire technology sectors, particularly Apache Spark and Ray from research projects into industry standards. Backed by $150 million in seed funding from Andreessen Horowitz, Lightspeed, Sequoia, and other leading investors at an $800 million valuation, Inferact is positioned to accelerate the shift from inference as a research problem to inference as a solved, commoditized, and profitable operating layer of the AI stack.Keywords: open-source inference engine, large language model serving, GPU optimization, PagedAttention, model deployment, serverless inference, enterprise AI infrastructure, multi-hardware support, distributed inference, PyTorch Foundation, managed services, AI infrastructure, generative AI, LLM optimization, production AI systems.

column5: Offers demand forecasting and enriched data analytics for companies in the material and chemical industry
column6: MIR Insight AS, founded in Oslo, Norway, in 2021 by Nuno Barros and Bjol R Frenkenberger, operates as a specialized provider of AI-driven market forecasting solutions. The company targets the process industries, with a particular focus on the material, chemical, textile, fiber, and plastic sectors. Its business model is B2B, delivering its technology as a SaaS solution to help clients mitigate risks associated with poor forecasting, such as excess working capital costs, overproduction, and resource waste. The firm's core offering is a proprietary AI platform that provides demand, supply, and pricing forecasts with high accuracy. This platform works by having clients upload their anonymized sales data, which MIR Insight then enriches with vast external market data. Utilizing neural networks and advanced techniques like similarity searches and clustering, the system identifies key market indicators and hidden correlations to generate dynamic, multi-factor forecasts. This process enables clients to shift from sentiment-based planning to precise, data-driven decision-making, helping them manage losses, optimize resource allocation, and enhance operational efficiency. A key feature of their technology is its energy efficiency compared to traditional AI methods. The leadership team's expertise is central to the company's value proposition. CEO Bjol Frenkenberger holds a Ph.D. from Oxford specializing in decision-making under uncertainty in startups. CTO Nuno Barros brings deep experience in machine learning and data science, while CDO Jonas Falkner has a research background in supply chain forecasting. The team also includes CCO Friedrich Weninger, who has over 25 years of executive experience in the materials industry. In January 2025, MIR Insight secured approximately $625K (€600k) in a seed funding round led by Vanagon Ventures, with participation from EWOR and Floris Capital, to advance its mission of merging sustainability with profitability through improved planning. column5: Provider of smart devices for intelligent incontinence solutions
column6: AssistMe GmbH is a Berlin-based MedTech startup developing intelligent digital assistance systems for professional elderly care settings. The company's flagship product, alea, combines Internet-of-Things technology, artificial intelligence, and cloud infrastructure to revolutionize incontinence management and care coordination in nursing homes. Founded on the principle that digitalization should enhance human care rather than replace it, AssistMe addresses one of the most pressing challenges in modern healthcare: delivering dignity-centered, efficient care while supporting overwhelmed care professionals.alea operates as a sensor-enabled ecosystem where specialized clips attached to smart incontinence products detect saturation levels, movement patterns, and fall risks, transmitting real-time data to a central cloud platform. Care staff receive notifications via mobile app or web-based dashboard, enabling need-based interventions rather than routine checks. The system integrates automated documentation that eliminates manual record-keeping, generates positioning protocols for pressure ulcer prevention, and provides facility managers with data-driven insights for resource optimization. Scientific validation through partnership with Neubrandenburg University of Applied Sciences confirms measurable improvements in resident quality of life, sleep quality, and caregiver working conditions, alongside documented cost savings averaging 23% in material and labor expenses.AssistMe's business model centers on recurring subscription revenue, with care facilities paying per-resident-per-month pricing and no upfront implementation costs. Major operators including Alpenland Group, Führer Group, and AWO have adopted the platform across Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. The company operates in strategic partnership with TZMO, a leading incontinence product manufacturer, ensuring product compatibility and market reach. The July 2025 €5.2 million growth funding round, led by Albers Investment and Brandenburg Kapital, positions AssistMe for international expansion and establishment of in-country manufacturing capabilities. column6: Synthesized provides an AI-powered test data infrastructure platform designed for enterprises to automate and accelerate software testing. Founded in 2017 by Nicolai Baldin and Denis Borovikov, the London-based company aims to resolve the bottlenecks in traditional Quality Assurance (QA) processes where obtaining realistic and compliant test data is a significant challenge. Founder and CEO Nicolai Baldin's background in machine learning and statistics, including collaborations with financial institutions and the NHS, highlighted the difficulty in accessing quality test data due to compliance barriers, which sparked the idea for the company. The company operates on a B2B SaaS business model, primarily targeting development and QA teams in highly regulated industries such as finance, insurance, and healthcare. Its revenue is generated through software licenses based on data processing volumes and database sizes, employing a usage-based pricing structure. Strategic investors and clients include major financial institutions like Deutsche Bank and UBS, which use the platform to improve their software delivery cycles. Synthesized has secured significant funding, including a $2.8 million seed round in March 2020 and a $20 million Series A round in September 2025. These funds are intended to fuel expansion into North America and Europe. The platform's core technology uses a high-dimensional machine learning engine to generate synthetic datasets that mimic the statistical properties and complex relationships of original production data without exposing sensitive information. This allows organizations to create privacy-compliant, realistic data for testing, development, and analytics. The platform integrates with a wide range of enterprise systems, including Snowflake, Oracle, SAP, and Salesforce, and can be deployed in cloud environments like Google Cloud. Key features include automated data masking, subsetting, and generation, which help companies accelerate release cycles, reduce costs, and ensure compliance with regulations like GDPR and HIPAA. column5: Digital Assistants for Hospitals
column6: sqior medical GmbH operates in the health-tech sector, providing digital assistance systems designed to optimize clinical workflows within hospitals. Founded in Munich, Germany, in 2022, the company targets the significant administrative burden faced by hospital staff, which is compounded by rising patient numbers and a shortage of skilled workers. The founders—Philipp Wolf (CEO), Matthias Eimer (Product), Nils Frielinghaus (Software), and Sven Floßmann (Software)—bring a combined 60 years of experience in the medical technology industry, having been involved in major hospital digitalization projects worldwide. This extensive background in medical engineering, business administration, product design, and software architecture informs their user-centric approach to product development. The company's business model is centered on a B2B, subscription-based Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platform. Its core offering consists of AI-supported digital assistants that function as smartphone-based applications for clinical personnel. These assistants analyze, automate, and control administrative processes across different departments and IT systems. The software consolidates information from various sources, providing real-time updates to all relevant parties, which facilitates better communication and automated task assignment. The product suite includes specialized assistants for different hospital functions: an "OR Coordinator" to manage the perioperative process, a "Bed Management" assistant for planning and assigning patient beds, and a "Physician Assistant" to handle daily administrative tasks for doctors and surgeons, including documentation and secure communication. sqior medical aims to bridge the gap between the mobile, fast-paced hospital environment and existing, often outdated, healthcare IT systems. By automating workflows and providing critical information on mobile devices, the platform allows clinical staff to dedicate more time to patient care and enables a more efficient use of resources like operating rooms and medical equipment. In March 2025, the company successfully closed a €4 million seed financing round led by Helsana HealthInvest and Vorwerk Ventures, with participation from existing investors QAware and WCap. This capital is intended to fund further research and development, team expansion, and a Europe-wide market expansion. column5: App-based electric scooter and bicycle sharing service
column6: Luup is a micromobility company founded in July 2018 by Daiki Okai, Ryotaro Makita, and Naomichi Okada. CEO Daiki Okai, a University of Tokyo graduate, initially envisioned a service to help caregivers reach patients in areas with poor transport access. This concept evolved into Luup's current mission: to create a transportation infrastructure that makes entire cities feel like a 'station-front area' by addressing last-mile mobility challenges. The company operates a sharing service for electric scooters and e-bikes through a smartphone application. Users can locate and rent vehicles from a dense network of designated 'ports' and return them to any other port within the service area. The service is designed for short trips, with a pricing model typically consisting of a base fee to unlock the vehicle and a per-minute charge. The app, which supports English, requires users to register with a credit card and, for e-scooter use, verify they are over 16 and pass a traffic rules test. A driver's license is not required to operate the e-scooters, a significant change following a revision to Japan's Road Traffic Act in July 2023. Luup launched its service in 2020 and has since expanded its operations to major Japanese cities including Tokyo, Osaka, Kyoto, Yokohama, Nagoya, and others. The company has established thousands of pick-up and drop-off ports, often located near train stations, convenience stores, and office buildings, aiming for a high-density network that enhances convenience for first and last-mile travel. As of early 2024, its fleet had grown to approximately 10,000 vehicles. The company has secured significant funding to fuel its expansion, raising a total of approximately 9.1 billion yen (around $68 million) by April 2023. It has formed strategic business and capital alliances with major transportation and real estate companies like Tokyu and Seibu Holdings to enhance the value of areas along their railway lines. column6: Cleanwatts Digital is a climate tech company specializing in AI-powered digital energy solutions. It officially launched as an independent entity in December 2025 following a management buyout led by founding partners José Basílio Simões (Executive Chairman), Jorge Landeck, and James McDougall (Vice-Chairman). The company's origins trace back to the experience of its predecessors, including Virtual Power Solutions and ISA (Intelligent Sensing Anywhere), in energy monitoring and management. Headquartered in Coimbra, Portugal, Cleanwatts Digital has expanded its presence to serve over 85 clients across four continents, including Europe, America, Africa, and Asia. The core of the company's offering is the Cleanwatts™ OS, a modular, cloud-based operating system designed to manage and optimize distributed energy resources (DERs). This AI-powered platform connects assets like renewable power plants, energy storage systems, and electric vehicle chargers, enabling real-time monitoring, predictive analytics, and optimization. The system allows clients to reduce energy costs, enhance energy security, and accelerate decarbonization efforts. Last year alone, the platform managed 1.5TWh of energy across nearly 35,000 IoT devices. Cleanwatts Digital's business model revolves around providing Energy as a Service (EaaS), often with zero upfront investment from clients. It serves a diverse client base, including commercial and industrial enterprises, real estate owners, data centers, public administration, and energy community managers. Notable clients include Millennium bcp bank, ANA airports, and Pestana hotels. The company develops Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) that aggregate distributed energy assets to provide flexibility services to the grid and enable participation in energy markets. This service helps clients generate new revenue streams while improving grid stability. The company also establishes and manages Renewable Energy Communities (RECs), allowing for the local sharing of clean energy. Since becoming independent, Cleanwatts Digital has secured strategic investments, including funding from Celtis Venture Partners and a €2.5 million deal with Magnify Capital Partners in January 2026. The company is ISO 27001 and 9001 certified, ensuring data security and quality management. It is actively involved in numerous R&D and innovation projects, often in collaboration with European consortiums and funded by programs like Horizon 2020 and Portugal's Recovery and Resilience Plan (PRR), to advance solutions for energy efficiency and smart grid management. column6: HAT.tec operates as a specialized software company focusing on the principle of Human-Autonomy Teaming (HAT). The company was established in 2018 as a spin-off from the Institute of Flight Systems at the Bundeswehr University Munich by Yannick Brand, Fabian Schmitt, and Professor Axel Schulte. This move was driven by their identification of a gap between academic research and industrial application in human-machine cooperation. The founders possess deep expertise in this domain; Brand has over seven years of experience in civil and military aviation and manned-unmanned teaming, while Schmitt specializes in the replanning of multi-vehicle missions. Professor Schulte contributes extensive experience from his work as a systems engineer, a research fellow, and a visiting professor at MIT, focusing on humans and automation. The company's business model is centered on developing software technology for the defence and civil industries. Business model build on design, development, integration, and distribution of these software solutions including maintenance and advisory services. HAT.tec targets applications such as manned-unmanned teaming (MUM-T), ground control stations, and reduced crew operations, aiming to enhance mission performance by effectively combining human cognitive strengths with the capabilities of artificial intelligence. The software-defined capabilities for connected mission systems are available for multi-domain applications (Land, Air, Sea) and  the firm's product portfolio includes intelligent agents for the semi-autonomous execution of tasks by unmanned air and ground vehicles, reducing reliance on manual operator input. One of its key offerings is the SCALE mission software suite, a modular system for airborne operations that manages geospatial, sensor, and tactical information to improve situational awareness for pilots and operators. HAT.tec's core philosophy is to augment, rather than replace, human capabilities. Their systems utilize AI for automated reasoning, planning, and decision-making to support humans in complex and high-stakes environments. As a testament to its operational standards, the company achieved EN9100 and ISO 9001 certification in 2020. The company has received backing from entities including the Bundeswehr University Munich and ESA BIC Bavaria.
