column5: Develops, constructs and operates wind and solar farms all around the world
column6: European Energy A/S, founded in 2004 by Knud Erik Andersen and Mikael D. Pedersen, operates as a significant developer in the renewable energy sector. The company's genesis was in Denmark, with its initial projects involving onshore wind farms in Germany. Co-founder and CEO Knud Erik Andersen brought prior entrepreneurial experience to the firm, having previously established a company specializing in control systems for wind turbines in 1983 and another in embedded computing in 1995, the sale of which provided funds to start European Energy. His engineering background from the Technical University of Denmark has been central to the company's growth. The firm has since expanded its activities to over 25 countries, reflecting a broad geographical diversification strategy. The company’s business model encompasses the entire lifecycle of renewable energy projects, from initial screening and development to construction and long-term operation. This integrated value chain allows European Energy to manage projects from greenfield development through to grid connection and ongoing asset management. Revenue is generated through multiple streams, including the sale of completed energy parks to institutional investors, the direct sale of electricity to the grid or through Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) with corporate offtakers, and the sale of green fuels like e-methanol. This model of asset rotation, where developed projects are divested to finance new growth, is a core component of its financial strategy. In January 2024, the company fortified its financial position through a partnership with Mitsubishi HC Capital, which acquired a 20% ownership stake for approximately EUR 700 million. European Energy develops and operates a diverse portfolio of renewable energy technologies. While its foundation is in onshore and offshore wind and solar photovoltaic (PV) farms, the company has strategically expanded into emerging sectors. A key area of focus is Power-to-X (PtX), which involves converting renewable electricity into green hydrogen and e-methanol. A landmark achievement is the Kassø facility in Denmark, the world's largest commercial e-methanol plant, which began production in 2025. This facility, powered by an adjacent solar park, uses green hydrogen and biogenic CO2 to produce fuel for industries like shipping. Furthermore, the company is advancing its capabilities in Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) to enhance grid stability and has a growing pipeline of storage projects. It also explores innovative applications such as Agri-PV, which combines solar power generation with agricultural activities on the same land. column5: Flexible benefits on a single card
column6: Based in São Paulo, Brazil, Alymente operates as a financial technology firm specializing in the corporate benefits sector. The company was established in 2017 by Felipe Maron, Marcelo Martins, and Andre Purri, who currently serves as CEO. The initial concept for the company arose from identifying a key market inefficiency: food service establishments faced high fees and unfavorable payment terms from traditional meal voucher companies. This observation led to six months of market research involving over 180 companies to develop Alymente's go-to-market strategy. Alymente provides a flexible benefits management platform for corporate clients, aiming to simplify the administration of employee perks for human resources departments. The business model is centered on providing a single, consolidated solution for managing various benefits, including meal and food allowances, transportation, wellness, and education, among others. For its corporate clients, Alymente offers a comprehensive administrative dashboard that includes people analytics, allowing HR teams to gain insights into the consumption habits of their employees. This platform enables companies to customize benefit packages, manage card orders, process payments, and export reports. The company also provides solutions for corporate incentives and award programs. The core of Alymente's offering to employees is a single card with the Mastercard or Visa brand, accepted at millions of establishments across Brazil. This provides employees with the flexibility to use their benefits across nine different categories as determined by their employer, moving away from the restrictive nature of traditional, single-purpose vouchers. Through a mobile application available for both Android and iOS, employees can manage their spending, use discounts from partner establishments, and make payments via QR code. The platform also integrates with services like iFood and Uber and offers access to discounts at pharmacies and other wellness services. column5: Elastin-based biomaterial scaffold for fat, enabling better soft tissue reconstruction procedures
column6: InSoma Bio is a biotechnology company developing injectable, protein-based biomaterials for plastic and reconstructive surgery. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Durham, North Carolina, the company's core mission is to enable surgeons to use a patient's own tissue to rebuild or replace tissue, offering an alternative to synthetic implants and fillers. The business operates on a B2B model, targeting surgeons and healthcare providers in the medical technology and reconstructive surgery markets. The company was founded by Dr. Stefan Roberts, Dr. Ashutosh Chilkoti, and Dr. Scott Hollenbeck. Dr. Roberts, the CEO, developed the foundational technology during his Ph.D. in Biomedical Engineering at Duke University. His background includes research at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, which motivated his work in translating scientific discoveries into clinical practice. Dr. Chilkoti, the Chairman, is the Chair of Biomedical Engineering at Duke University and a serial entrepreneur with multiple successful exits, including a publicly traded company. Dr. Hollenbeck, the Lead Medical Advisor, is a board-certified plastic and reconstructive surgeon with over two decades of clinical experience. InSoma Bio's primary product is the Fractomer Biomatrix, a scaffold designed to improve fat grafting procedures. This biomaterial is based on recombinant protein sequences found in the human body and is designed at the genetic level. A key feature is its "thermal switch": the material is a low-viscosity liquid at room temperature, allowing for easy injection with a patient's own fat tissue, and it solidifies into a porous, supportive scaffold only at body temperature. This provides structural support for the co-injected tissue, enhances its stability and volume, and allows for vascularization, which is critical for long-term tissue viability. The company has progressed through several funding rounds, including participation in the Y Combinator accelerator in 2020 and receiving grants. In June 2025, InSoma Bio was selected for the MedTech Innovator accelerator, the world's largest for medical device companies. The platform provides personalized use cases pathways and interactive, role-specific content, moving beyond passive video lessons. This strategy aims to drive measurable time savings and improve work quality for its clients. Revenue is generated through subscriptions to its platform, with a minimum commitment period of 12 months. Since its launch, the company has trained over 15,000 people. The startup has successfully raised a total of $4.55 million over two funding rounds. Its latest funding round in October 2024, led by Emerge Education with participation from Tomcat Ventures and angel investor Claudio Erba, will be used to accelerate international expansion. column6: Painterland Sisters is a consumer-packaged goods company specializing in organic, lactose-free, Icelandic-style skyr yogurt. It was founded in 2022 by fourth-generation dairy farmers, sisters Hayley and Stephanie Painter, with the mission to save their family's farm in Tioga County, Pennsylvania, amidst a challenging economic period for the dairy industry. The founders grew up on their family's regenerative organic dairy farm and, after leaving for college and travel, returned with the vision to create a product that would ensure the farm's sustainability and connect consumers directly with American farmers. The company's core product is a nutrient-dense skyr yogurt, which is high in protein, contains billions of probiotics, and has 6% whole milk fat, offering a richer and creamier texture than typical yogurt. The product line includes various flavors such as Plain, Vanilla Bean, Blueberry Lemon, and Meadow Berry, using organic cane sugar and real fruit. The business model is centered on a farm-to-spoon concept, utilizing milk from their own family farm and a network of over 25 other certified organic dairy farms in Pennsylvania that share a commitment to regenerative agriculture. This approach involves practices like rotational grazing, minimal tillage, and cover cropping. Painterland Sisters operates as a woman-owned, family-owned, and farmer-owned public benefit company, prioritizing positive impact alongside profitability. The company has demonstrated rapid growth since its launch, achieving national distribution in over 4,000 retail locations, including major chains like Whole Foods, Costco, and Publix. This expansion has positioned them as one of the fastest-growing yogurt brands in the natural channel, with a 208% year-over-year growth from 2023 to 2024 and over 5.7 million cups sold in 2024. The brand has received accolades such as the Best New Organic Food Product at Expo West and the 2025 Good Housekeeping Best Snack Award. column6: SkySnap, a Polish company founded in 2015 by Tomasz Kozlowski and Łukasz Czerwiński, provides specialized data services for the construction and infrastructure industries. The company leverages its extensive experience in surveying services to address critical pain points in the market, such as project delays and rework caused by inaccurate data. It operates primarily in Poland, serving major construction firms like PORR, Astaldi, and Trakcja S.A. The core of SkySnap's business is an online platform that processes and analyzes geospatial data collected from Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs), LiDAR, and static scanning. The platform delivers 2D maps, 3D models, and analytical reports, enabling tasks such as stockpile volume measurement, cut-and-fill analysis, and real-time comparison of as-built versus as-designed models. By automating the measurement process, SkySnap can deliver final products within 72 hours, a significant reduction from traditional methods. The business model centers on providing these data processing and analysis services, which help clients improve productivity, reduce costs, and minimize rework. The platform allows for remote site monitoring and quality assurance, equipping both field and office teams with tools to annotate digital models and share information. This enhances communication and provides a digital twin of the project, ensuring all stakeholders have access to timely and accurate data. The company's solutions utilize machine learning and artificial intelligence to extract key insights from geospatial data. SkySnap's services are tailored for various sectors within the construction industry, including road, highway, railway, utility, and commercial and residential construction. column5: Dodai Manufacturing PLC, a Japanese firm in Ethiopia, presently assembles and markets electric motorcycles in Addis Ababa
column6: Dodai Manufacturing PLC is an electric vehicle company operating in Ethiopia, focused on accelerating the transition to sustainable urban transport. Founded in 2023 by Japanese entrepreneur and former Uber executive Yuma Sasaki, Dodai—which means "foundation" in Japanese—assembles and sells electric motorcycles in Addis Ababa. Sasaki, a University of Tokyo graduate with experience at Uber Japan and an off-grid solar startup in Ghana, identified Ethiopia's potential for e-mobility after exploring various sectors. His mission is to solve large-scale transportation challenges, create jobs, and reduce reliance on fuel imports. The company's primary business involves the local assembly of imported electric motorcycle components and direct sales to consumers and businesses. Its target clients include individual commuters and gig economy workers, such as delivery drivers, who can realize significant savings on fuel and maintenance costs. To make its vehicles more accessible, Dodai has partnered with microfinance institution VisionFund to offer monthly payment plans. The business model is strategically aligned with the Ethiopian government's green initiatives, which include a ban on the import of non-electric vehicles and tax exemptions for EV parts. Dodai’s electric motorbikes are distinguished by their use of high-range lithium-ion batteries, which the company states last up to eight years, a significant improvement over the lead-acid batteries used by many competitors. These motorcycles can travel up to 150 km on a single charge. A key component of Dodai's long-term strategy is the development of a battery-swapping network. This system will allow riders to exchange depleted batteries for fully charged ones at swapping stations, addressing both charging infrastructure gaps and upfront affordability, as the battery can be unbundled from the initial purchase price. The company has partnered with Ethiopian Investment Holdings to establish 100 swap stations in Addis Ababa by the end of 2025. In March 2024, Dodai secured $4 million in a Series A funding round led by Japanese investors including Nissay Capital and Musashi Seimitsu, bringing its total capital raised to over $6 million. column6: Proxima is an AI-native biotechnology company revolutionizing drug discovery by illuminating the dynamic networks of protein interactions that drive biological function. Founded in 2019 and based in New York and Boston, Proxima has built a transformative platform that combines proteome-scale structural data generation with frontier artificial intelligence to unlock proximity-based therapeutics—next-generation medicines that control how proteins interact with one another rather than simply activating or inhibiting single targets. These proximity modalities, including molecular glues and PROTACs, promise to make historically "undruggable" disease targets accessible for the first time.At the core of Proxima's platform lies two breakthrough technologies working in concert. NeoLink, the company's proprietary data-generation system, uses cross-linking mass spectrometry (XLMS) to produce structural information on protein complexes at proteome-wide scale, capturing spatial relationships between proteins across the entire cellular landscape. This generates unprecedented datasets revealing how proteins interact in three-dimensional space—critical information that has remained largely unmapped, with fewer than 5% of human protein-protein interactions structurally characterized to date. Complementing this data engine is Neo-1, the company's atomistic foundation model series launched in March 2025 and optimized in partnership with NVIDIA. Neo-1 represents a breakthrough in computational drug design: it is the first AI model to unify de novo molecular generation with multimodal structure prediction in a single framework, enabling precision design of small molecules that can induce, modulate, or block specific protein interfaces. By generating latent representations rather than simply predicting atomic coordinates, Neo-1 can design entirely new drug candidates tailored to complex binding pockets and ternary complexes—capabilities essential for molecular glue discovery.Proxima's business model centers on strategic partnerships with leading biopharmaceutical companies, allowing the firm to simultaneously advance an internal pipeline while providing platform access to external collaborators. The company has secured multi-billion dollar research agreements with Johnson & Johnson, Bristol Myers Squibb, and Blueprint Medicines (acquired by Sanofi), with the Blueprint partnership alone worth up to $1.67 billion in potential milestone payments plus royalties. These collaborations validate Proxima's technology and provide non-dilutive capital to fuel continued platform development and internal programs. In January 2026, Proxima raised an oversubscribed $80 million seed round led by DCVC with participation from NVIDIA's NVentures, Roivant, and other strategic investors—one of the largest seed financings in biotech history. Multiple partnered programs are advancing toward clinical trials, with the first expected to begin in 2026, marking a critical inflection point as the company transitions from pure platform development to demonstrating therapeutic outcomes. Proxima operates at the intersection of artificial intelligence, structural biology, and medicinal chemistry, positioning itself as essential infrastructure for the next wave of pharmaceutical innovation targeting the 95% of the human interactome that remains structurally unexplored.Keywords: AI drug discovery, proximity therapeutics, molecular glues, PROTACs, protein-protein interactions, structural proteomics, machine learning, undruggable targets, computational biology, biotechnology

column5: Advancing precision treatments that target the aberrant proliferation driving many cancers
column6: Incyclix Bio, LLC operates as a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing precision treatments for cancer by targeting the cell cycle. The company was founded in 2020, initially as Arc Therapeutics, by a team of scientists with extensive experience in cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) inhibitor research spun out of G1 Therapeutics. The founders include Patrick Roberts, Jay Strum, John Bisi, and Fredric N. Eshelman, who collectively bring a history of successful drug development. Their journey began over a decade ago at G1 Therapeutics, where their work on the CDK4/6 inhibitor Cosela (trilaciclib) also highlighted CDK2 as a promising target for cancers that develop resistance. This insight led them to license the cell cycle program from G1 and establish Incyclix Bio to concentrate on this area of unmet medical need. The company's core business is the discovery and development of small molecule inhibitors of CDKs to treat advanced and resistant cancers. Its business model is centered on advancing its pipeline through clinical trials, a capital-intensive process funded by venture capital. Incyclix Bio generates value by achieving clinical milestones, such as FDA clearances and positive trial data, with the ultimate goal of bringing a product to market, likely through a strategic partnership or acquisition by a larger pharmaceutical company. To date, the company has successfully raised significant capital, including a $30 million Series B round in March 2022 and an $11.25 million extension in August 2025, from investors such as Boxer Capital, RA Capital Management, Eshelman Ventures, and Eli Lilly and Company. Incyclix Bio's lead product candidate is INX-315, a potent and selective oral inhibitor of CDK2. This compound is being developed to address the significant challenge of treatment resistance in various cancers, particularly in tumors where aberrant cell proliferation is driven by CDK2. The primary target patient populations include those with ER+/HER2- breast cancer that has become resistant to existing CDK4/6 inhibitor therapies and patients with other solid tumors characterized by CCNE1 amplification, such as certain ovarian cancers. INX-315 is currently being evaluated in a Phase 1/2 clinical trial (NCT05735080) to assess its safety, tolerability, and preliminary anti-tumor activity. The U.S. FDA has recognized the potential of this drug by granting it Fast Track designation for treating CCNE1-amplified platinum-resistant/refractory ovarian cancer, highlighting its promise in an area with high unmet need. column5: Boosting cellular homeostasis to prevent and treat diseases of aging
column6: Booster Therapeutics is a Berlin-based biotechnology firm established in 2020, concentrating on the development of a novel class of medicines designed to activate the body's natural protein clearance systems. The company was co-founded by Dr. Diogo Feleciano, Professor Dr. Darci Trader of the University of California Irvine, and the venture capital firm Apollo Health Ventures, as a direct result of Apollo's company creation initiatives. The foundational science stems from the pioneering work of its founders in proteasome biology. In October 2024, the company officially launched and announced it had secured $15 million in a seed financing round. The funding was co-led by Apollo Health Ventures and Novo Holdings, the investment arm of the Novo Nordisk Foundation. This capital is intended to advance the company's proprietary drug discovery platform and move its therapeutic candidates toward proof-of-concept. The corporate strategy is guided by Dr. Diogo Feleciano as Chief Scientific Officer and Dr. João Ribas of Novo Holdings as interim Chief Business Officer. The company's core business revolves around developing small molecule therapeutics that activate 20S proteasomes, a key component of cellular machinery responsible for degrading misfolded or damaged proteins. Unlike conventional protein degradation therapies that typically target a single protein at a time using ubiquitin tags, Booster's approach aims to restore the function of the 20S proteasome directly. This method allows for the clearance of a wide range of harmful proteins without needing ubiquitin, offering a more comprehensive solution for complex diseases driven by multiple protein dysfunctions. The initial therapeutic focus is on major neurodegenerative conditions such as Parkinson's and Alzheimer's disease, where impaired proteasome function is a known factor. Booster Therapeutics leverages its proprietary DGRADX™ platform, which originated in Dr. Trader's lab, to identify and develop its drug candidates. This platform integrates automated high-throughput screening with advanced structural biology, including X-ray crystallography, and computational tools to discover novel proteasome activator compounds. The business model is typical of a preclinical biotechnology company, focusing on research and development with the goal of creating a multi-disease pipeline to address various proteinopathies, potentially through future partnerships or licensing agreements. column5: AI-powered optical system for chronic wound analysis
column6: cureVision is a German medical technology company founded in 2020 by Johannes Ruopp, Richard Fobo, and Kerstin von Diemar. The founders, two of whom are medical technology engineers, developed the initial prototype to address the inadequacies in traditional wound care, where analysis often relies on imprecise tools like paper rulers. The company is headquartered in Munich, Germany. The firm has developed an MDR-approved, all-in-one hardware and software system for the analysis of chronic wounds. The handheld device utilizes optical sensors and computer vision to perform a 3D measurement of a wound's length, width, and depth, conduct tissue analysis, and document other healing parameters. This automated process is designed to be 90% faster than manual methods, generating a detailed wound report in about two minutes with 98% accuracy. The system aims to provide a more objective and reliable basis for treatment decisions compared to traditional subjective assessments. A web-based platform, cureVision® Web, allows for the central management of patient data, editing of wound reports, and tracking healing progress over time. cureVision operates on a B2B business model, targeting hospitals, nursing homes, outpatient care facilities, and home care services. The technology provides clients with significant time savings in documentation and a higher quality of care through precise and consistent data. The company has received funding from investors including Luminate, the European Union, AQAL Group, Angels4Health, and EIT Health. cureVision has also won several awards, such as the Health-i Award from Techniker Krankenkasse and Handelsblatt in 2023. column5: Creates software so that patients are not lost in the system
column6: If medical error was a disease, it would be the third commonest cause of death in the western world. What causes so much error? Clinicians have so many tasks to manage patients safely.  We are dependent on inefficient, error-prone, and expensive manual work for monitoring and referrals. Everyone is overwhelmed by the growing volume of patients, changing clinical guidelines, and inconsistent data. Salutare writes software so that patients don't get lost in the healthcare system. Salutare ONE is software-as-a-service (SaaS) that joins up clinicians with clinicians and gives patients control over how they access and manage their health data.  It makes referral for specialist care easy, such as from secondary care to a tertiary specialist centre or from a clinician to a multi-disciplinary team. It organises the monitoring of long-term patients and automatically orders required blood or radiological investigations. This takes the regulated, recurring, and consistent administrative work out of clinicians' tasks and automates them so clinicians can focus on patient care. Operationally over time, it assembles a detailed and organized patient database for hospitals to improve clinical research and clinical excellence.Salutare ONE Referral - digital MDT referral platform for Cancer MDTs or specialists which can work with any EPR, ONE Monitor - a monitoring platform for long-term conditions that can release 20-30% of outpatient appointments when coupled with PIFU (patient initiated follow up), thus shortening outpatient clinics.  Salutare ONE Testing is a cloud service for paperless phlebotomy. It lets patients go for their blood tests anywhere in a network or even nationally, including pharmacies.  It has been used as a hospital-based system for over 1 million patients.

column6: Frankly Insure is a Danish startup specializing in pet insurance, aiming to revolutionize the industry with its simple, transparent, and fair approach. Frankly Insure charges a flat fee of 25% on their insurance policies. This means that 25% of the premium paid by the customer goes to the company, while the remaining 75% is used to cover claims and other expenses. A unique feature of Frankly Insure's model is their money-back guarantee: if a customer does not make any claims during the year, they receive a refund at the end of the year. This approach not only incentivizes customers to maintain their pet's health but also builds trust and loyalty.Frankly Insure differentiates itself by offering comprehensive coverage without the usual pitfalls of bad cover, useless warranties, and lack of support. Customers have the flexibility to adapt their insurance plans according to their needs and can terminate their policies at any time without penalties. This level of flexibility and customer focus is rare in the insurance industry.The company makes money through the 25% flat fee on each policy sold. This transparent fee structure ensures that customers know exactly what they are paying for, fostering a sense of fairness and trust. By prioritizing customer satisfaction over maximizing profits, Frankly Insure aims to help as many pet owners as possible.In summary, Frankly Insure is a customer-focused pet insurance provider that offers simple, transparent, and fair policies with a unique money-back guarantee. column5: Mucosal protection platform for respiratory virus threats
column6: Leyden Labs is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing a portfolio of nasal sprays designed to provide protection against respiratory viruses like influenza and coronaviruses. The company was founded in 2020 by Koenraad Wiedhaup, Ronald Brus, Jaap Goudsmit, and Dinko Valerio, a team of industry veterans from companies like Crucell, which was acquired by Johnson & Johnson. The idea for the company originated during the first COVID-19 lockdown, with the mission to prevent future pandemics by developing products that protect against entire viral families. Leyden Labs' core technology is its Mucosal Protection Platform, which focuses on delivering broadly protective antibodies directly to the nasal mucosa, the entry point for many airborne viruses. Unlike traditional vaccines that rely on a systemic immune response, these antibody-based nasal sprays are designed to provide immediate protection by creating a barrier that neutralizes viruses at the site of infection. This approach is intended to be effective for everyone, including those with compromised immune systems, and to remain effective even as viruses mutate by targeting conserved regions of the viruses. The company's lead product candidate is PanFlu, a pan-influenza nasal spray featuring the human monoclonal antibody CR9114. Leyden Labs holds an exclusive license from Janssen Pharmaceuticals, a Johnson & Johnson company, to develop and commercialize CR9114 for mucosal administration. This antibody has shown the ability to protect against both influenza A and B strains in preclinical models. The company is also developing a similar program for coronaviruses. Recent data from clinical studies have shown that the nasal spray is safe and can maintain protective antibody levels in the nasal cavity. Leyden Labs operates on a business model centered on the research, development, and eventual commercialization of its proprietary nasal sprays. The company has raised significant capital to fund its clinical trials and platform development, securing approximately $257 million over four rounds from a syndicate of global investors including GV (formerly Google Ventures), SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Casdin Capital, and Polaris Partners. In January 2025, Leyden Labs acquired CoV Biotechnology Pte. Ltd., a Singapore-based company, to expand its research and development efforts and pandemic preparedness initiatives in Asia. column6: Samotics provides AI-driven monitoring for AC motors and rotating equipment, aiming to enhance performance and energy efficiency. The company's core technology, SAM4, is a plug-and-play system that analyzes electrical signals from the motor control cabinet. This non-intrusive approach allows for the detection of developing mechanical and electrical faults up to five months in advance, helping to prevent unplanned downtime and reduce energy waste. The system captures voltage and current signals, which are then processed by machine learning algorithms to identify failure patterns and offer actionable insights. Clients include major industrial companies such as ArcelorMittal, Nobian, and Anglian Water. Founded in 2015 as Semiotic Labs by Gerben Gooij, Simon Jagers, and Jasper Hoogeweegen, the company rebranded to Samotics in 2021. This change reflected its expanded focus beyond predictive maintenance to include energy efficiency optimization. Founder and former CEO Jasper Hoogeweegen has a background in econometrics and previously worked in asset management, which informed the company's data-centric approach to industrial maintenance. The company has secured significant funding, including a €14.5 million Series A round in 2022, to support its international expansion, particularly in the US market, and further develop its technology. The business model is based on providing its monitoring system as a service. Samotics serves asset-heavy industries where operational reliability and energy consumption are critical, such as manufacturing, water and wastewater, and chemical sectors. By offering a comprehensive solution that includes hardware, software, and analytics, the company helps its clients optimize maintenance schedules, improve operational efficiency, and contribute to sustainability goals by minimizing energy usage. column5: Digitizes and automates the tissue dissection workflow to help pathologists obtain more reliable molecular diagnostic test results
column6: Xyall is an innovative medtech company based in Eindhoven, Netherlands, specializing in automated tissue dissection solutions for molecular pathology laboratories. Founded in 2018, Xyall aims to revolutionize the tissue dissection process, addressing the challenges of manual, time-consuming, and error-prone methods that are typically used in tumor tissue extraction.The company’s flagship product, the Tissector, is an advanced, fully automated system designed to streamline the dissection of tissue samples. By combining robotics, digital pathology, and image registration technologies, the Tissector ensures that regions of interest (ROIs) from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) slides are accurately identified and extracted with high precision. This automation not only enhances the accuracy of dissection but also reduces human error, contamination risks, and variability between operators, ensuring high-quality samples for molecular analysis.Xyall’s Tissector system uses digital images from H&E-stained reference slides, allowing pathologists to annotate ROIs digitally. These annotations are then transferred to dissection slides, and the Tissector scrapes the tissue with precision, collecting the material into designated sample tubes without the use of liquids. This approach optimizes workflow efficiency and minimizes the need for manual intervention.To cater to various laboratory needs, Xyall offers different versions of the Tissector. The Tissector High Throughput (HT) is designed for high-volume laboratories, capable of handling up to 80 dissection slides per hour. On the other hand, the Tissector Table Top (TT) is a more compact version ideal for hospital-based laboratories, with the ability to run for more than two hours continuously.In addition to the Tissector products, Xyall also offers an Annotation Suite, which integrates with the Tissector systems, allowing pathologists to annotate slides digitally and facilitate seamless tissue dissection.Xyall has formed strategic partnerships with leading companies in the digital pathology space. Notably, a collaboration with Indica Labs has integrated their Tissector systems with Indica Labs' HALO® AP platform, streamlining digital pathology workflows from slide review to tissue dissection. Furthermore, Xyall has partnered with Motic to develop a high-precision tumor tissue dissection solution, combining Motic’s expertise in imaging with Xyall's automation technology.The impact of Xyall’s solutions on precision medicine is significant. By automating the tissue dissection process, Xyall ensures more accurate, reproducible, and scalable tissue samples, enhancing the quality of molecular diagnostic tests. This technology is crucial in the field of precision medicine, where accurate and timely diagnoses are essential for effective treatment planning.Through its innovative approach, Xyall is setting new standards in tissue dissection, helping to improve the quality of molecular diagnostics and contribute to the advancement of precision medicine.

column5: RF subsystems for satellite communications and electronic warfare
column6: Acorde Technologies S.A. is a Spanish company that designs, develops, and manufactures high-performance radio frequency (RF) front-ends and subsystems for satellite communications and electronic warfare. The company was founded in 1999 by José Luis García (1938-2011), a professor at the University of Cantabria who was a visionary in satellite communications and contributed to the creation of the Spanish military satellite communications system (SECOMSAT). He established Acorde to provide his students with international career opportunities. The company originated from a project for Indra, which sought to nationalize technology by finding a local designer and manufacturer for specific products. Acorde serves a global client base across the military, space, telecommunications, and broadcast markets, including international space agencies and Departments of Defense. The company's business model is centered on providing both standard and custom-built, build-to-spec solutions. Acorde's product portfolio includes Block Upconverters (BUCs), Low-Noise Block downconverters (LNBs), and Low-Noise Amplifiers (LNAs), which are available in stand-alone or redundancy configurations. The company is recognized as a worldwide reference in X and Ka frequency bands and also develops solutions for S, Ku, Q, and V bands. Acorde's equipment is engineered for reliability in harsh environments, such as on submarines and UAVs, and can be certified to MIL-STD-810G and MIL-STD-461E standards upon request. The company also has a business line, OCENTIC, which leverages its technological expertise to offer customized solutions for industry and renewable energy sectors. column6: Floatee, a company based in Labruguière, France, is focused on addressing the critical issue of drowning with its specialized apparel. The company was formally established in December 2021 by co-founders Philippe Bervas and Thibaut Pastier. The two met in engineering school and later both pursued careers in the aeronautical industry. The initial concept for an anti-drowning T-shirt emerged during an entrepreneurial school event, but the impetus to launch the company came after Philippe witnessed a child drowning. This event solidified their mission to create impactful products that could prevent similar tragedies. The company's core business revolves around the design, manufacturing, and sale of anti-drowning T-shirts for both children and adults. These garments function as both protective wear and life-saving devices. The primary product for children is an anti-UV (UPF50+), OEKO-TEX certified T-shirt that contains a discreetly integrated life jacket. This system is designed to automatically inflate in under five seconds upon complete immersion in water, turning the child onto their back to keep their airway clear. The trigger mechanism is sophisticated enough to prevent accidental inflation from rain or splashes. For adults, Floatee offers versions with both manual and automatic activation, suitable for various water-based activities like kayaking, paddleboarding, and boating. Revenue is generated through direct-to-consumer sales via its e-commerce website, with prices for the children's shirt around €149 and adult versions at €199 as of early 2024. The business model also includes the sale of single-use refill components, such as CO2 capsules and water-soluble sensors, required to reuse the T-shirt after it has been inflated. The T-shirt itself is designed to be reusable; the inflatable bladder can be detached, allowing the garment to be washed and re-armed for future use. A significant milestone for the company occurred in January 2023 when the founders appeared on the French television show "Qui Veut Être Mon Associé?" (the French equivalent of "Shark Tank"), which resulted in securing a new investment partner. Floatee also gained recognition by winning a gold medal at the prestigious Concours Lépine inventor's competition. column5: Rapid diagnostic platform for antibiotic susceptibility testing
column6: Microplate Dx is a diagnostics company that spun out of the University of Strathclyde in 2022, focused on combating the global threat of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The company was founded by Dr. Stuart Hannah (CEO), Professor Damion Corrigan (CTO), Professor Paul Hoskisson (CSO), and Dr. Poonam Malik (Chair). The founding team combines academic and industrial experience in biotechnology, medical devices, and biosensors. Dr. Hannah has over a decade of experience in diagnostics development, while Professor Corrigan is an expert in biosensors with multiple patents and spinout companies. The company is developing the RapidPlate™, a point-of-care diagnostic platform designed to quickly determine the most effective antibiotic for a bacterial infection. This technology combines hardware with proprietary data processing algorithms to deliver antibiotic susceptibility results in under an hour, a significant reduction from the two days required by current standard methods. The process involves adding a patient's sample, such as urine, to a cartridge that is inserted into the device. Early pre-clinical studies for its initial application, urinary tract infections (UTIs), have shown >95 diagnostic accuracy with a < 60-minute time to result. Microplate Dx's business model centers on selling its diagnostic platform and disposable test cartridges to healthcare providers like European pharmacies and aims for US market entry. The technology is intended to enable 'personalised prescribing', ensuring patients receive the correct antibiotic on their first visit, which helps to reduce the misuse of antibiotics and slow the development of AMR. The company's initial market focus is on UTIs, which affect over 92 million people annually and are responsible for a significant percentage of antibiotic prescriptions. In the future, the company plans to expand its platform to test for other drug-resistant infections, including sepsis, meningitis, and respiratory tract infections. To fund its development and clinical trials, Microplate Dx has secured significant investment. After an initial pre-seed round of over £500,000, the company closed a £2.5 million seed funding round in September 2023 and a followon investment round in 2025 (undisclosed sum). Key investors include Deepbridge Capital, the University of Strathclyde, Scottish Enterprise, SIS Ventures, and Boston-based Thairm Bio. column5: We imagine fashion as a service, where our users rent and swap high-end menswear garments as much as they like, for a monthly subscription fee
column6: Pool, a Berlin-based company founded in 2020, operates as a 'Fashion as-a-Service' platform, providing a subscription-based garment rental service for high-end menswear. The company was established by Rune Orloff and Kristian Rix, two Danish entrepreneurs residing in Berlin who questioned the sustainability of the traditional fashion consumption model. Their concept aims to reduce the environmental impact of the fashion industry by increasing the lifecycle of garments; they calculate that if a shirt is shared by two people, its carbon footprint drops by approximately 30%. The business operates on a membership model, where customers pay a monthly subscription fee that allows them to rent a specified number of designer pieces. This model provides an alternative to ownership, allowing consumers to access a rotating wardrobe and experiment with high-end fashion without the commitment of purchasing. For the fashion labels, Pool offers a solution for managing oversupply and unsold inventory, which is a persistent issue in the industry. The service is facilitated through a showroom in Berlin and, initially, via Instagram, with plans for a dedicated app. Customers can select items online, which are then delivered by bicycle courier on the same day in Berlin, or they can be picked up from the showroom. The service includes insurance to cover normal wear and tear, and all garments are professionally cleaned after each use. The company has secured partnerships with approximately 20 brands, including names like Commes des Garcons, Byborre, and Soulland. In January 2021, Pool secured a Seed funding round from investors including Axel Springer Porsche and Best Nights VC. column5: Modular plants converting used motor oil to marine fuel
column6: EnerPure is a Canadian cleantech company that has developed a patented technology for recycling used motor oil (UMO) into a high-quality, low-carbon marine fuel. Founded in 2009 by Todd Habicht in Winnipeg, the company was originally named HD-Petroleum. The technology was initially a prototype developed by Todd's grandfather, Bernard George Habicht, who was also the inventor of the rotary combine. Todd Habicht recognized the global potential of the technology, turning the backyard project into a commercially proven and patented process. The company's core business revolves around deploying modular, micro-scale recycling plants that are significantly less capital-intensive than traditional re-refining solutions, costing about 5% of the capex. This modular design allows for localized recycling, bringing the solution directly to the source of the waste oil and reducing collection costs. EnerPure's patented three-phase process involves pre-treatment and dehydration to remove contaminants, followed by thermal cracking and distillation to produce marine distillate fuel. The resulting fuel is compliant with the ISO 8217 standard and has a sulphur content below 0.1%, with a carbon intensity 14.6% lower than comparable petroleum-based marine fuels. EnerPure operates on a business model of building and operating these recycling plants. Its revenue is generated from the sale of the produced marine fuel. The company has proven its technology through a pilot plant in Southern Manitoba, which processed 1.6 million litres of UMO and sold over 1.2 million litres, validating market demand. Key customers include Maersk, the world's largest container shipping company, through an off-take agreement with Elbow River Marketing, a subsidiary of Parkland Corporation. The company has received funding from investors such as Sustainable Development Technology Canada (SDTC), Green Union Capital, and Cliffbrake, raising over $11.2 million. column5: Ambient Carbon's MEPS (Methane Eradication Photochemical System) creates value for customers by eradicating low-concentration methane emissions
column6: Ambient Carbon, founded in 2021 and based in Frederiksberg, Denmark, is a company focused on climate restoration by developing technologies to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions. The company's international team, which includes co-founders Matthew S. Johnson (Chief Science Officer) and David S. Miller (Chief Operating Officer), along with CEO David Kenney, combines scientific research with business acumen to create high-impact, deep-tech climate solutions. The core of Ambient Carbon's offering is its proprietary Methane Eradication Photochemical System (MEPS). This technology was invented at the University of Copenhagen and addresses the significant environmental challenge of methane, a greenhouse gas with a global warming potential 84 times that of carbon dioxide over a 20-year period. The MEPS technology utilizes a patented gas-phase photochemical process that generates chlorine radicals from salt, water, and electricity. When activated by UV LED arrays, these radicals break down low-concentration methane in a closed-loop system, effectively mimicking a natural atmospheric process. The system is designed to be non-invasive, ensuring that operations in its target markets are not disturbed. Ambient Carbon primarily serves the agricultural sector, specifically dairy and meat producers, which are responsible for a substantial portion of global anthropogenic methane emissions. A recent large-scale field trial at a 250-cow dairy barn in Denmark successfully demonstrated that the MEPS unit, housed in a standard 40-foot shipping container, can eradicate up to 90% of methane from ventilation air. Beyond methane, the system also removes ammonia and other odors, and it produces fertilizer as a byproduct, which can help reduce operational costs for farmers. The company also targets methane leakage from wastewater treatment plants and biogas production facilities. Ambient Carbon plans for a commercial launch of MEPS in the second quarter of 2026, scaling globally through distribution and manufacturing partnerships. column6: Aithra, a Toulouse-based deep-tech company, is commercializing a new method for producing technical ceramics. These sectors require ultra-resistant and miniaturized components for applications like satellite structures, electronic circuits, and biocompatible parts. Aithra's process is compatible with a wide range of materials, including zirconia, alumina, sapphire, diamond, and various metal alloys. This versatility allows for the creation of complex parts with controlled density and grain size, which is a significant advantage over traditional manufacturing methods that often force a choice between ideal materials and desired shapes. column5: Grocery shopping with weekly deliveries of locally-sourced, seasonal fruits and vegetables to combat food waste
column6: PimpUp operates as a direct-to-consumer enterprise addressing food waste at the production level in France. The company was co-founded by engineers Anaïs Lacombe and Manon Pagnucco, who met during their studies at EPF in Montpellier. Inspired by a trip to the United States and a desire to act on the significant food waste occurring before products reach stores, they launched PimpUp on October 16, 2020. Both founders were influenced by their family backgrounds connected to nature and agriculture, which fueled their mission to create a business with a tangible impact. The company's business model centers on creating a new sales channel for "imperfect" or surplus food products that would otherwise be discarded. PimpUp partners directly with over 150 producers and cooperatives, purchasing items that don't meet conventional retail standards due to size, shape, or overproduction. This approach provides producers with an equitable income for a larger portion of their harvest. The core offering is a subscription-based service for customizable baskets of fruits, vegetables, and, more recently, grocery items. These baskets are sold to consumers at a price point approximately 30% lower than traditional retail. Revenue is generated directly from the sale of these baskets through pre-orders, a system that allows PimpUp to manage its own inventory and avoid waste. PimpUp's service provides clients with access to fresh, seasonal products delivered to a network of over 170 local pickup points, including bakeries and libraries, facilitated by partnerships with organizations like La Poste. In late 2024, the company secured a significant €1.7 million in funding from notable tech and impact investors, including the co-founders of La Fourchette and Dataiku. This capital is earmarked for national expansion across France by 2026, optimizing logistics with proprietary software, and evolving into a comprehensive online anti-waste supermarket. The company also offers its services to businesses, providing anti-waste fruit baskets for employees as part of corporate social responsibility initiatives. column5: Building fully optical networks for a faster and more sustainable internet
column6: Astrape Networks is an innovative startup focused on revolutionizing the way data centers operate by building fully optical networks. Founded in 2022 by experts in semiconductors, telecommunications, and photonics, Astrape Networks aims to create a faster and more sustainable internet. The company is headquartered in Brainport Eindhoven, a hub for high-tech development, particularly in photonics.Astrape Networks serves data centers, which are facilities used to house computer systems and associated components like telecommunications and storage systems. These clients are typically large enterprises, cloud service providers, and organizations that require substantial data processing and storage capabilities.The market Astrape operates in is the data center infrastructure sector, which is crucial for the functioning of the internet and modern digital services. This market is growing rapidly due to the increasing demand for data processing and storage, driven by trends like cloud computing, big data, and the Internet of Things (IoT).Astrape Networks' business model revolves around selling its advanced photonics-based networking solutions to data centers. The company makes money by providing these high-speed, energy-efficient networks that reduce operational costs for data centers by lowering energy consumption and improving performance.The core technology behind Astrape Networks' solution is photonics, which involves the use of light (photons) to transmit data. Unlike traditional electronic data transmission, photonics can handle much higher bandwidths and speeds. Astrape's networks use multi-wavelength channels and advanced control signaling to transmit data through fast circuit switching. This means data is only converted into optical signals at the network's edges, eliminating the need for multiple conversions and making the process more efficient. This approach not only speeds up data transmission but also significantly reduces energy consumption, with current reductions at 20% and potential future reductions up to 60%.Keywords: Photonics, Data Centers, Optical Networks, Energy Efficiency, High-Speed Communication, Bandwidth, Cloud Computing, Telecommunications, Semiconductor, Sustainable Technology.

column5: We are reshaping how the world enjoys alcohol — one edible cocktail at a time. With patented production, explosive growth, and award-winning products, OSITOS is the first edible alcohol brand ready to scale globally
column6: OSITOS is creating a new category in one of the world’s largest and most traditional industries: alcohol. We turn cocktails into edible gummies with alcohol — a format that’s legal, scalable, and loved by consumers. Think Piña Colada, Strawberry Gin Tonic, or Mojito… but in solid form. We sell them in retail, online, and through hotels and events. But our long-term goal is much bigger: to become the global manufacturer of edible alcohol products for the entire industry.We’ve built proprietary foodtech to stabilize high-proof alcohol in a solid matrix — a challenge no other brand in the world has cracked at scale. This gives us a strong competitive advantage. Our manufacturing is fully operational, our products are sold in over 200 physical stores across Spain and Portugal, and we’ve reached over €300K in revenue in 2024 with zero marketing spend. We’re currently working on expanding into Netherlands, Poland and other European countries.Our business model is hybrid:B2C via our own brand (OSITOS), focused on retail, gifting and impulse purchase.B2B through EPIC, our manufacturing-as-a-service unit for third-party alcohol brands.This second model is highly scalable and capital-efficient: we enable major spirit brands to launch their own edible products using our know-how and production, with minimal time-to-market and no need for internal R&D.The global spirits market exceeds €500B annually. Even adjacent "fun" categories like liquor chocolates or alcohol-infused ice cream each exceed €500M–800M in annual sales. We believe solid-format alcohol has the potential to become a billion-euro category in itself — and we intend to lead it.We’re a team of three co-founders operating with high efficiency:Tamar Gigolashvili, co-CEO and strategist, with a background in law, business, and international growth.Ander Méndez, co-CEO and product lead, with experience in foodtech and startups from MassChallenge, and EIT Foods.Alejandra Caballero, head of sales, leading our presence in supermarkets and hospitality.To date, we’ve bootstrapped our way to product-market fit. We’re now raising our first funding round to scale retail, expand our B2B capacity, and invest in international growth. Our roadmap includes functional product lines (nutraceuticals), cannabis-infused edibles (in markets where legal), and eventually — our own production facility.We’re not just building a brand. We’re building infrastructure for a new product format that alcohol companies around the world are already starting to explore. We’ve done the hard part — the tech, the legal groundwork, the early market validation.Now we’re ready to grow.

column5: Care orchestration software automating clinical pathways
column6: UpHill is a Portuguese health-tech company that provides a care orchestration platform designed to automate and standardize clinical pathways for hospitals and other healthcare institutions. The firm was founded in 2015 by medical doctors Eduardo Freire Rodrigues, Duarte Sequeira, and Luís Patrão, who were motivated to address the variability and fragmentation in clinical practice. CEO Eduardo Freire Rodrigues is a public health specialist with a medical degree from NOVA Medical School and clinical research training from Harvard Medical School. COO Duarte Sequeira's master's thesis in Health Informatics and Management formed the basis for the first pilot version of an UpHill product. The founders' direct experience in the medical field provided them with firsthand insight into the challenges of inconsistent care delivery and its impact on patient outcomes. The company's core offering is a software platform that functions as a care orchestration and automation tool. It integrates with existing hospital information systems, such as Electronic Health Records (EHRs), to provide healthcare professionals with a unified view of a patient's journey. Key features include remote patient monitoring, task automation for clinicians, patient stratification to prioritize care, and the automatic generation of clinical record proposals. By mapping and automating best-practice clinical workflows, the platform aims to increase hospital capacity, improve adherence to medical best practices, and enhance patient outcomes, such as reducing hospital readmissions by up to 65% in some cases. UpHill's software is certified as a medical device. UpHill operates on a B2B SaaS business model, charging hospitals a licensing fee based on the number of users, typically on an annual or multi-year basis. Its clients are primarily large hospital units and healthcare providers in the Iberian Peninsula, including ULS Sta Maria, Luz Saúde, and the Institut Guttmann in Spain. The company's technology is reported to cover approximately 25% of the Portuguese population. In late 2023, UpHill launched Liber, a direct-to-consumer digital health service and mobile app that provides 24/7 access to doctors for acute issues and health promotion programs. The company has raised a total of €12 million over several funding rounds. A significant Series A round in March 2024 brought in €7 million, led by Explorer and a social impact fund from Redstone and EnjoyVenture, with participation from existing investors. This funding is aimed at international expansion into markets like the UK and Spain, along with doubling its team size. column5: Enhancing human potential through robotic solutions
column6: Adapta Robotics, a Romanian robotics company, specializes in creating adaptable robotic products for challenging automation scenarios across various industries. The company's business model involves a one-time purchase fee for the robot, supplemented by annual license and maintenance fees. The genesis of Adapta Robotics traces back to the founders' passion for robotics, cultivated within their team at the Polytechnic University of Bucharest. Founded in 2015 by engineers Mihai Crăciunescu, Cristian Dobre, and Diana Baicu, the venture initially operated as a corporate robotics department within rinf.tech, a software development company. This structure allowed them to develop their first product prototype with support from European Union funding. By 2021, the company spun off to become an independent entity, later securing a €2 million investment from Catalyst Romania to scale operations and enhance its product offerings. The company's flagship product is MATT (Mobile Automated Testing Tool), a versatile delta robot designed for the physical testing of hardware and software. MATT interacts with devices like smartphones, infotainment systems, and medical equipment by replicating human inputs such as tapping, swiping, and pinching with high precision. It is used across sectors including automotive, medical, consumer electronics, and aerospace for tasks ranging from R&D to quality assurance. The product line includes MATT Standard, MATT Extended for larger devices, and MATT Adapt, which integrates the software with a 6-DoF robotic arm for greater flexibility. Adapta Robotics also developed ERIS (Effective Retail Intelligent Scanner), a robot aimed at the retail sector. ERIS scans store shelves to identify out-of-stock products, verify price accuracy, and ensure planogram compliance. It operates semi-autonomously and can generate a full panorama of the shelves, providing real-time data to store associates and management systems. A strategic partnership with Carrefour Romania led to a customized version of ERIS named MARCEL. column5: Assisted reality solutions for hands-free digital workflows
column6: Get Your Way is a Belgian company that helps hospital pharmacies move from paper to digital workflows. We use hands-free scanning devices to improve traceability, reduce errors, and make day-to-day logistics easier for pharmacy teams. The solutions are made in Belgium and are designed for real hospital conditions.The company was founded in 2019 by Nicolas Dessambre, Antoine Malherbe, and Pierre Jenchenne, while they were students in the Startech program. The project started as an idea for connected smart glasses for cyclists and runners. It later pivoted to industrial applications, then to logistics, and finally to hospitals. The company was officially established in December 2020 and was supported by the VentureLab incubator. It is now accelerated by Ignity.Today, the company focuses on hospital pharmacy logistics. It provides a solution based on two components: hands-free devices, such as the aRdent ScanDisplay, and a web platform to manage operations, called Picking Pilot for Hospitals. These tools cover key workflows such as distribution, order reception, and inventory. Picking Pilot helps teams work with clear instructions, capture the right data at the right moment, and achieve strong traceability and compliance, including FMD-related workflows. The goal is to ensure that the right medication is delivered at the right time, in the right place, and in good condition.Get Your Way already works with several hospitals in Wallonia, such as CHR Citadelle in Liège, CH Mouscron, and CHU Namur. The company has also started projects in Brussels with CHU Brugmann, Cliniques Saint-Luc, and Cliniques Saint-Jean, and is currently expanding to other institutions.The business model is based on an all-in-one license that includes the hardware, the software, and full support for users and managers.Get Your Way continuously improves its solutions together with its hospital clients, adding new features to answer real needs in the field. The long-term goal is to extend traceability all the way to bedside scanning, ensuring full control from the pharmacy to the patient.The company has secured multiple funding rounds, including €300,000 in early 2023 and a further €850,000 in August 2024 from investors such as Industrya and Noshaq, to launch its aRdent product and support expansion.

column5: AI-powered robotic platform for manufacturing metal lattice structures
column6: TETMET is a deep-tech startup headquartered in Paris (La Défense, France), specializing in the design and industrial-scale manufacture of advanced lattice structures and architectured materials using robotics and artificial intelligence. Founded in 2023 by Tom Vroemen and Dr. Justin Dirrenberger, the company seeks to revolutionize traditional manufacturing by enabling the efficient production of large, complex, lightweight and high-strength structural parts that were previously possible only at small scale or with inefficient, costly methods. At the heart of TETMET’s offering is its proprietary production process, named Adaptive Spatial Lattice Manufacturing (ASLM). This vertically integrated platform combines AI-driven design software (LDS) with robotic assembly, fibre-laser welding and machine-vision control to build lattice-based structures at industrial scale, while minimizing material waste, energy consumption, and production costs. TETMET’s approach allows the creation of parts that are significantly lighter than their conventional solid counterparts—in some cases reducing mass by up to 70–80%—while maintaining structural strength and unlocking new material properties such as tuned thermal behavior or vibration control. The company already collaborates with players in aerospace, automotive, energy, defense, construction and space-related industries, indicating a broad applicability of its lattice-based manufacturing across sectors historically reliant on heavy materials and traditional production methods. TETMET markets itself not only as a manufacturer, but as a full-stack solution provider—from digital design to automated production—striving for a shift toward sustainable, decentralized and resource-efficient manufacturing. column5: Offers solution for modern cancer radiation therapy treatment through innovative AI technology
column6: MVision AI, a Finnish-based company founded in 2017, operates as a software-as-a-service (SaaS) provider in the medical technology market, specifically targeting radiotherapy departments in hospitals and cancer clinics. The company was established by Mahmudul Hasan, Jarkko Niemelä, and Saad Ullah Akram. Hasan's personal experience of losing a relative to cancer, combined with his background in software engineering and previous role at Varian Medical Systems, motivated him to address challenges in cancer treatment. The firm's core business revolves around its Guideline-Based Segmentation (GBS™) software suite, which leverages artificial intelligence to streamline and automate the critical process of treatment planning for radiotherapy. The company generates revenue by offering its cloud-based and local software solutions to healthcare providers worldwide. The primary product, Contour+, is an AI-powered tool that automates the delineation of organs-at-risk and lymph nodes on CT and MR scans. This process, known as contouring, is fundamental for creating safe and accurate radiotherapy plans. By automating this task, which traditionally is performed manually by clinicians, MVision AI's technology can reduce a workflow that takes hours to just minutes, aiming to make same-day treatment a reality. This automation significantly cuts down on patient waiting times, which can often be two to three weeks with manual planning. The software is designed to integrate seamlessly with existing treatment planning systems and adheres to GDPR and HIPAA for data protection. The GBS™ suite also includes 'Verify', a tool for assessing and comparing contour accuracy, and 'Guide', an educational environment for enhancing clinicians' contouring skills. More recently, the company introduced Dose+, a tool that uses machine learning to help optimize and personalize radiotherapy dose plans. The AI models are trained on diverse datasets following international guidelines (e.g., RTOG, ESTRO) to ensure high consistency and standardization, reducing variability by an average of 20%. Having been used to treat over 190,000 patients in more than 22 countries, the company has established a global footprint. column5: Autoscriber automates administrative actions in the electronic patient record
column6: Autoscriber is a Dutch healthtech company founded in 2021, specializing in AI-powered clinical documentation solutions. Headquartered in Eindhoven, with additional operations in South Africa, Autoscriber offers an ambient clinical intelligence (ACI) platform that automatically generates structured clinical notes from real-time doctor-patient conversations. This technology aims to reduce the administrative burden on healthcare professionals, allowing them to focus more on patient care. The company's software integrates advanced speech recognition and natural language processing technologies to extract relevant medical information during consultations. These structured summaries are compatible with major electronic health record (EHR) systems, including Epic, CompuGroup Medical, and ChipSoft, facilitating seamless incorporation into existing healthcare workflows. Autoscriber's origins trace back to a collaboration with CAIRElab at Leiden University Medical Center, where physicians and AI experts co-developed the initial version of the product. The company's leadership includes Co-Founders Jacqueline Kazmaier (CEO) and Koen Bonenkamp (CTO), along with a multidisciplinary team committed to enhancing healthcare delivery through technology. In 2024, Autoscriber secured a strategic partnership with Microsoft to scale its ACI platform across the EMEA region. This collaboration provides Autoscriber with access to Microsoft's resources and cloud infrastructure, enabling the company to meet the growing demand for its solutions. Autoscriber's platform supports multiple languages, including English, Dutch, German, Norwegian, French, Spanish, and Afrikaans, making it adaptable to diverse healthcare settings. The company's commitment to data security is evidenced by its adherence to ISO 27001 and NEN 7510 standards, ensuring compliance with international data protection regulations. By automating the documentation process, Autoscriber not only enhances efficiency but also contributes to improved job satisfaction among healthcare providers and better patient outcomes. The company's innovative approach positions it as a key player in the evolution of data-driven, patient-centric healthcare.

column6: United Visual Researchers (UVR) is a French technology company established in 2017 that specializes in advanced optical simulation and physics-based rendering software. Key features include path tracing, spectral rendering, light polarization, and the ability to model physical materials and environments with precision. This technology allows for detailed analysis of light uniformity, reflectance, and hotspots, which is particularly valuable in the automotive industry for evaluating specialized paints, interior fabrics, and display screens under various lighting conditions. The company's business model centers on empowering industries to adopt true-to-life digital twins, which serve as a single source of truth from design appearance to optical performance validation. This facilitates collaborative work among stakeholders and aims to accelerate innovation. column6: Established in 2001, iOmniscient is an Australian company specializing in artificial intelligence-based multi-sensory analytics. The company was co-founded by CEO Dr. Rustom Kanga and Managing Director Ivy Li as an evolution of a technology project they had been involved with for an Australian government-sponsored research group since the 1990s. Dr. Kanga's interest in AI began early in his career while leading a team developing one of the first commercial AI systems for Digital Equipment Corporation. Li has co-founded multiple AI companies and holds nearly 80 AI-related patents.iOmniscient operates in the security and surveillance market, serving a diverse client base across 30 different industries, including transportation, smart cities, law enforcement, retail, and industrial sectors. With systems implemented in over 70 countries, their business model focuses on providing outcome-based solutions rather than just selling products. This is often achieved through a Professional Services Division that offers risk analysis, system design, and turnkey implementation. Revenue is generated by delivering these comprehensive solutions, which can be bundled with hardware from partners like Lenovo as plug-and-play appliances. The company emphasizes a cost-effective approach, designing systems that can require fewer cameras, consume up to 90% less storage and bandwidth, and run on standard CPUs without the need for expensive GPUs.The company's core offering is an Artificial Intelligence Platform that analyzes data from multiple sources, including video, sound, and smell, to replicate human reasoning. This platform is built from over 100 modular analytics capabilities that can be combined to address specific use cases. Key technologies include facial recognition and behavior analytics in extremely crowded and complex environments, a capability protected by many of its 70+ international patents. The system can perform tasks like detecting an abandoned object in a crowd, even when obscured, identifying fights, managing queues, and recognizing license plates from 130 countries. Beyond video, the platform incorporates sound analytics for detecting events like gunshots or glass breaking and even smell analytics with products like the iQ-Nose for chemical scent detection. column5: We are working on a 3D Printing technology to be used in open space and on celestial bodies to manufacture large elements of space infrastructure
column6: Orbital Matter is a Polish-German space technology company, founded in 2022 by CEO Jakub Stojek and CTO Robert Ihnatisin, with the objective of becoming a construction company in space. The firm is developing a proprietary 3D printing technology designed to manufacture large-scale space infrastructure directly in orbit, on the Moon, and on Mars. This approach addresses the significant constraints of launching fully assembled structures from Earth, which must be built to be up to 70% heavier than necessary to survive the journey into space. The company's core technology is a patented, low-heat 3D printing process that functions in the vacuum and microgravity of space. Unlike conventional methods that require a slow cooling period, Orbital Matter's process does not generate heat, enabling much faster construction. By shipping raw materials instead of finished components, the company projects it can reduce launch weight by up to 70% and volume by a factor of ten, enabling the in-orbit creation of structures up to 20 times larger per rocket launch. The technology is intended for fabricating items such as large antennas, solar arrays, thermal radiators, walls for space stations, and lunar habitats. The founders' backgrounds are complementary. Jakub Stojek is a serial entrepreneur with a decade of experience in manufacturing. One of his previous companies was recognized by the Financial Times as the 22nd fastest-growing business in Europe, and he was named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 list. Robert Ihnatisin is a multiskilled engineer specializing in 3D printing, having previously worked in R&D at the 3D printing firm Formlabs, where he contributed to next-generation printers and patent applications. The two met at the Entrepreneur First accelerator in Berlin and bonded over a shared interest in hardware and manufacturing. Orbital Matter has secured over €1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Sunfish Partners and Dhyan VC, and a subsequent €1 million seed round led by Early Game Ventures. This capital is being used to advance the technology from NASA Technical Readiness Level (TRL) 5 to TRL 8, preparing for commercial readiness. The company has engaged in significant strategic partnerships, including a Memorandum of Understanding and a paid pilot agreement with Thales Alenia Space. Orbital Matter is also collaborating with industry leaders like OHB and Axiom Space on use cases and has been selected by the European Space Agency (ESA) to test its technology. A key milestone was the 'Replicator' mission, a demonstration launched aboard the maiden flight of the Ariane 6 rocket, which aimed to print a 50cm-long beam from a custom polymer using a three-unit CubeSat. A pivotal moment in the firm's history occurred in 2006 when a meeting with former U.S. Vice President Al Gore inspired van Oostrom to reorient the business from traditional development to a model centered on sustainability. The company's business model encompasses the entire lifecycle of a building, including (re)development, investment, and management. Edge develops new assets and retrofits existing ones to be smarter and more environmentally friendly. The firm's revenue is generated through the development and long-term operation of these properties, often speculatively, and held within a fund structure to retain control over building management and data. This strategy allows for continuous optimization based on performance data. Clients include major corporations such as Deloitte and Unilever. Edge's core product is a new generation of smart and sustainable buildings designed to be healthy for people and the planet. A landmark achievement is 'The Edge' in Amsterdam, which, upon completion in 2014, was recognized as one of the world's most sustainable office buildings, receiving a BREEAM score of 98.4%. These buildings integrate a dense network of IoT sensors—28,000 in The Edge alone—to monitor and manage everything from energy consumption and occupancy to indoor climate in real-time. Features include aquifer thermal energy storage, advanced solar panel integration, and smart lighting systems that reduce electricity use by up to 70% compared to typical offices. Beyond new builds, Edge launched 'EDGE Next,' a technology platform to upgrade existing buildings, and 'EDGE Workspaces,' offering flexible office solutions.
