column6: Fabstwines is a Luxembourg-based company operating a digital platform designed to connect wine enthusiasts with winemakers. The firm was founded in March 2023 by Fabienne Stanitz, who serves as CEO. Stanitz's background in the hospitality industry, coupled with her experience living in various countries, informed her vision to simplify the often-overwhelming process of wine selection for consumers. She identified a dual-sided market problem: consumers struggle to choose wines, and winemakers find it difficult to connect with the right customers. The company employs a hybrid B2C and B2B business model. For consumers (B2C), Fabstwines offers a matchmaking platform that provides personalized wine recommendations through an "edutainment" approach, which includes a "tasting game," educational content, and community features to help users discover new wines based on their specific taste profiles. For business clients (B2B), such as restaurants and hotels, the company provides expert consultation to create tailored wine lists that align with their clientele's preferences. The primary revenue stream is generated from yearly membership fees paid by winemakers who gain access to the platform to promote their products and events. Since its inception, Fabstwines has achieved significant market traction. After participating in Luxembourg's Fit 4 Start accelerator program, the company launched its MVP in November 2023, reportedly capturing 80% of the Luxembourg market within four weeks. Expansion into Germany followed in February 2024, where a waiting list of over 100 winemakers has been established. The platform initially focused on user recommendations but has evolved to prioritize giving winemakers from Luxembourg and the EU better market visibility and facilitating import/export opportunities. Future plans include global expansion into regions like Argentina and South Africa and the integration of AI for more advanced curation. Another feature, the Space Modeller, helps allocate shelf space to categories based on their potential. To address operational issues, the X-Ray Hub and mobile app identify and flag problems like out-of-stock items, incorrect pricing, or poor displays that lead to lost sales. column6: Qualia Studios is a research-driven robotics software infrastructure company that provides a purpose-built GPU cloud platform for training, fine-tuning, and deploying Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models—advanced multimodal foundation models that combine visual perception, natural language understanding, and physical robot control. Founded by Fabian Kerj in Copenhagen, Denmark, the company addresses a critical pain point in robotics AI development: the fragmented tooling, complex dependencies, and weeks of infrastructure setup required before teams can begin training VLA models on their robotics systems.The company serves a specialized B2B market comprising robotics companies, AI research institutions, autonomous systems developers, and individual robotics engineers building the next generation of spatial AI systems. Qualia's target customers include organizations developing humanoid robots, industrial manipulators, autonomous delivery systems, and other advanced robotic platforms. column6: 1-2-Taste is a Netherlands-based B2B digital marketplace for food and beverage ingredients, founded in 2018 by Jasper Schouten, Arjan Koudijs, and Jan Klawer. While suppliers set their own sales prices, 1-2-Taste facilitates the transaction and offers services like 30-day credit terms. The product offering is extensive, featuring a catalog of over 3,000 ingredients from more than 100 suppliers. Categories include flavors, colors, fruit and vegetable-based ingredients, sweeteners, texturizers, proteins, and nutraceuticals. These ingredients serve various sectors within the food and beverage industry, such as bakery, confectionery, dairy, beverages, and meat processing. The platform is built to be user-friendly, allowing customers to easily search, filter by application or certification, request quotes, and place orders. With warehouses in Europe and India, the company can provide fast delivery and local stocking for certain items to reduce shipping times. column6: Regen Organics operates within the circular economy to address sanitation and agricultural challenges in Kenya. The company processes organic waste, including agricultural and sanitation waste, transforming it into valuable agricultural inputs. This process helps to create a more sustainable and climate-resilient agricultural sector.The company was established as a result of the work of Sanergy, a social enterprise founded in 2011 by MIT students David Auerbach, Lindsay Stradley, and Ani Vallabhaneni. Their initial mission was to provide safe and affordable sanitation to residents of urban informal settlements in Kenya. Over time, they developed a system to collect and convert the waste into useful by-products. Regen Organics now commercializes these products, which include organic fertilizer and insect-based animal feed.The business model centers on collecting organic waste from cities and industrial processors, such as large-scale caterers and food processing plants. This waste is then treated and converted. The primary product is an organic fertilizer called Evergrow, which helps to improve soil health and crop yields for farmers. Another significant product line is insect-based animal feed, produced by farming Black Soldier Fly larvae on the organic waste. This high-protein feed serves the aquaculture and poultry markets.Regen Organics serves a diverse client base. On the supply side, it partners with municipalities and businesses to manage their organic waste streams. On the demand side, its customers are farmers and feed millers in Kenya. By providing these products, the company not only offers a solution to waste management but also provides farmers with effective, locally-produced alternatives to imported synthetic fertilizers and protein feeds.The company has achieved significant milestones, including receiving ISCC certification for its circular economy approach. column5: Flexible, high-resolution ultrasound sensors for multiple industries
column6: Novosound is a sensor technology company that designs and manufactures flexible, high-resolution ultrasound sensors for industrial, medical, and wearable markets. The company was founded in 2018 as a spin-out from the University of the West of Scotland by Dr. Dave Hughes (CEO and founder) and Richard Cooper. Hughes, who holds a physics degree from the University of Glasgow and a doctorate in engineering from the University of Strathclyde, developed the core patented thin-film technology during his time as a research fellow. This technology overcomes the limitations of traditional rigid and temperature-sensitive ultrasound sensors by using a printable, flexible core material, enabling high-resolution imaging on curved surfaces and continuous operation at high temperatures. The company's business model involves both selling its own branded products and providing custom solutions and R&D services for clients, essentially acting as a center of excellence for ultrasound. Its product lines include the Kelpie, a flexible sensor for inspecting complex geometries; the Belenus, for high-temperature asset monitoring; the Ceilidh, for detecting corrosion under composite wraps; and the Slanj platform, which powers wearable devices for biometric monitoring, such as the world's first ultrasonic blood pressure monitor. These products serve a diverse client base across sectors like Oil & Gas, Aerospace, Power Generation, Nuclear, and Healthcare. Clients include BAE Systems, GE Aviation, and Uniper. Revenue is generated through direct product sales, R&D contracts, and licensing deals, with a significant portion coming from North American markets. Since its inception, Novosound has secured significant funding to fuel its growth, including a £1.5 million seed round in 2018 and a £3.3 million Series A round in 2019 led by Foresight Group. The company has received numerous awards, including the Institute of Physics Business Start-up Award and recognition for its Belenus sensor at the Materials Performance Corrosion Innovation of the Year Awards. As of early 2024, the company has been awarded its 21st patent and continues to expand its international presence, particularly in the US healthcare and wearables markets through collaborations with institutions like the Texas Medical Center and Nasdaq-listed PAVmed Inc. column5: Software for creating patient education diagrams and animations in minutes
column6: Graphics et al. is an Australian-based company, founded in 2021 by Chris Pymble, that provides a browser-based platform for creating accessible health information diagrams and animations. The inspiration for the company came from Pymble's personal experience when her husband had a serious work accident and struggled to understand the text-heavy instructional materials provided to him while on heavy painkillers. With a background as a graphic artist, product developer, and lecturer in advanced surgical skills, Pymble identified a critical gap in healthcare communication, where complex information is often delivered in formats that are difficult for patients to comprehend, contributing to poor health literacy.The company operates in the digital health and SaaS markets, targeting healthcare professionals such as doctors, nurses, pharmacists, and allied health professionals. Its business model centers on providing a software solution that enables these professionals to quickly generate simple, scientifically accurate, and visually appealing educational materials for patients. The platform features a library of over 15,000 pre-approved and brand-compliant templates and assets, which significantly reduces the time needed to create a visual aid from minutes to seconds. This addresses the time constraints faced by healthcare providers and removes technical challenges related to design and accuracy.Revenue is generated through its software offerings, and the company is focused on enterprise clients, with pilot programs in development with organizations like the UK's National Health Service (NHS) and other health organizations in Australia and the United States. Graphics et al. has secured pre-seed funding from investors including Scale Investors, StartMate, and Australian Medical Angels to support its growth and platform development. The company is also working on integrating AI to further automate the creation of visual aids by allowing users to upload notes or PDFs which the system will then convert into low-literacy diagrams.Keywords: health literacy, patient education, medical animation, digital health, SaaS, visual communication, healthcare information, medical diagrams, health equity, MedTech

column5: Cellular agriculture to produce sustainable cultivated pork
column6: Meat Tomorrow, a Danish biotechnology firm founded in 2021, is positioned to address the escalating global demand for meat through cellular agriculture. The company was established by David Valbjørn, Matias Ankjær, Josef Christensen, Henning Kempf, and Jonathan Niclis. The founding team combines academic research with industry experience; CEO David Valbjørn is a 2023 graduate from the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) with a background in life science companies, while CSO Matias Ankjær previously held positions at Novo Nordisk. Scientific advisors Henning Kempf and Jonathan Niclis also bring experience from Novo Nordisk and the University of Copenhagen, specializing in stem cell research. The company is developing a technology platform to produce cultivated pork, aiming to provide a sustainable and affordable alternative to conventional meat production. Its core technology, which is patent-pending, leverages pluripotent stem cells to create various meat components like muscle and fat. This method allows for rapid cell division, a key step in making production faster and more cost-effective compared to earlier cultivated meat technologies. By stabilizing stem cells in their pluripotent state using specific signaling molecules, the company can generate high yields of cells before differentiating them into the desired meat tissues. This process is expected to reduce CO2 emissions by 52% and land use by 72% compared to traditional pork farming. Meat Tomorrow operates on a business-to-business model, intending to sell or license its production technology to the existing meat industry rather than becoming a direct-to-consumer meat producer. The company's goal is to enable established producers to transition towards a more sustainable method of meat production. Having started in a dorm room and developed at DTU Skylab, the company has a milestone of producing its first stem-cell meatball by early 2025 and anticipates its products could be available in supermarkets within seven to eight years. The firm has secured approximately $1.4 million in total funding, including a seed round of about $607,000 in September 2024 from investors such as Keystones, Danish Business Angels, and Accelerace. column5: Bridge the gap between patients and clinical research
column6: Klineo is a digital health company addressing the challenge of patient recruitment for oncology clinical trials. Founded in 2021 by a multidisciplinary team including medical oncologist Dr. Arnaud Bayle and two engineers from École Polytechnique, Thomas Peyresblanques (CEO) and Nicolas Drizard (CTO), the company aims to simplify the complex process of finding suitable clinical trials for both patients and physicians. The company operates a platform that uses AI-powered algorithms to connect doctors and patients with relevant clinical trials in under a minute. The service features two distinct interfaces, one for patients and one for healthcare professionals. Users can create a profile with specific medical information, and the platform's matching algorithms compare this data against the inclusion and exclusion criteria of a comprehensive, real-time database of all clinical trials open in France. The platform is free for patients and doctors; Klineo's revenue is generated through partnerships with industrial sponsors and academic institutions, such as Pfizer, AstraZeneca, and Unicancer, who benefit from more efficient patient recruitment. A significant milestone was a 2022 pilot project at the Gustave Roussy Institute, which led to the launch of a national platform for triple-negative breast cancer in collaboration with the patient association Collectif Triplettes Roses. In 2023, the platform expanded to include breast, skin, and lymphoma cancers. In April 2024, Klineo secured €2 million in a seed funding round from Bpifrance and business angels. This capital is intended to expand the platform's coverage to all cancer types in France by the end of 2024, with future plans to extend into other European countries, the US, and other disease areas like rare and neurological diseases. column5: Car sharing that is changing the mobility as a service market with 100% electric vehicles fleet for b2b and b2c clients
column6: Beepbeep mobilidade operates in the electric car-sharing market in Brazil, offering a station-based service for 100% electric vehicles. Founded in São Paulo in 2019 by André Fauri and Fabio Fagionato, the company emerged from Fauri's experiences in Silicon Valley, where he observed the rise of shared mobility solutions. Fauri, who also founded the Latin America Institute of Business (LAIOB), identified an opportunity to introduce a similar model in Brazil, anticipating the future growth of the electric vehicle market. The company's business model targets a broad consumer base, from millennials focused on sustainability to executives needing temporary transportation, positioning itself as a complementary option to ride-hailing apps. Revenue is generated through a pay-per-use system, where users are charged an initial fee plus a per-minute rate that decreases with longer rental durations. To access the service, customers use the Beepbeep mobile app to locate, reserve, and unlock vehicles. The fleet initially consisted of Renault Zoe models and later included the JAC iEV40 and Chery Arrizo 5E, all offering a range of around 300 km. Beepbeep established a network of "smart stations" for vehicle pickup and charging in partnership with companies like Indigo, a parking management firm. These stations are strategically located in commercial buildings, hotels, airports, and shopping centers across São Paulo and other cities like São José dos Campos and Campinas. The service allows for one-way trips between different stations and even between cities without additional costs. The company secured R$3 million in a pre-seed round from friends and former bosses in December 2018, followed by another R$3 million seed round in 2020 to fuel its expansion. However, in early March 2024, reports indicated the service's app was down and cars were unavailable, raising questions about the company's operational status. The name "Trueffles" is a blend of "true" and "truffles," meant to signify the process of uncovering information that is not immediately obvious and verifying it through linked sources. The company emphasizes data security, with servers located in Germany, and is currently optimized for desktop use. Trueffles has received support from organizations such as the Mediatech Hub Accelerator Babelsberg and Startup Incubator Berlin.Distinct from the research tool, there is a marketing consultancy named "Trueffle" that started in 2017. This entity helps mid-sized businesses with marketing strategies, brand positioning, and process optimization between sales and marketing departments. column5: The leading provider of dedicated funding solutions for online businesses and plays an important role in improving the supply of liquidity to the ecommerce sector
column6: Fulfin, operating under isarlend GmbH, is a Munich-based financial technology firm established in 2018 by co-founders Nathan Evans and Dr. Alfred “Fredi” Gruber. Dr. Gruber brings extensive experience from the finance industry, having worked for 14 years in investment banking and holding a Ph.D. in finance, while Evans has a background in the alternative lending sector. The company was founded to address a perceived gap in the market: the difficulty for rapidly growing e-commerce businesses to secure adequate financing from traditional banks.The company's primary business is providing flexible working capital and goods financing to small and midsize online retailers, particularly those operating on platforms like Amazon, eBay, or Shopify. Fulfin's business model is based on generating interest margins by refinancing its loan portfolio at a lower cost than the interest rates it offers to clients. Its core service involves a fully digitized loan application and assessment process, which allows for rapid credit decisions and disbursement, sometimes within 48 hours. The platform utilizes a proprietary AI-powered risk-scoring algorithm, Fulfin-Tech™, which analyzes a combination of bank transactions, e-commerce sales data, logistics, and inventory information to evaluate a company's creditworthiness. This data-centric approach enables Fulfin to offer loans using the client's inventory as collateral, a model less common in traditional lending.Fulfin primarily serves businesses based in Germany across various sectors including e-commerce, wholesale, retail, and skilled trades. The firm has established strategic partnerships to enhance its offerings, including a banking-as-a-service and financing cooperation with Varengold Bank since May 2022. The company has secured several rounds of funding, including a seven-figure seed round in 2019 and a Series A round of €4.35 million in August 2022, with investors such as Hevella Capital, Lakeside, and Stableton Financial. column5: Plattform for the collection, analysis and implementation of treatment outcomes in realtime
column6: Heartbeat Medical, established in 2014, is a digital health company headquartered in Berlin, Germany, that has positioned itself at the forefront of value-based healthcare. The company was founded by Yannik Schreckenberger, Sebastian Tilch, and Marc Tiedemann. Schreckenberger, who serves as CEO, previously studied physics and has been an entrepreneur in the digital health sector since 2010. Tilch's background is in biology, scientific journalism, and science communication, having worked for various media outlets and research institutions. This interdisciplinary foundation underscores the company's approach to integrating technology with patient-centered care.The core of Heartbeat Medical's business is its software platform designed to systematically collect and analyze Patient-Reported Outcomes (PROs). This involves using digital questionnaires and symptom tracking to measure a patient's health-related quality of life outside of the clinical setting. The platform, heartbeat ONE, is a GDPR-compliant, web-based system that can integrate with major Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems via HL7 and FHIR standards. It provides intuitive interfaces for collecting, visualizing, and analyzing this data in real-time, which helps medical staff in making therapy decisions. The service is primarily used in fields like orthopedics, particularly after joint replacement surgeries, and oncology, where it helps monitor mental health and psychosomatic aspects. Heartbeat Medical serves a diverse client base that includes hospitals, clinic groups, healthcare payers, medical device manufacturers, pharmaceutical companies, and research registries. For clinicians and hospitals, the platform aids in improving care delivery and provides a comprehensive overview of care quality. Pharmaceutical and medical device companies utilize the platform to generate Real-World Evidence (RWE) to demonstrate clinical value, which can accelerate drug approvals and market access. Payers and registries leverage the system to support value-based reimbursement models and enrich medical data with insights into patients' quality of life. The company's business model appears to be centered on providing this platform as a service to these various stakeholders. To date, the company has raised a total of $17.4 million in funding over four rounds, with its latest Series A round in April 2022 securing $8 million. column5: Screen-free interactive audio platform for children
column6: Yoto is a London-based interactive audio platform that produces connected, screen-free audio players for children. Founded in 2015 by Ben Drury and Filip Denker, the company was born out of the founders' concerns as new parents about the effects of excessive screen time on young children. Drury, a veteran of the digital music industry who previously founded and exited two audio tech companies, and Denker, an API expert, leveraged their experience to create a tactile and safe alternative to screen-based entertainment. Their vision was influenced by Montessori principles, emphasizing hands-on, child-led learning and play. The company's flagship products are the Yoto Player and the portable Yoto Mini. These devices allow children, typically aged 3 to 12, to play a wide range of audio content by inserting physical smart cards. The business model centers on the sale of these hardware devices and the accompanying physical content cards. Revenue is also generated through the Yoto Club, a subscription service with over 40,000 members, and partnerships with major content creators. The company's first prototype was funded through a successful Kickstarter campaign in 2017, and the second-generation player launched in early 2020. Yoto has secured significant funding, including a Series A round of $17 million in 2021 and a $22 million investment in 2023 led by the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative. Yoto's content library features over 1,200 titles, spanning audiobooks, music, podcasts, radio, and educational activities. The company has established licensing deals and partnerships with major names like Disney, Penguin Random House, Universal Music Group, and Warner Music Group. In addition to licensed content, Yoto invests in its own original IP, such as the popular 'BrainBots' series. The platform also offers a 'Make Your Own' card feature, allowing families to link to their own recordings, podcasts, or radio stations, adding a layer of personalization. The players function as Bluetooth speakers, have headphone jacks for personal listening, and include features like a nightlight, clock, and sleep sounds. column5: Artificial Intelligence for Video Analytics
column6: Videtics provides an artificial intelligence-based video analytics platform tailored for the smart city and smart building markets. Founded in 2019 by Alan Ferbach, Pierre-Alexis Le Borgne, and Alexandre Reboul, the company originated in Sophia Antipolis, France, a hub for AI development. The founders, who met at the 2018 SophIA Summit, combined their respective expertise in security, AI, deep learning, and software architecture to address a gap in the video surveillance industry. They observed that the vast majority of video feeds from existing camera networks were never analyzed, representing a significant pool of unutilized data.The company's core offering is the Videtics Perception software suite, which integrates with existing IP camera infrastructures to analyze video streams in real-time. This technology uses deep learning to detect objects, behaviors, and trends without resorting to facial recognition, aligning with the company's foundational principle of "Video - Ethics - Analytics". The platform is designed to reduce the cognitive load on human operators by flagging relevant events, such as unauthorized intrusions, traffic violations, crowd surges, or abandoned objects. For clients, which include local authorities like the cities of Nice, Cannes, and Monaco, as well as private enterprises such as Suez and EDF, the system provides actionable alerts and statistical data through dashboards and heat maps. This enables better resource optimization and informed decision-making regarding public space management, security, and mobility.Videtics operates on a B2B model, selling its software solutions to public and private entities that manage large camera networks. The system is designed to be compatible with a wide range of video management systems, preserving clients' existing hardware investments. After securing €2 million in a 2022 seed round led by Bpifrance, the company expanded its team and accelerated development. column6: AROBS Transilvania Software (AROBS) is a technology company founded in 1998 by Voicu Oprean, who currently serves as CEO and Chairman of the Board. Oprean, a graduate of the Technical University of Cluj-Napoca with a Master's in Business Administration, started the company in his parents' apartment after his desire to complete his Master's degree was deemed incompatible with his job at a previous company. AROBS began as a software development outsourcing business and has since expanded its operations globally. The company went public in December 2021, listing on the AeRO market of the Bucharest Stock Exchange (BVB) following the largest private placement in the market's history at the time, raising RON 74.2 million. The company's business model is structured around two main lines: software services and software products. The Software Services division provides custom software and embedded software development for a wide range of industries, including automotive, aerospace, marine, medical, travel technology, and enterprise solutions. They serve a global client base with partners in Europe and the Americas. AROBS specializes in areas like embedded systems, AI-powered solutions, cybersecurity, enterprise cloud applications, and intelligent automation. The firm has particular expertise in the automotive sector, delivering software engineering services for components like Body Control Modules, Infotainment Systems, and Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) to Tier 1 suppliers and OEMs. This expertise was recognized with the "Supplier of the Year" award for Engineering Services from Continental in 2021. In its Software Products division, AROBS has developed several proprietary solutions. A key product is TrackGPS, a comprehensive fleet management solution that offers real-time GPS tracking, fuel consumption monitoring, and driver behavior analysis. This product line serves over 11,000 clients in Europe and Asia and has established AROBS as a market leader in fleet management in Romania and a significant player in Central and Eastern Europe. Other products include solutions for business optimization (Optimall), and human resources management (True HR and dp-Payroll). AROBS has pursued an aggressive growth strategy through mergers and acquisitions, particularly since its 2021 stock market listing. Key acquisitions have expanded its presence in the US and Europe and strengthened its capabilities in automotive engineering, telematics, and enterprise software. column5: An open-source data platform that automatically wraps any SQL database with a real-time GraphQL+REST API for developers and a no-code data collaboration app for non-technical users
column6: Directus offers a composable, open-source data platform designed to give developers backend tooling while providing a no-code application for data management to non-technical users. The company's origin traces back to 2004, when founder Ben Haynes, then running a digital agency, sought to eliminate the inefficiency of building a new backend for every client project. This led to the creation of a tool that could generate an API and a user-friendly app on top of any SQL database. Haynes, who served as a Staff Sergeant in the U.S. Air Force specializing in Electronic Warfare and holds a BFA from the University of Connecticut, was later joined by CTO and Co-founder Rijk van Zanten.The platform functions by introspecting a client's SQL database and creating REST and GraphQL API endpoints for each table, without altering the underlying data. This allows organizations to connect data from various sources to power websites, mobile apps, internal tools, and data analytics dashboards. The system is database-agnostic, supporting PostgreSQL, MySQL, OracleDB, and Microsoft SQL Server, among others. It provides features like granular user permissions, role-based access control, version control for tracking content changes, and tools for data visualization and automation. This approach serves a diverse client base, from startups to large enterprises such as Bose and Tripadvisor, across industries like computer software, internet, and IT services.Directus operates on a hybrid revenue model. Its core platform is open-source and free to use for smaller entities. Revenue is generated through a self-service cloud offering with monthly subscriptions, and a commercial license required for organizations with over $5 million in annual revenue or funding that choose to self-host. An enterprise cloud option is also available for clients needing advanced configurations and dedicated support. The company secured $7 million in a Series A funding round in November 2022, led by True Ventures, bringing its total funding to $8.5 million.Keywords: open data platform, headless CMS, backend-as-a-service, BaaS, SQL database API, no-code app builder, data management, API generation, content management, data visualization, workflow automation, open-source backend, data democratization, enterprise data management, composable architecture, REST API, GraphQL API, internal tools, business intelligence, digital asset management

column5: Transforms bicycles into electric bicycles
column6: Virvolt, operating under the legal name RETRO FUTURISTE, was established in Paris, France, in 2019 by childhood friends Mehdi Najid and Jérôme Gaymard, who were later joined by Guillaume Roger. The founders' journey began in a garage, initially experimenting with electrifying skateboards before realizing the vast potential in converting conventional bicycles into electric ones. This venture was born from the observation that the high cost of new electric bikes, averaging around €1500-€2000, made them inaccessible for many. The company positions itself as a key player in the circular economy and sustainable mobility market. Its core business is the design and manufacturing of electric conversion kits for bicycles, allowing consumers to upgrade their existing bikes. This model serves a B2C market through direct sales and a network of over 450 partner bicycle shops that handle installation. Virvolt has also expanded into a B2B model, supplying its French-assembled motors to bicycle manufacturers for original equipment installation. Virvolt's product line includes several motor kits, such as the pedal-assist Virvolt 900 and the rear-hub Virvolt 750, designed and assembled in France, notably at Renault's Refactory plant in Flins. These kits are engineered to be repairable, with individual components available, contrasting with many sealed units on the market. The company offers different battery options, providing autonomy of up to 110 km, and emphasizes that its kits can be fitted to most standard bicycles. In addition to kits, Virvolt provides battery reconditioning and repair services, further reinforcing its commitment to sustainability. The company has transitioned from an initial workshop model to a more industrial one, focusing on becoming a motor manufacturer. This strategic shift involves co-designing and improving upon existing motor technologies to create more durable and aesthetically pleasing products. Financially, Virvolt has secured funding from investors including Afrimobility and has participated in accelerator programs like the European Startup Prize for Mobility. By offering a more affordable and ecological alternative to purchasing new e-bikes, Virvolt addresses a clear demand for cost-effective and sustainable transportation solutions. column5: Digital care companion for at-home palliative support
column6: Pal is a digital health platform designed to support families and caregivers of individuals with life-limiting illnesses by providing tools and resources for at-home palliative care. The company was founded in early 2022 by CEO Nara Moripen and COO Azi Doost. Moripen's personal experience caring for her mother, who passed away from small-cell lung cancer in 2020, was the driving force behind the company's creation. She identified a critical gap in support for family caregivers who often take on complex responsibilities without adequate guidance. The Pal mobile app serves as a digital companion that helps users plan care, monitor symptoms, and access practical, bite-sized resources. Key features include a shared care planner for team collaboration, at-home symptom monitoring tools, and a library of information on topics like pain management and communicating with healthcare teams. The platform aims to empower family caregivers, making them more capable members of the care team, which can help prevent complications and hospitalizations. Pal is designed for anyone affected by a serious illness, including patients and their caregivers. The company's business model involves partnerships with healthcare organizations, such as general practitioners, palliative care teams, and hospices, who recommend the app to patients and their families. Pal also engages in direct-to-consumer outreach through social media and online forums. In September 2023, Pal announced the closure of a €300,000 pre-seed funding round from investors including Plug and Play Ventures and a Rabobank Innovation Loan, which was aimed at funding the product launch. The startup was also the winner of the CareTech Network Program 2023, leading to a pilot collaboration with the municipality of The Hague to support independent living and reduce the burden on healthcare providers. column5: Nanosatellite constellation operator for Earth observation intelligence.
column6: Prométhée Earth Intelligence, established in January 2020 by Olivier Piepsz and Giao-Minh Nguyen, is a French NewSpace operator of nanosatellite constellations for Earth observation. The company aims to democratize the use of satellite imagery for crisis management and sustainable development by providing strategic and environmental intelligence services. Piepsz has an extensive background in the aeronautics and space industry, having worked at Dassault Aviation and Safran, including leading the Rafale Switzerland campaign. Nguyen's expertise lies in strategy and innovation within the space sector. The company's core offering is the development of a complete Earth observation system, which includes a constellation of nanosatellites, a mission control center, and a digital data exploitation platform. Prométhée secured initial funding of €2.2 million in 2020 from industrial investors, followed by a second round of €4.72 million in April 2022. This funding has been instrumental in developing its digital platform and preparing for the deployment of its satellite constellation. The company has received support from the French government, the public investment bank BPI, and the National Centre for Space Studies (CNES) under the France-Relance program. Prométhée launched its first satellite, ProtoMéthée, on November 11, 2023, which serves as a demonstrator for its planned constellation, named Japetus. The Japetus constellation will consist of 20 nanosatellites, each weighing under 50 kg and equipped with sub-meter resolution multi-spectral sensors, designed to provide high-revisit observation capabilities—monitoring areas as frequently as every 45 minutes. This system is enhanced by on-board artificial intelligence and inter-satellite connectivity, allowing for real-time alerts and rapid satellite tasking. The company operates on two main business models: "Earth Intelligence as a Service" and "Space Sovereignty as a Service". The first provides clients with access to satellite imagery and data analytics through its proprietary Earth Observation Platform (EOP). The second offers a turnkey solution for governments, particularly in emerging countries, to establish their own sovereign space observation capabilities. Applications for Prométhée's technology are extensive, covering maritime surveillance, critical infrastructure monitoring, ecosystem protection, prevention of natural disasters, and combating illegal activities like deforestation and illegal fishing. In June 2023, the European Space Agency (ESA) selected Prométhée as a Copernicus Contributing Mission, integrating its data into the European Union's Earth Observation program. column5: Pharyngeal electrical stimulation therapy restoring neurological swallowing control
column6: Phagenesis is a medical technology company that develops treatments for neurogenic dysphagia, or difficulty swallowing due to neurological damage. The company was spun out of the University of Manchester in 2007 by Dr. Conor Mulrooney and Professor Shaheen Hamdy. Professor Hamdy, a neurogastroenterologist, is noted as one of the most cited academics in the dysphagia field, and his research into neuroplasticity and the brain's control of swallowing formed the scientific basis for the company's core product. Phagenesis's main product is the Phagenyx® Neurostimulation System. This system utilizes pharyngeal electrical stimulation (PES) to treat the root cause of dysphagia by restoring neurological control of the swallow reflex. The therapy involves delivering personalized electrical pulses to the patient's throat (pharynx) for 10 minutes daily over 3-6 days. This is administered via a specialized, nasally-inserted catheter that can also function as a feeding tube, minimizing patient discomfort. The stimulation is designed to promote functional reorganization of the brain's swallow motor cortex, effectively retraining the brain to coordinate the swallowing process. column6: NOVUS GmbH is a German company operating in the electric mobility market, specifically targeting the premium, lightweight electric motorcycle segment. column6: Autonomous Knight is a Belgian hardware technology company developing a patented multispectral sensor system to enable all-weather autonomous transportation. This patented technology aims to replace the typical multi-sensor hardware stack with a single, integrated unit. column6: Based in Tallinn, Estonia, Warren.io operates as a multi-cloud infrastructure and data science platform. The company was founded in 2015 by Tarmo Tael, with the initial idea sparking from the experience of implementing over 500 e-commerce projects and recognizing the need for more efficient cloud resource management. In November 2020, Warren secured $1.4 million in a seed funding round led by Passion Capital, with participation from other institutional and angel investors. The platform is a white-labeled, self-service portal that is architected for high availability and scalability, utilizing a microservices architecture and proven open-source technologies like Ceph for distributed storage and KVM for virtualization. Key features include virtual machine provisioning with various operating systems, block and S3-compatible object storage, software-defined networking with capabilities like floating IPs and VPN services, and zero-downtime live migrations. For service management, the platform offers a built-in administrative console for client and billing management, user impersonation for support, and an API-first approach, ensuring all functionalities are accessible programmatically. The long-term vision is to create a decentralized network of local providers, allowing for the cross-selling of infrastructure resources. column6: Legume Technology, established in 2000 by Dr. Bruce Knight and his wife Jacky Knight, is a UK-based company specializing in microbial solutions to enhance agricultural productivity. Dr. Knight, a microbiologist with a PhD from Imperial College London, founded the company based on his expertise in beneficial soil microbes and nitrogen-fixing bacteria. His background includes work at the Rothamsted Research Institute and with companies like BASF, which informed his vision to create natural alternatives to chemical fertilizers.The company's core business revolves around producing and supplying high-quality inoculants and bio-stimulants for a wide range of crops. Its primary products, such as LEGUMEFiX and LIQUIFiX, utilize Rhizobium bacteria to enable legume crops to fix atmospheric nitrogen, a process that improves soil fertility and boosts crop yields. The product is a sticky brown powder that coats seeds, introducing millions of beneficial bacteria at planting. This process helps create root nodules that act as natural fertilizer factories for the plant. Beyond legumes, the company also develops mycorrhizal and Bacillus-based products for crops like wheat and corn to improve drought resistance and phosphate solubilization. Legume Technology serves a global market, with distribution in over 30 countries across Europe, North and South America, and Africa.A significant focus for Legume Technology is supporting smallholder farmers, particularly in Africa. Recognizing that expensive synthetic fertilizers and inappropriate packaging sizes are major barriers, the company has secured grants from organizations like the Gates Foundation to develop smaller, more affordable product packages. This initiative aims to make their biofertilizer technology accessible to millions of small-scale farmers, helping to improve crop yields and soil health without negative environmental effects. column6: Established in 2008 and headquartered in Rotterdam, Netherlands, Blue Phoenix Group operates as a pivotal player in the environmental services sector, concentrating on the recycling of incinerator bottom ash (IBA) from Energy-from-Waste (EfW) facilities. The firm addresses the critical need for sustainable waste management by transforming IBA, the residue from waste incineration, into valuable secondary raw materials. This process significantly contributes to the circular economy by diverting substantial volumes of material from landfills. The company, formerly known as Inashco, rebranded in January 2020 to unify its operations, including Ballast Phoenix Ltd, under the Blue Phoenix Group name. The core of Blue Phoenix's business model is processing IBA to extract ferrous and non-ferrous metals and to produce a clean mineral aggregate. These recovered materials serve distinct markets. The metals are sold back into the material economy, while the manufactured aggregates, known as Incinerator Bottom Ash Aggregate (IBAA), are supplied to the construction and civil engineering industries as a cost-effective and lower-carbon alternative to primary aggregates. The company's revenue is generated through a B2B model, based on the sale of these processed products and through service partnerships with EfW facilities. Its clientele primarily consists of EfW plant operators and civil engineering firms across a wide geographic footprint, including the United Kingdom, Germany, the Netherlands, the United States, Australia, Asia, and the Middle East. The company has demonstrated a consistent growth trajectory marked by strategic acquisitions and global expansion. A notable milestone was the acquisition of a majority stake by InfraVia Capital Partners in June 2022, which is intended to bolster further growth and development. Blue Phoenix has expanded its portfolio through acquisitions like CC Gruppe in Germany (2021) and RGS Nordic (2024), adding capabilities in areas such as fly ash and construction waste recycling. The firm is actively expanding its global presence, with a new plant under construction in Perth, Australia, and has established a significant operational footprint with over 20 ash treatment facilities. In 2021, the company reported revenues of approximately $309 million. column6: STRAYZ Petfood GmbH is a Berlin-based social enterprise operating in the pet food industry, founded in November 2020. The company was established by former colleagues Madeline Metzsch, Saskia te Kaat, and Stefanie Zillessen. The inspiration for the company came after co-founder Madeline Metzsch, a self-described "cat lady," was moved by the plight of a pregnant stray cat during a vacation in the Seychelles in 2019. This experience, coupled with their collective professional background at a successful Berlin-based children's food startup, Freche Freunde, equipped the founders with the expertise to disrupt a new market segment. The founders saw a gap in the pet food market for a purpose-driven brand with modern packaging and transparent, high-quality ingredients. The company's business model is centered on a "Buy 1, Give 1" principle, where every product sold results in a donation to animal welfare organizations. Revenue is generated through an omnichannel sales strategy that includes a direct-to-consumer e-commerce platform, which launched in April 2021 following a successful crowdfunding campaign, and a presence in over 2,400 retail stores, including major drugstores like Rossmann. For every can of pet food sold, STRAYZ donates a meal to a stray animal. The sale of non-food items, such as fair-trade socks, bags, and apparel, funds medical treatments like vaccinations and spaying/neutering procedures to address the root causes of animal homelessness. As of May 2024, the company has funded over 3.7 million meals, more than 13,300 medical treatments, and 683 neutering procedures through partnerships with 12 animal welfare organizations. STRAYZ offers a range of species-appropriate, organic pet food for both cats and dogs, manufactured in Bavaria, Germany. The products are formulated in collaboration with pet food nutritionists to have clean labels and are free from unnecessary additives, sugar, grains, and gluten. The cat food features a high meat content of up to 95% from a single protein source, making it suitable for cats with allergies, while the dog food recipes are also monoprotein. This commitment to quality and transparency aims to counter what the founders describe as "junk food" prevalent in the pet food industry. The company has secured pre-seed funding, including a €750,000 investment in June 2022 from investors like the Business Angels Club Berlin-Brandenburg and Justus Hammer. column6: Dunamis Charge, a manufacturer of electric vehicle (EV) charging solutions, was established in 2020 as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Dunamis Clean Energy Partners. Headquartered in Detroit, the company was founded by Natalie King, who serves as the CEO of both entities. King, a former attorney with a Juris Doctorate from Wayne State University Law School, transitioned into the clean energy sector after co-founding a solar energy firm in 2007. Following the dissolution of that company, she founded Dunamis Clean Energy Partners in 2012, initially focusing on energy auditing and efficiency solutions for commercial and industrial clients. The pivot into manufacturing began with LED lighting in 2015 after a supplier failure prompted a mentor to suggest she produce the components herself. The inspiration to enter the EV charging market reportedly came to King in 2018, leading to a period of research and development before the formal launch of Dunamis Charge. The company has since become the first Black woman-owned EV charger manufacturer globally. Dunamis Charge operates within the rapidly expanding EV infrastructure market, which is bolstered by government initiatives aiming to increase the number of public charging stations nationwide. The firm designs, engineers, and manufactures its EV charging hardware in the U.S., with a focus on sourcing components from local suppliers within a 30-mile radius of its Detroit factory. This strategy aligns with "Made in America" and Buy America, Build America (BABA) compliance standards. The company’s business model targets a diverse client base that includes residential customers, commercial property owners, workplaces, fleet operators, and municipalities. For commercial clients, the model presents an opportunity to generate revenue by turning parking lots into profit centers. Dunamis Charge generates revenue through the sale of its hardware and associated cloud-based software and support services. The company has also engaged in strategic partnerships, such as the "Communities in Charge" pilot program with DTE Energy, to deploy chargers in underserved communities, where the utility funds the hardware and installation, and host sites retain revenue from charging sessions. The company offers a suite of charging products, including Level 2 (L2) chargers for residential and commercial use, as well as DC Fast Chargers for public and high-volume applications. The L2 chargers offer a full charge overnight, while the DC Fast Chargers can replenish a vehicle's battery in approximately 30 minutes. These charging stations are designed to be user-friendly and reliable, supported by 24/7 customer service and maintenance. A key feature of their offerings is the integration of cloud-based software that provides management features for different industries. column5: Developing high-precision antibody diagnostics
column6: Biotome is an Australian medtech redefining diagnostic accuracy through precision immunology. Based in Perth, the company has developed a breakthrough platform that moves beyond the limitations of traditional protein-based assays. By targeting the immune system's most precise signals—specific amino acid sequences known as epitopes—Biotome unlocks high-resolution data to distinguish between closely related pathogens and identify high-risk disease variants with unprecedented specificity.At the heart of the company is a "sequence-to-serology" platform that collapses diagnostic development timelines from years to under 12 months. This proprietary ecosystem integrates AI-guided epitope prediction, ultra-high-density peptide microarrays (analysing up to 100,000 targets simultaneously), and PepLock™. PepLock is a first-in-class surface immobilisation technology that achieves 5-fold improvements in assay sensitivity and ensures robust protein attachment across multiple surfaces, from ELISA plates to magnetic beads and biosensors.Biotome’s lead product, Helitope®, addresses a critical unmet need in global health: gastric cancer prevention. While H. pylori infects over 4 billion people, only specific "CagA-positive" variants carry a high risk of cancer. Helitope is an accurate, patented diagnostic that identifies these high-risk patients, enabling doctors to make confident, risk-based follow-up decisions. By accurately filtering at-risk individuals, Helitope can prevent up to 70% of gastric cancers while reducing unnecessary, invasive gastroscopies by 40%.Biotome is a revenue-generating entity with a proven track record. As the only Australian provider of linear B-cell epitope mapping services, the company has generated $1.5M in revenue to date and validated its platform through more than eight successful multi-institute research collaborations. The company holds a formidable intellectual property position, with patents granted in 20 countries covering both diagnostic markers and its proprietary presentation chemistries.The company is led by an executive team with over 20 years of biotech and pharmaceutical leadership, supported by a world-class advisory board including Nobel Laureate Prof. Barry Marshall, the co-discoverer of H. pylori. To date, Biotome has secured 1.3M in equity funding and 1.8M in non-dilutive grants. column5: Online consultation solution, and the first choice of NHS GP surgeries
column6: eConsult Health operates as a key digital interface for the UK's National Health Service (NHS), providing digital triage solutions designed by practicing clinicians. The company's genesis dates back to 2013, when four General Practitioner (GP) partners at the Hurley Group in London sought a technology-driven solution to manage their workflow more effectively. This initiative was led by individuals including Dr. Murray Ellender, who now serves as the company's CEO. Dr. Ellender, a King's College London graduate with a background in emergency medicine and general practice, co-founded the company as a spin-out from the NHS, driven by his experience within the Hurley Group. He continues to practice part-time, which grounds the company's development in current clinical reality. The firm's business model is centered on providing its digital platforms to NHS entities, including GP practices, Primary Care Networks, and hospitals, which can be funded directly or through central NHS funding streams like the GP Forward View. Its core offerings, eConsult and eTriage, aim to streamline patient access and improve clinical efficiencies. The primary clients are NHS-based GP practices, Urgent Treatment Centres, and hospital Emergency Departments. In October 2024, eConsult was acquired by Huma, a global healthcare technology company, integrating its services into Huma's broader digital health platform. The company's flagship product, eConsult, is an online consultation platform used in over 3,200 NHS GP practices. It allows patients to submit their symptoms or requests electronically to their own GP, access NHS self-help information, and use a symptom checker at any time. This system gathers a structured history from the patient, enabling practice staff to triage cases effectively, directing patients to the appropriate care setting—be it a remote consultation, a phone call, or a face-to-face appointment. For emergency care, eTriage facilitates patient check-in and automates clinical prioritization upon arrival at a hospital. Patients use tablets to enter their medical history, which allows for quicker identification of the most critically ill individuals and reduces waiting times. Keywords: digital triage, online consultation, NHS, healthtech, primary care, emergency care, clinical workflow, patient access, GP services, telehealth platform

column5: Bioprocess solutions for advanced personalized therapies
column6: Antleron NV is a research and development company headquartered in Leuven, Belgium, that specializes in creating bioprocess solutions to advance personalized medicine. Founded in 2014 by Dr. ir. Jan Schrooten, the company's name and symbol are inspired by the regenerative capacity of antlers, reflecting its mission to enable the scalable and affordable manufacturing of living therapies. Jan Schrooten, who serves as the CEO, has a background as a materials engineer with a PhD in biomaterials and over 25 years of research experience in the field. Prior to Antleron, he was a senior research manager at KU Leuven, focusing on biomaterials and tissue engineering research, and co-founded Prometheus, the university's R&D division for Skeletal Tissue Engineering. Antleron's business model is centered on co-creating end-to-end solutions for the life sciences industry, particularly for companies in the advanced therapy, vaccine, and diagnostics sectors. They operate as a contract research organization (CRO) and technology provider, collaborating with a range of stakeholders from startups to large international industry leaders. The company's hybrid R&D approach combines wet lab research with digital technologies to accelerate the development of bioprocesses. The company's core technology integrates cells, biomaterials, 3D printing, and bioreactors to engineer medicinal products and processes. A key offering is their smart scale-down model service, which uses custom, lab-scale modular bioreactors combined with a digital twin platform called Nexus. This allows for the prediction, development, and optimization of bioprocesses from the lab bench to clinical-scale manufacturing. Their proprietary CellGuide® fixed-bed bioreactor platform is designed to improve the quality, consistency, and scalability of bespoke therapies. This 'factory-of-the-future' concept aims to tackle challenges in process development, quality assurance, and scalability for personalized cell and gene therapies. Antleron's services support therapy developers at every stage, including custom process development, feasibility studies, assay development, and providing regulatory-ready workflows aligned with EMA and FDA expectations. Their clients are typically biomedical and biotechnology organizations looking to move regenerative medicine and personalized therapies from the laboratory to patient application in a more efficient and affordable manner. By using digital twins and scalable bioreactors, Antleron aims to reduce the costs and time associated with traditional bioprocess development. column5: Corporate wellness platform for sustainable activity challenges
column6: Walk15 is a sustainable activity platform offering a B2B Software as a Service (SaaS) solution for companies to enhance employee engagement and track Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) metrics. Founded in 2019 by Vlada Musvydaitė-Vilčiauskė, the Lithuanian-based company originated from her personal project to create an engaging walking app for her family. Initially a consumer-focused fitness app, Walk15 pivoted during the COVID-19 pandemic to a B2B model, focusing on corporate step challenges to promote health and sustainability. The company's primary business model is based on B2B SaaS subscriptions, where businesses pay recurring fees for access to the platform. This provides their employees with the #walk15 mobile app and gives administrators access to an analytics dashboard to manage challenges and track ESG data. The platform is designed to be easily integrated into organizations, with Walk15 managing the customizable walking challenges. Revenue is also generated through partnerships with brands that offer eco-friendly and healthy products in the app's 'Steps Wallet'. The Walk15 app is free for individual users and available globally in 25 languages. Its core features include a pedometer, private and public step challenges, curated walking routes with audio guides, and a 'Steps Wallet' where users can exchange their steps for discounts on products and services. A key differentiator is its focus on sustainability; the app tracks CO2 savings by choosing to walk instead of drive and allows users to grow virtual trees that can translate into real-world planting projects. The platform integrates with various wearables and health apps like Apple Health and Google Fit, tracking steps without monitoring user location to ensure privacy. Since its launch, Walk15 has seen significant growth, expanding its client base to over 1,600 companies and its user base to nearly one million by late 2024. The company has successfully raised multiple funding rounds, including a Series A round in March 2025 that brought its valuation to €30 million. Walk15 has established a presence across Europe, with offices in Vilnius and Berlin, and serves a diverse client base that includes small businesses, large enterprises, and government organizations. column6: Cocoon Technologies Inc. is a software company operating in the public safety technology sector, with a stated mission to save lives during traffic stops. The company was founded as a limited liability company in May 2021 before being incorporated as a Delaware C-Corp in November of the same year. It is registered to do business in Ohio and Michigan and is headquartered in Detroit, MI. The impetus for the company's creation came to founder Dr. Leah Lewis, J.D., in 2021 amidst high-profile cases of deaths during police interactions. This personal drive led to the development of technology aimed at creating safer interactions between law enforcement and civilians. Cocoon Technologies targets government and law enforcement agencies at the federal, state, county, and local levels as its primary clients. The firm's core product is LARA (License and Registration App), a software solution designed to facilitate contactless policing during low-level traffic stops. LARA's objective is to reduce physical contact and potential conflict by creating distance, thereby averting danger and the spread of disease. This is intended to decrease the likelihood of violent encounters and subsequent wrongful death lawsuits against municipalities. The company has engaged with accelerator and incubator programs, such as Plug and Play Tech Center, to advance its development. column6: Secapp, a Finnish software company established in 2011, provides a robust platform for critical communications, alerting, and reporting. The firm originated as a deep-tech spin-off from a research and development project at the University of Jyväskylä, involving collaboration with fire and rescue services, hospital authorities, and police. The company’s foundation is rooted in the expertise of its team in developing communication solutions for entities like Nokia and the European Space Agency. The co-founder, Kari Aho, serves as the CEO and brings a substantial background in mobile technologies and telecommunications to the company. His academic and professional journey, including a Ph.D. in Mobile Technologies and Telecom from the University of Jyväskylä and experience in managing international R&D projects, aligns directly with Secapp's mission-critical focus. Aho's entrepreneurial ventures prior to leading Secapp involved cloud and mobile software technology, as well as critical infrastructure documentation tools, providing him with a comprehensive understanding of the market. Secapp operates on a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) business model, generating revenue through user-based subscription packages like "Prepare & Alert" and "Full & Integrated", with custom Enterprise options available. The company targets a diverse client base, including multinational corporations, fire departments, hospitals, schools, municipalities, and volunteer groups. Its platform is designed to ensure operational continuity and personnel safety by enabling mass notifications, targeted alerts to individuals and teams, and secure real-time communication. The service is accessible via native iOS, Android, and Windows applications, as well as through text messages, automated calls, and email, utilizing both commercial (WiFi, mobile networks) and professional (TETRA) communication channels. Key features include location tracking, geofencing, task allocation, and asset management. The platform is ISO 27001:2022 certified, underscoring its commitment to security. The company has achieved significant milestones, including securing a €2 million capital loan from Oppiva Invest to foster international growth and enhance the security of educational institutions. column5: Boulo is the recruiting industry’s go-to resource connecting women needing flexibility with employers who prioritize results
column6: Boulo Solutions operates as a recruitment platform focused on connecting companies with a diverse, often-untapped talent pool of women, caregivers, and military spouses. The firm was founded in Birmingham, Alabama, in 2018 by Delphine Carter and Catherine Gregory. Carter, the current CEO, drew from her personal experiences as a working mother and her professional background as a product and team manager at growing companies where she struggled to find diverse, quality candidates. She identified a segment of highly educated and experienced women—termed "carpool geniuses"—who were sidelined in their careers due to the need for workplace flexibility. This insight formed the foundation of Boulo's mission to bridge the gap for professionals with non-linear career paths. The company's business model centers on a technology-driven, skills-based matching platform combined with a personalized approach. Initially functioning as a staffing service for flexible and project-based work, Boulo has since expanded to include full-time roles. Revenue is generated through a subscription-based model for employers, introduced in late 2023, which offers tiered plans (Seed, Grow, and Scale) to cater to different hiring needs and budgets. This structure is designed to make diversity and inclusion initiatives more accessible for growing companies. For clients, Boulo handles sourcing, pre-qualifying candidates, and paperwork, aiming to accelerate the hiring process. The platform emphasizes a candidate's skills and life experiences through proprietary "360° profiles" to provide a more holistic view beyond a traditional resume. Boulo serves a range of clients, from startups to large corporations like Alabama Power and Protective Life, that promote flexible work cultures. The firm has raised approximately $4.11 million in funding over three seed rounds, with notable investments from Naples Technology Ventures and a group of angel investors. These funds are directed towards accelerating product development, including upskilling resources for candidates, with an ambitious goal of increasing the number of women in the workforce by 1% by 2030. column5: Tipping. Simplified
column6: TackPay Srl provides a financial software platform focused on digital tipping for the hospitality and service industries. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Genoa, Italy, the company addresses the decline in cash-based gratuities resulting from the global shift to cashless payments. The founding vision, conceived by a team including CEO and co-founder Matteo Tranchida, stemmed from observing the loss of tips in the Horeca sector due to a lack of digital tipping options. The company's core offering is a web and mobile application that facilitates the sending, receiving, and management of tips digitally. For customers, the process is streamlined via a QR code, allowing them to leave a tip using credit cards or digital payment methods without needing to download an application. This approach provides a frictionless experience designed to be as fast as tipping with cash. TackPay serves both individual tipped workers—such as servers, artists, and bartenders—and businesses like hotels, restaurants, and bars. For individuals, it offers a personal digital wallet to receive tips directly. For businesses, it provides a "Team Tipjar" feature that automates the collection, management, and distribution of pooled tips. This system allows for customizable tip-splitting rules, promoting fair and transparent remuneration among all staff members, including back-of-house employees. The platform also simplifies accounting for businesses by processing tips separately from their main revenue streams. Beyond the transaction, TackPay integrates a feedback mechanism, allowing managers to gather guest insights and performance data with each tip. The business model includes different subscription plans for businesses, with a free starter plan offering core functionalities like automated tip management and division. For individual users and tippers, the service is generally free, with transaction fees deducted from the received tip. The platform is built on Google Cloud, leveraging its infrastructure to ensure high performance and scalability as the company expands its operations internationally across Europe and North America. column6: Skolyn is a computational imaging and artificial intelligence company architecting the foundational technologies for the next era of diagnostic medicine. Our mission is to resolve the systemic inefficiencies confronting modern radiology, a field defined by a ~15% annual growth in imaging volume and a persistent 3-5% diagnostic error rate. We address these challenges not by analyzing existing images, but by fundamentally reconstructing and enhancing the imaging process itself.Our core technological differentiator is the Skolyn Clarity Engine, a suite of deep learning models trained on vast, terabyte-scale datasets of raw k-space data from initiatives like the fastMRI+ project. This unique capability allows us to reduce MRI scan times by up to 4x while simultaneously improving image quality. Built upon this foundation of enhanced images, the Skolyn Diagnostic Suite provides clinicians with a universal, multi-modal analysis platform. Our initial product roadmap targets the highest-value clinical areas, including Musculoskeletal (Knee), Neurology (Brain), and Oncology (Prostate, Breast).Each module is built upon the inviolable principle of Explainable AI (XAI); we reject the "black box" paradigm and provide a complete dossier of evidence for each finding to foster warranted clinical trust. The analytical validity of our models is benchmarked to the highest academic standards, targeting an AUC > 0.95 for critical findings. This positions Skolyn not as an incremental improvement, but as a paradigm shift in medical imaging.

The system's unique selling point is its predictive capability; it evaluates the potential extent of damage beneath the surface based only on visual data, a process that significantly reduces inspection procedure times from months to days. column6: Sunrock is a European developer specializing in integrated clean energy systems for the logistical and industrial sectors. He is also a partner at Stecc, a firm that invests in purpose-driven entrepreneurs. The company began by targeting the untapped potential of large logistics rooftops in the Netherlands for solar energy generation. From its origins, Sunrock established itself as the market leader for solar roofs in the Netherlands. A significant acceleration in its growth occurred in 2020 when it was acquired by COFRA Holding, a diversified holding company. This acquisition provided the strategic backing for Sunrock to expand its operations into Germany and France. Underscoring its commitment to social and environmental standards, the company achieved B Corp certification in 2024. In late 2024, Roger Knubben was appointed as interim CEO, taking over from Duijzer to guide the company's next phase of evolution. The company's business model centers on developing, financing, and managing solar energy assets, particularly large-scale rooftop installations. Sunrock serves commercial real estate owners, logistics companies, industrial clients, and public bodies. Revenue is generated through various models, including operational leases where Sunrock retains ownership of the solar systems while clients lease them and use the generated power. Another model involves customized power purchase agreements (PPAs) that allow tenants to buy clean energy at a discount to grid tariffs without capital expenditure. Sunrock manages the entire project lifecycle, from feasibility studies, financing, and permitting to the ongoing operation and maintenance of the assets. In response to market challenges like grid congestion, the business has evolved to offer integrated solutions. These include Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), smart Energy Management Systems (EMS), and EV charging infrastructure to optimize local energy consumption and provide grid flexibility. column5: Vertically integrated sodium-ion grid-scale energy storage systems
column6: Peak Energy, founded in 2023 by Landon Mossburg, Cameron Dales, and Liam O'Connor, is a U.S.-based company focused on designing and deploying grid-scale energy storage systems. The founders are industry veterans with extensive experience from companies like Tesla, Northvolt, Enovix, Zipline, and Apple. Mossburg, the CEO, previously led North America's expansion and automation at Northvolt and held leadership roles at Tesla. COO Liam O'Connor served as COO at Zipline and held senior supply chain positions at Lyft and Tesla. President and CCO Cameron Dales was previously the CCO at Enovix. The company is developing low-cost, giga-scale energy storage solutions centered on sodium-ion battery technology to support the transition to renewable energy. This technology is presented as a safer, lower-cost, and more reliable alternative to lithium-based systems, free from thermal risks and reliance on rare materials. Peak Energy's business model is vertically integrated, covering the entire value chain from cell R&D and manufacturing to system integration and grid interconnection. Its systems are designed to be modular and scalable, featuring a patent-pending passive cooling design that eliminates the need for active cooling and ventilation, thereby reducing common failure points and operational costs. Peak Energy's target market includes utilities, independent power producers (IPPs), data centers, and grid operators. The company aims to reduce the total cost of ownership for energy storage, helping clients meet rising energy demand without significant new generation and transmission investments. After emerging from stealth in October 2023 with a $10 million seed round, Peak Energy secured a $55 million Series A in July 2024, bringing total funding to $65 million. These funds support product industrialization and pilot deployments, with plans for a U.S. cell factory to begin production in 2026. The company deployed its first grid-scale sodium-ion system in Colorado in September 2025 and has secured a multi-year agreement with Jupiter Power to supply up to 4.75 GWh of its systems between 2027 and 2030. column5: Helps hospitals to deliver patient facing digital solutions
column6: DrDoctor operates as a health-tech platform focused on bolstering productivity and communication within the United Kingdom's National Health Service (NHS). The company was established in 2012 by Tom Whicher, Perran Pengelly, and Rinesh Amin. The founders, all former management consultants, identified the opportunity while working on healthcare projects and observing firsthand the inefficiencies in hospital outpatient departments, such as issues with appointment scheduling and patient communication. CEO Tom Whicher, a biomedical engineer by background, previously worked at a management consultancy firm where he was assigned to healthcare projects. This experience, combined with his earlier background in coding and naval architecture, shaped his approach to solving systemic problems within the NHS. Co-founders Rinesh Amin and Perran Pengelly also came from the same consultancy, with Pengelly focusing more on the IT side. Their collective frustration with the patient experience and administrative burdens led them to create DrDoctor. The company's primary business involves providing a patient engagement platform to NHS Trusts and Health Boards. Its revenue is generated by being commissioned by these NHS organizations. DrDoctor's platform is designed to digitize and automate patient communications and administrative workflows. The service allows patients to manage their appointments online, including booking, canceling, and rescheduling. It delivers digital letters, appointment reminders via text and email, and facilitates video consultations. For the NHS Trusts, this translates into reduced administrative tasks, lower rates of missed appointments ('Did Not Attends' or DNAs) by up to 30%, and decreased paper and postage costs by up to 70%. DrDoctor's platform, referred to as HybridOS, is a key component of its offering, designed to support a hybrid model of healthcare that blends digital and in-person services. The platform integrates with the NHS App and offers features like patient-led booking, automated slot refilling for canceled appointments, and the ability to send patients online forms. It also incorporates AI-powered tools to predict patient attendance and optimize clinic capacity. Serving over 70 NHS organizations and managing over 140 million appointments for more than 35 million patients annually, the company has achieved significant scale. A major milestone was securing £10 million in Series B funding in 2024 to accelerate product development and expand its reach. Coverage is provided for a wide range of merchandise, with exceptions for certain hazardous goods, valuables, and cash. In the event of a covered loss, the payment is made to the owner of the transported goods. The policy covers theft with verifiable evidence of violence or physical damage, as well as damages resulting from accidents like collisions or overturns, up to the insured sum. A mandatory requirement for coverage is a properly functioning GPS device at the start of the insured haul.
