column6: Founded in 2001 as a spin-off from the Bavarian Center for Applied Energy Research (ZAE Bayern), va-Q-tec AG emerged from the work of its founders, Dr. Joachim Kuhn and Dr. Roland Caps. Their extensive research in insulation materials laid the groundwork for the company's focus on vacuum insulation panels (VIPs) and phase change materials (PCMs). Dr. Kuhn, who served as CEO for many years and is now on the supervisory board, has a background in physics that was instrumental in developing the core technologies. The company is headquartered in Würzburg, Germany, and has grown to include additional production sites in Kölleda, Thuringia. va-Q-tec operates in the specialized market of thermal energy efficiency and temperature-controlled logistics. The company develops, manufactures, and markets high-performance thermal packaging and insulation solutions. Its business model centers on two main streams: the sale of its insulation products and a services division that offers a rental fleet of thermal containers and boxes. This 'Serviced-Rental' model is particularly prominent in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries, which require stringent temperature control for shipping sensitive goods like vaccines and clinical trial materials. Key clients include major pharmaceutical companies such as Roche and CSL Behring. The company also serves the food, appliance, and building industries. The core offerings are its vacuum insulation panels (VIPs), which provide insulation performance up to ten times more effective than traditional materials, and its phase change materials (PCMs), which store and release thermal energy to maintain specific temperatures. By integrating these two technologies, va-Q-tec produces passive thermal shipping containers and boxes capable of maintaining constant temperatures—from cryogenic to room temperature—for up to 200 hours without an external power source. A significant milestone for the company was its initial public offering on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in 2016. More recently, in early 2023, va-Q-tec entered into a strategic partnership with EQT Private Equity, which included a takeover offer, aiming to accelerate the company's growth and delist it from the stock exchange. column5: Provides AI-based diagnosis of osteoporosis to preserve lives
column6: Bonescreen GmbH, a medical technology software firm, emerged in February 2022 as a spin-off from the Technical University of Munich (TUM). The founding team, consisting of Jan Kirschke, Anjany Sekuboina, Malek El Husseini, Dominik Maurer, Sebastian Rühling, and Giles Tetteh, combines deep expertise in radiology, computer science, and finance. This interdisciplinary group largely knew each other from their time at TUM, where one founder is a radiology professor and four others pursued their doctoral studies, building on over two decades of research in the field. The company focuses on addressing the widespread, yet often undiagnosed, disease of osteoporosis. This condition leads to an increased risk of bone fractures, significantly impacting the quality of life, especially in older age. Bonescreen's core offering is SpineQ, an AI-powered software that conducts opportunistic screening for osteoporosis by analyzing existing computed tomography (CT) scans performed for other clinical reasons. This approach eliminates the need for additional patient examinations, radiation exposure, or clinician intervention. The software automatically analyzes the images to measure volumetric bone mineral density, a key predictor of fracture risk, and presents the data in an intuitive, color-coded heat map that makes minimal density changes visible to the human eye. Bonescreen's technology integrates directly into a hospital's Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS), providing a fully automated analysis that avoids disrupting the standard radiological workflow. A significant technical advantage is its ability to reliably analyze CT scans even with contrast agents, a challenge for other methods. The business model targets clinics and radiology practices, offering SpineQ directly and through sales partners. The company is working towards having its AI-supported bone density measurement recognized and reimbursed by statutory health insurance funds. Since its inception, Bonescreen has secured notable support and funding. In May 2023, the company received a €1.5 million co-investment from EIT Health as part of its Wildcard Programme. It has also won the German Founders Award for Digital Innovations and the Bavarian "Start?Zuschuss!" competition, receiving up to €36,000. The company is actively pursuing CE certification for SpineQ, which is anticipated in the spring of 2025, to enable full commercialization across the DACH region and beyond. column6: Find & Order, established in 2015 by Mickael Carvalho, Arthur Guelton, and Daniel Hideux, provides solutions to optimize operational flows for the retail and logistics sectors. column6: Healables Digital Health, Inc. is a HealthTech and SportsTech company founded in 2017 by Moshe Lebowitz and Dr. George Lowell. Healables operates on a business model with multiple revenue streams, including B2C and B2B2C sales of its consumer and professional products, as well as a SaaS freemium model for its health coaching app and data. column5: Helping blind and visually impaired people to navigate their environment and move around independently
column6: FeelObject is a French company dedicated to enhancing the autonomy of visually impaired and blind individuals through its primary product, Virtuoz. The company was founded in Toulouse in 2015 by Céline Favy-Huin and Sylvain Huin. Initially, they operated as an industrial subcontractor specializing in high-performance 3D printing with materials like carbon and kevlar for sectors such as automotive and aviation. A pivotal moment occurred at a scientific conference, sparking the idea to use their 3D printing expertise to address mobility challenges for the visually impaired. Céline Favy-Huin brought to the venture a unique perspective from her dual background in the paramedical field and human resources, which instilled a human-centric approach to her work. Sylvain Huin serves as the company's president. Driven by a desire for more meaningful work, the founders established a dedicated R&D division in 2016 to innovate for people with disabilities, focusing on visual impairment from 2017. After the pandemic, the founders decided to concentrate solely on Virtuoz and relocated the company to Petit-Quevilly, near Rouen, to be closer to a dynamic ecosystem supportive of their mission. The business model centers on selling the Virtuoz solution to public and private establishments. Clients include corporations, government institutions, museums, hotels, educational facilities, and healthcare centers. Notable customers include Procter & Gamble, Disneyland Paris, the French National Assembly, Orano, Enedis, the University of Perpignan, and the Geneva Museum of Art and History. Revenue is generated through the sale of these systems to organizations that wish to improve accessibility for their employees or visitors. The company has received backing from Le Village by CA and was preparing for a €600,000 fundraising round to scale up production and commercial efforts. Virtuoz is a tactile and vocal mapping system designed to help users create a mental representation of their environment. The solution combines 3D-printed tactile maps with an electronic unit that provides audio information when specific symbols on the map are pressed. These maps, made from a durable onyx material (nylon mixed with carbon fibers), detail key landmarks like stairs, elevators, and restrooms. Virtuoz is available in two formats: a portable 'mini' version that allows users to swap different floor plans, and a larger, stationary format for providing a general overview of a location. The system operates independently of a venue's infrastructure, requiring no connection or modification to the building. It is designed to be intuitive, empowering users to explore new indoor and outdoor spaces with confidence and independence. column5: Offers you a new way to discover and buy wine with the monthly subscription
column6: Le Petit Ballon is a French e-commerce company operating a direct-to-consumer wine subscription service. Founded in 2011, the company aims to simplify the wine purchasing experience for both novices and connoisseurs by making it less intimidating and more accessible. The venture was initiated by Martin Ohannessian, who, upon turning thirty, felt his lack of wine knowledge was a shortcoming. His initial attempts at oenology courses proved to be expensive and uninspiring, which led him to the then-emerging concept of subscription boxes. Ohannessian, a former musician, decided to apply this model to the world of wine. He partnered with Jean-Michel Deluc, a distinguished Master Sommelier formerly of the Ritz in Paris, to ensure high-quality wine selection. The founding team was completed by Matthieu Lesne, a former classmate of Ohannessian, and later joined by Clément Thibault as Managing Director. The business model is centered on a monthly subscription, delivering two curated bottles of wine to customers' doors. Each box is tailored to the subscriber's taste profile and includes tasting notes and a magazine, 'The Gazette', filled with food pairings, winemaker stories, and tips. This approach provides a guided discovery, helping consumers understand their own preferences and learn about wine in a straightforward manner. Beyond the subscription, customers can purchase wines directly from the company's online shop, often at a discount. Le Petit Ballon also operates physical retail stores in Paris and Lyon, which serve as hubs for meeting subscribers and hosting events. The company experienced rapid growth from its inception, starting with friends and family and quickly expanding through word-of-mouth. By December 2016, it had 60,000 subscribers and had shipped one million bottles. This success attracted the attention of French e-commerce giant Vente-Privée (now Veepee), which acquired a majority stake in Le Petit Ballon in April 2017 to bolster its own wine sales division. Despite the acquisition, Le Petit Ballon continues to operate as an independent brand, led by its founders. The company has also expanded its reach through the acquisition of the Spanish wine retailer Decántalo in 2022. column5: Telemedicine device for rapid cardiovascular disease diagnosis
column6: EFM S.A. is a Polish technology company, founded in 2022, developing solutions for the medical sector. The company's main focus is on accelerating the diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases (CVD) through its primary product, the Mudisocard system. This telemedical device is designed to enable the immediate diagnosis of critical heart conditions, addressing the often lengthy process of reaching a conclusive diagnosis which can take weeks or months. The Mudisocard system measures multiple heart parameters simultaneously. It captures the heart's contraction excitation (ECG), details of the contraction's development (auscultation), and the resulting movement of chest fluids (bioimpedance). This collected data is sent to a web platform where specialized algorithms analyze it, allowing healthcare professionals to assess heart parameters instantly. By comparing each heartbeat, the algorithms can detect subtle changes in the heart's electrical and mechanical dynamics that may indicate heart disease. This approach aims to streamline clinician workflows and reduce the need for numerous, costly medical tests. Since its inception, EFM has developed a functional prototype of the Mudisocard system and has filed for patents in the European Union, the United States, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and South Korea. The company has also achieved ISO 13485:2016 certification for its quality management system, a significant step for the commercialization of its medical device. The leadership team includes CEO Miłosz Jamroży, a medical doctor with a PhD in Biomedical Engineering and over a decade of experience in telemedicine product development, CFO Filip Janowski, CTO Aleksander Cudny, and Quality & Regulatory Affairs Director Karol Pawelec. The company is venture capital-backed, with investors including WorldUpstart, StartSmart CEE, and TERRA seed, and is considering future financing options, including an IPO, to fund upcoming milestones. column6: Project Omega is an advanced nuclear recycling company focused on re-establishing the United States' nuclear fuel cycle. column5: DeltaScan® Brain State Monitor is an EEG bedside device with a validated algorithm to support clinicians to optimize patient recovery
column6: Prolira BV is a medical technology company focused on addressing acute encephalopathy and delirium in hospitalized patients. Originating in 2015 as a spin-off from the University Medical Center Utrecht in the Netherlands, the company was founded by Rutger van Merkerk and Annemarie Willems. Van Merkerk's background is in strategic technology and regulation, while Willems specializes in bringing medical innovations to market. The company was established to commercialize a discovery made at the medical center: that a simplified EEG could rapidly and easily diagnose a delirium. The firm targets a significant and costly issue in healthcare, as acute brain failure affects millions of patients annually, leading to poor outcomes and high costs. Prolira’s business model centers on the sale of its core product, the DeltaScan® Brain State Monitor, and the recurring revenue from single-use disposable electrode patches required for each test. This positions brain state monitoring as a routine vital sign check, similar to monitoring the heart or lungs. The company serves hospital departments, with customers already established in the Netherlands, Germany, Austria, and the UK. Prolira's flagship product, the DeltaScan®, is a non-invasive medical device that provides an objective assessment of a patient's brain state at the bedside. It consists of a monitor and a single-use, three-electrode patch that simplifies the traditional electroencephalogram (EEG) process. Using proprietary AI-powered algorithms, the system analyzes EEG signals to detect characteristic brain wave patterns of acute encephalopathy, delivering results within minutes. This allows healthcare professionals to detect delirium earlier and more accurately than with subjective methods, enabling timely intervention. A key benefit is the potential to reduce the length of hospital stays, as demonstrated in a study involving 850 patients. The DeltaScan® has received EU-MDR approval in 2020 and FDA 510(k) clearance in 2023, paving the way for commercial expansion in Europe and the United States. column5: Secure orbital network for global B2B connectivity
column6: Rivada Space Networks, a German-based subsidiary of U.S. wireless technology company Rivada Networks, was founded in 2022 by Declan Ganley. Ganley, an Irish entrepreneur with a background in wireless communications and patented technologies, serves as CEO and established the company to build a unique global communications network. The company is headquartered in Munich with a secondary office in Berlin. The firm is developing a low-earth-orbit (LEO) satellite constellation named the "Outernet". This network is designed as a secure, high-speed optical mesh in space, comprising an initial 600 satellites interconnected by laser links. The architecture enables data to travel from origin to destination entirely within the space network, creating an ultra-secure and low-latency communications platform independent of terrestrial infrastructure. This "gateway-less" system is engineered to provide pole-to-pole coverage with latencies comparable to or better than terrestrial fiber over long distances. Rivada operates on a business-to-business (B2B) wholesale model, providing connectivity services to enterprise and government clients rather than directly to consumers. Its target markets include telecom, energy, maritime, aviation, mining, and government services, with a focus on clients requiring secure and resilient communications for critical operations. The company's revenue is generated through these wholesale agreements for its Outernet connectivity. As of mid-2024, Rivada had secured over $16 billion in service agreements. The company is working with Terran Orbital for the satellite manufacturing and SpaceX for launches, with initial services planned to be available globally in early 2026. column6: Icecat N.V. operates as a global syndicator of product information for the e-commerce market, positioning itself as a crucial link between brands, distributors, and retailers. The company was founded in 1999, with the public entity Icecat N.V. established in 2009, and is led by CEO and Founder Martijn J. Hoogeveen. Hoogeveen's background includes expertise in e-commerce, data science, and investing in various tech ventures, which has shaped Icecat's strategy of expansion through synergistic acquisitions, such as Iceshop and Syndy. The firm's primary business revolves around its Product Information Management (PIM) platform, which collects, standardizes, and enriches product data from manufacturers. This content, which includes specifications, marketing text, images, and videos, is then syndicated to tens of thousands of e-commerce platforms, comparison websites, and other channel partners. The service supports over 70 languages, facilitating global commerce for its clients. The business model operates on two main tiers: a free "Open Icecat" catalog that provides standardized product information with limited coverage, and a subscription-based "Full Icecat" service offering comprehensive, premium content and wider brand support. Revenue is generated from these subscriptions and other specialized services.Icecat's core offering is a cloud-based PIM-as-a-Service that can manage millions of multimedia product data-sheets. This platform is designed to support large, multilingual editor teams and integrates with major e-commerce systems like Shopify, Magento, and Amazon. A key feature is its ability to automate the flow of content, including updates to stock levels and pricing by connecting to distributor feeds. Beyond standard data, Icecat provides "A+ Content" and "Enhanced Product Stories," which allow brands to create immersive, multimedia-rich experiences on product pages, a feature shown to increase online conversion rates. The company also leverages AI to streamline its processes and has begun offering AI-powered solutions to corporate clients. In early 2017, Icecat successfully completed its IPO on the Dutch SME trading platform NPEX, using the proceeds to improve systems and expand the business globally. column6: PowerSync Technologies, founded in 2018, specializes in providing and managing electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure for Australian apartment buildings, also known as strata properties. The platform handles user billing automatically, ensuring residents only pay for the electricity they consume. It also includes load management capabilities to prevent overloading the building's electrical infrastructure, a critical feature for older buildings or those with limited power capacity. This system allows for the equitable distribution of power and costs among residents. PowerSync's business model involves working directly with apartment owners, body corporates, and strata managers to design and implement tailored charging solutions. The company offers a range of charging hardware and can integrate with existing systems if required. Their revenue is generated through the sale of hardware, installation services, and ongoing software subscription fees for the management platform, which includes billing, support, and system maintenance. The company's turnkey approach simplifies the entire process for strata committees, from initial consultation and site assessment to installation and ongoing operation. By providing a comprehensive solution that covers hardware, software, and billing, PowerSync aims to make EV charging accessible and manageable for the growing number of Australian apartment dwellers who are switching to electric vehicles. column6: Chevignon is a French ready-to-wear apparel company founded in 1979 by Guy Azoulay. Inspired by a dream of America and a passion for second-hand clothes, Azoulay began by reinterpreting an aviator jacket with a leather insert, giving birth to the brand. The name was borrowed from a friend, Charles Chevignon, for its appealing sound. The brand's initial success was built on its expertise in aged and distressed leather jackets, notably the "Fly Jacket," which became a bestseller in Europe in 1981. A key milestone was the 1984 launch of the "Tog's" down jacket, which featured an emblem of a flying duck and became an icon of street culture for a generation. The company's core products are centered around authentic, durable men's fashion, with leather jackets, denim, and down jackets as its signature pieces. Chevignon targets the urban adventurer who appreciates casual style and lasting quality. The business operates through an omnichannel model, selling its products via its official e-shop, physical retail stores, and department store corners. Over the years, the brand has expanded internationally, opening stores in Europe, Asia, and Latin America. In 2023, it launched in the U.S. market, marking a significant step in its global presence. The brand also offers collections for women and children. Chevignon has undergone several ownership changes throughout its history. It was acquired by Naf Naf in 1995, which was later bought by the Vivarte group in 2007. In 2019, the brand was sold to a consortium including the Royer Group, Stéphane Coolaert, and Thierry Le Guénic. More recently, in mid-2025, the company Amoniss, chaired by businessman Salih Halassi, became the new owner of Établissements Charles Chevignon. The brand also operates under a licensing model in certain regions, such as Latin America, where it is managed by Grupo Uribe. column6: Impossible Kicks operates as a key player in the high-growth sneaker and streetwear resale market, which is anticipated to reach $30 billion by 2030. The company functions primarily through a network of brick-and-mortar stores, which account for 90% of its sales, supplemented by an e-commerce platform and a mobile application. This physical retail focus allows the company to provide a tangible, luxury-oriented customer experience, differentiating it from online-only competitors.The business was established by brothers Wayne and John Mocadlo, launching its first store in January 2021. Wayne, a long-time sneaker collector, began reselling shoes in high school and later moved his business to Instagram before recognizing the opportunity for a physical retail hub in his home state of Connecticut. He partnered with his brother, John Mocadlo, who brought over two decades of business experience from the automotive industry to serve as CEO. The venture started with $60,000 of Wayne's personal funds and his private collection.Impossible Kicks has demonstrated significant financial growth, with revenues increasing from $14-$15 million in its first year to a reported $47.3 million in 2023. The company has secured $7 million in total funding over several rounds, including a Series B in May 2024, to fuel its expansion. The business model is centered on the buying and reselling of high-demand, limited-edition sneakers and apparel from brands like Nike, Jordan, Yeezy, and Supreme. Inventory is sourced through a network of bulk resellers and direct in-store purchases from the public, with a two-person, AI-assisted authentication process to ensure product legitimacy. The company's product pricing is dynamic, based on market demand and rarity, with items ranging from accessible streetwear to six-figure collector pieces.The target demographic is broad, spanning ages 13 to 55 and including both casual consumers and serious collectors, often driven by nostalgia and celebrity fashion trends. By establishing a physical presence in both primary and secondary markets, Impossible Kicks makes high-end resale products more accessible to a wider audience that values the ability to see and touch products before purchasing. column5: A company developing next-generation precision oncology treatments
column6: Flindr Therapeutics is a private, pre-clinical biotechnology company headquartered in Oss, the Netherlands, concentrated on creating next-generation precision oncology treatments.  The company originated in 2020 as a spin-off from the Netherlands Cancer Institute (NKI) and the Oncode Institute, initially named Immagene. Its establishment is rooted in the extensive work of its founders: Prof. Daniel Peeper, Prof. Christian Blank, and Dr. Maarten Ligtenberg, who serve as the CEO. Dr. Ligtenberg brings over a decade of experience in oncology, particularly in immuno-oncology and cancer target identification. Prof. Peeper is a distinguished professor in Functional Oncogenomics and heads the Department of Molecular Oncology & Immunology at NKI. Prof. Blank is a medical oncologist and a group leader at NKI, with a research focus on combination immune checkpoint inhibition. This convergence of expertise in functional genomics, immunotherapy, and translational research forms the scientific bedrock of the company.  Flindr's business model is centered on the discovery and development of a pipeline of first-in-class small molecule inhibitors for the precision treatment of cancer. The company's revenue generation will depend on the successful progression of its therapeutic candidates through pre-clinical and clinical trials, leading to potential licensing deals, partnerships with larger pharmaceutical companies, or future commercialization of approved drugs. The firm's primary clients are anticipated to be patients within specific oncology segments who can benefit from highly targeted therapies. In April 2024, the company secured €20 million in a Series A financing round to advance its lead program and expand its pipeline.  The core of Flindr's operations is its proprietary 'ImmunoGram Drug Discovery Engine'. This platform is a sophisticated cascade of activities including target identification, validation, clinical bio-informatics, and druggability assessments. It functions by reverse-translating the clinical heterogeneity observed in patients' tumor and host immune factors into robust laboratory models. This allows for the screening and selection of critical drug targets involved in clinical response. Flindr's lead program, identified through this engine, is a first-in-class small molecule inhibitor targeting RNF31 (also known as HOIP), a protein-stabilizing E3 ubiquitin ligase that is aberrantly activated in various solid and hematological cancers. Pre-clinical studies have shown promising results in ovarian cancer and B-cell lymphoma models, and the company has identified biomarkers to help select patients most likely to respond to the treatment. column6: Based in Tokyo, Japan, TeTra Aviation is a venture-backed aerospace company established in June 2018 by President and CEO Tasuku Nakai. The company focuses on the research, development, manufacturing, and sale of electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft for the burgeoning urban air mobility market. A key milestone was achieved in February 2020 when TeTra won the prestigious Pratt & Whitney Disruptor Award at the GoFly competition, which was sponsored by Boeing.TeTra is developing the Mk-5, a single-passenger, fully electric eVTOL designed as a personal aircraft. The aircraft is notable for its hybrid propulsion system, which utilizes 32 propellers for vertical lift and a single rear pusher propeller for horizontal flight. This design avoids the complexity of tilt-rotor mechanisms. The fuselage combines carbon fiber composite and aluminum to achieve a balance of high strength and low weight. For safety, the aircraft employs Distributed Electric Propulsion (DEP), ensuring that the failure of one or more electric motors can be compensated for by the others to allow for a controlled landing. The initial production models are targeted to have a range and cruise speed of 160 km/h (100 mph) and a flight time of one hour.The company's business model centers on selling its eVTOL aircraft as kit planes, primarily targeting individuals in the United States, where it would be classified under the experimental aircraft category. Pre-orders for the Mk-5 and the forthcoming Mk-7 model are available through its website. TeTra became the first Japanese company to receive a test flight permit from the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) for an eVTOL, conducting its first successful unmanned flight test in California in August 2021. The company is also exploring future applications, including providing aircraft for on-demand mobility services, potentially for events like the 2025 Osaka Expo.Keywords: eVTOL, urban air mobility, personal aircraft, electric aircraft, vertical takeoff and landing, kit plane, aerospace manufacturing, Distributed Electric Propulsion, Tasuku Nakai, Mk-5, Tokyo startup, GoFly Prize, personal transportation, aviation technology, carbon fiber composite, experimental aircraft, FAA certification, flight test, aircraft development, air mobility

column5: UPyTher’s mission is to provide custom drug delivery solutions that enable sustained localized administration of therapeutics
column6: Upyther B.V. is a preclinical-stage pharmaceutical company operating out of Eindhoven, the Netherlands, with a focus on transforming peritoneal cancer into a treatable disease. The company originated in 2020 as a spin-off from the Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e), founded by Professor Patricia Dankers, Dr. Peter-Paul Fransen, and Dr. Geert van Almen, emerging from the DankersLab research group. The founding team combines deep scientific expertise with commercialization experience; Prof. Dankers is a recognized leader in biomedical materials and supramolecular chemistry, Dr. Fransen brings over 15 years of research experience as an inventor of the core technology, and CEO Dr. van Almen holds a PhD in Medical Sciences and has over a decade of business development experience in life sciences. The business centers on developing long-acting hydrogel-drug formulations for diseases within the peritoneal cavity, a market with significant unmet medical needs. Upyther's proprietary technology allows for a liquid drug formulation to be injected into the peritoneal cavity, where it transforms into a soft gel. This gel acts as a local drug depot, ensuring a sustained and controlled release of chemotherapeutic agents directly at the tumor sites over several days. This method aims to increase the drug's dwell time and exposure, enhancing therapeutic efficacy while minimizing systemic toxicity compared to conventional treatments like hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC), which only permit short drug exposure. The company's business model is to develop and commercialize these specialty products, with a pipeline protected by patents until 2043. The company’s lead product, UPT-211, is in preclinical development for treating peritoneal metastases originating from colorectal cancer. The market Upyther addresses is substantial, with 1.3 million patients diagnosed with peritoneal cancer worldwide annually, a number projected to grow. The company's clients are primarily healthcare providers and pharmaceutical partners within the oncology sector. Upyther generates revenue through funding and strategic partnerships and plans for a Series A funding round to advance its lead product to clinical proof of concept. The firm has successfully secured undisclosed seed financing in June 2024 from investors including Essential Investments, the Brabant Development Agency (BOM), and TTT Medtech, which will accelerate the preclinical program for UPT-211 and support preparations for first-in-human clinical trials. column6: VerifX – The Infrastructure of Digital Authenticity!VerifX is a technology company developing the infrastructure of digital authenticity - a cross-platform verification system designed to protect creators, organizations, and the public from deepfakes, online impersonation, and AI-driven misinformation. In a digital world where synthetic media can replicate a person’s image, voice, or brand within seconds, VerifX focuses on verifying what is real, not detecting what is fake.The explosion of generative AI has made content creation faster and more accessible than ever, but it has also opened the door to large-scale deception. Politicians, officials, journalists, and online creators are increasingly targeted with impersonation scams, manipulated videos, and false statements. Detection-based tools have proven ineffective in the long term, as each new detection method only helps fake creators improve their models. VerifX breaks this cycle by shifting the focus to source verification and content authenticity, establishing a foundation of trust that is independent of the speed of AI innovation.Through its platform, VerifX enables verified individuals and organizations to connect their official social media accounts and upload or link authentic content. This verified content is indexed in the VerifX Trusted Content Graph - a continuously growing database of legitimate digital assets. When content appears online, users, journalists, or platforms can instantly check its authenticity through the VerifX website, API, or browser extension.Beyond verification, VerifX provides continuous monitoring of social networks and the wider web to detect impersonation attempts or synthetic copies of verified profiles. When suspicious content is found, users receive automated alerts and can initiate takedown requests directly from the dashboard. This dual-layer system gives creators and institutions proactive control over their digital presence.VerifX serves several high-risk sectors where digital identity and trust are business-critical: - Content creators and influencers in health, finance, and education, whose likenesses are often exploited in scams. - Public figures, experts, and journalists exposed to deepfake attacks that threaten credibility and public trust. - Institutions and enterprises such as governments, media organizations, and emergency services, where disinformation can have real-world consequences.For the public, VerifX introduces a simple, transparent way to verify content authenticity. For creators and organizations, it offers a scalable, cross-platform protection layer, ensuring that verified voices cannot be easily cloned, misrepresented, or weaponized.VerifX also supports the global movement toward AI transparency and accountability, aligning with upcoming regulatory frameworks like the EU AI Act and U.S. deepfake disclosure laws. By providing an independent authenticity infrastructure, VerifX helps platforms and policymakers implement verifiable trust standards without compromising freedom of expression.Ultimately, VerifX aims to become the standard for digital truth - an open, interoperable ecosystem where real content can be proven, and misinformation can be quickly exposed. By combining software innovation, cybersecurity practices, and insights from information defense research, VerifX is redefining how authenticity is verified online.In an era of synthetic media and information chaos, VerifX offers a clear, scalable solution - building a safer, more transparent internet where trust can be proven, not presumed.

column5: Email for Web3. A Multi-Blockchain Messaging Application that makes it possible to easily send and receive rich-media HTML messages between blockchain public addresses through a simple, email-like interface
column6: Mailchain operates as a communication layer for Web3, enabling users to send and receive messages directly between blockchain wallet addresses. The company was established to address the absence of a native, private communication method in the blockchain ecosystem, where users often have to rely on traditional channels like email or social media, compromising their pseudonymity. The genesis of Mailchain began in 2018 when co-founders Tim Boeckmann (CEO) and Rob De Feo (CTO) started experimenting with sending encrypted messages via transaction data on blockchains. Both founders brought relevant experience from their time at AWS, where Boeckmann led the Emerging Technologies startup strategy, working with key blockchain organizations, and De Feo, a software architect with over 15 years of experience, mentored hundreds of startups in AI and blockchain. This experiment evolved into an open-source project in 2019, and by 2021, they founded Mailchain as a formal company to build a more scalable protocol independent of blockchain transaction constraints. In September 2022, Mailchain secured $4.6 million in a seed funding round. The round was led by Crane Venture Partners and Kenetic Capital, with participation from other institutional and angel investors, including Acequia Capital and former Microsoft head of corporate strategy, Charles Songhurst. This capital was earmarked for expanding user and community onboarding. The platform consists of two main components: an open-source protocol and a user-facing inbox application that functions much like traditional email. It allows individuals, DAOs, and blockchain projects to communicate wallet-to-wallet. For instance, developers can send critical updates, artists can connect with their NFT collectors, and DAOs can engage with their members directly and securely. The system supports multiple blockchain identities in a single, unified inbox. Mailchain's protocol is purpose-built to handle encryption, addressing, transport, and storage, with a plan for progressive decentralization. Mailchain ensures privacy through end-to-end encryption; messages are encrypted on the client-side, stored on distributed storage, and not on the blockchain itself. This design means that not even Mailchain can access the content of the messages. The business model includes a "public good" quota, offering free messaging for typical users to ensure broad accessibility. Revenue is expected to be generated from high-volume senders, such as applications and businesses, who will be charged small fees (targeted below $0.005) for messages, creating a sustainable economic model to support the protocol and its infrastructure providers. column5: One-handed precision suturing device for safer and faster vascular surgeries
column6: Mellon Medical, established in 2013, is a Dutch medical technology company focused on advancing surgical suturing. The company was founded by vascular surgeon Mark Vrancken Peeters, who transitioned from his surgical practice to become the Chief Medical Officer of Mellon. This career change was driven by his belief that single-handed suturing could significantly improve procedural outcomes and his ambition to impact more than one patient at a time. In April 2024, Mellon Medical became part of the Demcon Group, a move intended to further support the development of its core product. The company has developed a platform technology centered around one-handed suturing, with its leading product being the Switch®, a disposable, precision-suturing instrument. This Class III medical device operates with a simple pinch of the thumb and index finger, freeing the surgeon's other hand to present the tissue. The device uses a straight, double-pointed needle that moves between two jaws, a mechanism designed to be faster and more precise than conventional suturing, which requires passing a curved needle between instruments. The Switch® is designed to facilitate the 'small bites' suturing technique, particularly for closing the abdominal wall, which research has shown can significantly reduce postoperative complications like incisional hernias. Its pencil-like shape and balanced weight are intended to provide ergonomic use for both right- and left-handed surgeons. Mellon Medical targets the global surgical suture and devices market, which was estimated to be worth over $3 billion. The company's business model revolves around the sale of its disposable Switch® device and accompanying suture sets. While the initial focus is on vascular surgery—specifically procedures like carotid artery surgery and kidney transplants—Mellon's technology is a platform applicable to a wide range of disciplines, including general surgery, gynecology, and urology. The company has secured approximately $7.1 million in funding through Series A and Series B rounds, with key investors including BioGeneration Ventures, Thuja Capital, and Oost NL. Mellon is collaborating with the Erasmus Medical Center for clinical validation and has partnered with Assut for the development and production of its suture sets. column6: Reframe Systems, founded in 2022 by a trio of former Amazon Robotics engineers, is addressing the housing crisis with a focus on construction technology. The founders, Vikas Enti (CEO), Aaron Small (Head of Operations), and Felipe Polido (Head of Technology), leverage their collective two decades of experience in scaling automated systems at Amazon to revolutionize homebuilding. The inspiration for the company stemmed from CEO Vikas Enti's desire to tackle significant global challenges, specifically the carbon emissions associated with construction, after becoming a father. The company operates on a vertically integrated model, managing design, engineering, construction, and site work to deliver turnkey homes. Reframe Systems targets the "missing middle" of the housing market—such as duplexes, triplexes, single-family homes, and accessory dwelling units (ADUs)—that sits between high-density apartments and single-family residences. Its business strategy involves establishing small, localized microfactories in regions experiencing housing shortages. These microfactories can be set up in under 100 days for less than $5 million, a fraction of the capital required for traditional large-scale modular plants. The company pursues a co-developer and builder business model, only building a factory once a minimum project pipeline is secured, and offers units that can qualify for both public subsidies and open-market pricing. Reframe Systems utilizes a proprietary software platform, physical AI, and vision-guided robotics to automate tasks like framing and sheathing within its microfactories. This system allows for the mass customization of housing designs to comply with local zoning regulations, building codes, and neighborhood aesthetics. The output is a modular panelized wall system, with elements like plumbing and wiring pre-installed, designed for rapid, snap-together assembly on-site. This process significantly reduces construction timelines and costs. The resulting homes are all-electric, super-insulated, and built to be climate-resilient and meet Passive House standards for energy efficiency. In July 2024, the company completed its first customer project, an affordable, all-electric ADU in Arlington, MA. With a recent $20 million Series A funding round, Reframe is scaling its operations, with projects underway in Massachusetts and California, and aims to produce one million housing units over the next 20 years. The company's business model centers on the development, construction, and operation of these geothermal power plants, providing baseload and dispatchable electricity. Rodatherm aims to deliver power at a levelized cost competitive with fossil fuels, even at an early scale. column6: Alva Energy is a nuclear technology company focused on increasing the power output of existing nuclear reactors in the United States. Founded in 2023 by CEO James Krellenstein, COO Garrett Wilkinson, and CTO W. Robb Stewart, PhD, the Cambridge, Massachusetts-based startup aims to address the rising electricity demand from sectors like AI data centers by productizing nuclear plant upgrades, known as "uprates". The company's core service involves transforming complex retrofit projects into standardized, turnkey offerings. This approach is designed to make the process of boosting reactor output faster, more predictable, and more cost-effective than building new nuclear generation capacity. Alva Energy manages the entire uprate lifecycle, which includes regulatory compliance with the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC), procurement of long-lead items, installation, and commissioning. The company's methodology centers on replacing steam generators and adding a second turbine generator, which can add 200–300 megawatts of capacity per reactor. This process utilizes technologically mature, regulator-ready methods with a proven history of safe operation, adapting techniques from successful uprates performed globally. By standardizing the scope and delivery, Alva converts these upgrades into repeatable and financeable infrastructure projects. The company's goal is to unlock a total of 10 gigawatts of new power from the existing U.S. reactor fleet. The business model is structured to work directly with utilities and large-scale power consumers, such as hyperscale data centers, to finance the retrofits. This off-balance sheet financing approach allows utilities to engage in high-value power purchase agreements (PPAs) without imposing increased costs on residential ratepayers, a key consideration amid community opposition to rising electricity prices. In February 2026, Alva Energy announced it had launched with $33 million in Series A funding. The round was led by deep-tech venture capital firm Playground Global, with participation from Segra Capital, NGP, and others. Pat Gelsinger, former CEO of Intel and VMware, joined Alva's Board of Directors as part of the investment, bringing experience in scaling complex technology infrastructure. column5: Digital twin solutions for industrial asset management
column6: Innomerics is a Spanish company founded in 2011 that provides digital twin-based asset management solutions for the power generation industry. The company specializes in the nuclear, hydropower, and combined cycle sectors. The firm was founded by David Galbally, Manuel Núñez, and Francisco del Valle, who have extensive experience in the electrical sector and backgrounds from institutions like the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. The company's core offering is software that optimizes the performance, maintenance, and operation of power plants. This is achieved by creating virtual replicas of physical assets, which integrate real-time data and advanced analytics to enable enhanced monitoring, predictive maintenance, and optimized operations throughout the asset lifecycle. Innomerics offers a suite of software products including pamONE for evaluating degradation, isiONE for streamlining inspection planning, and fatONE for real-time fatigue assessment. In addition to software, the company provides services in structural integrity, fracture mechanics, real-time monitoring, and failure analysis. A key technology is their use of advanced physics-based digital twins, which allow for the real-time simulation of power plant systems by integrating operational data from plant sensors with high-fidelity finite element models. This capability helps operators understand the impact of operating decisions on the remaining life of critical assets, optimize inspection strategies, and diagnose the root causes of malfunctions. The company is actively involved in research and development projects, often in collaboration with European Union programs like the INCEFA-SCALE project for nuclear safety and the SHERPA project aimed at modernizing hydropower plants. In 2024, Iberdrola recognized Innomerics in the "Innovation, Digitalization, and New Technologies" category at its Supplier of the Year awards for its work on digital twins supporting green hydrogen and hydraulic networks. The company also expanded its expertise by acquiring Inesco Ingenieros, a firm specializing in structural integrity and fracture mechanics. column5: A Web3 personal data relationship & permission marketing platform
column6: Profila is a Swiss-based company positioning itself as a Web3 platform for personal data relationships and permission-based marketing. Founded in 2015 by Shawn Jensen, Michiel Van Roey, and Luke Bragg, the company aims to rectify the imbalance in the digital data economy where user data is often collected and used without transparent consent or fair compensation. The founding team combines diverse expertise: Shawn Jensen, the CEO, brings over two decades of experience in senior management and product leadership roles globally. Michiel Van Roey, the Chief Revenue & Legal Officer, has a decade of experience as a business lawyer specializing in technology and privacy law at firms like Cisco and CERN. Luke Bragg, the Chief Marketing Officer, leverages 20 years of experience in digital marketing and creative solutions.The core of Profila's business is to provide a privacy-centric alternative to the surveillance-based advertising model dominated by big tech. The platform operates as an intermediary, enabling a direct and transparent data exchange between consumers and brands. For individuals, Profila offers a tool to consolidate, manage, and control their personal data. They can choose which brands to engage with and decide what specific data to share, effectively leasing their data rather than selling it. In return for sharing their data and attention, users are compensated, receiving a minimum of 50% of the advertising revenue, with the potential to earn up to 90% based on their engagement level. Users can also earn Zeke tokens for updating their data and interacting with content.For its business clients, which are brands seeking to build more authentic customer relationships, Profila provides access to accurate, zero-party data directly from consumers. This model allows companies to move away from guesswork and inaccurate third-party data, enabling them to create highly personalized marketing campaigns and services. The platform encompasses functionalities of Ad-tech, Mar-tech, CRM, and customer insights. Profila's revenue is generated by charging brands a transaction fee, which ranges from 10% to 50% of the amount paid to the individual user. column5: Producer of high-altitude, award-winning Rwandan teas
column6: Rwanda Mountain Tea is a privately owned holding company established in 2005, primarily involved in tea production and the management of its tea factories. The company was founded by Egide Gatera with the ambition to foster Rwanda's development into a global, productive, and inclusive country. Following the privatization of Rwanda's tea sector, the company acquired majority shares in several government-owned tea estates in 2006. The company's business model has shifted from primarily selling at the Mombasa Tea Auction to increasing direct private sales, which now include major buyers like Taylors of Harrogate, the creators of Yorkshire Tea. This direct sales approach allows for better price negotiation based on the consistent high quality of their tea. Rwanda Mountain Tea produces a variety of teas, including organic black CTC, Green Orthodox, Gold Blend, and Mild Blend teas. Its products are exported worldwide to Africa, Southeast Asia, Western Europe, and North America. The company operates eight tea factories, including Rubaya, Nyabihu, Kitabi, and the organically certified Rutsiro factory. The plantations are situated at high altitudes, between 1,500 and 2,300 meters, in regions with fertile volcanic soil, which contributes to the tea's unique, high-quality flavor profile. Beyond tea, the company has diversified its investments into hydropower generation and the fabrication of concrete materials. It operates two hydropower plants on the Giciye River, contributing approximately 8 megawatts of electricity to the national grid and ensuring a reliable power source for its remote factories. A strong focus on sustainability and community impact is central to the company's operations. Initiatives include empowering women, who are crucial to the tea-plucking process, by establishing daycare centers that provide education and a safe environment for their children. The firm has consistently won awards for its quality, including being the overall winner at the fourth Africa Tea Convention and Exhibition in 2019 and receiving prizes at the Gold Medal Tea Competition in the USA and Canada. column5: Nuclear fusion research using nanomaterials and electrochemistry
column6: Thunderchild Fusion is a research company exploring new pathways to nuclear fusion. The company is primarily owned by PJ King and the core team includes Professor Graham Cross, Dr. Mason Guffey, and Dr. Todd Rider. It operates as a sister company to ReResearch LLC, which was founded in 2010 to investigate alternative fusion approaches, including 'Low Energy Nuclear Reactions' (LENR). The company's primary research platform is the Thunderbird Reactor, a bench-top apparatus developed to study nuclear reactions in condensed matter systems. This reactor generates deuterium-deuterium (D-D) fusion within a palladium metal target. A key feature of its methodology is the use of two techniques to fuel the target: plasma-immersion ion implantation (PIII) and electrochemical loading. This dual approach has been shown to increase fusion reaction rates by 15% compared to using PIII alone. The research, published in Nature, provides the first reproducible demonstration that electrochemistry can enhance nuclear fusion rates. The work leverages 2D nanomaterials to examine the fundamental processes of fusion. This research builds on past efforts to re-evaluate 'cold fusion', a field that emerged in 1989 but was met with skepticism due to a lack of reproducible evidence. Thunderchild Fusion's business is focused on research and development rather than immediate energy generation. The Thunderbird Reactor serves as a tool for investigating methods to enhance fusion rates, aiming to make the science more accessible by moving it from large national laboratories to smaller, bench-top experiments. The research is led by professors from the School of Physics at Trinity College Dublin and involves collaboration with multiple international research institutes, including the National Ion Beam Centre at the University of Surrey, UK. As a privately funded institute, the company is focused on meeting a defined set of experimental goals. column5: Recyclable, waterproof packaging replacing polystyrene and waxed cardboard.
column6: Disruptive Packaging is an Australian company founded in 2016 by Evan Penn that specializes in sustainable packaging solutions. The company was established based on decades of packaging experience, initially self-funded after the founder exited a previous publicly listed company to focus on this new venture. The executive team, including Joint CEOs Wendy and Brandon Penn, brings extensive experience from the packaging, logistics, and supply chain sectors. The company's core product is URTHCOR®, a proprietary material designed to replace conventional waxed cardboard and expanded polystyrene (EPS) packaging. URTHCOR® is composed of up to 70% calcium carbonate, making it waterproof, highly durable, and 100% recyclable within a closed-loop system. This material offers superior thermal insulation and structural integrity, which helps to reduce food waste by protecting contents from damage and maintaining the cold chain. Another key product is URTHCOOL®, which is specifically engineered for industries requiring strict temperature control, such as seafood, pharmaceuticals, and fresh produce, and can be combined with Phase Change Materials (PCM) for enhanced thermal stability. Disruptive Packaging operates on a business-to-business model, serving clients in the fresh produce, seafood, meat, and poultry industries. Its customer base is global, with a significant presence in North America, Europe, and Australasia. The company has established manufacturing and recycling facilities to support its operations, including an 80,000-square-foot plant in Mexicali, Mexico, which serves the North American market tariff-free under the USMCA framework. To facilitate its closed-loop recycling model, the company has recycling infrastructures in locations including Australia, Malaysia, China, and Mexico, where used boxes and production waste are reprocessed into new products. The company has achieved several milestones, including winning the PMA A-NZ Tech Innovation Award in 2020 and a Worldstar Packaging Award in 2021. In March 2024, Disruptive Packaging announced it had completed a US$30 million growth capital raise led by Idealist Capital. This funding is intended to accelerate its expansion in North America, enhance operations, and support further investment in manufacturing capacity and innovation. column5: Low-cost beryllium refining for fusion energy
column6: Miresso is a Japanese startup, established in May 2023, that is focused on enabling the commercialization of fusion energy through a stable, low-cost supply of beryllium. The company was founded by CEO Masaru Nakamichi, who leveraged his research from the National Institutes for Quantum Science and Technology (QST), where he was the group leader of the Functional Materials Development Group. His background is in fusion blanket engineering, and he holds a Ph.D. in Engineering from Tohoku University. Co-founder Suguru Nakano, the Director of Technology Development, also worked with Nakamichi at QST on beryllium research and development. The company's core technology is a patented low-temperature refining process for beryllium, a critical neutron multiplier material needed for fuel self-sufficiency in fusion reactors. Traditional beryllium refining requires high temperatures over 2,000°C, making it expensive and energy-intensive, which creates a significant bottleneck for the fusion industry. Miresso's process uses a combination of chemical processing and microwave heating to dissolve beryllium ore at under 300°C and at normal atmospheric pressure, aiming to drastically reduce costs and energy consumption. This technology addresses the predicted shortage of beryllium, as a single fusion prototype reactor is estimated to require more than the current annual global production. Miresso's primary business involves the manufacturing and sale of beryllium. To scale up its technology, the company is building a pilot plant named "BETA" (Beryllium Testing Plant in Aomori) with a target completion for full-scale production in fiscal year 2027. The plant is expected to produce 1-2 tons of beryllium annually, supplying both the emerging fusion industry and existing markets in aerospace, medical imaging, and electronics. A commercial mass production plant with a 100-ton annual capacity is planned for 2031. The company's business model also includes a technology platform, offering R&D, consulting, and licensing of its low-temperature refining process for other mineral resources like rare earths and lithium, as well as for recycling applications. column5: EV charge point demand management and reservation platform
column6: Reserve & Charge is a UK-based company developing a platform for electric vehicle (EV) charge point reservations to address issues like charging anxiety and inefficient infrastructure use. The founder and CEO is Dr Ralf Kernchen. The venture is built upon the established 'Save-a-Space' parking reservation platform, which has processed over 15,000 reservations across ten train and tram station car parks. The company's core offering is a system-agnostic, API-driven platform that integrates with existing Charge Point Management Systems (CPMS), charging apps, and eMobility Service Providers (eMSPs). This enables EV drivers to book charge points in advance for a specific time and location, reducing queuing and uncertainty. The platform uses real-time data, including charger status and parking space occupancy from sensor technology, to automate and manage reservations. Key features include detecting late arrivals, early departures, and non-EVs blocking spaces (ICEing) to optimize charge point utilization. Reserve & Charge operates on a B2B model, targeting Charge Point Operators (CPOs) and eMSPs. For CPOs, the value proposition is increased revenue through maximized charge point usage and demand management. For eMSPs, integrating the reservation capability is designed to increase their app usage and build brand loyalty. The platform also provides reporting and analytics to help clients understand usage patterns and inform future infrastructure roll-out plans. The company has secured private investment and received a £360k grant from Innovate UK. A pilot project with Transport for West Midlands is planned to test the service. column6: MolPort operates as a specialized e-commerce platform and marketplace for sourcing chemical compounds, aimed at accelerating drug discovery for the scientific community. Founded in Riga, Latvia, in 2006, the company addresses the complexities researchers face in procuring chemical building blocks and screening compounds. The initial concept for the company originated in 2004 with founder Janis Oslejs, who, during his MBA studies, identified the significant challenge scientists at the Latvian Institute of Organic Synthesis faced in acquiring compounds from international vendors. Imants Zudans, who served as CEO for 17 years before being succeeded by Diana Zelencova-Gopejenko in September 2024, was the first employee. Zudans, with a background in chemistry and a PhD from the U.S., returned to Latvia with the goal of building a company that could make a meaningful contribution to his home country and the drug discovery industry. The business model is centered on providing a consolidated, searchable online database of chemicals from a vetted network of over 70 global suppliers. This marketplace structure simplifies the procurement process by allowing scientists to source compounds from multiple suppliers through a single point of contact, with MolPort handling the logistics, order consolidation, and customs clearance. The company does not mark up supplier prices, generating revenue by charging customers for the compounds and shipping. The platform offers access to millions of unique stock screening compounds and building blocks. A key feature is its advanced chemical structure search, which allows users to draw the molecule they need to ensure precise results. Beyond its marketplace function, MolPort provides value-added services such as sample reformatting, quality control testing at independent labs, and sourcing for custom synthesis projects. The platform also tracks supplier performance, offering data-driven insights to help clients select the most reliable sources. MolPort serves a global clientele, including top pharmaceutical companies and chemistry universities, across more than 70 countries. column5: Sustainable full-cycle land-based Black Cod farming
column6: The Black Cod Company is a Dutch enterprise pioneering the first land-based, full-cycle farming of Black Cod (sablefish) in Europe. The company was established by AquaFounders Capital, which is led by land-based aquaculture veterans Ohad Maiman, founder and former CEO of The Kingfish Company, and Thue Holm, founder and former CTO of Atlantic Sapphire. Their venture aims to address the high European demand for this premium fish, which is currently met almost exclusively through frozen imports from North American wild-catch fisheries. The business model centers on producing a high-value species locally to replace imports, ensuring a fresh, sustainable, and high-quality supply year-round for high-end restaurants and premium retail markets. Black Cod is known for its rich, buttery flavor and is one of the highest-priced fish globally. By farming it on land using a recirculating aquaculture system (RAS), the company minimizes its environmental impact through water filtration and reuse, creating a clean and controlled environment for the fish. This method provides optimal control over water quality, feed, and harvesting, differentiating its product from the primarily frozen, wild-caught supply. The company has secured a fully licensed site in Kamperland, in the province of Zeeland, the Netherlands, a region chosen for its clean seawater, existing aquaculture infrastructure, and specialized knowledge. The facility includes a building to be converted into a hatchery and initial production unit, with adjacent land for future expansion. In May 2025, The Black Cod Company secured an investment from the InnoGo! Fund, enabling it to import its first broodstock from North America and commence operations. The initial production target is 75 tonnes per year, with plans to scale up to 300 tonnes. column6: HyCarb is a cleantech company founded in 2024 that is commercializing a technology for producing low-cost clean hydrogen and metal-free graphitic carbon. column5: Global manufacturer of electrolytes for rechargeable batteries
column6: Enchem Co., Ltd. is a South Korean public company specializing in the development and production of electrolytes and high-functionality additives for rechargeable batteries and electric double-layer capacitors (EDLCs). Founded in 2012 by CEO Oh Jung-kang, who has an extensive background in chemical engineering and electrolyte development from his time at Cheil Industries and Samsung SDI, Enchem was established with the vision that rechargeable batteries for electric vehicles (EVs) held greater growth potential than those for smartphones. Initially facing rejection from major South Korean battery makers, Enchem began by supplying smaller companies in China. A significant breakthrough occurred in 2013 when the company partnered with LG Chem to co-develop secondary batteries for electric cars, marking its entry into the EV market. Since then, Enchem has expanded its client base to include major global players such as SK Innovation, CATL, LG Energy Solution, Tesla, and Panasonic, with its electrolytes being supplied to all of the world's top 10 EV makers, including Volkswagen and Ford. Enchem's business model is centered on the production and global supply of electrolytes, a critical material that enables ion transport in lithium-ion batteries. The company has pursued a strategy of aggressive global expansion and localization, establishing production facilities in close proximity to its major clients to ensure just-in-time delivery and reduce logistics costs. It operates plants in South Korea, China, Poland, Hungary, and the United States (Georgia), and has further expansion plans in North America and Europe. This global network is a key competitive advantage, particularly in light of trade policies like the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), which has created opportunities for non-Chinese suppliers. Enchem is notably the only domestic Korean battery material company receiving advanced manufacturing production credits (AMPC) under the IRA. The company's product portfolio includes electrolytes for various applications, including IT devices, EVs, and Energy Storage Systems (ESS), as well as for different battery chemistries like LFP and NCM. Despite recent financial losses attributed to a sluggish EV market, the company is expanding its production of LFP battery electrolytes and ESS products to meet growing demand and anticipates a rebound in profitability. column6: Tractor Beverage Company provides certified organic, non-GMO craft beverages exclusively for the foodservice industry. The company was founded in 2014 by organic farmer Travis Potter, who sought to create healthier drink options without artificial ingredients that he would be happy to serve his own family. Potter's journey began from his concern as a farmer about the legacy of the commodity-based agriculture system, leading him to explore and promote chemical-free, organic farming. The company was also founded by Justin Schneir and Griffin Barkley. Tractor Beverage's business model is centered on being a full-line beverage solution for foodservice partners, distinguishing itself by not being available in grocery or convenience stores. The company serves a wide range of clients, from fast-casual and fine dining restaurants to university, hospital, and workplace cafeterias, with its drinks served in over 7,500 locations across the United States. Its product portfolio includes over 25 flavors of carbonated and non-carbonated drinks, such as craft sodas, lemonades, iced teas, and refreshers, which are provided as syrups and concentrates for fountain machines and bubblers. The company has achieved significant growth, being named to the Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing private companies for four consecutive years. A key feature of Tractor Beverage is its commitment to sustainability and transparency. The company developed the Organic Impact Tracker, a tool that quantifies the positive environmental impact of choosing its organic products over conventionally sourced ones. This initiative is part of its broader mission to remove chemicals from the food system and promote soil health. column6: REBEL, formerly known as Rebelstork, operates a recommerce marketplace focused on giving overstock and open-box products a second chance. Founded in 2019 by Emily Hosie, the Toronto-based company initially centered on the baby gear market before expanding into home goods. Hosie, a retail industry veteran with experience at Saks Fifth Avenue and TJX Companies, identified a gap in the market after her own frustrating experience trying to resell gently used baby items. She discovered that a significant volume of returned and excess inventory from major brands and retailers was ending up in landfills, often due to a lack of a viable resale channel. The company's business model is built on partnerships with major retailers and brands, including Target, to manage their returned and overstock inventory. REBEL is not a traditional secondhand marketplace; it specializes in items that are typically unused but cannot be sold as new, such as those with damaged packaging or returned by consumers. The platform handles the entire reverse logistics process, including quality and safety inspections, condition rating, and professional photography before listing items for sale. This B2B service provides retail partners with a new revenue stream and a sustainable solution for managing returns. For consumers, REBEL offers access to brand-name products at significant discounts, often up to 70% off retail prices. A key component of REBEL's operation is its proprietary AI-powered pricing technology, REV™, which analyzes real-time data on product condition, market demand, and retail trends to set fair prices. This technology is designed to eliminate haggling and provide transparency for both buyers and sellers. The company has secured significant venture funding to scale its operations, including a Series A round that brought its total funding to over $25 million. A certified B-Corporation, REBEL emphasizes sustainability by diverting millions of pounds of products from landfills annually. column5: Giving the cities high precision parking data to manage the shared micromobility
column6: Sparkpark AS is a Norwegian technology company established in 2020 by co-founders Igor Pancevski and Thomas Bråten to address disorganized micromobility parking. The company provides a patented digital, dockless parking infrastructure for shared micromobility vehicles, such as e-scooters and e-bikes. The core of Sparkpark's offering is the Happy City® platform, a system combining hardware and software to ensure vehicles are parked with centimeter-level precision. The technology uses small, solar-powered antennas that can be mounted on existing city infrastructure and connect via a 4G LTE-M network. These antennas communicate with the vehicle's Bluetooth to validate its position within a designated and digitally calibrated parking zone. A user's trip cannot be ended in the operator's app until the system confirms the vehicle is correctly parked, tackling issues of street clutter and improving pedestrian safety. Sparkpark operates on a B2B2G (business-to-business-to-government) model, positioning itself as the link between micromobility operators and city municipalities. Its clients include vehicle rental companies and cities aiming to better manage urban mobility. The firm generates revenue by providing "Parking As A Service" and has engaged in pilot projects in European cities like Prague, Madrid, and in Poland with operator E-wings. The company has received support and funding from entities including the Research Council of Norway, Innovation Norway, and EIT Urban Mobility. It was also selected for the Scale-up programme in 2023 and is part of the Ville de Demain innovation ecosystem. column6: Myelin-H, also known as MyelinZ Group, develops AI-powered neurotechnology for monitoring brain and body health. The company was co-founded in 2021 by Dr. Zied Tayeb (CEO) and Samaher Garbaya (COO). Dr. Tayeb, a computer scientist who pivoted to neuroscience, was motivated by his mother's diagnosis with multiple sclerosis (MS). This personal connection led him to research brain-machine interfaces and develop the company's foundational technology. Garbaya, an engineer with a background in signal processing and machine learning, connected with Tayeb after he open-sourced his initial research. The company's core offering is a brain-machine interface platform that uses neuroscience, AI, and gamification to track, monitor, and enhance brain health. It serves multiple markets through three main products. "R-MMS" is a medical-grade software for the remote monitoring of patients with multiple sclerosis, providing clinicians with data on treatment effectiveness and disease progression. "BodyMirror" is a consumer-facing mobile application designed to improve cognitive and physical health through daily gamified exercises. "MyelinSpace" is a specialized neurotechnology developed to monitor and protect the cognitive functions of astronauts in extreme environments like deep space. Myelin-H's business model involves licensing its platform to pharmaceutical companies for clinical trials and partnering with healthcare providers. The technology translates complex biosignals into digital biomarkers, generating medical reports on a mobile dashboard for physicians. The company has engaged in multiple funding rounds, securing investments from firms like imec.istart, Technoport SA, and Luxinnovation. It has also participated in accelerator programs, including Fit 4 Start in Luxembourg and the US-based Care In Space Challenge by Axiom Space, which included mentoring from NASA. column5: Rapidly deployable, factory-built low-rise modular buildings
column6: Modulus Housing is a proptech company specializing in factory-built modular construction for low-rise buildings. It was founded in 2018 by Shreeram Ravichandran and P. Gobinath, alumni of IIT Madras. The initial inspiration for the company came from the founders' volunteer work during the 2015 Chennai floods, where they identified a need for rapidly deployable temporary housing for displaced individuals. The company operates on a cloud manufacturing model, utilizing a decentralized network of partner factories across India combined with a proprietary IP-based product suite to deliver modular infrastructure. This approach allows for the precision manufacturing of building components off-site, which are then assembled at the final location. Modulus claims this process can reduce construction timelines for certain projects to under 30 days. The firm has developed proprietary innovations in construction materials, including a fast-preparing concrete base and patented manufacturing processes, to increase the speed of assembly. It also focuses on lightweight, green concrete technology. Modulus Housing serves a diverse B2B client base that includes government entities, private sector companies like the Tata Group and L&T, NGOs, and CSR initiatives. Its product portfolio is varied, including modular hospitals (MediCAB), cold storage units, on-site offices for construction companies, schools, EV charging stations, and rural infrastructure. The company has executed over 1,500 projects across 21 states in India and parts of Africa. As of December 2025, Modulus Housing raised $7.83 million in a Series A funding round led by Kalaari Capital, Hero, and Samarthya to fund market expansion, R&D for a next-generation concrete modular system, and scaling its cloud manufacturing network. The company has been profitable, with cumulative revenue exceeding Rs 200 crore and operating revenue of Rs 54 crore in FY24. column5: Autonomous on-chain treasury management​ Working with decentralized organizations to push the frontiers of DeFi and trustless treasury management. Diversify your assets. Unlock liquidity. Receive yield. Retain governance
column6: Fyde Treasury Protocol operates as an on-chain treasury management platform, providing a solution for DAOs, protocols, and individual cryptocurrency holders. The company was established in the third quarter of 2022 by a team that includes Behrin Naidoo, Bo Zhang, and Carlos Noe S. . The founders' backgrounds are rooted in traditional finance and academia, with co-founder Behrin Naidoo conceiving the project while at London Business School, where he also co-founded the LBS Blockchain Society. Carlos Saavedra's experience spans investment banking and portfolio management at Deutsche Bank, while Bo Zhang previously worked as a portfolio manager at JP Morgan. The broader team possesses expertise from institutions like NASA, Cambridge, Stanford, and Web3 entities such as Synthetix and Wintermute. The protocol's core offering is its "Liquid Vaults," which are non-custodial smart contracts managed by AI. Users can deposit a variety of digital assets into these vaults to achieve diversification, generate yield, and access liquidity, all while retaining their governance rights over the deposited tokens. The platform addresses key challenges in crypto treasury management by using AI and on-chain network simulation models to auto-rebalance portfolios, manage risk, and optimize for downside volatility. When a user deposits assets, they receive the $TRSY token, a wrapper token that represents their share of the vault and tracks its overall performance. This mechanism allows users to gain broad market exposure and potentially grow their holdings with less volatility than holding single assets. Fyde generates revenue through platform fees, such as imbalance penalties and fees from yield strategies. The business model allocates 80% of this revenue to buy back its native governance token, $FYDE, with the remaining 20% funding operational expenses. The $FYDE token serves as a yield enhancer and is used to incentivize deep on-chain liquidity for the $TRSY token. The protocol launched on the Ethereum mainnet in December 2023. Fyde has secured $3.45 million in total funding over three seed rounds, with the latest round in December 2023 raising $3.2 million, led by OP Crypto and with participation from investors like Arrington Capital, Merit Circle, and Big Brain Holdings. column6: CEF Group is an Indian cleantech company founded by Maninder Singh in 2018, specializing in converting waste into compressed biogas (CBG).
