column6: Vivoka SAS, founded in Metz, France, in 2015, specializes in voice recognition and artificial intelligence technologies. The company was established by William Simonin, Vincent Leroy, and Geoffrey Heckmann, who were students at the EPITECH school of innovation at the time. Inspired by a desire to revolutionize human-machine interaction, the founders pooled their skills to focus on voice as a new interface. Simonin, who serves as CEO, holds a master's degree in entrepreneurship from the University of Kent and was named to the Forbes France "30 Under 30" list in 2022. In May 2024, Christophe Couvreur, an executive with extensive experience in the field, took over operational management as the new CEO, while Simonin remains president of the board. The company's core offering is the Voice Development Kit (VDK), an all-in-one software solution that enables businesses to create and integrate high-performance, secure, and offline voice assistants into their products and services. A key differentiator for Vivoka is its emphasis on offline functionality, allowing voice assistants to operate without an internet connection, which ensures data privacy and security. The VDK is a comprehensive toolkit that combines various speech technologies from leading global providers, including wake word detection, automatic speech recognition (ASR), natural language understanding (NLU), voice biometrics, and text-to-speech (TTS). This allows developers to benchmark, develop, and test different voice solutions through a single graphical interface. The business model primarily revolves around flexible subscriptions or per-device royalties for integrating the VDK. Vivoka has secured approximately $3.45 million in funding over two seed rounds in 2018 and 2019 from investors including MCH Gestion and Etchart. The company serves a diverse client base of over 100 customers across sectors such as robotics, logistics, consumer electronics, healthcare, defense, and aeronautics. Notable clients include major international groups like Eiffage, Thalès, and Suez. Vivoka has also established strategic partnerships with key players in the technology hardware and software space, including NXP Semiconductors, ID R&D, and BdSound, to enhance its VDK with advanced features like voice biometrics and superior audio processing. column5: Platform for designing and producing versatile sweet proteins
column6: Sweet Bliss is a translational research project operating within the BioInnovation Institute's (BII) Bio Studio program. The project is a collaboration with the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) and focuses on developing a platform to design and produce sweet proteins with versatile and tailorable functional properties. These proteins are intended for use in the food and supplements industry as a low-calorie, healthy alternative to traditional and synthetic sweeteners. The project is led by Principal Investigator Morten Sommer, a Professor of Bacterial Synthetic Biology at DTU, and Entrepreneur in Residence, Ali Fallah-Araghi. Sommer has a background in biophysics with a PhD from Harvard University and has founded several companies, including Union Therapeutics, Biosyntia, and Clinical-Microbiomics. Fallah-Araghi holds a PhD in Biotechnology from the University of Strasbourg and has over a decade of experience at Novozymes in various roles, as well as experience as the Director of Protein Engineering at the Singaporean startup Allozymes. Sweet Bliss is housed within the BioInnovation Institute in Copenhagen, Denmark, an international hub for life science innovation supported by the Novo Nordisk Foundation. As part of the Bio Studio program, the project receives significant support, including an annual grant with a market value of up to DKK 7,860,000 for a period of up to three years. Beyond funding, BII provides business development expertise, intellectual property support, access to an investor network, and use of its wet lab and office infrastructure. The primary goal is to engineer proteins that not only provide potent sweetness but also replace other functional properties of sugar, addressing consumer demand for healthier alternatives amid rising concerns about obesity and diabetes. The expected outcome is the formation of a viable startup capable of attracting seed or Series A financing. column6: Shifted Energy is a company operating in the energy storage sector, specifically focused on solving the intermittency challenges of renewable energy sources like wind and solar photovoltaic (PV). The company was founded in 2022 by Eirik Eide Pettersen (CEO) and Antoine Pahan (CTO). The founding team combines expertise from various fields, including startups, large corporations, and academic research at institutions such as Harvard and Princeton, accumulating 60 years of collective experience. Shifted Energy has developed a novel energy storage system that integrates pumped hydro and compressed air technologies. This hybrid solution is engineered to provide electricity at a significantly lower cost, reportedly half the cost of lithium-ion batteries, which are a common standard in the industry. The system is designed for geographic versatility, allowing it to be deployed in various locations without reliance on specific topographies or critical raw materials, a notable advantage over traditional pumped hydro and battery technologies. The company's technology is a closed-loop system, which enhances its flexibility and deployment potential. The primary market for Shifted Energy's solution includes producers of wind and solar PV power, as well as companies that service the electricity grid. By providing a cost-effective and scalable energy storage solution, the company aims to facilitate a more stable and reliable integration of renewables into the power grid. In 2022, Shifted Energy secured its first funding, raising €550k in a pre-seed round with the participation of EIT InnoEnergy. This funding was intended to help the company validate its technology and prepare it for market entry. column6: Admiral Maltings is a producer of artisanal floor-malted grains for the brewing and distilling industries, located in Alameda, California. Founded in 2017 by beer industry veterans Ron Silberstein (ThirstyBear Brewing Company) and Dave McLean (Magnolia Brewing Company), along with Curtis Davenport, who has a background in organic farming and small-batch malting. Their goal was to provide a local, high-quality alternative to the industrial malt predominantly used by the region's craft breweries and distilleries. The company operates out of a refurbished 20,000-square-foot World War II-era naval dry goods facility, which houses the first floor-malting facility in California since Prohibition. The business model centers on sourcing sustainably grown grain, such as barley, wheat, and rye, directly from family farms in California, including the Sacramento Valley and Tule Lake region. Admiral Maltings emphasizes regenerative and organic farming practices, including no-till and dry farming. The core of its operation is the traditional and labor-intensive method of floor malting, where grain is spread across a floor to germinate and turned by hand. This technique is believed to produce malt with superior flavor and aroma compared to industrial methods. The company sells its freshly kilned, small-batch malts directly to nearly 300 breweries and over 30 distilleries. Its clients include prominent names like Sierra Nevada Brewing, Anchor Brewing, and Russian River Brewing Co. In addition to its primary malting business, Admiral Maltings operates an on-site pub called The Rake. The pub, which overlooks the malting floor, exclusively serves beers and spirits made with the company's own malt, offering customers a direct taste of the product's impact. This vertical integration serves as a showroom for their malt and provides an additional revenue stream. The company also hosts events and malthouse tours, further engaging with the craft beverage community. column6: Evotrex is a California-based company developing intelligent, power-generating recreational vehicles (RVs) designed for off-grid travel without limits. The company emerged from stealth mode on November 6, 2025, with $16 million in Pre-A funding. The funding round was led by Xstar Capital, with participation from Unity Ventures, Kylinhall Partners, Vision Plus Capital, and the founders of Anker Innovations. The company was founded by a team of veterans from the power technology and electric vehicle industries, including CEO Alex Xiao, who spent over a decade building Anker into a leading mobile charging brand. He is joined by co-founders Bruce Yang (CTO), a former R&D leader at Geely Group, Stella Qin (Chief Brand Officer), an alumna of Anker with van-life experience, and Jack Zhan (COO), who has a background in supply chain management at Lenovo, IBM, and Anker. The founding team's journey began after Xiao and Qin spent seven months researching the RV market, identifying a growing demographic of younger adventurers seeking to take their equipment to remote, off-grid locations. Evotrex's primary product is a hybrid RV travel trailer that integrates a battery system with a gasoline engine. This serial hybrid system powers the trailer's onboard amenities—such as HVAC, lighting, and induction cooking—primarily from the battery. The gasoline engine then functions as an integrated generator to recharge the battery, enabling extended stays in remote locations without reliance on external power sources or traditional loud generators. The system is also designed to capture and reuse waste heat from the engine to help warm the cabin. This model targets adventurers who want modern comforts and reliable power for activities like skiing and fishing, far from conventional campgrounds. Manufacturing is planned to take place mostly in China, with final assembly in California. Evotrex aims to disrupt the RV market alongside other startups like Lightship and Pebble by catering to a younger, tech-savvy, and eco-conscious consumer base. The company plans to fully unveil its first product at the Consumer Electronics Show (CES) in January 2026 and aims to begin shipping by the end of that year. column5: BOLLINGER MOTORS - ALL ELECTRIC TRUCKS - BOLLINGER MOTORS
column6: Bollinger Motors, an American electric vehicle manufacturer, was established in 2015 by Robert Bollinger in the Catskill Mountains of New York. The founder's journey into the automotive world was unconventional; after graduating with an Industrial Design degree from Carnegie Mellon, he worked in advertising and later helped build and sell an organic cosmetic company. The capital from that sale provided the financial backing for Bollinger to pursue his lifelong passion for cars, initially sparked by a desire for an environmentally friendly and rugged truck for his organic farm. The company's initial focus was on consumer-oriented, rugged, all-electric SUVs and pickups. In 2017, the B1 SUV prototype was unveiled, featuring a distinct, angular design that garnered significant attention. Following the prototype's debut, the company relocated to the Detroit, Michigan area to leverage the region's deep automotive engineering talent pool. A major strategic pivot occurred in early 2022 when Bollinger Motors indefinitely postponed its consumer models, the B1 and B2, to concentrate on the commercial electric vehicle market. This decision was driven by the assessment that the commercial segment was more prepared for electrification. This strategic shift culminated in the company becoming a majority-owned subsidiary of Mullen Automotive (NASDAQ: MULN) in September 2022. Bollinger Motors now focuses on developing and manufacturing all-electric commercial trucks, specifically in Classes 4 through 6. The company operates as an Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), selling chassis cabs to commercial fleets and upfitters who then add specific bodies like contractor beds or delivery boxes. Production of its first vehicle, the Class 4 Bollinger B4 Chassis Cab, began in September 2024 at a facility in Livonia, Michigan, managed by manufacturing partner Roush Industries. The business model involves direct sales to fleet management companies and sales through a growing national dealer network that also provides service. Revenue is generated from vehicle sales, with significant financial incentives available to customers through federal and state programs, potentially exceeding $100,000 per vehicle. The flagship product, the Bollinger B4, is a Class 4 all-electric chassis cab built on a proprietary 40-inch wide frame, which is wider than the industry standard and designed to securely house batteries and components between the rails for improved safety and driving dynamics. It is powered by an 800-volt system and features two LFP battery packs from supplier Our Next Energy (ONE), totaling 158 kWh. This provides a range of up to 185 miles. The B4 delivers 323 horsepower and has a payload capacity of 7,325 pounds. Charging can be done via AC Level 2 in nine hours or DC Fast Charge in about two hours. Following the B4, the company plans to launch the Bollinger B5, a Class 5 truck with increased payload capacity, expected in 2026. Roof Maker's product line is characterized by its emphasis on maximizing natural light and thermal efficiency. Its products feature slim profiles and a frameless internal appearance to increase light flow. The company offers double and triple-glazed options, with its triple-glazed units providing high thermal insulation ratings. column5: Solar operator models for residential and commercial properties
column6: ALVA Energie, founded in 2024, is a Berlin-based energy company specializing in decentralized solar energy solutions for the real estate sector. The founding partners are Cecil von Croy, Alexis Cramm, Marc Schuhbauer, Franziskus Cramm, and Marian Hallal. The company provides 360-degree service for solar operator models on multi-family residential buildings and commercial properties across Germany. The company's core business revolves around the German "Mieterstrom" or tenant electricity model, where electricity is generated by solar photovoltaic (PV) systems on a building's roof and supplied directly to the tenants and commercial users within that property or district. This approach addresses the landlord-tenant dilemma by creating financial incentives for property owners to invest in renewable energy while offering tenants lower energy costs. ALVA Energie manages the entire process, including consulting, planning, financing, installation, and the long-term operation of the energy systems, which can also integrate heat pumps and electric vehicle charging infrastructure. By acting as the energy supplier, ALVA simplifies the process for property owners and tenants. ALVA Energie's business model is vertically integrated, allowing it to handle all key steps in-house. It offers flexible arrangements for property owners, including roof leases, system leases, and operator models. For tenants, the company provides locally produced green electricity directly, partly under its "KARLSSONN" brand. The company serves private property owners, larger real estate companies, and investment funds. In July 2025, ALVA Energie successfully closed its first funding round, securing over €5 million from investors including Triodos Bank, Württembergische Energie GmbH, and Brandenburg Kapital GmbH to scale its operations. Since its founding, the company has completed over 50 projects and aims to double this number by the end of 2025. column6: Pehle Jaisa, an agritech startup founded in 2022, is focused on decentralizing the production of organic fertilizers in India. The company's core service is providing farmers with organic fertilizers that are customized to specific crop types and regional soil requirements. This approach aims to create a circular rural economy, enabling villages to become self-sufficient in generating their own fertilizer, gas, and electricity from local waste streams. column5: We make ordinary smartphones act as payment terminals
column6: Dapio, formerly known as Paymob, is a London-based financial technology company established in 2019 by fintech veterans Kosta Du and Grigory Gurbanov. The firm operates as a payment solutions provider, with a core offering that transforms Android smartphones into point-of-sale (POS) terminals using Near Field Communication (NFC) technology. This 'Tap to Pay' solution is designed to serve a market segment that has been historically underserved by traditional payment providers, specifically micro-businesses, sole traders, and gig economy workers. By eliminating the need for clunky and expensive hardware, Dapio provides these businesses with access to the same robust payments infrastructure as larger organizations. The company's primary product is a mobile application that allows businesses to accept contactless payments from credit cards and e-wallets directly on their NFC-enabled Android phones. Beyond its direct-to-customer app, Dapio offers its technology as an embedded finance solution through a Software Development Kit (SDK) and App-to-app callback APIs. This allows partners such as POS vendors, banks, and other fintech platforms to integrate Dapio's 'Tap to Pay' functionality into their own applications. The company's business model extends to a suite of financial tools including multi-currency IBAN accounts (EUR, USD, GBP), virtual and physical corporate cards with spending controls, and online checkout solutions for e-commerce. Revenue is generated from these payment processing services and financial products. Co-founder and CEO Kosta Du, an entrepreneur with nearly two decades of experience in tech ventures, was motivated by his own difficulties in accessing financial services upon moving to the UK. His international background, with time spent in Moscow, New York, China, and Egypt, informed his vision to simplify financial services for businesses globally. In March 2022, Dapio secured $3.4 million in a Series A funding round co-led by African payments giant Flutterwave and Techstars, with participation from PactVC and Asymmetry Ventures. This capital has been aimed at fueling the rollout of its 'Tap to Pay' solution across the UK and Europe, targeting the significant portion of the market that uses Android devices. column6: Alkagesta, founded in Malta in 2018 by Orkhan Rustamov and Kamran Aghayev, is a global commodity trading house. The company invested in a Used Cooking Oil (UCO) recycling plant and launched a biofuels trading desk, obtaining ISCC EU certification for sustainability traceability. column6: Kabisa is an electric mobility company operating in Rwanda, establishing an ecosystem for electric vehicles (EVs) in East Africa. column6: Factor2Energy is developing a CO2-based geothermal power system to provide scalable and emission-free energy. The company's journey began in 2019 when it was incubated within Siemens Energy, where the concept was initially developed and refined. A key milestone was achieved between 2022 and 2023 with a successful proof of concept in partnership with MOL Group in Hungary, which validated the technology under real-world operating conditions. It can access a broader range of geothermal sites, particularly those with moderate temperatures, due to the favorable properties of CO2, such as its lower viscosity and strong natural thermosiphon effect. This eliminates the need for subsurface pumps and complex binary systems. Furthermore, the method reduces environmental impact by avoiding fracking, ultra-deep drilling, and high water consumption. By leveraging existing, proven components and drilling technologies, Factor2Energy aims to accelerate the time to market and lower the capital investment required for geothermal power projects. The business model focuses on deploying this proprietary geothermal technology to generate clean power. The system works by injecting liquid CO2 deep into the ground where it is heated, causing it to rise to the surface through a production well. The heated CO2 then drives a turbine to generate electricity before being cooled, re-compressed, and re-injected, creating a continuous, closed-loop cycle. This process is designed to be a cost-effective solution for baseload power generation, contributing to the energy transition. Based in Bengaluru, the company was founded by Vijay Nirani, who serves as the Managing Director. Nirani, an industrialist with a background in business and global family-managed business, leveraged his experience in the sugar industry to establish TruAlt Bioenergy, transforming traditional sugar mills into bioenergy parks. The company holds the distinction of being the largest ethanol producer in India based on installed capacity, operating five distillery units in Karnataka. These facilities utilize feedstocks such as sugarcane juice, molasses, and increasingly, maize and surplus rice. TruAlt's core business involves selling ethanol to public Oil Marketing Companies like Indian Oil, Bharat Petroleum, and HPCL as part of India's Ethanol Blending Programme (EBP). Its product portfolio also includes Extra Neutral Alcohol (ENA) for the beverage industry, as well as by-products like liquid CO2 and dry ice. Through its subsidiary, Leafiniti Bioenergy, TruAlt is also one of the first producers of Compressed Biogas (CBG) under the government's Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation (SATAT) scheme, also producing fermented organic manure. The company's business model is vertically integrated, with a reliable supply of raw materials sourced largely from promoter-group entities. Revenue is generated primarily through the sale of ethanol to OMCs, with its top five customers accounting for over 92% of its revenue in FY25. In June 2025, TruAlt was granted an Oil Marketing Company (OMC) license, allowing it to directly market and retail clean fuels like Bio-CNG and ethanol-blended petrol, alongside conventional fuels. The company plans to establish over 100 fuel stations across Karnataka and Maharashtra. Looking ahead, TruAlt Bioenergy intends to expand into new verticals, including the production of Second Generation (2G) Ethanol, Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), and other allied biochemicals. It has entered into partnerships, including a collaboration with GAIL for CBG plant development and memorandums with Japanese firms for potential bioenergy collaborations. The company launched its Initial Public Offering (IPO) in September 2025 to fund capital expenditure for multi-feedstock operations and working capital needs. column6: Kitar is a technology-driven company in Indonesia focused on the second-hand mobile phone market, founded in 2024 by Frank Zhou. The company operates an e-commerce platform that facilitates the recycling and reselling of used smartphones to promote sustainability and tackle electronic waste. The founder, Frank Zhou, is a graduate of Tsinghua University’s Department of Electronic Engineering with a background in internet products. His experience includes being a core executive at Guazi Second-hand Cars in China and incubating Shopee's food delivery business in Southeast Asia starting in 2021. The idea for Kitar emerged when Zhou observed a high demand for second-hand iPhones among food delivery riders in Vietnam, revealing a significant unmet need in the Southeast Asian used-device market. The company's team comprises individuals with experience from major internet firms like Shopee, ByteDance, and Alibaba. Kitar's business model combines both B2C and C2C approaches. It establishes trust through a standardized process for inspecting and certifying pre-owned devices, addressing a key point of friction in the second-hand market. The company acquires used phones from individual sellers through its online platform and a network of offline stores, offering services like at-home pickup in Jakarta and secure data wiping. These devices then undergo a thorough inspection with over 50 checkpoints before being sold as certified pre-owned products with a warranty of up to one year. The platform also has an authorized Apple reseller store on Shopee. Initially focusing on the Indonesian market, Kitar operates physical stores and service points in the Greater Jakarta area (Jabodetabek) with plans to expand. In early 2026, the company secured over USD 10 million in a pre-Series A funding round. This round was led by Source Code Capital, with participation from Hike Capital and MindWorks Capital. The capital is intended to enhance AI capabilities, improve supply chain infrastructure, expand its offline collection network, and support localized operations for further expansion into Southeast Asia. column5: Drone Automation Platform | AI Data Processing
column6: Dronehub is a Polish company specializing in automated drone-in-a-box systems for industrial monitoring, inspection, and data collection. The company originated as Cervi Robotics in 2015, founded by Vadym Melnyk, and rebranded to Dronehub in 2020 to focus exclusively on its drone automation platform. Melnyk, a data science engineer with a background in robotics and machine learning, founded the company while still a university student in Poland. His interest in robotics began at age fifteen, and prior to Dronehub, he gained experience through various robotics projects and a role at Microsoft developing a program to support early-stage startups. Dronehub's core offering is an integrated ecosystem comprising autonomous drones, a ground-based docking hub, and AI-powered software. The system is designed for industries with large infrastructure, such as energy, security, and construction, to automate monitoring, reduce costs, and acquire real-time aerial data. The business model centers on selling this comprehensive hardware and software package, which operates on a SaaS (Software as a Service) basis. The key product is the "Hub," a docking station that enables fully autonomous drone operations 24/7. A notable feature is its patented mechanism that automatically swaps a drone's battery in under two minutes, allowing for continuous missions without human intervention. The hubs are weather-resistant, vandal-proof, and equipped with climate control to ensure operability in diverse conditions. Drones can be equipped with various sensors, including RGB, thermal, and LiDAR, which can be changed automatically within the hub. The accompanying software processes the visual data collected by the drones, transforming it into actionable business insights using AI-based object recognition and providing advanced reports. This platform can be deployed on the cloud or a client's server infrastructure and integrates with third-party systems. Significant milestones include securing its first major client, PKN Orlen, in 2019 to automate infrastructure monitoring at a refinery. The company has received multiple grants, including $1.9 million from the Polish National Centre for Research and Development (NCBR) in 2021. In 2022, Dronehub was a finalist in the GENIUS NY accelerator, the world's largest competition for uncrewed aerial systems, securing a $500,000 award and establishing a U.S. presence. This led to a partnership with Marquardt for a technology installation at their New York facility. column5: Affordable renewable electricity retailer for Singapore businesses
column6: Flo Energy Singapore Pte Ltd is an electricity retailer established in 2020, positioning itself as Singapore's largest independent energy retailer. The company was co-founded by Matthijs Guichelaar and Ernst Westendorp, who identified a market opportunity for affordable renewable energy to accelerate the global energy transition. Guichelaar previously founded Amsterdam-based Vandebron, a green energy company, while Westendorp had extensive experience in the Asia-Pacific region. They launched Flo in Singapore with their personal savings, starting in a small shophouse and growing the team to over one hundred people within three years. The company's business model centers on providing 100% renewable electricity to businesses and, in the future, residential customers in Singapore. It operates in Singapore's Open Electricity Market (OEM). Flo Energy differentiates itself by exclusively offering renewable energy plans, refusing to provide conventional fossil fuel-based options. To ensure price stability for its clients, the company purchases electricity upfront through futures contracts, offering fixed-rate plans for durations of 12 to 24 months. Its revenue is generated through the sale of these electricity plans. A key part of its strategy is leveraging a proprietary in-house technology platform, which automates processes and reduces operational costs, allowing the firm to offer competitive pricing. Flo Energy's core product is renewable electricity, supplied with a guarantee called 'The Flo Commitment'. This involves matching 100% of a customer's electricity usage with regional Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs), which are then redeemed on the customer's behalf quarterly, allowing them to make verified renewable energy claims. In addition to its primary electricity retail services, Flo has expanded its offerings to include Flo Solar Solutions for capital-free solar facility deployment, tenant management solutions for multi-tenanted properties, and comprehensive metering solutions. Customers can monitor their usage and manage their accounts through the FlowSmart online dashboard. Since its launch, Flo has served over 1,750 large business customers. The company expanded its operations to Australia in 2023. Global energy company Vitol has invested in Flo to support its growth into new markets, although it is not involved in daily operations. column6: CliniNote, a Polish health-tech company founded in 2020, is focused on improving the management of clinical data. The company was established by Robert Lugowski (CEO), Rafal Szmuc (COO), and Professor Jan Poleszczuk (CTO), who combined their experience in the HealthTech sector to address inefficiencies in clinical data collection and utilization. The initial concept was developed in collaboration with clinicians from the National Institute of Oncology in Warsaw, aiming to create solutions for structured clinical data. The core of CliniNote's business is a platform that uses artificial intelligence and natural language processing (NLP) to help healthcare professionals create structured clinical notes in real-time. This system is designed to seamlessly integrate with existing hospital information systems (HIS) and electronic health records (EHR) as a browser extension, which avoids the need for complex and costly IT integration projects. The platform includes several modules: the CliniNote Assistant for real-time documentation support, DataCollector for centralized data management, and DictEditor for creating shareable templates and dictionaries. These tools work together to reduce the time clinicians spend on paperwork, decrease repetitive data entry, and improve data quality. CliniNote operates on a B2B business model, serving a range of clients including healthcare providers, pharmaceutical companies, contract research organizations (CROs), and site management organizations (SMOs). Its technology is applied in areas such as clinical trials and real-world evidence (RWE) generation. For clinical trials, the system simplifies protocol adherence and can automate electronic Case Report Form (eCRF) input. In RWE, it facilitates the collection of structured data during routine clinical work for later analysis. The company has secured collaborations with major industry players like Novartis, MSD, and IQVIA. After an initial development phase from 2020 to 2022, the platform was launched in late 2022/early 2023. In the fall of 2023, CliniNote secured its first institutional seed funding round led by the Berlin-based fund Sunfish Partners, along with support from healthcare business angels. column5: All-in-one e-bike drive unit with automatic transmission
column6: E2 DRIVES is a Belgian electric mobility company founded in 2013 by Arthur Deleval and Simon Godfrind. Deleval, an automotive and mechanical engineer, conceived the initial idea and patented it in 2012. He was joined by Godfrind, a PhD candidate in microelectronics, to create the first prototype, leading to the formal establishment of E2 DRIVES. The company operates as a subsidiary of the French sports retailer Decathlon S.A. and specializes in developing and producing advanced drive systems for e-bikes. The company's flagship product is the OWURU drive unit, an integrated system that combines a dual-motor setup with a planetary gearbox to provide both electric assistance and a stepless, continuously variable automatic transmission (CVT). This design eliminates the need for a traditional derailleur and cassette, allowing for smooth gear changes even under load or at a standstill. The system is engineered to maintain a constant pedaling cadence for the rider by continuously adjusting the gear ratio. The first generation of the OWURU unit, designed for city and trekking use, delivers 65-120 Nm of torque and has a gear range of 265%. It has been integrated into Decathlon's BTWIN LD 920 E e-bike. E2 DRIVES initially intended to license its technology, securing a partnership in 2015 that ended in 2017. Following this, the company pivoted towards developing its own complete e-bike before entering into a partnership with Decathlon in 2020, which led to Decathlon acquiring the firm. The company's business model is now focused on designing, prototyping, testing, and validating these drive units exclusively for Decathlon's electric bikes. E2 DRIVES has received support from private and public investors, including the Walloon Region and Nivelinvest. column6: Banbu is a Spanish sustainable cosmetics brand founded in 2019 with a mission to revolutionize the beauty industry by decoupling product efficacy from environmental and health harm. column5: Climate-positive, modular housing for at-risk communities
column6: homeD Modular is a Canadian social impact company focused on alleviating homelessness and providing affordable housing through volumetric modular construction. The company was co-founded by architect James Law, CEO Michele Tung, and Frank Christiaens. The inspiration came when Law witnessed people in Mumbai using precast water pipes as shelter, which reminded him of his own childhood in Hong Kong's shanty-towns and sparked the desire to design dignified housing solutions. Together, the founders combined their expertise in architecture, international business, and strategy to establish the company. homeD designs and manufactures high-performance, climate-positive modular homes, serving clients such as non-profit organizations and municipalities to address housing crises. The business model centers on the 'homeD Circle of Good,' which emphasizes local manufacturing, providing fair wage employment and training, and building safe, sustainable communities. Revenue is generated through the sale and deployment of their modular housing units for projects focused on below-market housing, from emergency shelters to multi-level buildings. They also partner with organizations like the Old Brewery Mission, which manages support services for residents, aiding their transition to permanent housing. The company's primary products are BoxPods, which are cost-effective, zero-carbon compliant, and adaptable modular units. These self-contained units originate from precast concrete box culverts and include a kitchenette, a full bathroom, and living space. They can be stacked up to six levels high or used as freestanding structures, offering flexibility for dense urban environments and remote communities alike. A key feature is the ability to set up 'pop-up' factories for local assembly, which not only speeds up construction but also engages the local workforce in building their own communities. column5: Sneaker reuse and recycling program supporting micro-enterprises
column6: Sneakers4Good operates a program for reusing and recycling athletic shoes, preventing them from ending up in landfills. The company partners with running clubs, retailers, gyms, and marathon organizers to collect gently worn, used, and new sneakers. In return for the collected shoes, the partner organization receives a payment, which they can use for their own causes or donate to a charity of their choice. The collected footwear is given a second life by being distributed to micro-entrepreneurs in 24 developing countries, such as Haiti, Cambodia, and Guatemala. These small business owners, often families, sell the shoes in their local markets, creating income opportunities and fostering economic sustainability in their communities. This model is described as providing a "hand up, not a hand out." Sneakers4Good supplies its partners with collection boxes, marketing materials, and prepaid shipping bags, handling the logistics of the program. For retailers, the program pays $2 per pair of eligible shoes, with additional incentives available. Sneakers4Good is a division of Funds2Orgs, a social enterprise specializing in shoe drive fundraising, and was founded by Wayne Elsey. Elsey's background includes working in a shoe store stock room, running a large shoe manufacturing company, and starting a global charity focused on shoes before becoming a serial social entrepreneur. The idea for Sneakers4Good emerged from the growing demand for sneaker recycling within the running community. The company states that over 70% of the global population utilizes repurposed clothing and shoes and that hundreds of millions of pairs of shoes are discarded annually by Americans, taking 30 to 40 years to decompose in landfills. column5: Automate your B2B Order Process with AI
column6: Hyperfox is a Belgian SaaS company that automates B2B order processing for manufacturers, distributors, and logistics companies. The platform uses AI to capture, validate, and streamline incoming orders from every channel: email, EDI, API, or web portals, reducing manual work and errors in the order-to-cash flow. By connecting seamlessly with ERP, WMS, and eCommerce systems, Hyperfox helps companies process more orders with fewer resources.In most mid-sized manufacturing and distribution companies, order processing is still highly manual. Customer service teams spend hours re-typing orders from emails, PDFs, or Excel files into ERP systems. Errors are frequent, communication with customers is fragmented, and scaling operations becomes difficult without adding staff. As labour shortages grow and order volumes rise, these inefficiencies directly impact margins and customer satisfaction.Hyperfox replaces repetitive back-office tasks with intelligent automation. Its platform combines generative AI and business logic to:- Capture structured and unstructured orders from any source (email, EDI, API, portal).- Validate them against contracts, prices, stock, credit limits, and approval flows.- Streamline the output by pushing validated orders automatically to ERP or WMS systems.The result: faster order cycles, fewer errors, and a more proactive customer service team.TechnologyAt the core of Hyperfox is its proprietary agentic AI engine, trained on real-world order data to understand and extract information from complex, unstructured documents. The platform integrates with major ERP systems like Odoo, Microsoft Business Central, SAP, and Exact Online.Hyperfox is active in Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany, & UK with customers in food distribution, manufacturing, and logistics. Companies such as Joma Sport Belgium and Manna Foods use Hyperfox to process thousands of orders monthly with significantly less manual effort. The company recently secured a €300K VLAIO innovation grant to develop its proprietary AI order agentic system and expand its presence in the EU region.The addressable market for AI-driven order automation is growing rapidly, fuelled by labour shortages, digitalisation of B2B commerce, and increasing ERP connectivity. Hyperfox positions itself at the intersection of AI, process automation, and supply chain digitalisation.Hyperfox’s mission is simple: keep humans in flow. By eliminating repetitive administrative work, companies can refocus their people on value-adding tasks: customer relationships, sales, and innovation. The long-term vision is to build an autonomous, collaborative network where AI agents across suppliers, customers, and logistics partners exchange structured intents instead of documents: a new era of frictionless B2B trade.

column5: Practicality and technology to keep your health up to date
column6: Health4All is not a traditional startup but a significant national research and development project operating within Portugal's health sector. Commencing in November 2020 with a projected duration until June 2023, the initiative functions as a multidisciplinary consortium. This consortium brings together 11 companies and 13 research and development (R&D) organizations. Leadership is provided by Health Cluster Portugal and Siemens Healthineers, with the primary beneficiary being the FCT – Foundation for the Science and Technology. The project's core mission is to foster a comprehensive ecosystem in Portugal dedicated to the research, development, production, and commercialization of Smart Health medical technologies. This initiative received substantial financial backing through the COMPETE 2020 program, under the System of Support for Scientific and Technological Research. The total eligible cost amounted to approximately €6.34 million, with the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) contributing around €4.27 million. Health4All's research is centered on preventing and treating non-communicable diseases to reduce premature mortality from conditions like cancer, as well as cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and neurodegenerative diseases. column6: Africa Improved Foods (AIF) is a social enterprise established in 2016 to combat malnutrition and improve food security in Africa. These products are sold in retail markets, making nutritious options affordable and accessible to a broader consumer base. This commercial expansion is a key part of the company's strategy for financial sustainability and continental growth into markets like Ethiopia, Ghana, and Nigeria. The company works with over 90,000 smallholder farmers across Rwanda and the region, providing training and support to improve crop quality and reduce post-harvest losses, particularly from aflatoxin contamination. This approach has created a reliable supply chain for AIF while boosting farmer incomes and improving the local maize market. column5: Stone-milled craft flours from regenerative, identity-preserved grains
column6: Cairnspring Mills is a regional flour mill established in 2016 in the Skagit Valley of Washington state, specializing in stone-milling fresh flour from identity-preserved grains. The company was co-founded by CEO Kevin Morse, a group of local farmers, bakers, and economic development leaders. Morse's background as a farmer, conservationist, and his Italian-American heritage inspired the mission to rebuild local food systems and create a business that brings value back to the community and farmers. The business was founded to address several challenges, including the financial viability of local farmers pressured by the commodity system, the preservation of the Skagit Valley's agricultural heritage, and shortening the supply chain between farmers and customers for bulk crops like wheat. The company operates on a fully traceable, regenerative model, contracting directly with Pacific Northwest growers who use practices that promote soil health. Cairnspring Mills pays its growers approximately 30% more than commodity prices in exchange for high-quality grains grown to the company's specifications. The milling process utilizes traditional stone grinding, which retains more of the whole grain, including the nutrient-rich germ and bran, resulting in a product with superior flavor and nutritional value compared to industrially processed flour. Cairnspring Mills serves a customer base that includes prominent artisan bakeries, restaurants, retailers, and home bakers who value the product's quality, flavor, and sustainable origins. Its client list includes numerous James Beard Award-winning chefs and renowned bakeries. The company's business model involves both B2B and B2C sales channels. Products are sold through wholesale distributors like the Puget Sound Food Hub, directly to bakeries, online, and in retail locations including Whole Foods and local grocers in Washington and Oregon. In 2024, the mill produced 6.8 million pounds of flour and generated $6.4 million in revenue. column6: SAF One is a development platform launched in 2023 to deliver sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) solutions to the global aviation sector. The company was co-founded by Novus Aviation Capital, an aircraft leasing and financing platform, and Sencirc Holdings Ltd, an investment firm focused on the circular economy. The founders include Mounir Kuzbari, Co-CEO of Novus Aviation Capital, and Deepak Munganahalli, founder of Sencirc. Kuzbari brings extensive experience in aviation finance and previous investment in renewable energy, while Munganahalli contributes expertise in the energy sector and waste-to-value project development. The company's business model is centered on developing, owning, and operating SAF production infrastructure to support the aviation industry's net-zero carbon emission goals. SAF One is technology-agnostic, meaning it does not limit itself to a single production method. It has formed strategic partnerships to advance its projects, selecting Honeywell UOP's Ecofining™ process technology to convert waste oils, fats, and greases into SAF and appointing Tata Projects as its engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) lead. The company pursues a decentralized production strategy, aiming to build smaller, localized plants near airline partners to optimize logistics and utilize local feedstock. To secure its supply chain, SAF One acquired Green Biotrade, a UAE-based feedstock and biofuels trading company, enhancing its ability to source and manage the biomass necessary for production. The company's clients are primarily in the aviation industry, including airlines, airports, and other stakeholders. In January 2026, SAFFA Fund I, LP, an investment fund backed by major aviation players like Airbus, Air France-KLM, and Qantas, invested up to $30 million in a SAF One project in the Middle East, which is expected to break ground in 2026 and begin production by late 2028. column5: Laptop-sized personal electric vehicle for urban mobility
column6: Cocoa Motors, Inc. is a Japanese company founded in 2013 by Kuniako Saito that designs, manufactures, and sells a portable electric vehicle called the WALKCAR. The idea for the 'car in a bag' came to Saito during his master's studies in electric car motor control systems, driven by the desire to have transportation that could be carried. After a prototype was introduced in 2015, the company began worldwide sales in 2020 following five years of development. The WALKCAR is a laptop-sized, lightweight personal mobility device, weighing approximately 2.9 kg (6.4 lbs), making it portable enough to be carried in a backpack. Its body is constructed from carbon fiber and aircraft-grade aluminum. The vehicle is operated hands-free, with users controlling acceleration, deceleration, and turning by shifting their weight on four pressure-sensitive sensors embedded in the platform. Stepping off the device brings it to an automatic stop. The WALKCAR features four-wheel independent suspension to absorb vibrations and navigate uneven surfaces. The motors are integrated into the wheels to maximize space and power. The company offers different models, including the WALKCAR 2 and WALKCAR 2 Pro. The standard model reaches a top speed of 10 km/h (6.2 mph) with a range of about 7 km (4.3 miles), while the Pro version can achieve 15-16 km/h (9.3-10 mph) with a slightly shorter range. The battery requires about 60 to 90 minutes to fully charge. The business model is centered on direct-to-consumer sales of the WALKCAR and its accessories, such as tires and chargers, through its official website. The product is aimed at city dwellers, offering a solution for last-mile transportation and enhancing mobility in urban environments. column5: Nuclear fusion technology for carbon-neutral baseload power
column6: Pranos Fusion Private Limited is a Bengaluru-based startup founded in May 2024 by Roshan George and Shaurya Kaushal, positioning itself at the forefront of India's push into clean energy. The company's name blends the Sanskrit word 'prana' (life force) with 'cosmos'. The founders, friends for nine years before launching the company, were inspired by a 2021 breakthrough at the Joint European Torus (JET) facility, which sustained a fusion reaction for five seconds. This event shifted their perspective from fusion being a purely scientific puzzle to an engineering challenge ripe for commercialization. Shaurya Kaushal has a Ph.D. in computational fluid dynamics and a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering, while Roshan George is a computer science engineer who previously worked in the corporate renewable energy sector. Pranos Fusion is developing a novel approach to nuclear fusion, the same process that powers the sun, by focusing on magnetic confinement fusion (MCF) with a distinct methodology. The company is working on a compact, spherical tokamak architecture. Its strategy diverges from conventional designs, aiming for quicker iterations at a smaller scale and with lower capital expenditure. This approach is structured in a three-stage plan: first, design and simulation; second, the construction of a compact, lab-scale magnetic confinement device to test and optimize plasma control; and third, scaling up to a commercial fusion reactor. A core component of their strategy is 'Jenga,' a digital twin platform that integrates physics with engineering systems to shorten the cycle between simulation, building, and testing. By leveraging advanced plasma software and machine learning algorithms, Pranos aims to reduce design and simulation time from months down to approximately ten days. The startup's primary business model is the eventual sale of its fusion technology. The ultimate goal is to provide a clean, reliable baseload power source to the grid, which is a significant advantage over intermittent renewables like solar and wind. The technology promises to produce energy without greenhouse gases or long-lived radioactive waste, using deuterium (found in seawater) and tritium as fuel. The company has been incubated at the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR) in Bengaluru and has a core team of six members and six advisors. Pranos secured seed funding of approximately $417K in a round on May 14, 2025, from investors including the Startup India Seed Fund (SISF) and Rahul Seth of Industrial47, a deep-tech fund. column5: It uses the Ethereum blockchain and biometric technology to develop a financial application
column6: Humaniq operates as a financial ecosystem built upon blockchain technology, aiming to integrate the world's unbanked population into the global economy. The company was established in London, United Kingdom, in 2016 by Alex Fork. Fork, an author and expert in cryptocurrencies, was inspired to create a solution for financial inclusion after discussions with Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin. The founding team also includes Dmitry Kaminskiy and Anton Mozgovoy. A significant milestone for the company was its Initial Coin Offering (ICO) in April 2017, which successfully raised $5.1 million from 11,600 participants. This followed a pre-ICO in December 2016 that raised $110,000. The core of Humaniq's business is a mobile application available for both iOS and Android operating systems. The platform is designed to provide financial services to individuals without access to traditional banking, a demographic estimated to be over two billion people globally. The business model is centered on its mobile platform, which leverages the Ethereum blockchain to ensure secure and transparent transactions. Revenue is generated through small fees from third-party FinTech startups and financial organizations that utilize the Humaniq API to offer services like P2P lending, insurance, and loans. The company also plans to earn from a percentage of shares in startups that grow within its incubator and accelerator program. Humaniq's primary service is its mobile app, which provides users with a secure digital identity and a wallet for its native cryptocurrency, HMQ. A key feature is its use of biometric authentication, employing face and voice recognition to create and access accounts, thus removing the need for traditional forms of identification like passports or signatures. This is particularly beneficial for users in emerging economies who may lack formal documentation. The app is designed with a simple, image-focused user interface to be accessible for individuals with low literacy levels and to function on low-end smartphones. Transactions on the platform, facilitated by the HMQ token, are zero-fee. The ecosystem also allows third-party developers to build and offer services through an open API, fostering a wider range of financial products. By 2018, the app had surpassed 400,000 users across 16 African countries. column6: In een wereld waarin data de sleutel is tot duurzame ontwikkeling, levert Dutch Sensor Systems (DSS) de technologie om geluid – een vaak onderschatte maar essentiële omgevingsfactor – meetbaar, zichtbaar en betekenisvol te maken. Met onze geavanceerde IoT-geluidssensoren, werkend op energiezuinige LoRaWAN-netwerken, stellen we overheden, stedenbouwkundigen, industrieën en wetenschappers in staat om op een betrouwbare en schaalbare manier geluidsdata te verzamelen, analyseren en toepassen.Onze missie – Serving the world with sensible insights – sluit naadloos aan op meerdere Sustainable Development Goals (SDG’s) van de Verenigde Naties:	•	SDG 3 – Goede gezondheid en welzijn: Langdurige blootstelling aan geluidsoverlast is schadelijk voor zowel de fysieke als mentale gezondheid. DSS helpt bij het identificeren en verminderen van geluidsbelasting in stedelijke en industriële omgevingen, met als doel gezondere leefomstandigheden voor iedereen.	•	SDG 9 – Industrie, innovatie en infrastructuur: Onze technologie vertegenwoordigt het snijvlak van slimme infrastructuur en digitale innovatie. Door geluid te integreren in smart city-oplossingen dragen wij bij aan slimmere, efficiëntere en duurzamere stedelijke ontwikkeling.	•	SDG 11 – Duurzame steden en gemeenschappen: DSS bevordert leefbare steden door gemeenten en projectontwikkelaars inzicht te geven in geluidsprofielen van wijken, evenementen en verkeersstromen. Dit stelt hen in staat om leefomgevingen te ontwerpen waarin rust, veiligheid en comfort centraal staan.	•	SDG 13 – Klimaatactie: Geluidssensoren zijn vaak onderdeel van bredere omgevingsmonitoring en kunnen gebruikt worden in combinatie met klimaatdata, bijvoorbeeld om effecten van vergroening of verkeersmaatregelen in kaart te brengen.Wat DSS uniek maakt, is de combinatie van technologische betrouwbaarheid, lage energiebehoefte en directe praktische toepasbaarheid. Onze plug-and-play sensoren zijn snel inzetbaar, vergen nauwelijks onderhoud, en leveren direct data op die via open standaarden beschikbaar is voor integratie in bestaande dashboards en systemen.Met een internationale blik en partnerschappen in onder andere Europa en Noord-Amerika, zijn we actief bezig met de uitbreiding van een wereldwijd distributienetwerk. The company's business model targets the short-haul transportation and helicopter markets, with plans to price its flight services comparably to high-speed rail tickets. column6: Qi Health is a digital telehealth company founded in 2022 by CEO Camilla Sievers and CTO Nam Le. The company provides a platform that connects patients with certified TCM practitioners for virtual consultations. Based on these consultations, practitioners create personalized, prescription-strength herbal medicine formulations that are delivered directly to the patient's home. Qi Health primarily targets female health-related conditions such as period pain, PMS, PCOS, endometriosis, hormonal imbalances, infertility, and menopause. The business model is centered on providing patients with direct online access to doctors and customized herbal remedies, enabling a holistic approach to long-term healing. It emphasizes a holistic journey to health by aligning physical, mental, and emotional well-being with natural cycles. The company reports high success rates, with over 90% of patients finding full relief within three to six months. column5: Cloud platform for biomedical data and AI-driven medicine
column6: ATGENOMIX is a data and machine learning company that provides a cloud-native biomedical informatics platform for precision medicine. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in Taipei, Taiwan, the company was co-founded by Chang Ming Tai and CEO Allen Chang. Allen Chang's background includes serving as a senior product manager and R&D manager at Trend Micro, where he led teams in developing machine learning technologies for petabyte-scale data, experience that directly informs Atgenomix's focus on managing complex biomedical data. The company's core product is the Atgenomix SeqsLab platform, a Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) that enables clinical laboratories and research institutions to manage and analyze large-scale biomedical data. The platform is designed to operationalize biomedical data, analytics, and machine learning workflows, handling the complex infrastructure required for genomic data processing so researchers can focus on analysis and interpretation. SeqsLab integrates cloud services and software to support data integration, tool engineering, analysis automation, and regulatory compliance. It utilizes industry standards like GA4GH (Global Alliance for Genomics & Health) and FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) to ensure data is findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable. The business model centers on providing this integrated platform to clients such as Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) testing providers, medical centers, and bioinformatics developers. These clients use SeqsLab for a range of applications including precision oncology, rare disease diagnosis, reproductive medicine, and clinical whole exome analysis. The platform accelerates research by automating and speeding up workflows; for example, it can process in hours what might take a week with conventional methods. Atgenomix partners with major cloud providers like Microsoft Azure and is a Google Health trusted partner. The company has raised $1.66M in funding from investors including Darwin Venture Management and TransLink Capital. column5: Affordable, semi-autonomous electric utility vehicles for agriculture
column6: Boson Motors manufactures intelligent, affordable electric utility vehicles and stationary energy storage units, primarily targeting the agricultural sector. The company was founded in 2017 in Fremont, California, by Arun Seelam and Suri Bhupatiraju, who were software engineers at Google. Seelam, the current CEO, comes from a family with a background in the commercial trucking business, while Bhupatiraju serves as COO. They envisioned creating easily programmable, Android-powered electric vehicles to address the gap between advancing automotive hardware and lagging software. The company's core products are light-duty electric utility trucks, like the LX40 model, designed to automate agricultural tasks such as crop spraying, inspection, and materials transport. Key features of their vehicles include semi-autonomous capabilities like "Follow Me" shadowing and pre-programmable path following, operated through a simple Android interface. These vehicles utilize custom-built, safe, and long-lasting lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries, which the company develops in-house along with the powertrain and software. This vertical integration allows for meticulous quality control. The vehicles are designed for rugged, off-road terrain and offer a payload capacity of up to 2,000 lbs, a significant increase over standard utility vehicles. Boson Motors operates on a B2B model, aiming to make clean energy and autonomous mobility accessible to farmers, ranchers, and other commercial clients who have been traditionally priced out of such technology. The company began by developing a powertrain, battery, and software solution to retrofit existing vehicle chassis before moving towards producing a full-stack vehicle. While headquartered in California and focused on the U.S. market, the company established manufacturing operations in India to leverage lower operational costs for testing and validation. Boson Motors participated in the Techstars Farm to Fork Accelerator in 2020, which helped refine the vehicle's design to address key pain points in agriculture, such as labor shortages. The company has received an undisclosed amount of seed funding from investors including Techstars, FalconX, and Zoho Corporation. Revenue is generated through both individual product sales and a subscription service, which offers a 10% discount and ensures regular deliveries for customer retention.The firm was established by Igor Solovyov, whose personal journey as a pet parent directly shaped the company's mission. Faced with persistent tear-stain issues with his Maltipoo, Solovyov experimented with numerous high-end kibbles to no avail. The recipes are formulated with a high meat content, typically 80% human-grade fresh meat, offal, and bones, supplemented with 20% fruits and vegetables. The product line is explicitly free from grains, gluten, soy, and artificial additives, positioning it for dogs with allergies or sensitive stomachs. The company offers various protein menus, including beef, lamb, and more novel sources like horse and insect, catering to diverse dietary needs and preferences. column6: Electra Bicycle Company, a subsidiary of Trek Bicycle Company, operates within the lifestyle and leisure segment of the cycling industry. Founded in 1993 in Leucadia, California, by Swiss national Benno Bänziger and German transplant Jeano Erforth, the company was established to reintroduce the concept of recreational and transportational cycling to a market dominated by sport-focused bikes. Bänziger, with a background in graphic design and experience working for brands like K2 and Adidas, identified a gap in the market for bicycles designed for fun and everyday use. The founders pooled $30,000 in personal savings to launch the company, initially facing skepticism from dealers before gaining traction. The company's business model centers on the design and sale of cruiser, comfort, and hybrid bicycles, as well as a line of electric bikes and related accessories, apparel, and parts. Manufacturing was initially contracted to a Taiwanese firm to manage production costs. Electra distributes its products primarily through a network of independently owned bicycle shops across North America and has expanded its reach globally with subsidiaries and distributors in Europe, Asia, and other regions. A significant milestone occurred in January 2014 when Trek Bicycle Corporation acquired Electra, providing substantial resources for growth in financial, supply chain, and distribution areas while allowing the brand to maintain its product and marketing autonomy. A cornerstone of Electra's product line is its patented Flat Foot Technology®, introduced in 2003 with the Townie model. This design alters the traditional bicycle geometry by moving the pedals forward and the seat back, which allows a rider to place their feet flat on the ground while seated, enhancing comfort and control. This feature proved instrumental in appealing to casual cyclists and those new or returning to biking. In 2002, the company diversified with the "Stream Ride" series, which drew inspiration from Southern California's hot rod culture, featuring exaggerated frames and elaborate paint jobs. The company entered the e-bike market in 2013 with the Townie Go!, which integrated a pedal-assist motor and has since expanded its electric offerings. column6: Mentessa GmbH is a German software company that has developed an AI-powered platform for skill-based employee connection, learning, and collaboration. column5: Pay-as-you-go solar home systems for Africa
column6: RDG Africa, founded by Rune Gunnar Dige in 2018, is a provider of clean energy solutions to underserved communities in Southern and Central Africa. The company operates in Zambia and the Democratic Republic of Congo, with a vision to facilitate economic and social development through access to clean energy and financial inclusion. The company's business model is centered around a pay-as-you-go (PAYG) system, which makes essential renewable energy products affordable for off-grid households and small businesses. This model allows customers to make payments over an extended period, eliminating the significant upfront cost barrier. Products offered include solar home systems, solar water pumps, refrigerators, and smartphones. The sales process involves a network of agents who demonstrate the products to communities, supported by service centers in provincial towns. Once a customer is approved for a loan and makes a small deposit, they receive the product and make subsequent payments to receive power keycodes that activate their systems. Upon completion of the loan, the system is permanently unlocked for unlimited use. RDG Africa has secured funding from various partners to expand its operations. In August 2025, Inside Capital Partners made a strategic investment to help the company broaden its product range and regional footprint. In October 2024, Acumen's Hardest-to-Reach initiative invested $1.25 million to fund inventory purchases of solar home systems, aiming to provide energy access to 66,000 people and supply solar generators to 180 small businesses in Zambia. This investment was structured as an Impact Indexed Loan, where the interest rate decreases as impact milestones are met. column5: Transparently produced timeless apparel using organic materials
column6: ISTO, an acronym for Independent, Superb, Transparent, Organic, is a Portuguese direct-to-consumer fashion label focused on creating timeless apparel. The company was founded in Lisbon in July 2017 by Pedro Palha, Pedro Gaspar, and Martim Manoel, who launched the brand from a living room with the goal of being independent of fashion industry trends and investor constraints. Palha's background includes experience in finance and working at a tech incubator in Berlin before returning to Portugal to explore the textile industry. The business operates on a direct-to-consumer model through its e-commerce website and physical stores in Lisbon, with plans for international expansion, including a store in London. ISTO’s core business philosophy revolves around what it calls "radical transparency"; it openly shares the cost breakdown of each item, including materials, labor, and logistics. The brand avoids seasonal collections, instead offering a single, permanent collection of wardrobe staples that it continuously refines. This "slow fashion" approach emphasizes quality over quantity, producing long-lasting items from organic and natural materials. All production is based in Portugal, utilizing factories held to high standards of social responsibility. The company and its suppliers are GOTS (Global Organic Textile Standard) certified, ensuring the use of organic materials and sustainable practices. In July 2025, ISTO announced a strategic partnership with the investment firm Altaz Capital to support its international growth, enhance operations, and strengthen its financial foundations without compromising its core values. column5: Fungi-based biopesticides to protect pollinators
column6: Quorum Earth is a biotechnology company founded in 2023 that develops biological pest control agents to combat invasive insects and protect pollinators like bees. The company is headquartered in Brooklyn, New York. The company was co-founded by Chris Kantrowitz, a serial founder in gaming, software, and biotech, and Dr. Nicholas Naeger, an entomologist with over two decades of experience dedicated to honeybee preservation. Their advisory team includes prominent mycologist Paul Stamets and other experts in pesticide regulation and manufacturing. Quorum Earth's core technology centers on the fungus *Metarhizium*, which is transformed into a biopesticide. The company has developed a platform that naturally modifies *Metarhizium* to target specific pests. These modifications are minimal, allowing the altered fungi to be considered genetically identical to the original by regulators, which is expected to facilitate a faster and more cost-effective approval process. The initial focus is on combating the varroa mite, a significant threat to honeybee populations worldwide and a leading cause of colony collapse. While *Metarhizium* is highly effective and non-toxic to bees, its commercialization has been challenging because it struggles outside its natural habitat, a problem Quorum's platform aims to solve. The company operates in the AgTech and agricultural chemicals industries. It secured seed funding in 2023 and has received investments from firms including Climate Capital, IndieBio, Deep Future, LOI Venture, and SOSV. Quorum Earth intends to begin international sales of its varroa mite product in 2025, with a broader mission to address other invasive insect populations without causing environmental harm. column6: Founded in 2021, Testasy began as a Polish-Swiss health care startup headquartered in Zurich, with an additional base in Warsaw. The company, officially registered as GobiX GmbH, was established by Dr. Michel Bielecki. Initially, Testasy focused on addressing challenges presented by the COVID-19 pandemic by developing a platform for at-home lab testing. The service aimed to make lab results more accessible and understandable for individuals. The platform's core offering was a system for telemedically supervised COVID-19 diagnostics. This involved features like video consultation appointments, patient appointment management, and the secure delivery of encrypted PDF results to comply with medical record standards. A key component of their technology was a semi-automated, computer vision-assisted model that could recognize positive or negative test results, which was then verified by a doctor. This process significantly reduced the time required for issuing certificates, streamlining a 7-minute task down to 10 seconds. The business model targeted the need for rapid and reliable testing, integrating with laboratory partners and the Swiss Health Service (BAG) to issue official certificates. Sensing a shift in market dynamics and technological advancements, the company has since pivoted from its original focus. Testasy is no longer active in its initial capacity and has rebranded its efforts toward Testasy AI, which is also referred to as illumicell AI. This new venture is aimed at the fertility care market. The reconstituted team behind Testasy AI includes a medical doctor and former NATO Chief Medical Officer, a past McKinsey consultant handling strategy, a rocket scientist whose technology is central to the new product, and an AI specialist with extensive experience in creating medical algorithms. The company's seed funding round occurred in December 2021, and its evolution into the AI-driven fertility space reflects a strategic response to capture new opportunities. column6: Reekom provides industrial-scale re-commerce and reverse logistics solutions, enabling brands to revalorize returned and non-marketable products. Founded in 2022 by Guillaume Perret du Cray, an engineer with 15 years of experience in supply chain and logistics at companies like Unilever and Veepee, Reekom was established to address an operational gap in managing product returns. Hélène Feugier, with a background in industry and impact from Schneider Electric and Mokki, joined as COO in 2023. The company operates a business-to-business model, serving brands in the ready-to-wear, footwear, leather goods, furniture, and home decoration sectors. Its client roster includes notable names such as Veepee, BonneGueule, Paradigme, and Camif. Reekom's business model is service-based; it does not purchase products from its clients but instead charges a per-piece, per-operation fee for its services, allowing brands to retain ownership of their stock. This approach ensures a direct and significant return on investment for the brands. The company's comprehensive service includes receiving, quality control, cleaning, disinfection using ozone and UV technology, ironing, minor repairs, professional photography, and preparing items for resale. In June 2025, Reekom announced a €4.5 million fundraising round to open a 3,500 m² mechanized reconditioning center in La Courneuve, Seine-Saint-Denis. column6: Talet-e Srl is a mobility technology company focused on accelerating the transition to sustainable urban transport. Founded in 2021 by Marco Dau, Sertac Yeltekin, Paolo Gagliardo, Claudio Cesario, Michelangelo Liguori, Pierluigi Vinciguerra, Antonello Corrado, and Federico Giannandrea, the Messina-based firm specializes in the electric conversion of existing gasoline-powered scooters. The idea originated with Michele Dau during the 2020 lockdown, who identified a need for an economical and adaptable solution to facilitate the switch to electric two-wheelers. The company's core offering is the "Talet-e POWER Kit," a proprietary system for retrofitting internal combustion engine scooters into electric vehicles. This service is designed for owners of popular scooter models, such as the Honda SH, Piaggio Liberty, and Vespa GTS, allowing them to retain their vehicle while eliminating emissions. The process involves removing the original engine, transmission, fuel tank, and exhaust system and installing an electric motor, batteries, and control electronics. Talet-e manages the entire process, including the complex administrative steps of vehicle re-homologation and updating the registration certificate to reflect the electric conversion. The components removed are sent to specialized companies for material recycling, aligning with circular economy principles. Talet-e's business model targets both individual scooter owners and corporate fleets. Revenue is generated from the sale and installation of these conversion kits, which cost approximately €2,500, inclusive of installation and administrative handling. The firm also partners with a network of authorized mechanical workshops, which act as installation and service centers. These partners can install kits for Talet-e customers or sell the conversions directly. To support its growth, Talet-e secured €2.65 million in a seed round in May/June 2024, combining debt financing from Banca Progetto and UniCredit with equity from the family office RA.MO.CAR srl and other private investors. The conversion kit provides performance comparable to the original vehicle while offering the benefits of electric mobility, such as access to restricted traffic zones (ZTL) and reduced running costs. The system includes batteries providing up to 70-110 km of range, which can be recharged in about four hours from a standard household outlet. An accompanying mobile application allows users to monitor battery status and locate nearby charging stations. The company has received official homologation for its conversion platforms for key scooter models, enabling its market entry. Talet-e plans to open its first flagship store in Rome to spearhead its distribution phase. In addition to selling directly to businesses, BUOONOfarm also offers home-grow kits containing the coffee-based substrate for consumers to cultivate their own mushrooms. column6: Brightmind.ai is a neurotechnology company founded in Vienna, Austria, in 2022 by Tamara Gerbert and Florian Lerchbammer-Kreith. The stated goal for its initial migraine application is to reduce the number of migraine attacks by over 50%. The company's roadmap includes conducting large-scale clinical trials, obtaining regulatory approvals from bodies like the FDA, and establishing reimbursement pathways with insurers to ensure accessibility. column5: Patented power quality solutions reducing electricity waste
column6: XCT Energy is an energy technology company that provides power quality solutions designed to reduce electricity waste and improve operational efficiency for industrial and digital infrastructure clients. The firm was co-founded by Chad Freese, who serves as CEO, and Benoit Allehuat, the Chief Capital Officer. The leadership team also includes Pharoah Green as CFO and Connor Cash as CCO. Another entity, XCarbon Technologies, established in 2021 and also referred to as XCT, acts as the exclusive global distributor for the core technology. The company's core offering is the deployment and management of the patented XECO technology platform. XCT Energy is the exclusive commercial and installation arm for XECO systems, which consist of hardware and software that dynamically tune electrical networks. The technology works by balancing current across phases, reducing harmonics, and stabilizing voltage in real-time to solve power quality issues. This process mitigates problems like harmonic distortion, poor power factor, and I²R (resistive) losses, which are common in facilities with heavy electrical loads from motors, VFDs, servers, and chillers. By resolving these inefficiencies, the system lowers overall energy consumption (kWh), reduces peak demand, and can bring facilities into compliance with standards like IEEE 519. XCT Energy serves high-demand environments such as data centers, manufacturing plants, cold storage, food and beverage processing, and water treatment facilities. Its business model focuses on engineering and deploying customized solutions tailored to each site's specific electrical profile. The process begins with a site assessment to identify savings potential, followed by system design, installation, and commissioning. Installation is designed to be non-disruptive, typically occurring in parallel with existing electrical systems without requiring operational shutdowns. The company provides verifiable results by deploying revenue-grade metering to measure reductions in energy usage.
