column5: Affordable molecular allergy testing for accessible diagnosis and personalized health management
column6: Self.co is a Lithuanian digital health platform transforming allergy and food intolerance diagnosis through proprietary molecular-level testing combined with AI-driven personalized care. Founded in 2015 by allergy specialist Gintautas Gylys and his son Tautvydas Gylys, the company emerged from a clinical need: while nearly 40% of the global population experiences allergy-like symptoms, most suffer from misdiagnosis or lack access to accurate testing due to high costs and long wait times. Self.co's solution combines advanced microarray technology—which the company designs and manufactures in-house—with digital-first healthcare delivery. The platform screens for up to 98 common allergens (IgE testing) and 220 possible food intolerances (IgG testing) from a single 20-microliter blood sample collected at home. With over 137,000 medical tests performed and 12 years of clinical expertise backing its methodology, Self.co has reduced diagnostic costs by up to 75% compared to traditional laboratory testing, pricing tests between €69 and €99.Self.co operates in both B2B and B2C segments, serving individual consumers seeking at-home diagnostics while simultaneously developing partnerships with healthcare providers, insurers, and diagnostic networks across Europe. The company's business model combines direct-to-consumer test sales with subscription-based access to its digital health platform, where users receive personalized recommendations and long-term management tools. Revenue is generated through test purchases and potential commission-based partnerships with integrated healthcare systems. The company's proprietary technology and data from thousands of patient cases provide a clinical foundation that competitors relying on generic tests cannot match, creating defensible differentiation in a crowded diagnostics market.Self.co's expansion into Germany, Austria, Ireland, and the UK—supported by its recent €2.56 million Series A funding led by Iron Wolf Capital and backed by Innovation Agency Lithuania grants—positions the company to become a  leading European digital platform for allergy management by 2030. The platform's next evolution includes smart symptom questionnaires to help users pinpoint their conditions, expanded intolerance panels (including lactose and histamine sensitivity), proprietary dry-blood collection devices, and deeper integration with existing healthcare systems and pharmacy networks. column5: Student-led solar racing team for sustainable mobility
column6: aCentauri Solar Racing is a student-led team from ETH Zürich that designs, manufactures, and races solar-powered vehicles. Founded in the spring of 2022 by six students, the project has since expanded to over 100 members. The team's primary mission is to compete in the Bridgestone World Solar Challenge, a 3,000 km race across the Australian outback, to promote sustainable technology in mobility.The team operates as a non-profit association and relies on external sponsors and crowdfunding to finance the development and construction of their solar cars. column5: Producer of evidence-based knee-rehab skates, with smart functionalities
column6: MAXM Skate provides a rehabilitation solution for patients after knee surgery, combining a patented skate device with a digital application to improve recovery outcomes. The company was founded over a decade ago by Dr. Matthew Liptak, a South Australian orthopaedic surgeon who identified a need for a more effective post-surgery rehabilitation tool. The idea was inspired in 2011 when Dr. Liptak observed a patient in a regional town using a skateboard for post-operative exercises, resulting in an accelerated recovery. The core product is a skate-like device worn on the injured leg, featuring integrated Bluetooth sensors that track the knee's range of motion. This data is transmitted to a mobile app, allowing both patients and clinicians to monitor progress in real-time. The system is designed to facilitate at-home rehabilitation, increase patient motivation through a gamified experience, and improve compliance with exercise programs. The business model involves selling the device and its associated digital program to hospitals, rehabilitation clinics, and through a global distribution network. The company's clients are patients recovering from knee procedures like total knee replacements. Development milestones include an initial prototype in 2012, followed by R&D assistance from the Medical Device Partnering Program (MDPP) starting in 2013 to create the sensor technology. Flinders University's Medical Device Research Institute (MDRI) later helped develop more advanced sensors. Clinical trials conducted in partnership with Flinders University demonstrated that patients using MAXM Skate achieve better range-of-motion more quickly, have shorter hospital stays, and report significantly better mental health outcomes compared to standard care. The solution has been shown to save healthcare systems a considerable amount per patient. MAXM Skate has secured regulatory approvals including TGA in Australia, FDA in the US, and the CE mark in Europe, and is now sold in numerous countries across several continents. In 2025, the company was named a finalist in the MedTech Innovator APAC Accelerator Program. column5: The fair-fee food delivery platform empowering local restaurants, rewarding drivers, and giving customers real value
column6: Smusho is a next-generation food delivery platform designed to make food delivery fair, affordable, and community-driven. Built in Melbourne and proudly supporting local business ecosystems, Smusho challenges the high-commission, high-cost model used by major delivery apps. Our mission is to empower local restaurants, reward delivery drivers fairly, and give customers transparent, low-cost access to great food.Unlike traditional platforms that charge restaurants up to 30% commission, Smusho operates on a simple flat-fee structure — restaurants pay only $3.50 per order, and customers just $1.50, creating a total delivery cost of $5.00. This model ensures everyone wins: restaurants keep more profit, customers enjoy cheaper meals, and drivers are paid fairly with a $7.50 guaranteed payout per delivery (funded 70% by restaurants and 30% by customers).Smusho is more than just delivery — it’s a community platform that helps restaurants grow sustainably and customers engage with local food culture. Through our DIY Meal Kit feature, customers can order fresh, pre-prepared ingredients from their favourite restaurants and cook them at home. This unique offering encourages healthier eating, reduces waste, and helps restaurants expand their reach beyond traditional delivery orders.Another key innovation is Smusho’s Weekly Meal Scheduling, allowing busy individuals, families, and professionals to pre-plan their meals with automatic deliveries from trusted local eateries. This builds routine revenue for restaurants and repeat engagement from customers.Smusho’s growth engine is its built-in Referral Program, rewarding users, restaurants, and drivers with $1 credits for every successful delivery they help generate. This drives organic expansion without expensive marketing campaigns and strengthens community participation.The platform’s core is built using modern no-code and AI-enhanced infrastructure, ensuring agility, scalability, and seamless multilingual user experience — key for serving Australia’s diverse, multicultural communities. The app is optimised for accessibility in English, Chinese, Hindi, Arabic, and Vietnamese, covering 85% of Australia’s primary non-English-speaking populations.Supported by partnerships with local councils, Smusho is currently preparing its soft launch in Melbourne with assistance from Gig Workers’ Hub and local “Buy Local” campaigns under the City of Melbourne’s economic development initiatives. column5: Locally-sourced potato crisps for the East African market
column6: Hollanda FairFoods, operating under the brand name Winnaz, is a Rwandan company specializing in the production of potato crisps. Founded in 2014 by Thijs Boer and later joined by Pascal Murasira, the company was born from Boer's MSc research in Development Economics in Rwanda. Boer, an agricultural economics graduate from Wageningen University, identified a gap in the market: despite being a major potato producer, Rwanda had minimal local processing and imported most of its snacks. Starting with modest investments from family and friends, and support from the Dutch embassy, the company began production in 2015, initially selling just 200 bags of crisps per week. The company's business model is vertically integrated, managing the potato value chain from seed to the final snack product. It sources high-quality potatoes directly from over 2,000 smallholder farmers in Rwanda's Northern region, known for its volcanic soils. A key part of its strategy involves creating a sustainable market and improving the livelihoods of these farmers. Hollanda FairFoods provides them with training, agronomic advice, access to micro-finance, and pays prices approximately 33% above the market average. This partnership enables farmers to increase their yield, quality, and income. Winnaz crisps are kettle-cooked and marketed as a premium, crunchy snack available in flavors like Salted, Paprika, Salt & Vinegar, and Pizza. The company differentiates itself by using sunflower oil and has introduced biodegradable packaging. Initially producing two tonnes per day, the factory upgraded its capacity five-fold in 2018. Winnaz is now a market leader in Rwanda, producing millions of bags annually and has expanded its distribution to Uganda, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Kenya, and Burundi. The brand targets the growing urban middle class and promotes its products at sporting and music events. column5: AI-native platform integrating biomedical data and knowledge graphs to accelerate hypothesis generation in drug discovery
column6: Kiin Bio is building KiinOS, an AI-native platform designed to accelerate drug discovery by enabling researchers to generate and test therapeutic hypotheses faster and more reliably. At its core, KiinOS integrates multi-modal biomedical data—including genomic, chemical, clinical, and literature-derived sources—through a knowledge graph architecture optimized for AI reasoning.The platform functions as a virtual scientist, equipped with curated biomedical context and optimized for real-time interaction. It leverages large language models (LLMs), domain-specific ontologies, and automated reasoning tools to support users in surfacing non-obvious relationships, predicting biological targets, and validating compound-disease interactions. The system is designed to reduce the time and cost of early-stage R&D by guiding scientists through complex biological questions with structured, explainable outputs.KiinOS is aimed at pharmaceutical companies, biotech startups, and academic labs that seek to enhance their in silico discovery capabilities. The platform can be used to explore novel drug mechanisms, identify repositioning opportunities, and prioritize assets for further experimental validation. Its knowledge engine continuously ingests public and proprietary data and harmonizes it into a machine-readable biomedical graph, enabling context-aware hypothesis generation and cross-domain discovery.The company was founded in 2024 by Filippo Abbondanza (CEO), Mark Davies (Chief Data & Scientific Officer), and Bogdan Urse (CTO), combining deep experience in computational biology, AI infrastructure, and pharmaceutical informatics. Their shared mission is to make drug discovery more intelligent, transparent, and data-driven.In 2025, Kiin Bio secured a 1.9€ million seed round to further develop its platform and expand collaborations with pharma and biotech partners. column5: End-to-end support for smallholder cacao farmers.
column6: Kennemer Foods International, Inc. (KFI) is a Philippine agribusiness company founded in 2010 by Simon Bakker that specializes in the growing, sourcing, and trading of high-quality cacao beans from smallholder farmers. Bakker, originally from the Netherlands and now based in the Philippines, serves as the CEO and was named the "Social Entrepreneur of the Year" by the Schwab Foundation in 2016. Before KFI, he was a founding investor and the Chief Financial Officer of Enderun Colleges. KFI was established in Davao, Philippines, to address the challenges faced by smallholder farmers, such as low productivity, lack of access to quality inputs, and limited market access. The company's business model is centered on providing an end-to-end solution for cacao growers. This is primarily executed through its Cacao Growership Program, which offers contract farmers high-yielding planting materials, technical training, farm inputs, and a guaranteed market for their produce. KFI signs 10-year contracts with farmers and commits to purchasing their entire food-grade production at prices linked to the global market, typically around 85% of the world market price. The program is designed to significantly increase farmer income, with simulations showing a potential fourfold increase in household income once cacao trees mature. To support this ecosystem, KFI established a network of "cacao doctors"—farmer entrepreneurs trained by KFI to coach other growers, consolidate beans, and provide support services. Initially started as a buying and post-harvest center, KFI adapted its model upon realizing the limitations of existing low-yield production. The company now has a long-standing strategic relationship with Mars, Inc., which is its largest customer and collaborates on research, technology, and best practices. To further support farmers, KFI established a subsidiary, Agronomika Finance Corporation, in 2016 to provide accessible financing for farm development. Loan proceeds are often delivered in-kind to ensure they are used for their intended purpose, with repayments collected through an automatic retention from sales to Kennemer. The company's operations span across the Philippines, with a network of over 20,000 smallholder farmers and more than 19,000 hectares under management. column5: AI-powered X-ray systems for intelligent ore sorting.
column6: Beijing Hollister Technology, established in 2010, is a national high-tech enterprise specializing in the development of X-ray intelligent sorting systems. The company's core team originates from the Department of Precision Instruments at Tsinghua University, bringing nearly two decades of research experience in X-ray technology and product development. The founder, Guo Jin, holds a master's degree from Tsinghua's precision instruments department and previously worked at GE Healthcare's CT division. This background in both geological and medical CT technologies inspired the company's direction. Initially, from 2010 to 2015, the firm focused on creating and selling core X-ray detector components for various sectors like security, industrial non-destructive testing, and medical fields.In 2015, the company pivoted to leverage its expertise in high-precision sensors and intelligent material recognition algorithms, leading to the independent development of an X-ray intelligent sorting machine for the mining industry. The product was launched commercially in 2017. The technology operates by using X-ray detectors to see the internal structure of ores and then employs AI algorithms to differentiate between valuable minerals and waste rock, which are then separated by a high-pressure air jet system. This dry sorting process eliminates the need for water and reduces the use of chemical agents common in traditional wet sorting methods, aligning with environmental sustainability goals. The system is designed to be robust, with waterproof, mud-proof, dust-proof, and explosion-proof capabilities to withstand harsh mining environments.The business model centers on providing these advanced sorting machines to the mining sector, serving a wide range of clients from large state-owned enterprises to industry leaders. Its customer base includes prominent names such as China Minmetals, Zijin Mining Group, and China National Coal Group. The company has successfully implemented its technology across various mineral types including non-ferrous metals, ferrous metals, non-metallic minerals, and coal. It has also expanded its market reach internationally, with equipment sold in Europe, Africa, the Americas, and Central Asia. column6: Next Mobiles is a French company specializing in the rental of new and refurbished smartphones and other tech devices to both individuals and businesses. The company's core offering is a subscription service that allows customers to rent new or reconditioned smartphones from brands like Apple and Samsung. This service includes a comprehensive benefits package, such as insurance covering breakage, theft, and oxidation, with a promise of device replacement within 24-48 hours. Next Mobiles operates in the circular economy by reconditioning used devices in-house in France. These refurbished phones undergo a 98-point inspection to ensure quality and are guaranteed for the entire rental period. This focus on refurbishing extends the life of the devices and presents a more sustainable and cost-effective option for consumers. The company serves both the B2C market and a B2B segment through 'Next Mobiles Pro', which provides tech equipment and fleet management services to over 700 businesses. The company operates coffee shops in several Colombian cities, including Bogotá and Cartagena, and has expanded internationally with locations in Mexico City and New Delhi, India. column6: Therm Solutions, Inc. is a carbon project developer focused on decarbonizing the global food supply chain. Founded in 2021 by CEO Fritz Troller and Vice President John Tinsley, the company develops and scales climate solutions by creating carbon credits that incentivize sustainable practices. The company's business model centers on generating revenue through the sale of high-integrity carbon credits. It targets super pollutants—highly potent greenhouse gases like refrigerants and methane—which are prevalent in the food industry. Therm operates in voluntary, compliance, and Scope 3 insetting markets, serving clients such as grocers, convenience stores, cold storage facilities, and farmers. Their two main products are Refrigerant Carbon Credits™ (RCCs) and Food Waste Diversion Credits. The RCCs promote the adoption of climate-friendly refrigerants and have received high ratings from BeZero Carbon, including an 'AA' rating that places them in the top 2% of carbon projects globally. The Food Waste Diversion Credits program, listed on Verra's VCS Registry, incentivizes grocery retailers to send surplus edible food to donation centers instead of landfills, simultaneously addressing food insecurity and methane emissions. One such project involves over 1,300 retail locations and is expected to generate more than 112,000 metric tons of CO2 equivalent credits annually. Therm began by focusing on cooling systems and has since expanded to address the entire food supply chain. The company has issued over 2 million Super Pollutant Carbon Credits across the United States, Canada, and Europe. It secured a $1.75 million seed round in 2021, followed by a $3.6 million Series A round in August 2025 from the same private investors to accelerate global expansion. column6: racksnet GmbH, founded in 2020 by Sebastian Fuhrmann, offers a cloud-based software solution designed to streamline IT network management for a diverse range of clients, including small, medium, and large enterprises, as well as IT service providers. This approach eliminates the need for specialized knowledge of command-line interfaces (CLI) for each vendor, simplifying network operations. The platform facilitates network planning, configuration, administration, and documentation. This includes support for white-box and brite-box hardware and software, such as the open-source network operating system SONiC. This strategic alignment allows clients to avoid vendor lock-in and leverage cost-effective open networking hardware. column5: Elzeard | the app for the growers to make easier their production process
column6: Elzeard, established in 2019, is an AgTech firm providing digital tools for specialized crop planning and production management. The company's name is inspired by Elzéard Bouffier, the protagonist in Jean Giono's story, "The Man Who Planted Trees," reflecting a mission of patient and impactful environmental restoration. The venture was brought to life by co-founders including Florence Amardeilh, who serves as President & Head of Innovation. Her background in customer relations, market development, and launching new products is complemented by Gilles, the CEO & Head of Software Development, an expert in information processing technologies, knowledge representation, and AI. Another co-founder, whose prior experience at a software publisher ended when the founder was ousted along with the company's human-centric values, was motivated to build a business with a strong social and solidarity-based foundation from the outset. The company operates within the agricultural technology (AgTech) and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) markets, specifically targeting farmers in horticulture, arboriculture, and floriculture. Its business model is subscription-based, offering monthly and annual plans with a minimum three-month commitment for monthly subscriptions. Special pricing is available for new farmers or those with less than one hectare of land, and a dedicated package is offered for entrepreneurs in the project planning phase. Revenue is generated through these subscriptions, which are billed semi-annually via the GOCARDLESS platform. Elzeard's core offering is a comprehensive mobile and web application designed to streamline farm operations and support the transition to agroecology. The platform aims to reduce the mental workload for producers, who often rely on notebooks and spreadsheets, by providing a centralized tool for management and decision-making. It features three main service modules: a planning tool that helps farmers program production with technical information on planting dates, seed quantities, and maturation times; a management function for daily monitoring of operations and resource allocation; and a traceability component that offers transparency and labeling for distribution channels. The application facilitates the sharing of agricultural knowledge and technical itineraries, promoting a more efficient dissemination of experience. This initiative is part of a larger project called 'Serre des Savoirs' (Greenhouse of Knowledge), which underscores the company's commitment to open knowledge and digital commons. All subscription tiers include maintenance, updates, and ongoing developments. Recognized as a social and solidarity economy enterprise (ESUS), Elzeard has secured innovation awards such as the i-Nov competition, which is part of the France 2030 plan. column5: Gantry-less 3D construction printing for sustainable housing
column6: Initially named Impact3D, Verustruct was founded by former SpaceX engineer Nick Callegari and emerged from Yale's innovation ecosystem in late 2024. Callegari, a Princeton engineering graduate, leveraged his technical expertise from developing structures for the Polaris Dawn Crew Dragon mission to address housing insecurity and the environmental impact of construction. The startup is developing a novel, gantry-less 3D printing technology that fabricates entire building walls complete with integrated plumbing, electrical wiring, and insulation. Verustruct's proprietary system, known as translational slip-form printing, uses a compact printer tethered to a material truck. This method avoids the large gantry frames typical in additive construction, allowing the printer to scale the wall layer by layer while embedding all necessary utilities during the printing process. This integrated approach is designed to accelerate construction, reduce costs, and minimize waste. The company is also creating its own software and sensor system to ensure the precise placement of internal components. Aiming for sustainability, Verustruct is experimenting with carbon-negative materials, including Portland cement alternatives and basalt fiber tension rods. The company's business model is to work directly with affordable housing developers and municipalities, staying involved throughout the construction process to ensure cost savings are passed on to residents. Verustruct has garnered significant early-stage support, securing multiple awards at the 2025 Startup Yale competition and a $2.44 million oversubscribed pre-seed funding round led by Necessary Ventures and Anorak Ventures in September 2025. column6: Pyrogen Energy, Inc. manufactures and sells a revolutionary waste-to-energy system designed to convert various forms of waste into electricity and other valuable byproducts. The system can process a wide range of feedstocks, including municipal solid waste (MSW), yard trimmings, food scraps, non-recyclable paper products, and wood debris. The resulting syngas can then be used for steam production or to generate electricity via patented steam turbines. The electricity produced can be sold directly to utility providers, creating a new revenue stream for clients. column5: Advanced small modular reactors for industrial heat
column6: ZettaJoule, Inc. is a U.S.-based clean energy company established in August 2023, developing advanced small modular reactors (SMRs) to provide clean heat and electricity for industrial applications. The company was co-founded by President and CEO Mitsuo Shimofuji, who envisioned a scalable, clean energy approach for industrial and high-tech companies. The co-founding team also includes Executive Vice President and Chief Commercial Officer Jeff Harper. ZettaJoule has assembled a global team of experts from organizations like the Japan Atomic Energy Agency (JAEA), the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, and the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission. The company's core technology involves modernizing a proven Japanese high-temperature gas-cooled reactor (HTGR) design. This technology, derived from the JAEA's HTTR which began operating in 1998, allows ZettaJoule's reactors to deliver process heat up to 950°C, significantly higher than conventional water-cooled reactors. This high-temperature capability makes the reactors suitable for hard-to-abate sectors and a wide range of industrial uses, including oil and gas, chemical manufacturing, steelmaking, mining, and the production of hydrogen and e-fuels like Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF). In addition to process heat, the reactors can provide reliable, 24/7 zero-carbon electricity for data centers and microgrids. The first product line will be a microreactor with a capacity of 30 megawatts thermal and 12 megawatts electric. ZettaJoule operates on an "Energy-as-a-Service" model, offering flexible ownership options. Clients can choose to own and operate the SMR facilities themselves or have ZettaJoule manage, staff, and operate the plants, with the client acting as an off-taker. The company is headquartered in Houston, Texas, with additional offices in the Washington, D.C. area, and in Tokyo and Mito, Japan. ZettaJoule has received investments from firms including Globis Capital Partners, Coral Capital, Archetype Ventures, and SOSV. In December 2025, the company received a formal endorsement for its ZJ HTGR project from Aramco Services Company, an affiliate of the operator of the largest refinery in the United States, underscoring the technology's potential for industrial applications. column5: Automated basalt fiber reinforcement for sustainable construction.
column6: Fiber Elements is an Austrian company specializing in the automated manufacturing of basalt fiber reinforcement structures for the construction industry, offering a sustainable alternative to traditional steel-reinforced concrete. Founded in Leoben in 2023 by architect-turned-entrepreneur Wolfgang Fiel, the startup aims to address the construction sector's significant carbon footprint. Fiel's career has focused on sustainable materials in both research and practical applications, leading him to recognize the potential of combining basalt's natural properties with a holistic design-to-manufacturing approach. The company's core technology, developed in collaboration with leading Austrian universities such as the Technical University of Leoben (MUL), the University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU), and the Vienna University of Technology (TU Wien), revolves around the fully automated production of three-dimensional, load-path-oriented basalt fiber structures. column6: Fertilis Pty Ltd, an Australian medical technology company headquartered in Adelaide, is focused on advancing in vitro fertilization (IVF) treatments through the automation and standardization of laboratory procedures. Founded in 2019 by Professor Jeremy Thompson and serial entrepreneur Marty Gauvin, the company aims to improve embryo quality and quantity, addressing the low success rates and high costs associated with traditional IVF. The company's scientific foundation is rooted in over two decades of research by Professor Thompson, the Chief Scientific Officer, an internationally recognized embryologist with over 40 years of experience in reproductive health. His idea for a micro-device to automate IVF originated in the late 1990s and was further developed in 2017 in collaboration with the Centre for Nanoscale Biophotonics, utilizing micron-3D printing technology. Marty Gauvin, the CEO, brings extensive experience in commercializing technology and has founded several successful startups. His expertise lies in translating complex research into market-ready solutions. Fertilis targets the global fertility market, specifically IVF clinics and their embryologists. The company raised AUD$2.75 million in a seed funding round in 2021, led by Horizons Ventures, to fund clinical trials and team expansion. A subsequent Series A round was planned to bring its first product to market. The core of Fertilis's offering is a new class of 3D-printed micro-devices, including the microICSI and microIVF systems, designed to automate and standardize critical IVF steps like intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) and embryo culture. These devices, smaller than a pinhead, can hold individual oocytes or embryos in a controlled environment that more closely mimics the conditions inside the human body. By using microfluidics to create a slow, consistent flow of nutrient-rich culture medium, the technology minimizes environmental stress on the embryo, such as changes in temperature and light, which are common when manually moving cells between petri dishes. A key feature of the microICSI device is the elimination of the holding pipette, simplifying the injection process, reducing physical stress on the egg, and cutting the procedure time in half. This allows embryologists to potentially double their capacity and requires less specialized training. Research in animal models has shown the devices can increase blastocyst development rates and improve procedural efficiency. column5: AI-driven ecosystem extending electric vehicle battery lifespan
column6: Originally founded as Bavertis in 2021 and rebranded to PULSETRAIN on September 18, 2024, the Munich-based company is developing an AI-driven ecosystem to enhance electric vehicle (EV) battery efficiency and longevity. The founders of Bavertis were Niclas Lehnert and Lukas Obkircher, and the PULSETRAIN founding team includes Leopold König, Thomas Plaschko, and Niclas Lehnert, who bring extensive experience from the battery sector. The company's core technology is a software-defined, modular multilevel inverter system that integrates the battery management system (BMS), inverter, and charging electronics into a single unit. This "in-battery" solution reconfigures battery cells thousands of times per second, allowing the battery to generate AC or DC voltage directly, which eliminates the need for a separate conventional inverter. This approach aims to extend battery life by up to 80%, enable faster charging, reduce system costs, and improve overall vehicle efficiency and safety. By monitoring and controlling each battery cell individually with proprietary microchips and AI algorithms, the system can optimize performance and health. This also allows the use of battery cells that might otherwise be discarded during manufacturing, reducing waste. The technology is designed to be safer, operating at lower voltages, and enables features like bidirectional charging through a simple software update. Bavertis has received undisclosed amounts in grant funding in 2022 and 2023 from investors including EIT Urban Mobility and GEC Scaling Factory. As PULSETRAIN, the company secured €6.1 million in seed funding to accelerate product development and industrialization. The company's business model targets B2B clients in the mobility sector, acting as a technology supplier for the automotive industry and beyond. Initially focusing on two-wheelers and commercial vehicles like electric construction machinery, the company is expanding into the automotive, aviation, agriculture, and shipping sectors. They collaborate with partners, such as ABT e-Line, to develop and integrate their battery modules into various applications. column6: Peregrine XR, operating under the parent company Iron Will Innovations Canada Inc., is a technology firm specializing in wearable interfaces for the virtual reality (VR) market. The company's journey began with an idea to make the hand a direct interface for digital interaction, leading to the launch of its first product, the "Peregrine Glove," in 2009. Initially, the firm targeted the PC gaming market, particularly Real-Time Strategy (RTS) and Massively Multiplayer Online (MMO) games, offering a glove with proprietary touch-sensing technology that functioned as a set of programmable hotkeys. This early version sold thousands of units across more than 30 countries. A significant pivot occurred in 2016 when the founder, after experiencing an Oculus DK1 headset, recognized the technology's immense potential for the emerging VR space. The company's core product is the Peregrine VR Glove, which is designed to replace traditional controllers and provide a more natural, hands-on presence in virtual environments. The glove allows users to perform actions like grabbing, twisting, and pinching to interact with digital objects. It operates on patented TouchPoint technology, where contact between a finger and the thumb or palm is registered as a button press or action. The current pre-order version features Bluetooth connectivity, haptic feedback, and integrated Lighthouse tracking for positional awareness. The system is built on the OpenXR standard, ensuring compatibility with thousands of Steam VR applications, and connects with headsets such as the HTC Vive, Valve Index, and XTAL 3. The pre-order price for a pair of Peregrine VR Gloves is listed at $2,499.95 USD. Peregrine XR's business model centers on the direct sale of its hardware to consumers and enterprise clients. While its roots are in gaming, the company now has a strong focus on industrial training applications. These gloves enable realistic simulations for work-related tasks involving tools and parts, allowing companies to train employees in high-consequence scenarios. The company operates on a venture capital-backed model, having completed a Series A funding round of $3 million in 2009 and a Series B round in 2010. A subsequent venture round was recorded in September 2023. Based in Lloydminster, Alberta, Canada, Iron Will Innovations aims to be a leading global choice for VR glove interfaces. column5: A cryptocurrency platform part of the Materra ecosystem simplifying Web3 experiences by enabling trading and real-world asset exchange for ultrahigh purity nano copper powder
column6: Cuprum Coin (CUNP), launched in 2021, was the world’s first project to introduce the concept of tokenizing ultra-high-purity nano copper as a new category of real-world asset. The project was created to explore the emerging intersection between advanced materials science and next-generation digital financial infrastructure at a time when no regulatory framework for virtual assets existed globally.During its active development phase (2021–2024), Cuprum Coin raised over $1.5 million USD through private funding and community support. These resources were used to design, document, and validate a pioneering model for a programmable commodity backed by scientific-grade nanomaterials. The project built an early international following and engaged with scientists, engineers, and strategic partners who later became foundational contributors to Materra’s Scientific Council.The core mission of Cuprum Coin was to demonstrate that nano-scale materials – such as copper with purity above 99.99% and particle size below 30 nm – would become one of the most impactful commodity classes of the 21st century, enabling breakthroughs in aerospace, clean energy, AI hardware, medicine, and next-generation electronics. The project anticipated the future need for a digital marketplace capable of representing these materials as verifiable, transparent, and programmable real-world assets.Cuprum Coin served as an early technical and conceptual framework, outlining how an ecosystem combining in-house nano production, RWA tokenization, and institutional-grade exchange infrastructure could operate at global scale. Throughout its development, the project produced extensive documentation, scientific models, tokenomics architecture, and operational blueprints. These assets laid the groundwork for what would eventually become the Materra ecosystem.By 2024, global regulations matured, the UAE emerged as a world leader in digital asset frameworks, and nano-materials gained strategic relevance in multiple sovereign innovation agendas. In this environment, the founder made the strategic decision to consolidate all scientific, technological, and economic components of Cuprum Coin into a broader, regulated, and institution-ready platform — Materra Lab FZCO, headquartered in Dubai.Today, the legacy of Cuprum Coin continues through Materra’s advanced work in nano gold, nano silver, nano copper, graphene, titanium, lithium, platinum, silicon, and future programmable commodities. Materra extends the original Cuprum vision into a sovereign-scale scientific and digital infrastructure, developed in alignment with the UAE’s long-term innovation strategy.Cuprum Coin remains an important predecessor project:• First conceptualization of nano-commodity tokenization (2021)• Over $1.5M invested in early research, architecture, and development• Formation of key scientific relationships now active within Materra• Creation of the original nano-RWA economic model• Early international community and market validation• Foundational milestone in the evolution toward Materra’s sovereign platformWhile Cuprum Coin itself is no longer active as an independent venture, its achievements represent the starting point of a multi-year journey that culminated in the creation of Materra — a next-generation ecosystem positioned to establish the world’s first nano-commodity marketplace and scientific production infrastructure anchored in the United Arab Emirates.

column5: Onsite PFAS testing for rapid, actionable results
column6: 12-15 Molecular Diagnostics, Inc., operating as Verralize, is a biotechnology company that develops next-generation testing and diagnostics solutions. Founded in 2018 by Dr. Saion Sinha, a nanotechnology expert, the company was originally named 12-15 Molecular Diagnostics, a title reflecting its focus on molecular testing at the 12th and 15th levels of specificity. The company later rebranded to Verralize to symbolize its mission to reveal the unseen and revolutionize testing across multiple industries. The founder, Dr. Sinha, holds a Ph.D. in Condensed Matter and Materials Physics from the University of Kentucky and serves as a professor at the University of New Haven. His research into nanotechnology and biosensors led to the creation of the company. The company's core technology is a "lab-on-a-sensor" platform utilizing electrochemical biosensors for the rapid, on-site detection of contaminants and pathogens. This platform was initially applied to create a 7-minute saliva test for COVID-19 with high accuracy. The company has since pivoted to address the pressing issue of PFAS, or "forever chemicals," contamination in water. Its flagship product is a portable PFAS test kit that delivers lab-quality results in minutes, a significant reduction from the typical weeks-long wait for traditional lab results. The system consists of a reusable, thermos-sized analyzer and a disposable, single-use sensing lid containing a graphene-based biosensor array. It is designed to be user-friendly, affordable, and require minimal training, making advanced testing accessible to a broader range of users, including public and private water companies, municipalities, and laboratories. Verralize’s technology detects PFAS down to 4 parts per trillion (ppt) and provides results in approximately 12-15 minutes. This enables real-time decision-making for water quality management, remediation process control, and regulatory compliance. The business model appears to be centered on the sale of these testing systems and disposable sensor kits. Verralize has engaged in several partnerships to advance its technology, including a collaboration with I.W. Tremont for nano-sensor manufacturing and alpha testing with BioLargo, Inc. to validate the test kit's performance with PFAS treatment systems. The company has been recognized for its work, receiving the “Innovator of the Month” honor from Connecticut Senator Chris Murphy in March 2024. column6: Good Heat, founded in early 2025 by Bauke van Gent, Tom Geiser, and Bruis van Vlijmen, is a climate tech startup focused on decarbonizing industrial heat. The EMS also handles electricity market participation and automated energy trading across its assets. By managing the entire project lifecycle—from development and financing to operation—Good Heat removes the technology and investment risk for its industrial customers. The founding team brings together extensive experience in the energy sector. CEO Bauke van Gent has a background in developing large-scale renewable energy projects at companies like Neoen. CTO Bruis van Vlijmen specializes in battery technology and AI-driven optimization from his research at Stanford University and work at Transition VC. Chief Energy Markets Officer Tom Geiser has expertise in energy trading and previously led Australian operations for Rondo Energy, a high-temperature heat battery company. column6: BuyWander Inc. is an online auction retailer specializing in the resale of returned retail goods. Launched in February 2024, the Spokane, Washington-based company addresses the logistical and environmental issues of retail returns by purchasing truckloads of items from various retailers and reselling them to consumers at a significant discount. The business model is centered on an online auction marketplace where customers bid on inspected, new, or like-new products. Bidding for each item starts at $1 on a 24-hour, no-reserve auction. Revenue is generated from the sale of these goods, with the company reporting a monthly revenue of $370,000 in March 2025 and an average order value near $80. The company was founded by serial entrepreneur Jordan Allen, along with co-founders Brock Kowalchuk and Matt McGee. Allen previously founded the vacation rental company Stay Alfred and the real estate bidding platform Doorsey. Kowalchuk, who serves as co-CEO, brings operational and financial expertise from his time as CEO of the e-commerce company Kaspien. McGee is an expert in supply-chain logistics with previous experience at Overstock.com, Wish.com, and Maersk. This leadership team combines experience in entrepreneurship, e-commerce, and logistics. BuyWander's process involves using AI and other technology to scan, sort, and identify products for resale. After a manual quality check, items are photographed and listed on the company's website. To manage logistics costs, the company does not offer shipping; instead, customers who win auctions pick up their items curbside from the company's warehouses. In addition to online auctions, the warehouses also operate as bin stores where customers can search for deals. The company has demonstrated rapid growth, moving through four warehouses in under a year to accommodate its expansion and processing six semi-trucks of merchandise per week as of April 2025. In April 2025, BuyWander raised $2 million in a seed funding round led by Triple Impact Capital to support its expansion, including opening a new 30,000-square-foot warehouse in Kent, Washington. column6: Lunettes de Zac is a French company operating in the circular economy, specializing in the collection, refurbishment, and resale of used eyeglasses. For every three pairs of glasses sold, one hour of work is generated for a person with a disability. Lunettes de Zac operates with a strong eco-responsible focus. The company sells the refurbished frames at affordable prices, often allowing for full reimbursement by French health insurance. About 70% of their inventory consists of reconditioned frames, while the remaining 30% are new frames made from recycled materials like plastic bottles and seashells. The startup, co-founded by Vanbremeersch and Antoine Lamblin, opened its first physical store in Roubaix and a second one in Lille. column5: Mealworm-derived proteins and biofertilizers for agri-food sectors
column6: Protiberia, legally known as VILLA INSECT S.L., is a Spanish deep-tech company founded in 2022 that specializes in sustainable insect farming. Headquartered in Villamalea, Albacete, the female-led startup was co-founded by CEO Ana González and Head of R&D Jose González. The company focuses on the industrial breeding of the Tenebrio molitor, or mealworm, to produce high-value raw materials from what is considered a potent bioconversor. These materials include protein flour for animal feed, lipids for the food industry, chitin for pharmaceutical and cosmetic applications, and frass (insect manure) as an organic biofertilizer. Protiberia's business model is twofold. The company's core operation involves the production and sale of Tenebrio molitor eggs and neonates to a decentralized network of associated farms, called "Protigranjas". Protiberia provides training and technology to these partners who handle the larval fattening stage. Once the larvae are grown, Protiberia processes and commercializes the final products. This model is designed to increase productivity and reduce risks for farmers by centralizing the most complex and costly reproductive phase. Secondly, the company offers a licensing model for its proprietary automation technology, which integrates AI, computer vision, and IoT to optimize breeding cycles and reduce operational costs by an estimated 15-20%. Operating on a circular economy and zero-waste principle, Protiberia utilizes organic waste from local agri-food industries to feed the insects, requiring minimal water and land compared to traditional livestock. The company has received significant public funding and has formed strategic partnerships with research centers and technology firms to advance its R&D. Since its launch, Protiberia has achieved several milestones, including winning awards from Coca-Cola, Expansión, and the Madrid City Council, and being selected for the Lanzadera business accelerator program in 2024. column5: Electric robotic arms for harsh environment operations
column6: Fluid Wire Robotics is a deep tech company developing fully electric and modular robotic arms designed to operate in extreme environments. The company was founded in 2022 as a spin-off from the Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna in Pisa, Italy, by Marco Bolignari (CEO), Marco Fontana (CTO), Francesco Damiani, Gianluigi Grandesso (COO), and Ivan De Leonardis (CMO). The project originated at the university's Institute of Mechanical Intelligence under the supervision of Professor Marco Fontana, leveraging his extensive experience in robotics and applied mechanics. The company's core innovation is its proprietary "Fluid Wire" technology, a fluid-based transmission system. This design places all electrical and electronic components, such as motors and sensors, into a remote, sealed actuation unit outside of the robotic arm itself. Power is then transmitted from this external box to the robot's joints via the Fluid Wires. This delocalization of components results in a lightweight, "hollow" arm structure that is inherently proofed against harsh conditions like radiation, explosive atmospheres, high temperatures, vacuums, and subsea pressures, without needing complex and costly adaptations. The system offers benefits such as high-precision force control without fragile sensors, modularity for easy customization, and enhanced safety and reliability. Fluid Wire Robotics operates in the industrial tech and machinery markets, targeting sectors including nuclear energy, space exploration, and underwater operations. The business model focuses on providing these enabling robotic systems for inspection, maintenance, and repair in critical infrastructures. The company has secured a total of $2.13 million (€1.2 million) in seed funding across two rounds from investors including RoboIT, Scientifica Venture Capital, Pariter Partners, and Deep Blue Ventures. Fluid Wire Robotics was selected to join NATO's Defence Innovation Accelerator for the North Atlantic (DIANA) 2025 cohort to advance dual-use applications of its technology for critical infrastructure resilience. column6: iEthico Limited, a UK-based health-tech company founded in 2020, operates as a pharmaceutical sourcing platform designed to address global medicine shortages. The company was co-founded by CEO Debra Ainge and Renee Kalia, who serves as Head of Operations. Ainge's background includes a PhD in Organic Chemistry and executive roles at AstraZeneca, Clinigen, and Parexel, providing deep experience in drug development and the pharmaceutical supply chain. MedSupply Intelligence is a data solution that uses AI to provide real-time market insights and forecasts on potential drug shortages. This feature acts as an early warning system, sending alerts to users about emerging supply issues and suggesting alternative sourcing options. By aggregating data from public, private, and proprietary sources, the company aims to deliver actionable intelligence that supports all stakeholders in the pharmaceutical supply chain, from pharmacies and hospitals to wholesalers and manufacturers. The business model is centered on direct-to-consumer sales, with products available for purchase with an optional integrated lock and a five-year warranty. column5: Integrated power solutions for digital infrastructure sectors
column6: In 2023, a bottleneck was tightening around the digital world. The explosive growth of AI and cloud computing demanded massive new data centers, but the electrical grid couldn't keep up. Into this gap stepped Kenneth Davies, an industry veteran who had already founded Google Energy and led Microsoft's global renewable strategy. He launched Takanock to solve a simple, yet critical problem: how to power the next wave of digital infrastructure when the grid itself is the constraint. The company’s playbook was to develop on-site power solutions for large-scale data centers. Instead of waiting years for utility upgrades, Takanock provides power directly at the site, serving as the primary source until the local substation is ready. Afterwards, these same assets transition to support the wholesale grid, enhancing overall stability. This dual-purpose model accelerates the deployment of new data centers in power-starved markets like Northern Virginia and Phoenix, where Takanock is already executing projects. The market saw the opportunity. In June 2025, Takanock announced a major strategic event: a $500 million capital commitment from two heavyweights in the infrastructure world, ArcLight and DigitalBridge. This investment wasn't just a validation of the company's approach; it provided the capital to execute on existing long-term contracts and scale its operations across the United States. By bringing the power and the data center together, Takanock is not just building infrastructure; it's building a new model for how the digital world gets built.

column6: X-Hemp is a Tasmanian company founded in 2020 by Andi Lucas that processes industrial hemp into environmentally friendly building materials. One of its significant projects includes supplying materials for the University of Tasmania's Forestry Building in Hobart, which has committed to using X-Hemp products in future projects to maintain its carbon-negative status. X-Hemp generates revenue through the sale of its various hemp-based products via wholesale channels and an online retail shop. column5: Design research advocating for non-toxic building materials
column6: Healthy Materials Lab (HML) is a design research lab within Parsons School of Design dedicated to placing human and environmental health at the center of all design decisions. The lab was co-founded in 2015 by architect Alison Mears and interior and furniture designer Jonsara Ruth. Their shared interest in the health impacts of design, beyond aesthetics and energy use, led them to establish HML, focusing on raising awareness about toxic chemicals in building products and creating accessible resources for designers and architects. The founders' backgrounds directly inform the lab's mission. Mears, an architect and former Dean of the School of Design Strategies at Parsons, and Ruth, the Founding Director of the MFA Interior Design program at Parsons, both observed a gap in the conversation around sustainability, which often overlooked the direct impact of material toxicity on human health. Ruth previously designed furniture for Q Collection, focusing on products free from common toxics like flame retardants and formaldehyde, while Mears' architectural work included a focus on the social impacts of housing. Together, they received a grant in 2015 to study building materials in affordable housing, which often contain the most harmful ingredients due to budget constraints. HML operates as a non-profit, supported by grants from foundations like the Freedom Together Foundation (formerly The JPB Foundation) and The Angelo Donghia Foundation, as well as through partnerships and donations. The lab serves a wide audience, including architects, designers, students, educators, developers, and manufacturers. Its business model is centered on research, education, and advocacy. HML provides a variety of resources, many of which are free, such as online courses, a Healthier Materials Library, project case studies, and tools and guides. They have educated over 25,000 people through online courses and have influenced the living environments of over 570,000 people through collaborations. The lab's core services include evaluating building materials, promoting transparency from manufacturers, and developing innovative solutions with healthier alternatives like hemp-lime (a term they introduced to replace the misleading 'hempcrete') and mineral-based paints. A key initiative is the Healthy Affordable Materials Project (HAMP), a collaborative effort to reduce toxic chemical exposure in affordable housing. HML collaborates with community organizations, government agencies, and manufacturers to implement these healthier materials in real-world projects, demonstrating their viability and benefits. column6: ChargeBot provides a mobile power solution designed for commercial landscaping and lawn care professionals. By enabling on-the-go charging, ChargeBot helps reduce the number of batteries a crew needs to purchase and minimizes downtime spent manually managing battery charging. Operating as a Public Benefit Corporation and a certified B Corporation, Town Hall is committed to a "planet positive" business model, aiming to contribute more to the environment than it consumes. This commitment is reflected in its product design, which heavily utilizes recycled materials. For example, their puffy jackets feature 100% recycled down, liners, and shells, and the company aims to have all its products made entirely from recycled materials. The company also donates 3% of its annual revenue to community non-profits. Town Hall’s business model centers on direct-to-consumer sales through its website, as well as partnerships with retailers like REI and Christy Sports. The product line is designed specifically for children's needs, eschewing the common practice of simply scaling down adult apparel. Key features include "grow seams" that can be removed to extend the garment's length, ensuring longevity and facilitating a "hand-me-up" culture where gear is passed on to multiple children. Their inaugural collection included items like the Mountain Town Winter Jacket, Around Town Cold Weather Jacket, and Down Town Puffy. The company actively involves children in the design and testing process through its "Kidsumer Insights" program to ensure the apparel meets the demands of active kids. column6: Ocean GeoLoop AS is a Norwegian green technology firm focused on commercializing solutions to combat climate and environmental crises. The company was formally established in 2020, but its foundational technology stems from the "Ocean Project," a research initiative started in 2006 by founder and inventor Dr. Hans Gude Gudesen. The company's primary business is providing point-source carbon capture technology to industrial emitters, such as those in the cement, lime, aluminum, and waste-to-energy sectors. Its business model centers on a Build-Own-Operate (BOO) approach, aiming to generate recurring revenue per ton of CO2 captured, supplemented by potential income from biomass sales and ocean purification services. Ocean GeoLoop has reported revenues, primarily from its subsidiary Energi Teknikk AS, reaching NOK 235.7 million in 2024, up from NOK 172.9 million in 2023, while continuing to invest heavily in technology development. The company is publicly traded on the Oslo Børs Euronext Growth market under the ticker OCEAN. Ocean GeoLoop's flagship offering is its "Carbon Capture by Nature" technology, a proprietary, water-based process designed to remove CO2 from industrial flue gas. A key differentiator of this system is that it operates without the use of amines or other toxic chemicals, addressing significant health, safety, and environmental concerns associated with conventional methods. The technology is designed for high efficiency, with tests demonstrating capture rates exceeding 90% and low energy consumption. A significant milestone was achieved in August 2023, when its industrial pilot plant at Norske Skog Skogn successfully completed 3,000 hours of autonomous operation. column6: ABSORA GmbH, legally registered as Technology Reef GmbH in September 2023, is a German materials science company developing solutions for noise and vibration silencing. Its key features include the absorption of both airborne sound and vibrations, particularly at low frequencies, and the ability to smoothen airflow. The material is produced using a patented process for lateral micro-perforation, which enables broadband sound absorption without conventional insulation. The company states that HSA3 is fully recyclable, reusable, and repairable, aligning with circular economy principles. ABSORA's business model is centered on forming partnerships with companies to integrate HSA3 into their products. The company provides support from the initial design proposal to market entry. Key application areas include architecture (suspended ceilings, acoustic louvers), mobility (in-exhaust silencers, heat shields), and household appliances (enclosures for fans and compressors). In late 2025, ABSORA secured €1.25 million in a pre-seed funding round led by venture capital firms HEARTFELT_ and Marvelous, with participation from business angels. This capital is intended to scale up series production of the HSA3 technology and initiate industrial projects, targeting a European market for lightweight construction and sound insulation estimated to be worth over €200 billion. The company's headquarters are in Berlin, Germany. column6: Food for All Africa is a non-profit social enterprise that operates as West Africa's first and largest community food bank. This recovered food is then distributed to vulnerable populations such as children, the elderly, and the mentally challenged through community organizations, orphanages, hospitals, and schools. Food for All Africa utilizes mobile technology to connect sources of excess food with those in need. Its business model is based on partnerships and donations from individuals, corporations, and government agencies like the U.S. Agency for International Development. The organization's programs are multifaceted, including direct feeding initiatives, emergency relief, a school feeding program for institutions not covered by government aid, and the Mother and Infant Nutrition Improvement Program (MINIP). Beyond food distribution, the enterprise focuses on long-term solutions by providing sustainable vocational and social development programs to help unemployed youth gain technical and professional skills. A significant part of its mission involves advocacy. The organization works with stakeholders to improve the food supply chain and collaborates with the Ghanaian government on policy, such as the National Food Donors Encouragement Act, to facilitate food donations. Since its inception, Food for All Africa has served millions of meals and recovered over a million kilograms of food, significantly impacting food insecurity in the region. column6: Neurotrim Systems GmbH, a med-tech company founded in April 2021, is commercializing a method for physio-training that has been in development for over a decade. column6: HonestDog GmbH, founded in 2022, operates as a curated online marketplace with a mission to address fundamental issues within the pet industry, specifically the often-unregulated online sale of dogs. By doing so, the company mitigates the risks of genetic disorders and behavioral issues often associated with dogs from puppy farms. Revenue is generated through a multi-faceted model that includes subscriptions, commissions, and advertising. The company secured seed funding in May 2023, indicating investor confidence in its business model and mission.  For prospective owners, the service provides a streamlined and trustworthy process to find a dog, offering detailed information about breeders, their practices, and the health records of the animals. Breeders gain access to the 'HonestDog Club', which provides discounts from partner companies like Fressnapf, a major pet supplies retailer. column6: Yanekara Inc. is a University of Tokyo spin-off technology company founded in June 2020 by Keisuke Matsufuji and Daichi Yoshioka. The company's name reflects its mission to transform the energy system "from the roof" (Yanekara in Japanese). Matsufuji, who serves as CEO, became interested in energy solutions after a childhood science project on solar cooking and later studied power grid balancing using electric vehicles at the University of Tokyo. Co-founder and COO, Daichi Yoshioka, developed an interest in environmental issues and energy policy, studying in Germany and the UK before joining forces with Matsufuji. Their collaboration began as a research project in 2019 to use EVs as energy storage, which gained traction and funding, leading them to establish the company to accelerate social implementation.Yanekara develops and sells both hardware and cloud software to create virtual power plants (VPPs) by controlling distributed energy resources like EVs and storage batteries. The company’s business model targets both residential and corporate clients, offering solutions for businesses to manage fleets of commercial EVs and for homeowners to achieve energy self-sufficiency. Key products include the "YaneBox," a bidirectional charger that allows multiple EVs to be charged directly from solar panels and discharge power back (V2X), and "YaneCube," a smart switch that adds remote control capabilities to existing EV charging outlets to optimize charging schedules and reduce electricity costs. The company also offers "Yanekara One," a digital membership service for solar power owners that automates the storage of surplus electricity. Yanekara generates revenue through the sale of its hardware products and subscription fees for its cloud-based energy management services.The company has engaged in several proof-of-concept projects, including with Japan Post to manage its delivery EV fleet and with the city of Kitakyushu to test V2X functionality. The company handles the entire process for the customer, from consultation and site analysis to design, obtaining regulatory approvals, installation, and ongoing 24/7 monitoring and maintenance, which includes panel cleaning. By generating their own power, customers can reduce their utility bills, lower their carbon footprint, and increase their property value by an estimated 3% or more. column5: Giving classic cars a new life with a 100% electric drive
column6: Voitures Extravert, a Dutch company founded in 2016 by Martijn van Dijk and Jurgen Moerman, operates in the niche market of classic car electrification. The business focuses on converting classic Porsche 911s into fully electric vehicles, targeting collectors and enthusiasts who desire the iconic design aesthetic combined with modern, sustainable technology. The company's business model revolves around sourcing donor vehicles, primarily from the 1970s and 1980s, and performing a complete, ground-up restoration and electric conversion. This process is underpinned by a single technical platform strategy to ensure reproducibility and quality, rather than converting a client's existing car. Revenue is generated through the sale of these finished, high-cost builds, with prices starting over $300,000.The company's flagship product is the "Quintessenza," an all-electric reimagining of the classic Porsche 911. Each vehicle is stripped to its bare chassis and then rebuilt with all-new or fully refurbished components. Voitures Extravert developed its own proprietary technology for the powertrain and software systems, including an operating system that supports over-the-air updates. The electric motor provides substantial torque, enabling acceleration from 0-62 mph in under six seconds. The battery pack, initially a 58-59 kWh unit, is distributed throughout the car to achieve an ideal 50/50 weight distribution, a significant shift from the original's rear-heavy nature, and offers an estimated range of around 250 miles. Modern conveniences such as custom adjustable suspension, power steering, air conditioning, and enhanced braking systems are integrated to improve comfort and reliability for daily driving.The founders, van Dijk and Moerman, launched the company with the mission to "colour the streets again with iconic classics, based on technology of the future." Their entrepreneurial journey was driven by a perfectionistic approach, choosing to develop much of their technology in-house rather than buying off-the-shelf components. This led to a longer-than-anticipated development phase before the first cars were delivered. column5: Self-cleaning nanotech film and AI-powered soiling analytics
column6: Swish Solar provides a solution to the efficiency losses solar panels suffer from sand and snow accumulation. The company was founded by CEO Miswar Syed and CTO Amirhossein Boreiri and is based at Velocity, the University of Waterloo's startup incubator in Kitchener, Canada. Syed's interest in this problem began during his time in Saudi Arabia, where he observed the significant impact of dust on solar panel performance. This experience, combined with a challenging first winter in Canada in 2023 that highlighted the issue of snow buildup, led to the development of Swish Solar's core technology. The company's offering consists of two main products: SwishScreen and SwishOS. SwishScreen is a patent-pending, self-cleaning nanotech film that can be retrofitted onto existing solar panels. It is designed to remove sand, dust, and snow without requiring water or moving parts, recovering up to 95% of lost efficiency. Complementing the hardware is SwishOS, an AI-driven analytics platform that analyzes environmental conditions to predict soiling rates and determine the most cost-effective cleaning schedules for solar operators. This integrated system aims to automate and optimize solar maintenance, reduce operational costs, and maximize energy output. Swish Solar's business model targets solar asset operators, including utilities, Independent Power Producers (IPPs), and Operations & Maintenance (O&M) providers. The company establishes partnerships for field testing, OEM integration with panel manufacturers, and software integration with asset management platforms. In November 2025, the company announced it had closed an oversubscribed US$1.5 million pre-seed funding round led by Friday Ventures, with participation from Velocity Fund, Front Row Ventures, Alif Fund, and Suno Growth. This capital is intended to accelerate market adoption, support product manufacturing, and further develop the AI models as the company scales toward commercialization. Swish Solar has already secured pilot deployments with major solar operators in North America and the Middle East. column6: This entity addresses the challenge of energy curtailment, a situation where surplus energy is wasted when generation from renewable sources exceeds grid demand. column5: Clean Power for Marine Structures
column6: Zoexpower is an Aberdeen-based clean-tech company targeting the blue economy with a novel wave energy converter (WEC) system. The firm was founded by Aslihan Penley, a chemical engineer who transitioned from a successful career in the oil and gas industry with major firms like Subsea7 and Technip. Her journey into wave energy started in 2015, leading to the incorporation of ZOEX POWER LTD in early 2020. Penley’s experience in complex subsea projects informed her pragmatic approach to solving historical challenges in the wave energy sector, specifically the ability to generate power from smaller sea states and ensuring device survivability.   The company is developing a system that can be attached to existing marine structures such as aquaculture barges, breakwaters, and offshore platforms. Its core technology consists of a compliant fender that moves with the waves, connected to a patented double-link arm mechanism. This design intensifies the wave motion, allowing an electro-mechanical generator to produce power even in wave heights under two meters, a significant advantage over many existing WEC designs. The system dually functions as an 'ActiveFender,' offering protection to the host structure from impact. Zoexpower utilizes proven, robust components, including a ball-screw generator from aerospace supplier UmbraGroup, to mitigate technical risks.   Zoexpower’s business model focuses on product sales, initially targeting off-grid, diesel-displacement applications. The primary entry market is the rapidly growing aquaculture sector, where the WEC units can power feed barges, replacing carbon-emitting diesel generators. Beyond aquaculture, the company targets auxiliary power for offshore oil & gas installations and marine data sensors. The long-term strategy involves scaling production to reduce costs, with a goal of becoming competitive with offshore wind and entering the utility-scale market. The company has achieved significant milestones, including securing funding from Scottish Enterprise, Equity Gap, and Innovate UK, and deploying its first 100 kW prototype at the Port of Aberdeen in mid-2024. column6: Megaliter Varunaa is a Hyderabad-based startup that provides urban wastewater management solutions. column5: On-farm biogas systems for agricultural waste valorization
column6: GreenFarm, established in 2022 by CEO Frank Wennerberg, provides a climate and energy concept designed to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from agriculture. The process yields a residual product that is an optimized fertilizer, enhancing nutrient absorption by plants and minimizing nutrient seepage into the local water environment. The entire system, housing all mechanical and electrical components, is a modular technical unit designed for easy integration into new or existing farm infrastructure. The business model includes providing these scalable environmental treatment concepts with a rapid deployment time of five months from order to operation. column5: Upcycling plastic waste into sustainable construction materials
column6: The Plastic Flamingo, also known as The Plaf, is a French-led social enterprise founded in 2018 with operations centered in the Philippines to combat marine plastic pollution. The company was established by co-founders François and Charlotte Lesage, alongside Jean Marie and Veronique Desabres. The primary offerings are "eco-boards" and "eco-lumbers," which serve as sustainable alternatives to traditional wood for construction, furniture, and disaster-relief shelters. These products are rot-proof, splinter-free, and termite-free. The company’s business model has a threefold impact: environmental, social, and educational. Socially, The Plastic Flamingo provides employment and upskilling opportunities to individuals from low-income families. Educationally, it runs awareness campaigns and webinars to inform the public about plastic pollution and recycling. The company generates revenue through the sale of its recycled products to companies and NGOs, and also offers Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) services. The Plaf has received seed funding from investors including Charter Next Generation and Plug and Play APAC. column5: Circular auction platform providing royalties for watchmakers
column6: Marteau & Co. is a Swiss-based online auction platform launched in July 2025, dedicated to the resale of timepieces from independent watchmakers. The company was founded by Arthur Touchot and Léonard Pictet, who met in 2015 and have a combined experience of over 20 years in the watch industry. Touchot's background includes roles as a journalist for The New York Times and The Financial Times, a senior editor at HODINKEE, and a senior executive at Phillips auction house. Pictet has nearly 15 years of experience within the Richemont Group, with roles at Jaeger-LeCoultre and A. Lange & Söhne. The platform's business model is centered on a concept analogous to the Artist's Resale Right (Droit de Suite) seen in the art world, which ensures creators receive a percentage of the price when their works are resold. Marteau & Co. implements a "Maker's Fee," guaranteeing independent watchmakers a 3% royalty of the hammer price when one of their watches is sold on the platform. This fee is taken from the buyer's premium. The company aims to address the issue where watchmakers, unlike other artists, do not typically benefit financially from the appreciation of their work on the secondary market. Marteau & Co.'s fee structure includes a 20% buyer's premium, which is lower than the typical 25% to 30% at major auction houses, and no seller's fees apart from a flat CHF 500 charge per watch for logistics. The platform is not intended to compete directly with major auction houses but rather to connect collectors with watchmakers and provide a system that sustains the craft. The company curates a selection of timepieces, meticulously photographs and catalogues them with detailed commentary, and presents them in online auctions. The first online auction is scheduled for the fall of 2025. column5: Minimal-invasive wastewater pipe interior lining solutions
column6: RG Rohrgroup GmbH is a specialized German engineering and services company focused on the trenchless, internal rehabilitation of wastewater pipes. This method is applied through existing openings in the plumbing system, which avoids the need for structural demolition, such as breaking open walls, floors, or ceilings. The technology is DIBt (German Institute for Building Technology) certified and is designed to be odorless, quiet, and less disruptive than traditional pipe replacement, allowing for rehabilitation to occur while buildings remain occupied. The company primarily serves commercial clients, including housing associations, property managers, hospitals, hotels, and rehabilitation clinics. It also provides services for private residential customers, particularly for pipes that are difficult to access. The business model has expanded to include a franchise system, launched in 2024, to facilitate growth. This model allows franchisees to operate under the Rohrgroup brand, utilizing its established business processes, training, marketing, and technology. column6: IotaOrigin UG, founded in Cologne, Germany in 2021, provides a web-enabled supply chain traceability solution for international trade in conflict-free minerals. The company developed a platform called "Hideless" which utilizes IOTA's distributed ledger technology (DLT) to help companies comply with international regulations such as the EU's Conflict Minerals Regulation (2017/821) and the OECD Due Diligence Guidance. This EU regulation, effective since January 1, 2021, mandates that EU importers of tin, tantalum, tungsten, and gold (3TG) ensure their materials are sourced responsibly and do not finance armed conflict. The startup, which originated from the University of Aachen, addresses the challenge of documenting the provenance of raw materials from conflict-affected and high-risk areas. IotaOrigin's application replaces paper-based systems, allowing all parties in the supply chain—from mines and exporters to importers and processors—to digitally record and verify the journey of minerals. The use of IOTA's Tangle network enables fee-free, secure, and transparent documentation. A key feature of the platform is its use of end-to-end encryption, which allows stakeholders to prove compliance and exchange necessary information without revealing sensitive trade secrets like pricing or volume. IotaOrigin's business model focuses on monetizing and optimizing supply chain data while offering digital and free traceability of goods. The platform aims to standardize and digitize trade, financing, and insurance within the largely undigitized mining sector. By ensuring a transparent and ethical supply chain, IotaOrigin helps create market access for small-scale miners and supports local communities, aligning with the UN's Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The company is also exploring solutions to integrate cryptocurrency payments to simplify international transactions, reduce fees, and support the objectives of the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI).
