column6: Constellations Petites Maisons Inc. is a company that designs and produces prefabricated modular homes with a focus on ecological responsibility and innovative design. Officially founded in 2021 by François Turgeon, the company is based in Lachute, Quebec. Turgeon, a multidisciplinary artist and yoga teacher, was inspired to create houses in isolated locations after renovating a lakeside cottage in 2016. Together with his partner Gaétan Serrigny, he developed the company's first product, the Kujuk ecopod, during the pandemic. Constellations emphasizes the use of local, eco-responsible materials, such as PurBond wood, and energy-efficient features like triple-glazed windows and optional structural insulated panels (SIPs) to create passive-house-level efficiency. This approach can reduce heating energy consumption by 50% to 80% compared to a conventional house. Constellations offers a range of customizable models, including the Arfan, Kujuk, and the family-oriented Lesah. The designs are noted for their intelligent use of space, inspired by van life and boat interiors, featuring multi-purpose countertops and smart storage solutions. The company serves a variety of clients, from individuals seeking a simplified lifestyle to businesses in the ecotourism sector like campgrounds and outfitters. They also assist clients with their real estate projects through a network of certified partners. In 2022, the company received recognition at the 24th Défi OSEntreprendre, winning awards at the local, regional, and national levels. column5: Organic waste processing for renewable energy generation
column6: Alimentary Systems is a New Zealand-based company that designs and builds integrated waste treatment plants to process organic waste, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and create renewable energy. The company was co-founded by Harmaan Madon and Matthew Jackson. Madon has a background in mechanical engineering, material science, and developing sustainable biofuels with Mercedes, while Jackson has experience with high-growth companies in New Zealand and Asia. The company's core product is the Bioenergy Resource Recovery Plant (BRRP), a system that treats various organic waste streams—including wastewater sludge, food waste, green waste, and agricultural byproducts—and converts them into bioenergy and other valuable outputs. The technology, which mimics a cow's digestive system, combines anaerobic digestion (AD) and thermal hydrolysis (TH) to process mixed waste materials. This approach aims to increase renewable energy output, reduce landfill waste, and lower waste disposal costs for clients. The process also recovers nutrients like phosphorus and nitrogen, creating organic fertilizers that improve soil health. Alimentary Systems operates on a circular economy business model. Its revenue streams are projected to come from the sales of bioenergy, organic fertilizers, and carbon credits. The company targets municipalities and industrial clients to help them achieve carbon neutrality and zero-waste goals. It has formed partnerships with waste management companies like SiteCare Limited and Smart Environmental's Betta Bins to tackle sewage sludge and food waste challenges in New Zealand. While currently pre-revenue, the company has secured grant funding and seed capital to scale its technology, with plans to develop a 10-tonne per day facility in Nelson, New Zealand. column5: P2P electric vehicle charging via blockchain payments
column6: Share&Charge, founded in Germany in 2016 by Dietrich Summermann, began as a peer-to-peer (P2P) electric vehicle charging platform utilizing blockchain technology. The system operated through a mobile app where users could locate and pay for charging using a blockchain-powered wallet with transactions handled in 'crypto-euros' backed 1:1 with real euros. The initial platform, a collaboration with Slock.it, used Ethereum's blockchain for secure and reliable transactions. By May 2017, the app launched on iOS and Android with over 1,000 charging stations registered in Germany, demonstrating the potential to significantly expand the country's charging infrastructure by leveraging privately owned stations. In March 2020, the Share&Charge Foundation launched the Open Charging Network (OCN), a decentralized e-roaming product for the European market based on the Open Charge Point Interface (OCPI) protocol. This network used a smart contract on the Energy Web Chain to route charging sessions between different service providers without a central intermediary. Another entity, operating as EV Sharecharge (sharecharge.io), is an electric mobility partner focused on building a widespread EV charging network, particularly in India. This company, owned by parent company Winet Infratel, offers B2C charging services at public locations like malls and hotels, and B2B solutions for businesses. column5: We're building foundational infrastructure that the entire golf ecosystem can plug into
column6: GolfAuth: Golf's Digital Trust InfrastructureGolfAuth is building the authentication and provenance layer for the $100 billion golf equipment industry - think Carfax meets digital identity, but for golf clubs.The Problem We're SolvingThere's a $1 billion hole in golf. Every year, 2+ million counterfeit golf clubs flood the market. But counterfeiting is just the visible symptom of a deeper problem: golf equipment exists in a complete data void.When a golfer buys a $600 driver, that transaction creates zero digital footprint. No provenance. No ownership record. No specification history. The club becomes invisible the moment it leaves the store. This creates cascading problems:- Golfers can't prove authenticity when selling, can't track what they own, lose clubs with no way to recover them- Retailers accept trade-ins blind - guessing at specs, condition, and fair value- Fitters start from scratch every session because fitting data isn't linked to equipment- OEMs have zero visibility into what happens after the first sale - no lifecycle data, no resale patterns, no way to protect their brand- The secondary market operates on trust and hope, with buyers paying premium prices for unverifiable authenticityAnd it's getting worse. AI is now enabling counterfeiters to create sophisticated fake websites in minutes and reverse-engineer club designs with increasing precision. Traditional defences - serial numbers, holograms, engravings - are easily replicated. They provide a false sense of security.What We're BuildingGolfAuth creates verified digital identities for golf equipment.Every club gets a "digital twin" - a permanent, immutable record that captures:- Provenance: Complete ownership chain from retailer to current owner- Authentication: Trust scores based on verified purchase history- Specifications: Shaft, lie angle, loft, grip - all permanently recorded- Fitting Data: Launch monitor results, performance metrics, modification history- Valuation: Real-time market value based on model, condition, and provenanceThe key innovation is how we build this network without friction.We don't require new hardware, NFC chips, or point-of-sale integrations. Instead, golfers create provenance themselves by uploading tyransactional information for a Trust Score. We recognise the manufacturer, the equipment, the retailer, and document to provenance and fractional data. This "golfer self-service" model removes the biggest barrier to adoption - we don't need to convince thousands of retailers to change their workflows. The network builds organically as golfers register their equipment.Why This Is Infrastructure, Not Just an App.GolfAuth isn't a consumer app that happens to authenticate clubs. We're building foundational infrastructure that the entire golf ecosystem can plug into:- OEMs can verify their products are authentic, run Certified Pre-Owned programs, and access lifecycle intelligence they've never had- Retailers become trusted verification points, offer premium trade-in services, and differentiate with authenticated used inventory- Fitters capture data permanently through GolfAuth Pro, building comprehensive client profiles that travel with the equipment- Golf Courses become "Lost & Found Heroes" - scanning found clubs and automatically reuniting them with owners- Marketplaces can integrate authentication via API, adding trust layers to secondhand transactions- Governing Bodies (Golf Australia, USGA, R&A) can embed GolfAuth as a member benefit, creating instant distribution at scaleNetwork effects are fundamental. Every authenticated club increases the value of the network for everyone. Every verified retailer makes the trust scores more meaningful. Every integration expands the ecosystem.

This collaboration aims to increase the utilization of existing charging infrastructure and provide a more seamless experience for drivers. zuup serves individual EV drivers as well as commercial fleets. For businesses, zuup Roam offers a centralized platform for managing all vehicle charging, providing features like consolidated monthly billing, driver and vehicle management, and RFID access cards for simple tap-and-go charging. column5: EV charging devices using existing lamppost infrastructure
column6: SimpleCharge is a Latvian startup founded in 2021 that develops and operates electric vehicle (EV) charging devices that can be installed on existing lamppost infrastructure. This approach allows businesses, communities, and individuals to adopt EV charging with minimal upfront investment. The company has partnered with charging point operator Eleport and has received support from EIT Urban Mobility to test and scale its business model. column5: Subscription-based organic waste collection for Philadelphia residents
column6: Circle Compost is a woman-owned Philadelphia-based company founded in 2016 by the husband-and-wife duo, Michele and Dave Bloovman. The company was born from their desire to reduce the amount of organic waste, such as food scraps and leaves, sent to landfills. Michele, a food scientist, and Dave, with a background in textile recycling, were inspired to start the business after Dave saw a chart at a 2015 conference showing that food scraps made up nearly 30% of landfill composition. They decided to create a localized, simple alternative for waste disposal, viewing it as a way to set a positive example for their two daughters. The business operates on a subscription-based model, offering weekly or bi-weekly curbside collection services for households, restaurants, cafes, schools, and offices in various Philadelphia neighborhoods. Customers are provided with a 2-gallon or 5-gallon bucket to collect their organic waste. Pricing for households is structured monthly, with different rates for weekly or bi-weekly pickups and options for bucket swaps or just having the bucket emptied. For its residential routes, the company utilizes a combination of e-bikes with trailers and trucks to minimize its carbon footprint. Commercial clients with larger volumes receive customized plans and pickups using trucks with liftgates. As of late 2023, the company services over 2,500 customers and composts more than 25 tons of food scraps monthly. The collected organic material is processed at partner urban farms, such as Novick Urban Farm, where it is turned into nutrient-rich compost. This finished compost is then used by local farms and gardens to grow healthy produce, closing the loop from table to farm. Circle Compost also offers seasonal services like Christmas tree and pumpkin recycling. In a significant development, Bennett Compost announced its acquisition of Circle Compost in December 2025, with the merger set to take effect in 2026. The move was initiated by Bloovman to create efficiencies and strengthen the local composting scene by eliminating route redundancies and combining forces. column5: Haptic feedback sensor glasses for the visually impaired
column6: LeadMe GmbH is a Vienna-based startup developing assistive technology for blind and visually impaired individuals. The company was co-founded by CEO Ing. Tobias Holzinger, MBA MSc, and CTO Dipl.-Ing. Thomas Scheu, BSc. The team also includes CCO Annalena Aumer and Marie-Agnes Arlt. The idea originated from a desire to solve the societal problem of blind individuals injuring themselves on obstacles that a traditional white cane cannot detect. Holzinger acts as the link between the technical and business aspects, while Scheu leverages his experience from the Institute for Material Science and Technology at TU Wien for prototype development. The core product is the LeadMe Sensor Glasses, designed to enhance mobility and safety for the visually impaired. These glasses look like conventional sunglasses to remain inconspicuous but are equipped with sensors that scan the user's surroundings. The system detects obstacles at head and chest height—such as tree branches, temporary signs, or truck ramps—which are common hazards missed by a long cane. Instead of audio alerts, the glasses provide real-time haptic feedback through actuators in the temples, allowing the user to "feel" the environment and avoid injury. This design choice consciously avoids camera systems to ensure real-time feedback, maintain user privacy, and guarantee a long battery life. LeadMe develops its product in close collaboration with visually impaired people to ensure it meets their specific needs. The company aims to offer an affordable and user-friendly solution compared to other available technologies that are often expensive or conspicuous. LeadMe has established a key partnership with the Hilfsgemeinschaft der Blinden und Sehschwachen Österreichs (Austrian Association in Support of the Blind and Visually Impaired) and is part of the Impact Hub Vienna community. The company holds patent number 524252 for its technology. column6: Principia MBS GmbH provides a cloud-native multibody simulation (MBS) solution designed specifically for the Onshape computer-aided design (CAD) platform. The company's mission is to become a leading provider of cloud-native MBS tools, aiming to streamline the design validation process for engineers. The project started in 2023, with the company's origins tracing back to a conversation in 2021. This integration enables engineers to validate complex designs virtually, determining loads and analyzing various quantities before physical prototypes are built. The platform's features include a modern web-based user interface, CAD-simulation model synchronization, bidirectional data flow for efficient iterations, and a simulation archive for version control. By using cloud-based numerical solvers, the solution aims to shorten waiting times for simulation results. The company states its tool can help customers save up to 75% of their time in the design validation process. The business model is based on providing the software as a service (SaaS). Principia MBS serves engineers across various industries, including robotics, automotive, agricultural technology, and aerospace. The company engages with potential customers through live demos to discuss challenges and demonstrate the software's capabilities. A notable use case involved the 3D printer manufacturer Incus, which utilized Principia MBS to optimize the product development process for its Hammer Pro40 metal 3D printer by calculating motor torque and assembly movement. column5: Decentralized carbon capture and biomass valorization technology
column6: Beaver Nexus operates in the cleantech and agtech sectors, focusing on decentralized carbon capture and biomass valorization. The company has developed a patented, mobile pyrolysis system known as the Transportable Wood Reactor (TWR). This technology is engineered to convert agricultural and forestry residues directly on-site into biochar and pyroligneous acid (PA), which is also known as wood vinegar. The core of their offering is the TWR, a modular reactor that utilizes advanced thermal decomposition. Its processes are optimized by AI to ensure a clean and low-emission solution, specifically designed for managing biomass in remote and rural areas. By using this system, farmers, forest operators, and landowners can transform waste materials into valuable products. The biochar produced sequesters carbon for long periods while improving soil fertility and water retention. Simultaneously, the pyroligneous acid is being developed as a natural biopesticide and plant biostimulant. This dual-output creates a regenerative system that supports sustainable agriculture and contributes to climate action. Beaver Nexus's business model intersects cleantech, agtech, and carbon finance. The company enables its clients to generate carbon credits that are certified under recognized standards, providing an additional revenue stream. They partner with research institutions, municipalities, and industrial entities to validate the impact of their technology, ensure compliance with standards such as those in the EU, and scale their systems for global distribution. column5: Reducing consumer food waste through community-based events
column6: Taste Before You Waste is an Amsterdam-based non-profit foundation established in November 2012 with a mission to combat consumer food waste. column5: Efficient thermophotovoltaic panels converting heat to electricity
column6: Heat2Power (H2P) is a startup launched in 2024 that develops and designs highly efficient thermophotovoltaic (TPV) panels that generate electricity from high-temperature heat sources. The company’s core product is a modular, solid-state panel based on patented air-bridge TPV technology, which converts heat to power at scales ranging from kilowatts to megawatts. This technology is designed to be paired with high-temperature thermal energy storage (TES) systems, providing an economical way to recycle waste heat and add on-demand capabilities to renewable energy sources like wind and solar. The company was co-founded by an interdisciplinary team from the University of Michigan, including Professor Stephen Forrest, who serves as CEO, and Professor Andrej Lenert, the Chief Scientist. Forrest is a recognized leader in optoelectronics and a seasoned entrepreneur, having founded five companies. Lenert brings extensive experience in TPV energy conversion and leads a lab at the university focused on the technology. Heat2Power’s technology was developed over years of research at the University of Michigan, with key breakthroughs including a 32% efficient cell in 2020 and a record 44% efficiency in 2024. The startup was launched with assistance from Innovation Partnerships and received early-stage venture funding from the Accelerate Blue Fund in January 2025. Heat2Power's TPV panels function similarly to solar cells but are engineered to convert infrared radiation from heat into electricity. The proprietary air-bridge design improves efficiency by recycling unabsorbed photons, allowing the cells to operate across a wide temperature range (900-2000ºC). This makes the technology suitable for various heat sources, including industrial waste heat, thermal batteries, and modular nuclear reactors. The panels directly harvest radiation, eliminating the need for intermediate heat exchangers. The company serves industrial clients, factories, data centers, and grid operators by providing a low-cost alternative to fossil fuels for continuous or on-demand power. By storing intermittent renewable energy as heat and converting it back to electricity when needed, the system aids in grid stabilization through time-shifting and demand response. column6: BioSam Inc. is a Canadian AgTech company founded in 2022 by CEO Dr. Meysam Taghinasab and COO Dr. Mahsa Alimi. column5: Community-owned infrastructure for energy, food, and livelihood
column6: OakTREE Initiative is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization based in Oakland, California, that develops community-owned and governed infrastructure to address local needs for energy, food, and economic opportunity. The organization was founded when Crystal Huang and Miles reviewing their respective work in community-centered solutions and decided to merge their parallel paths into a shared vision. Crystal's background is in building the People Power Solar Cooperative, where she focused on creating a just transition to renewable energy through community ownership. Miles' work concentrated on redesigning energy architectures, like thermal microgrids, to be compatible with and beneficial for economically challenged communities. The core of OakTREE's strategy is the development of what it calls "inter-structure," a model that combines physical infrastructure with social interdependence to foster self-reliance and resilience. This model facilitates the creation of neighborhood-scale, modular systems such as thermal microgrids, Closed Cycle Greenhouses (CCGs), and community e-kitchens. The thermal microgrids connect buildings in a network to share heating and cooling from aggregated sources like solar thermal panels and heat pumps, reducing costs and reliance on external utilities. CCGs provide local, low-emission food production, with their excess heat being repurposed into the thermal microgrid, creating a symbiotic energy and food system. These physical assets are intended to be the foundation for human connection, shared responsibility, and local economic activity. OakTREE's business model is multifaceted. As a nonprofit, it has secured over $4 million in funding from public institutions and philanthropic partners. It also generates revenue through commercial applications, offering "Heat-as-a-Service" (HaaS) to businesses; this revenue is then used to help finance community installations. The organization serves underserved neighborhoods, starting in Oakland, working directly with residents to design and implement systems that they will own, govern, and maintain. This approach includes workforce cultivation, training local residents in the skills needed to build and sustain the infrastructure, and fostering entrepreneurial development to create local jobs and enterprises. column5: Processed and packaged traditional Angolan organic foods
column6: FoodCare Lda is an Angolan food processing and packaging company founded in 2020 by Marlene José. After gaining experience in various manufacturing industries, José launched FoodCare in 2019 as a pilot project to promote Angolan cuisine and create economic opportunities for local farmers. The company officially registered as a private limited company in 2020. José's background includes studies in International Relations and supply chains in Portugal, an executive training in Emerging Markets at Harvard University, and participation in the Founder Institute Luanda startup accelerator. FoodCare addresses food safety and accessibility issues by processing and packaging traditional, nutrient-rich Angolan products that are often otherwise restricted to informal markets due to contamination during processing. The company operates under the brand name "mavu," which means "earth" in the Kimbundu language. Its product line includes processed and packaged items like cassava leaves (Kizaca/Pondu), pumpkin seeds (Egusi), mushrooms, mopane worms, peanut butter, and various flours. These products are certified by HACCP and the U.S. FDA, which enables the company to serve both local and international markets. The company's business model focuses on adding value to local agricultural products, thereby reducing food waste and supporting the entire agri-food value chain, including small-scale farmers, transporters, and distributors. FoodCare supports farmers in transitioning to more sustainable practices, such as solar-based irrigation systems. Revenue is generated through sales in major Angolan supermarkets like Hypermarket Kero, e-commerce deliveries via its website, and exports. As of November 2025, 95% of its products are exported to markets in Europe, North America, and other African countries, including Congo, Namibia, and Kenya. To overcome previous production limitations, FoodCare secured a private credit investment from BFA Asset Management's Kimbo Fund in late 2025 to scale its capacity and meet significant international demand. The proposed product, a novel composite material, is engineered by developing bacteria that can produce both synthetic spider silk and calcite, the primary component of limestone. The goal is to create a material with comparable strength to conventional bricks but with a much smaller environmental footprint. The technical approach involves designing and harmonizing a synthetic gene for pyriform spider silk (pysp1), which is then used in bacterial cultures for protein production and subsequent biocementation processes. column5: Organic fertilizer from brewery byproducts for agriculture
column6: BrewCycle is an Austrian agri-tech startup that transforms brewery byproducts into sustainable, organic fertilizers. BrewCycle collects this beer waste, such as brewer's spent grain (BSG), and transports it to a university laboratory for analysis. Since different beers yield varying nutrient profiles, the waste is analyzed and then enhanced to stabilize and improve its nutrient content. The final product is a 100% organic fertilizer suitable for both conventional and organic farming. Tests conducted on corn seeds have shown the fertilizer's performance to be comparable to conventional fertilizers, with the added benefits of improved soil fertility and disease resistance due to its micronutrient content. BrewCycle generates revenue through the direct sale of its fertilizer to farmers. The target market includes farmers seeking high-quality, affordable alternatives to traditional fertilizers. By offering a product that is competitive in both performance and price, the company provides a dual benefit: it helps brewers reduce waste disposal costs and their environmental footprint, while supplying farmers with a sustainable product that can enhance crop yields. The startup has established partnerships with 7sternbräu for its supply of beer waste and with omni.farm for real-world product testing, both of which have reported positive outcomes. BrewCycle plans to expand its operations by partnering with more breweries and entering new markets within and beyond Austria. The company's business-to-business model targets builders and construction professionals, offering a sustainable alternative to conventional materials without compromising on performance or safety. column6: Fluff Stuff Oy is a Finnish textile technology company established in 2022, operating from Helsinki. The firm focuses on creating environmentally friendly, plant-based materials designed to replace traditional down and feather fillings in the textile, interior, and clothing industries. The company was co-founded by Tea Auramo and Amir Tahvonen, both alumni of Aalto University's Creative Sustainability master's program. Their collaboration stems from a shared vision of shifting the textile industry towards renewable, plant-based resources. Tea Tehilah Auramo also serves as the company's CEO. Fluff Stuff's core product is a premium textile filling derived from the seed hairs of the cattail plant. This material is processed to compete with conventional down in quality and performance, offering softness, insulation, and fluffiness. The company highlights cattail as a readily available, invasive, and perennial plant that can be cultivated in wetland areas, such as peatlands, contributing to nutrient capture from urban runoff. Utilizing cattail also presents an ethical and potentially more cost-effective alternative to traditional down production. Operating on a business-to-business model, Fluff Stuff targets manufacturers in the textile and apparel sectors as its primary clients. The company provides the filling material for integration into products requiring insulation and softness. Having participated in the Kiuas Accelerator program, the company is currently in a piloting and proof-of-concept phase, seeking to partner with textile brands focused on sustainable transformation. column5: Sewage sludge carbonization producing biochar and syngas
column6: Orbital Biocarbon is an infrastructure company that develops, finances, owns, and operates regional facilities for sewage sludge disposal. The company, founded in 2022 by President John Day, was established to address disposal capacity constraints and rising costs for wastewater utilities, particularly in the U.S. Northeast. Day, an entrepreneur in energy, water, and clean-technology, has a background in developing and financing major infrastructure projects, including the award-winning microgrid at Pittsburgh International Airport. He is joined by co-founder Thomas Hurkmans, an entrepreneur with experience in starting and growing over 30 companies in the energy and clean technology sectors. The company's business model centers on providing long-term, contracted disposal capacity for wastewater utilities and their haulers. Orbital Biocarbon's revenue is generated primarily from sludge tipping fees, which account for nearly three-quarters of its income. Additional revenue streams include the sale of biochar (approximately 25%) and a small percentage from carbon credits. This model allows utilities to stabilize disposal costs and avoid the risks associated with public financing and facility operation. Orbital Biocarbon utilizes a carbonization technology from the German company PYREG to transform sewage sludge into valuable products. The process involves drying the sludge and then heating it in an oxygen-free reactor, which breaks down contaminants like PFAS, pathogens, and microplastics. This thermal decomposition creates two main outputs: a hydrogen-rich synthesis gas (syngas) and biochar. The syngas is used to generate thermal energy that is recycled back into the system, reducing the need for external fuel sources. The resulting biochar is a stable, carbon-rich material that can be sold for various applications, including land remediation, agriculture, and as a partial replacement for industrial products like coal and cement. The technology has been verified by the U.S. EPA for its ability to destroy PFAS contaminants. The company is developing its first facility in the Pittsburgh area, projected to be operational by mid-2027, with plans to expand throughout the Northeast. In December 2025, Orbital secured a significant investment led by Toby Z. Rice, President and CEO of EQT Corporation, to accelerate its project development. column5: Traditionally made, chemical-free organic foods from India
column6: Gyros Organic Farms is a clean-food brand founded in August 2022 by Yogesh Tyagi, Richa Singh Chandel, Pratik Mishra, Aditya Thakur, and Aakash Chaudhary. The company emerged during the COVID-19 pandemic from the founders' realization of how industrialized and adulterated everyday essential foods had become. Richa Singh Chandel, a biology graduate, was particularly intrigued by the decline in immune response and the link between refined oils and cardiovascular ailments, which led her to explore traditional, authentic food production methods. The company operates on a B2C, B2B, and B2B2C business model, rejecting centralized factory production in favor of a decentralized network of micro-units run by rural women and smallholder farmers. This model aims to empower micro-farmers by providing resources, training, and direct market access, ensuring them a stable income. The business is rooted in a belief that purity in food should come from hands, not machines. Gyros Organic Farms operates micro-units in several Indian states, including Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Gujarat, and Rajasthan, to produce small-batch, chemical-free essentials. The product line includes A2 Bilona Cow Ghee made with traditional hand-churning, hand-ground spices, and stone cold-pressed oils. The oils, such as sesame, groundnut, and coconut, are extracted using a traditional method with wooden plungers and a stone base at low temperatures to preserve nutrients and flavor. The company guarantees freshness by dispatching all products to customers across India within 14 days of preparation. Following a recent funding round in late 2025, Gyros plans to establish more micro-units, support more farmers, and expand its product categories to include pulses, jaggery, flours, and honey. column5: Community renewable energy platform connecting local producers
column6: Northern Power & Light (NP&L) is a Distributed Energy Resources Provider that connects local renewable energy producers, primarily small-scale hydro, with residents and businesses in New York. The company was founded in 2018 by brothers Ethan and Emmett Smith and Louise Gava, stemming from a multi-generational family involvement in Adirondack hydroelectric power projects since the 1970s. The founders' family, the Smiths and Foleys, operated small hydro businesses, and the launch of NP&L was spurred by changes in New York's electricity market and the rollout of the state's Community Renewables program. The business operates on a model similar to a farmers' market, creating a platform where local renewable energy producers can sell directly to consumers. This structure aims to provide producers with a better rate for the power they generate, helping them remain viable against fossil fuel energy producers without increasing costs for customers. NP&L manages the connection with the utility, billing, and customer service to facilitate a direct link between consumers and local renewable energy sources like hydro, solar, and wind. Customers, who are typically National Grid users, can sign up to contract directly with a specific local producer. While the electricity is pooled in the grid, this model allows customers to choose who generates the power on their behalf. The service is designed to have no additional cost compared to standard utility service. In November 2025, Northern Power & Light was acquired by Solar Simplified, a national community solar subscriber aggregation and management company. The all-cash acquisition was aimed at expanding Solar Simplified's footprint in New York by integrating NP&L's subscriber network and project portfolio. As part of the acquisition, founders Emmett and Ethan Smith joined the Solar Simplified team to continue growing the NP&L business line. column5: In-orbit megawatt-class fusion power for space industry
column6: Zephyr Fusion is developing an in-orbit, megawatt-class fusion power source to facilitate large-scale industrial activities in space. The company was founded by Dr. Galen Burke and Dr. Edward Hinson, who serve as co-founders. Both founders have PhDs in Nuclear Engineering and Engineering Physics and accumulated over 35 years of combined experience in experimental fusion research at institutions like Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison. They have been collaborators since their time in graduate school in 2010. Zephyr Fusion aims to address the power limitations of satellites, which typically operate on kilowatt-scale solar power, constraining high-power applications in orbit. The company's solution is a compact magnetic confinement system that leverages the vacuum of space, allowing for a dipole magnetic confinement device to create the large plasma confinement regions needed for fusion without requiring bulky reactor hardware. This approach is made viable by recent advancements in high-temperature superconductors (HTS) and significantly lower launch costs. The technology is designed to provide megawatt-class power at a fraction of the cost of equivalent solar arrays, potentially catalyzing a new space economy that includes large-scale industry, in-orbit data centers, and high-power electrical propulsion. The company is a Y Combinator participant and is seeking introductions to satellite, defense, and other teams with an interest in megawatt-class power in orbit. column6: Raptrac AG is a Swiss agricultural technology company focused on developing solutions for sustainable and regenerative farming. column6: WEnCoop operates as the first energy cooperative in Greece and Europe established for and by women entrepreneurs. Initiated by the Greek Association of Women Entrepreneurs (SEGE), a non-governmental organization founded in 1997 to support businesswomen in Greece, WEnCoop was officially established in June 2021. The statutes were signed by 60 founding female members, and the cooperative has since grown to include 66 members. The cooperative was spearheaded by Apostolina Tsaltampasi, who serves as the President of both WEnCoop and its initiating body, SEGE. Tsaltampasi is also the founder and CEO of the business consultancy OECON Group and has a long history of advocating for female entrepreneurship, earning her the title of Female Entrepreneurship Ambassador from the European Commission in 2010. Her vision was to create a vehicle for women, regardless of their background, to participate in the green energy transition, gain energy independence, and implement sustainable practices in their businesses. The business model is centered on collective action in the energy sector. WEnCoop develops and operates renewable energy projects, allowing its members—who are women entrepreneurs from diverse sectors such as crafts, farming, services, commerce, and tourism—to become active participants, or "prosumers," in the energy market. By pooling resources, members can collectively finance and benefit from clean energy production. This structure aims to reduce operational costs for their individual businesses through lower energy expenses and generate income, thereby increasing their financial resilience. The cooperative operates a 1MW solar power plant in Kassandreia, Chalkidiki, and has plans to develop three additional photovoltaic parks. The produced energy is intended for member consumption, with future applications potentially including electric mobility. A portion of the profits is also reinvested into the community, with a focus on supporting vulnerable groups. The primary service is the production, storage, and supply of clean energy for its members. A key benefit for the members is achieving energy self-sufficiency and cost reduction, which would be difficult to attain individually. Beyond the financial advantages, WEnCoop focuses on education and empowerment, having provided training on energy efficiency to over 500 women. The cooperative also aims to tackle energy poverty and promote social solidarity, positioning itself as a replicable model for other regions. column6: Books Beyond Borders is a Singapore-based social enterprise that operates a bookstore selling second-hand books to fund educational projects for girls in Nepal. The company was founded by Randall Chong, who was inspired to act after a solo backpacking trip to Nepal in 2017, where he witnessed children, particularly young girls, working instead of attending school. This experience led him to leave his job and dedicate himself to raising money for education in Nepal. The enterprise started modestly, with Chong initially selling his own used books on the online marketplace Carousell and collecting donations from friends. It began operating out of his grandfather's spare bedroom before moving to a warehouse and eventually opening a physical retail location. The primary business model involves collecting and selling gently used books donated by the public. The company maintains stringent quality checks for its book donations. In addition to its main bookstore at Maxwell, Books Beyond Borders runs warehouse sales and roving pop-up stores to make the books more accessible. To encourage donations, the store offers a discount voucher to individuals who drop off five or more books. The company's social mission is central to its operations. A portion of sales is allocated to its 'Girl Scholarship Programme', which provides full scholarships for girls in rural Nepal to complete their grade 11 and 12 education. This intervention is critical, as many girls drop out after grade 10 due to the high cost of relocating to a city for further education, trapping them in a cycle of poverty. Since its inception, Books Beyond Borders has contributed over S$40,000 to various educational programs, including classroom projects, scholarships, and the establishment of school libraries. The business has rehomed over 20,000 books. Expanding its social impact, Books Beyond Borders launched a sister brand, Two Storytellers, in 2024. This brand offers ethically made, handcrafted gifts, such as wool toys and journals, made by over 50 artisan women in Nepal. This initiative provides a sustainable income for these women, many of whom are mothers, empowering them to support their families and keep their children in school. column5: Biotech startup pioneering in vitro marine ecotoxicity testing to help industries develop products that are safer for marine ecosystems
column6: INNOV&SEA, established in early 2023, is a spin-off from the University Côte d'Azur, operating from Nice, France. The company was co-founded by a team of four with deep scientific and business experience: Dr. Pauline Cotinat (President), Emmanuel Michelot (Business Development Manager), Dr. Stéphanie Barnay-Verdier (Scientific Expert), and Prof. Paola Furla (Scientific Expert). The foundation of their work stems from years of research at the Nice Institute for Research on Cancer and Ageing (IRCAN), where the team pioneered a method for culturing cells from the sea anemone, *Anemonia viridis*, in 2013. This research background in marine invertebrate stress response, cell biology, and Cnidarian physiology forms the scientific core of the company. The firm provides the chemical and cosmetics industries with a specialized service to assess the ecological impact of their products on marine life. Revenue is generated by performing these ecotoxicity tests for clients, who range from raw material manufacturers to formulators of finished products like sunscreens. The business model centers on offering a non-animal testing alternative that aligns with growing consumer demand for sustainable products and corporate eco-design goals. The company's services have attracted around twenty clients across France and Europe. INNOV&SEA's core offering is the 'Viridis' test, an *in vitro* ecotoxicity analysis using cell cultures from the sea anemone and its symbiotic algae. This method stands out as it assesses cytotoxicity on both the animal cells and their photosynthetic partners, providing a more holistic view of potential harm. The technology is the culmination of eight years of lab research supported by institutions like CNRS and Sorbonne University. A key differentiator is its non-invasive nature, which complies with the "3R" principles (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) by avoiding the use of live animals, an approach that is often more costly and complex. Clients receive precise and reproducible results in under 20 days, enabling them to evaluate everything from individual ingredients, like UV filters, to the final product formulation as it would enter the marine environment. This allows brands to obtain an "Eco-Score" to validate and guide the eco-design of their products. column5: Laser-based dissolved gas analysis for power transformers
column6: Mayak Oy is a Finnish company specializing in the development and manufacturing of online monitoring systems for power transformers. Founded in Helsinki in 2023, the company's primary product is the Laser DGA, an innovative device for online Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA). DGA is a critical method for assessing the health of power transformers by analyzing gases dissolved in the transformer's insulating oil, which can indicate potential faults. The company's core technology combines tunable diode laser absorption spectroscopy (TDLAS) with vacuum gas extraction to provide highly accurate and selective measurements of various fault gases, including carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, methane, and acetylene. This TDLAS-based approach offers significant advantages over traditional methods like non-dispersive infrared (NDIR) or photoacoustic spectroscopy (PAS), as it is not susceptible to cross-sensitivities from other volatile organic compounds in the oil, ensuring more reliable diagnostics. The system is designed for maintenance-free operation and does not require consumables like calibration or carrier gases. The development of the Laser DGA began in 2020 by a team with deep expertise in optics, electronics design, and applied laser spectroscopy, who had previously worked on projects such as TDLAS for the European ExoMars mission and remote sensing of greenhouse gases. Mayak Oy serves clients in the power and utilities sector, providing them with tools to prevent unexpected transformer failures, reduce maintenance costs, and enhance grid reliability. The company's business model centers on selling this high-tech hardware and associated software. The Laser DGA system has been tested in a pilot project on a 500 kV substation transformer, and the company is now producing small batches for certification and further pilot programs. column5: The Best Electric Cargo Bike | CERO Bikes – Los Angeles, California
column6: Cero Bikes was a Los Angeles-based company founded in 2016 by Kiyoshi Iwai and Sawako Iwai, which ceased operations in early 2025. Kiyoshi Iwai, a UCLA MBA from the Tokyo area, was motivated by a passion for the environment and a desire to offer a solution to the car-centric culture of Los Angeles. The company's name, 'Cero,' is derived from the Spanish word for 'zero,' reflecting its mission of zero-emission, sustainable transportation. The company's sole product was the Cero One, a compact electric cargo bike. Its design was inspired by the Japanese 'Mamachari' utility bicycle, reimagined for modern urban use. The development of the Cero One was a collaboration with veteran bicycle engineers Forrest Yelverton and Zach Krapfl, both previously with GT Bicycles. Initial funding was secured through a successful Indiegogo campaign in 2017, which raised approximately $25,000, enabling the first production batch. The business operated on a direct-to-consumer model via its website, though it was also building a network of specialty e-bike dealers. The Cero One was marketed to urban commuters and families as a car replacement for daily errands, capable of transporting everything from groceries to children. A key feature was its modular cargo system with front and rear racks, each supporting up to 55 lbs, and compatible with various baskets and accessories, including child seats. A distinctive design choice was the use of a smaller 20-inch front wheel and a larger 26-inch rear wheel, intended to lower the center of gravity and improve stability and maneuverability. The bike was equipped with high-quality components, including a Shimano STEPS mid-drive motor (initially the E6050 and later the E6100 model) and a 504Wh removable battery, offering a range of up to 105 miles. Later generations of the Cero One featured upgrades such as a Gates Carbon Drive belt and a 5-speed internally geared hub, reducing maintenance needs. The bike was classified as a Class 1 e-bike, providing pedal assist up to 20 mph. Despite its innovative design and winning a EUROBIKE Gold Award, the company faced a cash flow crisis due to market overstock following the pandemic-driven production increase, leading to its closure. column5: Frugal innovation for fair global water distribution
column6: Vitru Water is a German startup focused on resolving economic water scarcity in developing regions through demand-based distribution of the essential resource. The company was co-founded by Yannick Beyer, David Walter, and Katrin Trautwein. The founding team's journey is rooted in academic research and hands-on fieldwork. Walter and Trautwein, who studied civil engineering together, gained practical experience during a water project in Indonesia for their bachelor's thesis and by building a suspension bridge in Sri Lanka with the group Engineers without Borders. The core concept for Vitru Water emerged from a BMBF research project at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT), where Walter and Trautwein worked on implementing a new type of water supply system for 10,000 people in northern Vietnam. Recognizing that the research-based solutions were too complex for the open market, they decided to develop a more streamlined version. Beyer, a childhood friend of Walter, joined the team, contributing his expertise in innovation and business management. Vitru Water's business is centered on tackling economic water scarcity, a situation where sufficient water is available but existing supply systems fail to distribute it adequately, a common issue in tropical developing regions. This often leads to unfair distribution, conflicts, and system failures. The company's primary clients are governments and project partners in the Global South. Rather than focusing on profit maximization, the company operates with a strong purpose-driven approach. The main product is 'Vitruvio', a simple, robust, and low-maintenance tank-based solution designed to be installed at junctions within existing water supply systems. Vitruvio enables a fair division of water based on regional needs through a radial weir overflow mechanism that requires no active operation once set up. This prevents conflicts and allows communities to manage water distribution themselves, ensuring a reliable, long-term supply. A pilot system based on this concept, implemented between 2015 and 2020 in Northern Vietnam, already provides a fair water supply to approximately 10,000 people. The company has secured funding for projects in Assam, India, with the first scheduled to start in September 2024, aiming to bring its first commercial products into operation in 2025. column5: National gift card for Dutch thrift stores
column6: Nationale Kringloopbon provides a national gift card redeemable at thrift stores across the Netherlands, targeting both individual consumers and businesses. This structure was chosen to navigate the legal complexities of a universal gift card. The company generates revenue by taking a commission or percentage from the transactions with partner stores. column5: Data-driven finance and compliance automation for agriculture
column6: Regeno is a financial technology company focused on the agricultural sector in the United Kingdom, providing data-driven tools to facilitate the transition to regenerative farming practices. The company was founded by Sven Poppelmann, who serves as CEO and has a background in both farming and technology, including experience at Farmdrop connecting ethical food producers with consumers. He is joined by CTO Alan Cole and Founders Associate James Harrop. Regeno's core offering is a platform that simplifies farm compliance and unlocks financial benefits for farmers. A key feature is the AI-powered 'Farmwalk' tool, which allows farmers to capture photos, videos, and notes during their regular farm inspections. The AI automatically tags and files this evidence for various compliance schemes like the Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI), Countryside Stewardship (CS), and Red Tractor, saving significant administrative time. This collected data is then used to generate a 'RegenScore,' a proprietary metric from 0-100 that quantifies a farm's regenerative practices. A higher RegenScore can unlock better interest rates and cashback rewards on loans through Regeno's network of partner lenders. The company acts as an introducer to these lenders, earning fees from successful loan arrangements. Beyond its compliance and finance tools for individual farmers, Regeno also provides a management platform for land agents and consultants to oversee multiple client farms from a single dashboard. The company has a strong focus on data security and is certified as 'Farm Data Safe,' ensuring farmers retain ownership and control over their data. Regeno also engages the wider community through initiatives like 'Adopt-a-Hectare' and a 'Farm Funding Marketplace', which allow individuals and investors to directly support farmers transitioning to regenerative agriculture. The company's stated mission is to regenerate 1 million hectares of UK farmland by 2030. column5: Converting agricultural waste into bio-based chemicals.
column6: Aurelia Innovations is a clean technology startup that has developed a proprietary process to convert lignocellulosic biomass, such as agricultural waste, into fermentable sugars and high-purity lignin. The primary outputs are essential building block chemicals for Sustainable Aviation Fuels (SAFs) and other biofuels, as well as bioplastics. column5: B2C marketplace for second hand, refurbished and upcycled kids products
column6: Tildi, operating under the legal name Prowd GmbH, is a Munich-based company founded in 2023 that functions as a technology platform for the circular economy, with a specific focus on the kids' segment. The company was established by co-founders Sofie Morber and Doris Schoger, who were later joined by Rohith Premachandran as co-founder and CTO in 2024. The idea for Tildi originated from the founders' personal experiences as mothers and aunts, combined with a strong interest in recommerce. Sofie Morber's journey began when she sought high-quality second-hand online options for her daughter and couldn't find a suitable solution. Doris Schoger brought industry insight from her background running a recommerce-focused blog, which is how she and Morber connected. Tildi provides a comprehensive technology and logistics infrastructure for brands and retailers, enabling them to participate in the resale market without having to build their own systems from scratch. The business model is multifaceted, offering services that include an online marketplace, a "Resale-as-a-Service" solution, and trade-in programs. For its B2B clients—brands, retailers, and professional resellers—Tildi offers solutions to handle returns, overstock, refurbished goods, and B-stock by managing grading, digitization, and resale through its fulfillment infrastructure. This allows brands to extend their products' lifecycle and tap into a growing secondary market. The company also operates a direct-to-consumer marketplace where families can purchase a wide array of quality-checked second-hand items for children, including clothing, toys, strollers, and books. The platform serves two primary client types: families looking for affordable and sustainable products for their children, and business partners aiming to integrate circular practices. Revenue is generated by facilitating sales on its marketplace and through its service offerings to brands. For consumers, Tildi offers a convenient way to trade in used items, while for brands, it provides various partnership models, such as a white-label trade-in solution that can be integrated into their own shops, or simply connecting their existing stores to the Tildi marketplace via APIs. This dual approach positions Tildi as a key enabler of circular commerce in the children's product sector, aiming to make recommerce profitable and sustainable for all parties involved. column6: PlanMyKids is a FamTech startup simplifying the organization and booking of extracurricular activities for busy families. Founded in 2020 by David Watkins, PlanMyKids was inspired by the struggle many parents face when trying to manage and coordinate children’s enrichment activities amidst busy schedules. PlanMyKids provides a comprehensive solution to alleviate this cognitive overload, especially for working parents juggling career and family life.Mission and VisionPlanMyKids empowers parents by offering an intuitive, AI-powered platform that assists in planning, booking, and managing their kids' activities. Our goal is to become the go-to service for family activity management, serving as a bridge between families and activity providers.The ProblemPlanning activities for children is a daunting task, especially for mothers who often carry the bulk of this responsibility. Over 40% of parents report stress from managing their children’s activities. Traditional tools—like spreadsheets and manual searches—are inefficient, causing frustration and limiting access to suitable programs, particularly for kids with unique needs.Solution: A Concierge-Like MarketplacePlanMyKids offers an AI-enhanced digital concierge, My Itinerary Assistant (MIA), which personalizes the experience for each family. With PlanMyKids, parents can:Share Preferences: Parents complete a short survey outlining family preferences and each child’s interests.Receive Curated Options: The platform curates and updates a list of activities, enabling collaboration with other caregivers.Stay Organized: Parents can access bookings, schedules, and important details via a mobile-friendly app, reducing missed activities and increasing confidence.This streamlined process reduces the time and stress involved in activity planning, providing parents with a reliable and supportive tool.Market OpportunityPlanMyKids operates in the $30 billion U.S. market for children’s extracurricular activities, such as camps and afterschool programs, with demand driven by the needs of over 28 million children ages 5-12. Additionally, PlanMyKids aligns with the growing FamTech industry, as families increasingly seek tech solutions to manage daily responsibilities.Business Model and Revenue StreamsPlanMyKids connects parents with activity providers in a marketplace model. Revenue comes from commission on bookings and subscription options for parents. Providers benefit from expanded reach without needing new infrastructure, as PlanMyKids integrates with existing camp and class management systems.Competitive AdvantagePlanMyKids stands out as a productivity tool for parents, contrasting with basic directory services or manual methods like search and spreadsheets. By integrating with popular management software for providers, the platform offers a seamless onboarding experience and advanced personalization for families.Traction and Early SuccessPlanMyKids has made significant progress with its MVP, helping over 300 parents plan $400,000 in activities. Testimonials reveal that parents value the time savings, while providers appreciate the performance-based revenue model that reduces upfront marketing expenses.Why Now?Demand for solutions like PlanMyKids has grown as work-care balance becomes increasingly essential. COVID underscored the need for tools that support families, and parents are actively seeking technological assistance for daily responsibilities. PlanMyKids is well-timed to capture market share in the expanding FamTech sector.Future PlansTo accelerate growth, PlanMyKids is seeking a $475,000 pre-seed investment, with funds allocated toward key hires, product development, and marketing. Plans include expanding to new regions, integrating with more camp management systems, and enhancing the capabilities of MIA.PlanMyKids provides a much-needed service for modern families, streamlining the process of finding, planning, and attending children’s activities. With a clear roadmap and strong early traction, PlanMyKids is positioned to become a leader in family activity management and a trusted resource for parents across the U.S.

column6: Specializing in the complex cultivation of microbes and microbial communities, OPE Group is a biotechnology firm originating from Delft Technical University. column6: The National Energy System Operator (NESO), formerly National Grid ESO, is a publicly owned corporation responsible for operating Great Britain's electricity transmission network. It was legally separated from its parent company, National Grid plc, in 2019 and was fully nationalised via a £630m government acquisition in October 2024 to address potential conflicts of interest and to better steer the country's energy strategy. NESO is chaired by Paul Golby with Fintan Slye as its CEO.The organisation's core function is to balance the nation's electricity supply and demand on a second-by-second basis, ensuring the system's frequency remains stable at 50Hz to prevent power failures. It does not own any generation assets or physical infrastructure but directs electricity flow from generators across the high-voltage transmission network to regional distribution network operators. NESO's responsibilities are expanding to include strategic, long-term planning for both electricity and gas systems, integrating new energy sources like hydrogen and carbon capture to support the UK's net-zero emissions goal.As part of its evolving role, NESO is developing new markets and services to manage system stability as more intermittent renewable energy sources connect to the grid. Initiatives include the Demand Flexibility Service, which incentivises consumers to shift energy use away from peak times, and the Open Balancing Platform, a new system to dispatch power from battery storage and smaller units more efficiently. column5: Patented, carbon-negative, hemp-based interlocking building panels
column6: Sativa Building Systems, founded in 2018 by Zach Popp, develops and manufactures sustainable, hemp-based construction materials. The founder's journey began after his infant daughter became ill due to black mold, prompting him to seek non-toxic, mold-resistant building alternatives. With a background in construction, Popp researched hempcrete, a material popular in Europe known for being non-toxic, mold-resistant, fire-resistant, and rot-resistant. He identified challenges with traditional hempcrete installation, such as labor intensity and long drying times, which led him to develop a precast, interlocking panel system.  The company's flagship product is the patented Z Panel, a carbon-negative, hempcrete block panel designed for wall construction. These panels are engineered to be breathable, non-toxic, and resistant to mold, pests, rot, and fire. The Z Panel system features a unique interlocking design that integrates with conventional 2x4 or 2x6 wood framing, speeding up the construction process. In March 2025, the Z Panel became the first hempcrete product in the United States to receive an ICC-ES (International Code Council Evaluation Service) Report, verifying its compliance with national building codes and standards.  Sativa Building Systems operates in the growing green construction market, which is driven by an increasing focus on sustainability and eco-friendly practices. The company's business model includes direct sales of Z Panels to contractors, builders, and developers. To navigate the lengthy code certification process, the company also began producing and selling 'The Cultivated Tiny Home,' a tiny-home-on-wheels built with Z Panel technology, as this category is not subject to the same building code restrictions. The firm has received significant backing, including a $1.9 million Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) contract from the U.S. Army to develop lighter, bio-based insulation materials using hemp and mycelium (mushroom) binders. column5: Backstay-mounted vertical wind turbine for sailing yachts
column6: ampStay is developing a vertical axis wind turbine that utilizes a sailing yacht's slanted backstay as its rotational axis to generate electrical power. This design approach aims to provide a solution for the increasing energy demands on modern sailboats, which power everything from navigation electronics to refrigerators and air conditioning. The system is designed to be a quiet and vibration-free power source, addressing a common issue with traditional wind generators. The turbine consists of modular, individual segments, allowing it to be adapted to various stay lengths. A generator is mounted directly below the rotor, beginning to supply power at wind speeds of approximately 8 knots. The system is designed to use the stronger and more consistent winds found in the upper mast area, a space that is typically unused for power generation. Depending on the installed rotor height (from 7 to 10 meters), the system is rated to produce between 600 and 1000 watts of power. An integrated charge controller ensures a reliable power supply for charging batteries. The company notes that the design does not require an additional mast, leaving the stern of the yacht unobstructed. ampStay Windenergie ltd. is comprised of a team of managers, technicians, and sailors. The company's development timeline indicates that wind tunnel tests began in the first quarter of 2022, followed by outdoor performance and sailing tests from 2022 through 2025. The final product design and production preparations are scheduled for 2025, with the start of production and acceptance of advance orders planned for the fourth quarter of 2025. Sales are expected to commence in 2026. The development has been supported by the Institute for Renewable Energy in Vienna and partly funded by the Austrian Research Agency (FFG). While the primary market is sailing yachts, the company also sees potential applications for its turbines on ski lifts, cable cars, and other remote facilities. column6: Based in Artigues-près-Bordeaux, France, Sunbooster is a clean technology firm established in 2010, operating within the alternative energy equipment sector. This action simultaneously cools the photovoltaic cells and cleans their surfaces, mitigating power losses from overheating and soiling. The firm also provides remote supervision and monitoring applications for its installations. The business generates revenue through the sale and installation of these optimization systems. column5: Provider of solar radiation measurement solutions
column6: The story begins in 1830 when Dutch pharmacist Petrus Jacobus Kipp opened an instrument business in Delft. Initially a side venture to his pharmacy, the business gained traction with an invention called the Kipp generator, an apparatus for preparing small volumes of gases. After Petrus's death, the firm was continued by his sons, Anthonius and Wilhelmus, who renamed it Kipp & Zonen, meaning 'Kipp & Sons'. A pivotal moment came in the 1920s when the company shifted its focus to building instruments based on the thermopile principle. This led to the creation of the first pyranometer in 1927, an instrument designed to measure solar radiation. This innovation set the company on a new trajectory, establishing it as a key player in the field of solar radiation and atmospheric monitoring. Their instruments became essential for meteorology, climatology, and later, the renewable energy sector. The company's long history of specialized innovation made it an attractive target. In a significant event for the nearly two-century-old firm, Kipp & Zonen was acquired by Hach Company in December 2017. Hach, a subsidiary of Danaher, integrated the Dutch instrument maker into its OTT HydroMet group, a collection of companies focused on environmental measurement. This acquisition marked the next chapter for Kipp & Zonen, placing it within a larger global corporation while allowing it to continue its legacy of providing class-leading instruments for measuring the world around us.

column6: The story of Solectria Renewables begins as a classic spin-off. In 2005, founders James and Anita Worden launched the company from their existing electric and hybrid vehicle business, Solectria Corporation. They decided to focus squarely on one critical component of the growing renewable energy market: the solar inverter, a device that converts the direct current (DC) generated by solar panels into the alternating current (AC) used by the power grid. Headquartered in Lawrence, Massachusetts, Solectria Renewables set out to manufacture high-performance inverters for residential, commercial, and utility-scale systems. Leveraging over two decades of experience in power electronics, the company quickly established a strong brand. They focused on producing reliable, efficient, and bankable inverters, which resonated with solar developers and installers, particularly in the northeastern United States before expanding nationally. This focus on quality and engineering allowed them to become a leading commercial solar inverter manufacturer in the U.S. The company’s trajectory took a significant turn in 2014. Yaskawa Electric, a multi-billion dollar Japanese company and a global leader in factory automation and motor drives, announced it would acquire Solectria Renewables through its U.S. subsidiary, Yaskawa America, Inc. The move was strategic for both sides. For Solectria, it provided global scale, significant resources, and the stability of a century-old manufacturing giant. For Yaskawa, it was a direct entry into the large and growing U.S. solar market, complementing its existing strength in Japan’s solar market. Following the acquisition, the company became Yaskawa Solectria Solar, blending a strong U.S. brand with a global manufacturing powerhouse.

column5: Develops wireless sensors that measure the efficiency of geothermal systems
column6: Based in Karlsruhe, Germany, enOware GmbH operates as a specialized developer of sensor systems tailored for monitoring in geothermal energy, fluid-based pipe systems, and broader environmental applications. The company was established in July 2014 as a spin-off from Systec & Services GmbH by Karl G. Linder, who serves as CEO, and Simeon Meier, who acted as CTO until mid-2018. The foundation for the company was partly laid by the nomination of their YouFootprint energy portal for the NEO 2013 award and support from KIC InnoEnergy's Entrepreneurship Initiative. enOware's business is centered on providing hardware and software solutions that make environmental data more accessible and actionable for its clients, which include drilling companies, well constructors, heating system suppliers, and research institutes. The company generates revenue through the sale of its sensor products and by providing research and development services, including microcontroller software development and electronics for prototypes. In October 2015, the firm secured an undisclosed amount in a seed funding round from investors including High-Tech Gründerfonds (HTGF), LBBW Venture Capital, and EIT InnoEnergy to advance its technology and accelerate market entry. The company's flagship product line was the GEOsniff system, a miniaturized, wireless measuring capsule designed to improve the efficiency and quality of near-surface geothermal systems. This spherical sensor, just 20mm in diameter, navigates through the fluid-filled pipes of a geothermal probe to record real-time data on temperature and pressure. The collected data is transmitted wirelessly via an automated docking station to the YouFootprint online portal and a corresponding smartphone app, enabling system monitoring, optimization, and enhanced operational safety. For its work, enOware was granted the European Geothermal Innovation Award in 2017. While development on some GEOsniff products was halted in 2018, the company continues to offer other sensor solutions like INDUsniff for pipe system monitoring and ENOsniff for environmental monitoring in buildings. column5: Sustainable interior materials data and impact assessment
column6: Intermatter provides a material library and impact calculation tools to aid designers, architects, and interior builders in making sustainable choices. Established in 2020 by Marije Remigius, the platform addresses the challenge of limited sustainability data and lengthy certification processes in the interior design industry. Remigius leverages 25 years of experience in interior building to lead the company. The core of Intermatter's offering is its material library, which contains over 200 interior materials. The platform simplifies complex data by using a six-color scale, from blue (best practice) to grey (avoid), to provide a quick sustainability indicator. Alongside the color-coding, it provides specific data on Eco-costs and CO2 emissions per square meter, allowing users to measure the total environmental impact of materials and entire projects. Intermatter operates with a mission to make all interiors sustainable and is structured to become a steward-owned company, where profits are reinvested to serve this mission rather than shareholders. The business model includes several services: a free-to-use material library, a 'Project Impact Calculator' for assessing project sustainability, one-on-one consulting sessions, and workshops for teams on sustainable and circular interior design. column5: AI-powered platform redesigning farms into multifunctional landscapes
column6: AgroDesign is a technology firm that specializes in converting traditional farms into sustainable, multifunctional agricultural landscapes. The company leverages a proprietary digital platform that integrates satellite imagery, artificial intelligence, agronomy, and ecology to provide detailed farm analysis and redesign services. The process begins with digitizing and georeferencing the farm's current state. Subsequently, the platform processes satellite images from the last 10 years to analyze flood frequency, water stress, and biomass variation, combining this data with soil and altimetry information to create a comprehensive map of the farm's productive potential. Using this data, AgroDesign redesigns the landscape by incorporating nature into areas with the lowest opportunity cost to maximize benefits for biodiversity and production. The company was co-founded by Lucas Alejandro Garibaldi and Lucas Andreoni. Garibaldi is an Agricultural Engineer with a PhD in Agricultural Sciences, focusing on agroecology, pollination, and promoting sustainable productive transitions. Andreoni, also an Agricultural Engineer, has extensive experience as a manager of agricultural productions and as a CREA advisor for over 15 years. He is the founder of the agricultural consultancy Biored, where he directs technical operations on over 12,000 hectares and advises companies in Argentina, Uruguay, and Spain on restoring agricultural systems with a focus on soil regeneration. Operating under the 'Ecological Intensification Paradigm,' AgroDesign guides the transformation towards multifunctional agricultural landscapes, emphasizing the implementation of biological corridors and patches to enhance both productivity and sustainability. The firm's target clients are agricultural businesses seeking to improve efficiency, resilience, and profitability in alignment with current demands for sustainable production. By synergizing production with biodiversity conservation, the company aims to diversify and add value to the services that agricultural establishments provide to society. As of 2025, the company has redesigned 13 farms, intervening in over 14,800 hectares and restoring over 1,200 hectares. column5: China Longyuan Electric Power Group Corporation provides wind power in China. The company was founded in 1993 and is based in Beijing,
column6: In the early 1990s, China’s economic engine was beginning to roar, and with it, an insatiable appetite for energy. In 1993, a new entity was formed, not in a garage, but under the guidance of the Ministry of Energy of the People's Republic of China. This was the beginning of what would become China Longyuan Power Group. Its initial mandate was to explore energy-saving and new energy technologies. This wasn't a story of individual founders with equity stakes, but a strategic state initiative. The company was China's earliest specialized firm focused on wind power development. For years, the company operated as a wholly-owned subsidiary of state-owned giants, methodically building its expertise. The playbook was straightforward: become a leader in the burgeoning field of renewable energy. The pivotal moment arrived in December 2009. Under the leadership of its then-Chairman, Zhu Yongfan, China Longyuan Power launched its initial public offering on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, raising over $2 billion. This event marked its transformation from a purely state-controlled entity to a public company, earning it the title of "China's First New Energy Stock." Today, the company's primary business is the development and operation of wind farms. It has grown to become the largest wind power operator in China and a significant force on the global stage, a testament to its strategic beginnings within the state apparatus and its successful transition to the public market.

column5: Heat pump automation using dynamic electricity prices
column6: Eleflex provides a smart energy management solution for residential and commercial buildings. Its core product, HeatAdapt, is a smart module designed for air-to-water and ground source heat pumps that automates and optimizes heating based on dynamic hourly electricity prices, weather forecasts, and grid fees. This allows property owners with variable-rate electricity plans to significantly reduce heating costs by shifting energy consumption to off-peak, cheaper hours. The HeatAdapt system works by creating a daily heating schedule that analyzes market prices, weather patterns, and the building's specific thermal properties to determine the most efficient times for heating and hot water production. The technology was developed in collaboration with data scientists from Tallinn University of Technology (TalTech) and has backgrounds at companies like Bolt, Nortal, and Starship. A study conducted during the 2023/24 heating season across several Nordic homes demonstrated average annual savings of 14% to 24%, with monthly savings reaching up to 31%. The system is also compatible with solar panels, optimizing heating schedules to use surplus solar energy and increase self-consumption. Eleflex operates on a hardware-plus-subscription model. Customers must have a HeatAdapt or HeatAdapt PRO smart controller installed. The company offers different subscription plans, with the first year of service for residential buildings often included with the device purchase. The HeatAdapt PRO version is available for larger systems (over 20kW) and offers more advanced features like real-time energy tracking and control for hybrid heat source setups. The company is registered as SoftProject OÜ in Tallinn, Estonia. column6: Addressing twin crises in the construction sector—a significant labor shortage and its 37% contribution to global greenhouse gas emissions—impact.build emerges as a pivotal ETH Zurich spinoff established in April 2025. A key feature of this method is its ability to compact the material without requiring formwork or chemical additives, which simplifies the building process and reduces waste. The resulting structures are fully recyclable, aligning with circular economy principles. The firm's business model centers on leveraging this robotic technology to produce mass-customizable building elements. Initially, impact.build is targeting the USD 180 billion prefabrication market with an offering of low-carbon, fire-resistant, and acoustically insulated walls. Its platform integrates custom extrusion tools and autonomous mobile machinery with a proprietary high-yield-stress mix design, enabling on-site adaptability and robotic surface finishing. By automating what is traditionally a labor-intensive process, the company aims to deliver low-carbon construction at a competitive price point, directly tackling the high costs associated with ecological building methods. The company has secured early-stage support, including CHF 50,000 from the Venture Kick initiative in 2025, to advance its mission.
