Items with a resale value below €5 are donated to charities as the handling costs would exceed the proceeds. column5: Autonomous, self-charging drones for grid infrastructure inspection.
column6: Voltair is developing a network of autonomous, self-charging drones to conduct inspections of critical infrastructure, with an initial focus on the power grid. Founded in 2025 and based in Seattle, WA, the company emerged from the University of Washington and was part of YC's W26 batch. The founding team includes CEO Ronan Nopp, CTO Hayden Gosch, CGO Avi Gotskind, and COO Warren Weissbluth. Nopp and Gosch, friends since middle school, both studied electrical and computer engineering at the University of Washington. Gosch developed a passion for energy infrastructure during an internship at Seattle City Light, while Nopp gained expertise in commercial drones through work with the Air Force and DARPA. Gotskind previously consulted on go-to-market and government affairs for aerospace companies, and Weissbluth has experience in operations research and with NSF-funded startups. Voltair's business model is centered on providing data as a fully managed service, where clients request inspection coverage and receive the data without needing to own or operate any hardware. The company's primary clients are power utilities, who currently spend billions annually on equipment inspections. Voltair aims to reduce this cost and improve inspection frequency from years to a 60-day cycle, addressing hazards like overgrown vegetation and faulty equipment that can lead to wildfires and power outages. The long-term vision is to expand this drone network to serve other markets, including telecom, rail, and pipeline inspection, as well as applications in weather monitoring, forestry, and insurance. The core of Voltair's product is a hybrid fixed-wing drone capable of long-range flight and hovering for detailed assessments. A key feature is the drone's ability to recharge itself in the field using inductive charging pads mounted directly on utility poles, which eliminates the need for manual battery swaps and enables persistent, autonomous operation. Each charging pad unlocks approximately 1,000 square miles of coverage. The weatherized aircraft are designed to fly in adverse conditions and can capture RGB, thermal, and LiDAR data to identify maintenance issues and build 3D corridor models. By June 2025, Voltair had built five prototypes and validated its self-charging mechanism on actual power lines. The company has raised $500K in a seed round. column6: GMD® GmbH – Edge AI & Sensor Intelligence for Climate ResilienceThe GMD® GmbH, headquartered in Innsbruck, Austria, is a verified GreenTech company and officially recognized Verified Social Enterprise (VSE), developing AI-driven IoT sensor systems and digital platforms for natural hazard prevention and critical infrastructure protection. Founded in February 2024 by Steve Weingarth, GMD combines advanced Edge AI, radar and seismic technologies, and data-driven risk management to increase safety and climate resilience in mountainous and infrastructure-critical regions.GMD’s core mission is to transform environmental data into actionable intelligence. Through the proprietary GeoSenseAI® Platform, GMD enables municipalities, infrastructure operators, and emergency services to detect, predict, and respond to natural hazards such as floods, debris flows, rockfalls, and landslides in real time. This scalable SaaS platform integrates AI-based analytics, real-time data visualization, and automated alerting functions — empowering blue-light organizations and civil protection units to make faster, data-backed decisions when every second counts.Technology and InnovationGMD develops highly specialized Edge AI IoT sensors that operate autonomously under extreme alpine and environmental conditions. The company’s portfolio includes:Radar sensors for detecting rockfall, blockages, and flow velocity in mountain streams.Seismic and impact sensors for structural monitoring and slope stability.Smart weather and water-level stations for hydrological and meteorological analysis.LoRaWAN / NB-IoT communication systems for long-range, energy-efficient data transmission.All devices connect to the GMD Data Hub, where measurements are processed via machine learning algorithms and combined into predictive models. This edge-to-cloud architecture ensures high data availability, security, and scalability — even in remote alpine regions.Strategic PartnershipsGMD collaborates with leading industrial and scientific partners, including Infineon Technologies, Silicon Austria Labs, the University of Innsbruck, and the MCI International University. These partnerships drive continuous innovation in radar signal processing, AI model training, and sensor calibration.In cooperation with municipalities such as Kufstein and Kitzbühel, and research institutions like the German Alpine Club (DAV) and Rhätische Bahn (RhB), GMD implements pilot projects that demonstrate real-world applications of its systems in alpine hazard zones and infrastructure networks.Key ProjectsAlpine Climate Net (Interreg Project) – Building a cross-border network of smart weather stations across Austria, Italy, Germany, and Switzerland for climate adaptation and hazard prediction.Smart Alpine Radar Weather Station (SARWS) – A high-precision radar-based monitoring system for hydrology, construction, and environmental applications.DAV Water Resource Monitoring (Neue Prager Hütte) – Autonomous IoT sensors and transmitters measuring alpine spring discharge under extreme climatic conditions.Kitzbühel Smart City Initiative – Radar-based traffic and environmental monitoring system for urban planning and sustainability.Impact and SustainabilityAs a Verified Social Enterprise, GMD is committed to measurable ecological and social impact. Its technologies contribute directly to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly in climate action (SDG 13), sustainable cities (SDG 11), and industry innovation (SDG 9).By enabling early warning and predictive analytics, GMD’s solutions reduce risks for populations, infrastructure, and ecosystems — fostering a safer, more resilient future for communities in the Alpine region and beyond.Scalability and Market OutlookThe market for AI-based natural hazard management is rapidly expanding, driven by climate change and increasing demand for resilient infrastructure. column5: Vertically integrated sustainable and organic knitted textile manufacturing
column6: Pratibha Syntex is a vertically integrated, sustainability-focused manufacturer of knitted textile products, established in 1997 by Shiv Kumar Chaudhary. Headquartered in Indore, India, the company manages the entire textile value chain, from cotton farming to finished garments, in what it calls a "Farm to Fashion" model. The company was founded with a vision to create a business rooted in natural fibers, evolving from a small spinning unit in Pithampur into one of India's largest exporters of sustainable apparel. The founder, Shiv Kumar Chaudhary (1952-2025), began his career in his family's machinery and chemicals business before establishing Pratibha Syntex. His goal was to build an enterprise that not only achieved business success but also positively impacted lives and served a greater purpose. This ethos is carried on by his son, Shreyaskar Chaudhary, the current Managing Director, who holds a degree in Textile Technology from UMIST, Manchester. Shreyaskar has been pivotal in advancing the company's sustainability mission, initiating the 'Vasudha' organic farming project in 1999, which has grown to involve thousands of farmers. Pratibha Syntex's business model is centered on sustainability and vertical integration. The company's operations encompass spinning, knitting, dyeing, and garment manufacturing. It produces a wide array of products, including casualwear, innerwear, sleepwear, thermals, and activewear for men, women, and children, with an annual garment production capacity of over 60 million pieces. The company serves major global apparel brands in over 40 countries. A core component of its operation is its direct partnership with over 20,000 farmers, engaging them in organic and regenerative cotton farming practices. This approach helps restore soil health, ensures fair pricing for farmers, and provides a traceable, sustainable raw material source. Sustainability is a foundational principle for the company, which has implemented numerous eco-friendly initiatives. These include a zero liquid discharge facility that recycles 100% of its water, rainwater harvesting systems, and significant investments in renewable energy, such as a 2.5 MW rooftop solar power plant. Pratibha Syntex aims to use 100% sustainable materials and achieve 70% decarbonization by 2030. The company was the first apparel manufacturer in India to be Fair Trade certified (2008) and has achieved Cradle to Cradle (C2C) certification for some of its products, signifying that they are designed for safe and circular lifecycles. To enhance efficiency and quality, the firm has adopted automated technologies in its manufacturing processes, including its cutting and spinning departments. The company's business model targets a range of clients, including wastewater treatment plant operators, municipal utilities, healthcare facilities, mobility manufacturers, and agricultural producers. By developing a UVC LED with superior performance to existing mercury lamps, SQUIDLED intends to retrofit the extensive global UVC market. column5: Hardware-in-the-loop testing for complex energy systems
column6: Heating Performance Lab (HPL) is a digitized testing institution for highly dynamic measurement methods. The company originated as a spin-off from the Institute for Energy Efficient Buildings and Indoor Climate at RWTH Aachen University, leveraging years of team experience in operating test bench infrastructures for advanced energy systems. The core of HPL's service is its hardware-in-the-loop (HiL) test benches, which enable the analysis of complex energy systems in a realistic, laboratory-controlled environment. This process involves coupling real hardware components, such as heat pumps or PV inverters, with dynamic, real-time simulation models of other system parts, like a building's envelope. This integration allows for highly dynamic and repeatable testing under a wide array of boundary conditions, combining the benefits of field and lab tests. HPL provides several key services. 'Field Test in the Lab' offers measurement and evaluation of heat pumps under realistic, dynamic conditions to determine annual key performance figures. The company also specializes in 'System Controller Evaluation,' conducting simulative and experimental tests of system controllers by emulating virtual values. Furthermore, HPL offers 'Test Bench Development,' where they consult on and develop hydraulic concepts, climate chambers, and support the creation of cloud-based data infrastructures. The firm plans to have its laboratories accredited according to DIN EN ISO/IEC 17025. The company is managed by CEO Stephan Göbel and Technical Director Thomas Henn. column6: The story of Vbites begins in 1993 with a company called Redwood Wholefood, a pioneer in the plant-based food scene. Its trajectory significantly changed in 2007 when entrepreneur and activist Heather Mills acquired the company, rebranding it as Vbites to align with her existing vegan cafés. It was a dramatic turn for a company that had been at the forefront of the vegan movement for decades. The story took another twist in January 2024 when Heather Mills bought the company's assets back from the administrators in a £1 million rescue deal. Through her entity Vegan Solo Consulting, Mills took back control, waiving millions in debt owed to her to secure the deal. This pre-pack administration allowed the Vbites brand to continue, with Mills re-employing a portion of the staff and vowing to rebuild the business herself.

column5: One of the leading providers of residential care in Ireland
column6: Brindley Healthcare operates as one of Ireland's largest privately-owned nursing home groups, managing a network of residential care facilities across the country. The company was founded in 2000 by Amanda Torrens, a Donegal businesswoman who identified a gap in the market for purpose-built, private nursing homes in her native county. Her journey began while working in healthcare in Northern Ireland, which inspired her to acquire land and build the first 35-bed nursing home, Brindley Manor, in Convoy, County Donegal. The group's business model is centered on providing residential and personal care services for the elderly. A key part of its operational strategy involves designing facilities with specific resident needs in mind; for instance, after traveling to Sweden for research, Torrens designed a home specifically to cater to individuals with dementia, Alzheimer's, and brain injuries, featuring smaller common spaces to reduce noise and a layout with fewer corners to prevent confusion. Revenue is generated through the provision of long-term residential care in its nursing homes. The company serves residents in urban and rural communities, offering compassionate care tailored to individual needs. Brindley Healthcare has pursued a significant growth trajectory through both new developments and strategic acquisitions. Initially focused in the northeast, the company expanded its presence to counties including Mayo, Galway, Kildare, and Laois. A major milestone occurred in January 2019 when Brindley Healthcare secured a €10 million investment from BGF, its first in the Republic of Ireland, to fuel its expansion plans. This partnership facilitated the acquisition of two additional homes, expanding the portfolio to 10 facilities and approximately 600 beds. The investment also led to the appointment of former Minister for Health, Mary Harney, to the board as Non-Executive Chair. In September 2020, the French multinational care operator Orpea (now emeis) acquired a 50% share in Brindley, leading to a successful exit for BGF. Amanda Torrens exited the business in 2022. column5: Award-winning, 100% plant-based, dairy-free cheese alternatives
column6: Violife is a global brand specializing in the development and production of plant-based, vegan foods. Originating in Thessalonica, Greece, in the 1990s, the company was founded by three friends who wanted to create a cheese alternative they could eat during Greek Orthodox fasting periods, which prohibit dairy. The parent company, Arivia, was established in 1990 as a producer of dairy-analogue cheese and made dairy-free development a strategic priority in 2012. The brand name comes from the Greek word 'Vios,' meaning life, so Violife translates to 'life squared.' The company offers a wide range of award-winning, 100% vegan, non-dairy, and non-GMO products, including alternatives for cheese in various formats like slices, blocks, grated shreds, and creamy spreads, as well as plant butter, dips, and coffee creamers. All products are free from major allergens such as dairy, lactose, soy, gluten, nuts, and preservatives. The business serves vegans, vegetarians, flexitarians, and consumers with dietary restrictions in over 50 countries. Its products are sold through major retailers like Tesco, Whole Foods Market, and Pizza Hut, and it also operates a professional line for the foodservice industry. In November 2019, Violife was acquired by Upfield, which was later renamed Flora Food Group in 2024. This acquisition positions Violife under the umbrella of the world's largest plant-based food transformation company. The brand has achieved significant milestones, including launching in the UK in 2013 and the US in 2017. By 2023, Violife became the #1 dairy-free cream cheese in the US and achieved the same status in Canada by 2025. column5: Seasonal thermal energy storage solutions for buildings
column6: SeasonCell AG is a Swiss company focused on the development and distribution of energy systems, specializing in seasonal thermal energy storage. Founded in December 2023, the firm operates in the research and development sector, aiming to provide custom solutions in the fields of energy, environmental protection, and sustainability. The company's core technology involves storing excess heat collected during the summer, often from sources like solar-thermal panels, and making it available for heating buildings during the winter. This approach is designed to create a more sustainable heating model without CO2 emissions. The company is registered in Horw, Switzerland. The management team includes Simon In-Albon, who serves as the President of the Board of Directors. SeasonCell collaborates with European research groups in energy technology and integrates robotics, autonomous systems, and machine learning into its research and development of thermal energy processes. The company was a participant in the Swissbau Startup Challenge, which highlights emerging companies in the construction industry. Seasonal thermal energy storage (STES) systems, like those developed by SeasonCell, can be implemented at various scales, from single buildings to entire district heating networks. The technology commonly uses underground storage methods, such as borehole thermal energy storage (BTES), where heat is stored directly in the ground, or large, insulated water pits. These systems can significantly reduce reliance on fossil fuels for heating and can be combined with heat pumps to optimize efficiency. column5: Disinfection solutions using proprietary HOCL technology
column6: Loxotec GmbH specializes in developing, producing, and marketing hygiene, water, and infection prevention solutions based on hypochlorous acid (HOCL). The company's journey began two decades ago when Chief Research and Development Officer, Dr. Kurt Kaehn, a biochemist, was introduced to HOCL by Russian engineers. Together with Russian scientists, he brought the active ingredient to Germany and developed a proprietary electrochemical process, ECALIT®, to stabilize HOCL, making Loxotec a pioneer in the field. The founding team includes Bernhard Foglar-Deinhardstein, Dr. Kurt Kaehn, and Elmar Baumert. Foglar-Deinhardstein, the Managing Director, founded Loxotec after a successful venture in the veterinary sector. Dr. Kaehn contributes his extensive experience as a biologist and chemist, leading the development of the machines and the active substance. Elmar Baumert, a lawyer with a background in finance and industry, provides management and restructuring expertise. The team was later joined by Valeria Foglar-Deinhardstein and Magdalena Liebl, who added sales and marketing knowledge. Loxotec operates in two main business areas: Hygiene Solutions and Animal Health. For industrial and professional clients, the company offers customized solutions for water, surface, and air disinfection under its 'Anolin' brand and as a white-label supplier. These products are manufactured using the company's proprietary HOCL technology, which is highly effective against pathogens without being harmful to human or animal tissue. In the animal health sector, Loxotec produces and markets products under its own brands, Sanocyn and Loxovet, which are used for wound and skin care in pets and livestock. These products, developed in collaboration with veterinarians, are distributed exclusively through them to ensure proper medical guidance. The company's business model is centered on providing comprehensive disinfection solutions. Loxotec has a production facility in Bensheim, Germany, opened in 2020, with a capacity of 24,000 liters per day and laboratory facilities for quality assurance. The firm is ISO9001 certified, ensuring adherence to current quality standards. Its products are compliant with EU biocide regulations, making them marketable across the European Union. The head office is located in Vienna, Austria. column6: Oxcia has a unique technology platform that innovatively uses oxidative stress and the DNA Damage Repair process to develop novel projects. Oxcia recently announced that the EIC (the European Innovation Council) has selected Oxcia’s OXC-201 to receive an EIC Transition grant of 2.5 million Euros.  Oxcia is the only Swedish company to receive the grant in this call 2023 and this is a recognition of the outstanding science, projects and team existing at Oxcia.The lead project, OXC-101 is in late phase 1 for  hematological and solid cancers. OXC-101 is a  "mitotic MTH1 inhibitor" with dual action. It combines a new and innovative way to attack how the cancer cell defends itself against oxidative DNA damage with a proven way to stop the cancer cell from dividing. Via this unique two-way mechanism, OXC-101 induces cancer-specific oxidative stress and oxidative DNA damage, prevents repair of the DNA damage and stops the cancer cell from growing. The result is that the cancer cell dies. Healthy cells are only marginally affected, which lays the foundation for OXC-101 good tolerability. Other potential benefits include increased efficacy and size of applicable patient population, efficacy in chemoresistant tumors, addressing heterogeneity within the tumor, synergistic potential with other anti-cancer drugs as well as a primer for immuno-oncology drugs to increase IC response rate. Furthermore, OXC-101 shows effect in autoimmune morbidities such as psoriasis and Crohn's disease. OXC-101 has potential to halt cancer development in many cancer indications. The first focus indication is R/R AML and MDS.OXC-201 is the lead compound for the treatment of fibrotic and inflammatory diseases. It is a novel small molecule OGG1 inhibitor, currently in preclinical development. By exploiting the DDR concept this well-tolerated compound provides a unique way to block the onset of inflammation and fibrosis. As a first step, OXC-201 is developed as a ground-breaking new approach for the treatment of IPF. OXC-201 blocks the binding between damaged DNA and OGG1. This hinders the onset of as well as the ongoing inflammation and fibrosis. OXC-201 acts early in the inflammation and fibrosis cascade (transcription level), blocking multiple key molecular pathways of IPF, with potential not only to attenuate but also halting the disease. Besides IPF, OXC-201 has potential in a number of other fibrotic and inflammatory indications, e.g. allergic asthma. column6: Genius Hub, also known as Heat Genius, is a UK-based company specializing in smart home heating solutions. It is compatible with a wide range of heating systems, including gas, oil, biomass boilers, heat pumps, and various forms of electric and underfloor heating. column5: Global renewable energy development
column6: In 2003, Jigar Shah and Claire Broido Johnson founded SunEdison with a revolutionary idea for the solar industry. They pioneered the "solar-as-a-service" model, using power purchase agreements (PPAs) to finance and build solar installations for customers with no upfront cost. This approach allowed clients like Whole Foods to buy cheaper, clean power directly from the panels on their roofs, which SunEdison would own and operate. This innovative business model made SunEdison North America's largest solar services provider, leading to its acquisition by silicon wafer manufacturer MEMC Electronic Materials in 2009 for $200 million. This marked a strategic pivot for MEMC, which, recognizing the opportunity, renamed itself SunEdison in 2013 and shifted its focus entirely to renewable energy. To fuel aggressive growth, SunEdison employed complex financial engineering. It created two publicly traded subsidiary companies, known as "yieldcos"—TerraForm Power and TerraForm Global—to buy the solar and wind projects it developed. This structure initially delighted investors, sending the parent company's stock soaring. However, the model relied on a constant stream of acquisitions and cheap debt. An ambitious, debt-fueled buying spree, including the $2.4 billion acquisition of First Wind, pushed the company's liabilities to over $11 billion. After a failed attempt to acquire Vivint Solar, investor confidence collapsed. In April 2016, SunEdison, once valued at nearly $10 billion, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

column5: Waterless, composting toilets for residential and commercial use
column6: Ecodomeo is a French company specializing in the design and manufacturing of waterless, ecological dry toilets. Founded in 2009 by Emmanuel Morin, the company was born from a desire to contribute to sustainable development by creating an accessible, modern, and user-friendly alternative to traditional flush toilets. The core of Ecodomeo's technology is a patented separation system that uses a conveyor belt, operated by a mechanical pedal or an electric motor, to separate solid waste and toilet paper from urine. This process eliminates the need for water, sawdust, or chemicals. Liquids are directed toward a wastewater treatment system, while solids are transported to an external composting unit where earthworms and bacteria convert them into usable compost. This composting process is highly efficient, requiring the compost to be emptied only every 3 to 10 years. An air suction system ensures the toilets remain odorless. The company's business model involves the direct sale of its toilet systems, which are manufactured in its workshop in Marseille with over 90% of parts sourced from the Rhône Alpes region of France. Ecodomeo serves a diverse client base, including private homes, alternative housing projects, campsites, hotels, and facilities in remote locations like mountainsides. The toilets are designed to be robust and adaptable to various environments, including areas prone to frost or salt air. The product line includes models like the Neodyme, Zircone, and Tentale, featuring materials such as polyester resin, stainless steel, and polyethylene, with prices starting from €2,370. By eliminating the need for a water flush, the system saves an estimated 15,000 liters of water per person annually and can reduce household water consumption by 30-40%. column5: Novel ice storage heat pump systems
column6: Nullpunkt AG is a Swiss company that develops, produces, and sells a novel ice storage heat pump system for heating and cooling single-family homes. It was founded by Michael Egli, Pascal Barmet, and Thomas Degelo. The founders, all mechanical engineers with over a decade of experience running an engineering firm together, sought to replace their own oil heaters but found existing solutions like geothermal probes to be too complex and air heat pumps too noisy. They identified ice storage as an ideal but commercially unavailable solution that was either too expensive or bulky for residential use. This led them to develop their own compact, high-performance, and affordable ice storage system. A prototype successfully heated a single-family home during the winter of 2023, prompting the founders to bring the product to a wider market. The company's core product is a complete system that combines a heat pump with an ice storage unit. It operates by extracting latent heat that is released when water freezes into ice. This energy, captured and stored from ambient air during warmer periods, is then used by the heat pump to provide heating during colder times, especially at night. This method allows the heat pump to operate with a higher source temperature compared to conventional air heat pumps, increasing efficiency. For homes with underfloor heating, the system can also provide cooling in the summer. Nullpunkt targets homeowners directly for sales and also collaborates with a network of installation partners. The system is designed to be a complete package and cannot be combined with an existing air heat pump. Today, Walmart.ca is a major player in Canadian e-commerce, visited by over 1.5 million people daily, complementing its vast network of over 400 stores nationwide. The company continues to invest heavily in its online and in-store experience, striving to be the most trusted retailer for Canadians.

column5: Mobile application preventing distracted driving for workplace safety
column6: Drive Commander is a mobile application designed to automatically prevent distracted driving by detecting vehicle motion and placing employee devices into a restricted safe mode that blocks access to phone features while the vehicle is in motion. The platform operates without requiring hardware installation, beacons, or vehicle telematics integration—deployment occurs exclusively through over-the-air installation to employee smartphones and tablets running iOS or Android operating systems. Administrators configure corporate safe driving policies through a cloud-based management portal, controlling which applications remain accessible in safe mode (such as GPS navigation), whether hands-free calling is permitted, emergency call protocols, and reporting capabilities that track driver compliance and policy overrides.The application directly addresses the employer's legal duty of care under UK Health and Safety legislation and the Corporate Manslaughter and Corporate Homicide Act 2007. By providing documented technical controls over distracted driving—particularly mobile phone use, which accounts for 68% of distracted driving incidents reported by fleet operators—Drive Commander enables organizations to demonstrate reasonable organizational structures and safety systems to regulatory authorities and courts. The company's positioning emphasizes risk reduction and regulatory compliance as the primary value proposition rather than cost optimization or efficiency gains.The market opportunity stems from a documented gap between corporate policy adoption and actual driver compliance: while 80% of UK employers have written mobile phone policies, drivers continue to use devices while driving, creating a significant prosecutorial risk for organizations. The solution targets fleet operators, logistics companies, transportation providers, and any organization operating a significant vehicle fleet where employee driving creates organizational liability exposure. By automating policy enforcement rather than relying on policy education alone, Drive Commander shifts the burden of compliance from individual driver behavior to organizational infrastructure.Keywords: distracted driving, workplace safety, occupational health, employer liability, mobile safety, compliance technology, fleet management, safe driving policies, prosecution prevention, corporate duty of care, health and safety legislation

column6: Project-S Space and Beyond Technologies UG is a German space technology firm focused on orbital sustainability and asset protection. Headquartered in Garching bei München, the firm operates at the intersection of space technology, artificial intelligence, robotics, and data analytics. This system is designed to track objects as small as 1 cm, identifying them by size, material, and rotation in real-time, regardless of lighting conditions. Complementing this is an "Automatic Collision Avoidance System," which employs predictive algorithms and AI to autonomously execute fuel-efficient maneuvers, aiming to reduce future collision risks and operational costs for satellite operators. For clients in the insurance and asset management sectors, Project-S has developed a software-only "Risk Analytics & Insurance Optimization" platform. This tool converts historical and real-time collision data into predictive, long-term safety insights, enabling more accurate risk quantification and potentially optimizing insurance premiums. Looking toward future market needs, the company is also working on Active Debris Removal (ADR) solutions that use AI and reinforcement learning to autonomously capture and de-orbit debris. Furthermore, it has laid out a roadmap for In-Space Servicing, Assembly, and Manufacturing (ISAM) capabilities, envisioning a future platform for on-orbit satellite maintenance, refueling, and assembly to extend asset lifespans. column5: Personalized T-cell immunotherapy for advanced-stage cancer
column6: SeqCure Immunology is a Stockholm-based immunotherapy startup founded in 2017 by Karolinska Institute scientists Robert Wallin, Ludvig Linton, and Vidar Wendel-Hansen. The company is focused on developing curative, personalized cell therapies for patients with advanced-stage cancer, including those who may not benefit from other treatments. The founders leverage their deep expertise in immunology and tumor biology. CEO Vidar Wendel-Hansen holds a PhD in tumor biology and has management experience from pharmaceutical companies like Novartis and Gilead Sciences. CSO Robert Wallin is an Associate Professor of Immunology, and COO Ludvig Linton has a background in intestinal immunology and biotech project management. The company's core product is SeqCureNEO, a highly individualized T-cell immunotherapy. The treatment process begins with analyzing a patient's blood and tumor samples to identify unique tumor-specific mutations, known as neoantigens. Using a proprietary algorithm, the company fishes out rare, tumor-specific T-cells from the patient's blood, which are then expanded and activated before being reintroduced to the patient. A key differentiator of SeqCureNEO is that it does not involve genetic engineering; instead, it enriches and strengthens the patient's existing weak anti-tumor immune response. This approach, which uses whole blood as the source material rather than tumor tissue, avoids the need for additional surgical procedures. SeqCure Immunology's business model involves seeking funding for preclinical and clinical development, with the eventual goal of partnering with a larger industrial entity for global marketing. The company has outlined a plan to initiate clinical trials and is seeking capital to complete the final preclinical development of SeqCureNEO. The firm believes its method is applicable to at least 50% of advanced cancers, representing a significant market opportunity within the rapidly growing cancer immunotherapy sector. column5: Developing New Mexico uranium assets using ISR technology
column6: Verdera Energy Corp. is a private Canadian corporation centered on the development of advanced uranium assets within New Mexico, which hosts the most significant uranium resources in the United States. The company was spun out from enCore Energy Corp. to specifically focus on and unlock the value of its New Mexico assets. On March 18, 2025, Verdera acquired multiple uranium projects from an enCore subsidiary, including the Crownpoint, Hosta Butte, Nose Rock, West Largo, and Ambrosia Lake-Treeline projects. This transaction gave enCore a majority stake in Verdera. Verdera's business model is focused on advancing uranium projects amenable to In-Situ Recovery (ISR), a mining extraction method with lower environmental impact compared to conventional techniques. The ISR process involves dissolving uranium underground and pumping it to the surface, which avoids large open pits and waste rock piles, and allows for land restoration after operations cease. The company is strategically positioned in the Grants Uranium District, a region that has historically accounted for nearly 40% of all uranium mined in the U.S. Verdera controls mineral rights over approximately 400 square miles in this district. Its principal asset is the Crownpoint and Hosta Butte Project, which has a permitted production capacity and is located near a licensed processing facility. Other key projects include Nose Rock, West Largo, and Ambrosia Lake. The company serves the nuclear energy industry by aiming to provide a reliable domestic source of uranium to meet growing demand in the United States. In early 2026, Verdera closed a $20 million financing to fund drilling, metallurgical studies, and engineering work, particularly for its Crownpoint and Hosta Butte Project. This financing is part of a go-public strategy through a reverse takeover transaction with POCML 7 Inc., a capital pool company, which will result in Verdera Energy Corp. being listed on the TSX Venture Exchange. The leadership team includes CEO Janet Lee-Sheriff, who has extensive experience in mineral extraction and community engagement, and directors like Kevin Bambrough, former president of Sprott Inc., and Mark Pelizza, a 45-year veteran of the uranium industry. Strategic shareholder enCore Energy provides access to technical expertise in ISR operations. Key clients include utilities, data centers, and other large industrial power users in high-demand regions like California, Texas, and Oklahoma. This strategy addresses the growing need for grid stability driven by the rise of data centers and the increasing penetration of intermittent renewable energy sources. column5: This program will provide a coordinated, international response to the problem of missing and exploited children
column6: The International Centre for Missing & Exploited Children (ICMEC) is a private, non-governmental, 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization with a global mission to combat child sexual exploitation, child pornography, and child abduction. Headquartered in Alexandria, Virginia, the organization was conceptualized following the "Dutroux Affair" in Belgium in 1996, a case that highlighted the need for a coordinated international response to crimes against children. The Board of Directors of the U.S. National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) approved the creation of ICMEC in 1998 to handle the increasing volume of international requests for assistance. ICMEC was officially launched in April 1999 at the British Embassy in Washington, D.C. The organization operates on a public-private partnership model, collaborating with governments, law enforcement agencies from over 120 countries, civil society, and private industry to build a global network dedicated to child protection. Its operational framework involves national capacity building, where it assesses and helps fill gaps in national laws, policies, and response systems. A core activity is training law enforcement, prosecutors, judges, legal professionals, and educators, having trained over 155,000 professionals to date. ICMEC also spearheads multi-sector coalitions, such as the Financial Coalitions Against Child Pornography and technology working groups, to disrupt the mechanics of child exploitation. One of its key programs, Project VIC, provides technology that streamlines law enforcement investigations by using a robust hash database to quickly identify previously known child abuse material. Funding for ICMEC is derived from a combination of corporate partnerships, government funding, grants, and philanthropic donations. The organization's research arm, The Koons Family Institute on International Law and Policy, conducts and commissions research to advocate for changes in laws and treaties to better protect children worldwide. Dr. Franz Humer, a Swiss-Austrian businessman with an extensive career in the pharmaceuticals industry, including as former Chairman of Roche, serves as the Chairman of the Board. Ambassador Maura Harty, who previously served for 27 years in the U.S. Foreign Service and created the State Department's Office of Children's Issues, has been the President & CEO since November 2014. Her background in diplomacy and crisis management, including service as U.S. Ambassador to Paraguay, directly informs ICMEC's global strategy and partnerships. Tuebor Energy's business model centers on providing these high-performance components to manufacturers in the electric mobility sector, including electric vehicle (EV) and air taxi producers. By improving battery efficiency and enabling the use of more abundant materials, the company aims to help lower the cost of electric mobility solutions. column5: Socially responsible hot sauces funding rural electrification
column6: SOCHILI is a Dortmund-based social enterprise that produces and sells hot sauces and spices with a mission to empower communities in the Global South. The company was founded by Moritz Everding, whose passion for chili sauces, sparked during a trip to Mexico in 2010, merged with a desire to create a product with a significant social purpose. Noticing a gap in the market for socially conscious chili sauces, he established SOCHILI to address energy poverty and create fair trade opportunities. SOCHILI's core social impact is its "1 product = 1 day of electricity" initiative. For every product sold, a donation is made to the Africa GreenTec Foundation, which provides and installs solar power, giving families in rural Senegal access to electricity for the first time. This model directly combats energy poverty, which affects one in two people in rural Senegal, and supports families who cannot afford electricity even when available.  In addition to its energy initiative, SOCHILI is committed to establishing fair and sustainable supply chains. The company partners directly with "Ferme Hallier," a Fair-trade certified farm in Senegal where a women's cooperative cultivates the chilis organically and regeneratively. The chilis are processed into a puree on-site before being shipped to Spain for final production, where other high-quality ingredients are added to create the final sauces. This process ensures fair compensation for farmers and anchors the value chain within the local community. The product lineup includes various hot sauces with flavors like Habanero & Mango, Habanero & Mustard, and Jalapeño & Garlic, as well as a range of spice toppings. column5: Foodprint - Social supermarket & food redistribution network
column6: Foodprint is a mobile application developed in New Zealand to combat food waste from the hospitality sector. Founded in 2019 by Michal Garvey, the platform connects consumers with eateries like cafes, restaurants, and supermarkets that have surplus food. These establishments list unsold but perfectly edible food on the app at a discount, typically starting from 30% off the original price. Consumers can then browse, order, and pay for these items directly within the app before collecting them from the business. The idea for Foodprint emerged from Garvey's personal experiences with food waste while working in the hospitality industry in the US and her time spent in Sweden, a country with a strong sustainability culture. Having studied web development and worked for a food-tech startup in London, she returned to New Zealand with the vision to create a local solution. Foodprint launched in Auckland in June 2019 and has since expanded to over 20 cities across New Zealand. The business model serves both eateries and consumers. For businesses, it provides a new revenue stream for food that would otherwise be discarded, reduces disposal costs, and attracts new customers. For consumers, it offers access to affordable, high-quality meals while allowing them to make an environmental impact. The app includes features like an interactive map, search filters for dietary needs and location, order history, and trackers for money and carbon saved. Foodprint facilitates the transaction but does not handle the food directly, meaning vendors operate under their existing food control plans. Its AI agents are trained on energy-specific workflows and can process public data as well as user-uploaded documents to provide tailored results, turning weeks of research into minutes. After a soft launch in May 2025, Greenvi AI secured its first paying customers from the US. In May 2025, the startup also received a €25,000 grant from the EIC's 'Seeds of Bravery' program, a European initiative to support Ukrainian tech startups. column5: Fairtrade cashews sourced and processed in Tanzania
column6: Mama Cashew is the first Fairtrade-certified cashew nut processor in East Africa, operating under the brand name of the trading company Listram Commodities Co. Ltd. Founded in October 2021 by business and life partners George Hokororo (also referred to as George Listram) and Maria Verschoof, the company was established to improve the livelihoods of smallholder farmers, promote sustainability in the cashew supply chain, and generate local employment, particularly for women. Maria Verschoof, who is from the Netherlands, had a background in creating employment opportunities and moved to Tanzania after meeting George Hokororo, a long-time cashew trader who wanted to establish an ethical processing factory. The company operates a processing factory in Mtwara, the center of Tanzania's cashew market. Its business model focuses on disrupting the conventional cashew supply chain, where 95% of Tanzania's raw nuts are exported to Asia for processing before reaching consumer markets in Europe and the US. By processing the cashews locally—from steaming and peeling to roasting and packaging—Mama Cashew retains economic value within Tanzania, reduces transport costs and emissions, and creates jobs. The company employs over 600 people, mostly women, and provides them with benefits such as health insurance and lunch. Mama Cashew works directly with over 1,600 small-scale farmers, utilizing a contract farming model instead of the fluctuating prices of the auction system. This model guarantees farmers a Fairtrade minimum price plus an additional premium, helping them secure a stable income. The company provides traceable and sustainable cashew nuts for export to Europe and the USA, serving clients like the Dutch brand Johnny Cashew. As the first and only Fairtrade certified processor in the region, Mama Cashew is pursuing HACCP certification to meet the highest international food safety and quality standards. column6: Fidra Energy is an independent battery energy storage business established in 2024 and headquartered in Edinburgh, UK. column5: Northern German producer of specialty and white cheeses
column6: Rücker GmbH is a German dairy company specializing in milk and cheese, with a history dating back to 1890. Founded by Eduard Wilhelm Rücker on the island of Fehmarn, the business is now a fourth-generation family enterprise managed by Klaus and Insa Rücker. The company has grown to become one of the largest private dairies in Germany, operating through two main sites: Rücker GmbH in Aurich and its sister company, Ostsee-Molkerei Wismar GmbH in Wismar. In early September 2025, it was announced that Meggle is set to acquire Rücker, pending approval from antitrust authorities, which will mark the end of its 135-year history as an owner-managed family business. The company's business model revolves around processing milk from approximately 700 farmers in Northern Germany, whose farms are located within 80 kilometers of the North or Baltic Sea. This "coastal farmers' milk" is used to produce a wide range of dairy products, including cheese, butter, and milk powder. Rücker serves various client segments, including retail food trade, wholesalers, the foodservice and delicatessen industry, and industrial clients for further processing. Their products are distributed in about sixty countries worldwide. The company's production facilities specialize in different areas: the Aurich plant focuses on white cheese (like Hirtenkäse), butter, and milk powder, while the Wismar facility is dedicated to naturally matured semi-hard cheese specialties. A key feature of their cheese production is the traditional maturation process on untreated spruce wood boards, with regular hand-brushing using salt water and red cultures. Rücker's product portfolio includes well-known brands such as Alter Schwede, Alt-Mecklenburger, and Friesischer Hirtenkäse. The company also offers halal and kosher certified products and has expanded into plant-based alternatives under the Vega Lecker brand. Annually, the firm processes around 700-800 million kilograms of milk to produce approximately 90,000 tons of cheese, 20,000 tons of butter, and 20,000 tons of milk powder. column6: Petit Bateau is a French clothing brand with origins tracing back to 1893 in Troyes, the former capital of the French knitting industry. The company was officially founded in 1920 after Étienne Valton, son of the original hosiery factory founder Pierre Valton, invented the modern cotton panty by cutting the legs off traditional long johns. This innovation was inspired by the children's nursery rhyme, "Maman les p'tits bateaux qui vont sur l'eau ont-ils des jambes?" ("Mummy, do the little boats on the water have legs?"), which also gave the company its name. The business operates on a multi-channel distribution model, selling its products through approximately 400 of its own boutiques, 4,300 partner stores, its e-commerce website launched in 2006, and a dedicated range for large supermarket chains. This strategy makes the brand accessible to a wide range of consumers. Its global presence extends across Europe, Asia, the Middle East, and the United States, with 55% of its sales generated in France. The business model also incorporates a second-hand marketplace, allowing customers to buy and sell used Petit Bateau clothing. Acquired by Groupe Rocher in 1988, Petit Bateau was later sold to the American investment fund Regent in 2025, a firm specializing in the revitalization of heritage brands. The brand is known for its high-quality, durable clothing, primarily for babies and children, but expanded to include adult collections in the 2000s, transforming it into a trans-generational label. Core products include iconic items like cotton T-shirts, bodysuits with American necklines, and raincoats. The company emphasizes sustainability and quality, with many of its textiles certified by Oeko-Tex to be free of harmful substances. Petit Bateau has collaborated with numerous fashion designers and houses, including Karl Lagerfeld, Christian Lacroix, Maison Kitsuné, and Miu Miu, who have reimagined its classic pieces. The company serves clients such as local energy companies, industrial corporations, and energy traders by providing them with biomethane and power. Its revenue is generated through the sale of this green energy and by offering tailored solutions for creating a circular economy, particularly for the agriculture and food industries. VORN establishes long-term partnerships with these industries to process their organic waste and by-products—such as manure, silage, and food residues—into biomethane. This approach provides a reliable disposal method for its partners, improves their carbon footprint, and produces high-quality fertilizer that is returned to farmers. The company's core service is the production of biomethane, a renewable alternative to natural gas. It operates several plants in Germany and is expanding its presence across Europe, with a significant focus on Italy, Spain, and Poland through both greenfield (new builds) and brownfield (acquisitions and modernizations) projects. For instance, VORN is constructing its first plant in Ferrara, Italy, which is expected to be completed in mid-2026 and will supply the thermal energy needs of approximately 7,000 households. The company is also integrating advanced technologies like carbon capture and liquefaction to produce food-grade CO2 from its processes, further enhancing the environmental benefits. column5: Equipment platforms capturing and destroying emerging water contaminants
column6: AxNano, founded in 2011 by Charles Gause, operates as a technology commercialization company with a clear focus on addressing environmental contamination. The firm is dedicated to the development and deployment of equipment platforms designed to capture and destroy PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances), also known as "forever chemicals," and other emergent contaminants. AxNano's business model centers on selling and leasing these deployable equipment platforms to a client base that spans government and commercial sectors, primarily within the waste management and environmental engineering industries. Revenue is generated through various models, including direct purchase, lease agreements, and a Hardware-as-a-Service (HaaS) or Device-as-a-Service offering. The company's product portfolio features two primary systems that work in tandem. The first is the PFAS Effluent Treatment System (PETS), a mobile and modular unit for on-site wastewater treatment that concentrates PFAS waste, reducing volumes by up to 10,000 times. This technology was originally invented by the Army Corps of Engineers' Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC). Following concentration, the second system, Supercritical Water Oxidation (SCWO), is employed. SCWO is a hydrothermal process that uses a unique supercritical phase of water to rapidly and completely break down hazardous chemicals with a destruction efficiency of up to 99.999%. This provides an alternative to conventional disposal methods like landfilling and incineration. AxNano's strategic approach involves a "Busnical" process, which balances business and technical risk mitigation across technology, market, and execution. The company became part of the technology accelerator Triad Growth Partners in 2013 and has leveraged partnerships with global corporations, research universities, and federal agencies to advance its technology. A significant milestone includes securing over $6.4 million in non-dilutive Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) funding and an additional $3 million from venture capitalists. As of early 2024, the company was working to raise another $7 million to scale operations and fulfill new contracts. The leadership team includes CEO Doug Speight, a serial entrepreneur who joined to steer the company through its early commercialization phase. The founder, Charles Gause, brought over 25 years of experience in technology development and contract research, having previously established the nanoWorks Division of Luna Innovations. column6: Hoting Innovations AB is a Swedish technology company focused on disrupting the single-use packaging industry with sustainable alternatives to plastic.The company was founded in 2022 by CEO Per Larsson, Anders Mårtensson, and Björn Nilsson. The idea originated when friends Nilsson, Mårtensson, and Bernt Lindman sought to create new job opportunities in their hometown of Hoting. This machine utilizes a unique rotational engineering process with proprietary tooling to rapidly remove water from pulp, creating continuous, high-speed production flows. Finally, its porous 3D tooling technology produces high-quality, rigid surfaces for the final product. Together, these technologies create a final product from BCTMP pulp that is strong, water-resistant, compostable, and recyclable, offering a viable replacement for plastics in applications like food packaging. column6: The Consumer Council for Water (CCW) is the statutory consumer body representing the interests of water and sewerage customers in England and Wales. Established on October 1, 2005, under the Water Act 2003, it operates as an executive non-departmental public body sponsored by the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra). CCW functions independently of the water companies and the economic regulator, Ofwat, to provide a strong, unified voice for consumers in national debates and policy-making. The organization's primary role is to advocate on behalf of both household and business water users, ensuring their priorities shape regulatory decisions and industry practices. CCW provides impartial advice, support, and complaint resolution for customers who have been unable to resolve issues directly with their water companies. In the 2022-23 period, it handled over 13,000 customer complaints and more than 40,000 telephone calls, securing over £914,000 in financial redress for customers. This contributes to a total of £36 million returned to customers since its inception. CCW's business model is funded by a small levy on the water bills of all customers in England and Wales, which is passed to Defra via a charge issued by Ofwat to the water companies. The organization's work is evidence-led, relying on extensive research into customer views on issues like service quality, affordability, and environmental performance to inform its policy positions and advocacy. It scrutinizes company business plans, especially during the five-yearly Price Review process, to ensure they align with consumer expectations for service improvements and investment. Key campaigns have focused on areas such as water affordability, support for vulnerable customers, and improving market performance for business clients. column6: When you think about what keeps a satellite running for decades, orbiting hundreds of miles above the Earth, the answer is often sunlight. Capturing that sunlight and turning it into reliable power is the business of Azur Space. For over 60 years, this German company has been a global leader in developing and producing highly specialized multi-junction solar cells for the space industry. The company's story begins in 1964, not in a garage, but as a division of the German electronics giant Telefunken. Its mission was to create the solar cells for Germany's very first satellite, which was aptly named "Azur". After the satellite's successful launch and mission completion in 1969, the project's name stuck, though the company itself would formally adopt the AZUR SPACE name much later in 2007. Over the decades, the company evolved through various corporate structures, including AEG and Daimler Chrysler Aerospace. It remained at the forefront of solar technology, hitting milestones like producing its first triple-junction solar cell in 2001. These aren't your typical rooftop solar panels; they are high-efficiency, radiation-hardened cells designed to power critical missions, from commercial satellites to the Hubble Space Telescope and probes sent to Jupiter and Mercury. In 2021, a new chapter began when Azur Space was acquired by 5N Plus, a Canadian producer of specialty semiconductors and performance materials. The move solidified Azur's supply chain and positioned it for future growth. Today, as a subsidiary of 5N Plus, Azur Space continues to operate from its base in Heilbronn, Germany, expanding its production capacity to meet the ever-growing demand for power in space.

column6: Lakewater Nutrient Capture provides a service-based, turnkey solution for removing phosphorus from water bodies to combat nutrient pollution. column5: Sustainable, pesticide-free urban farming
column6: HerbaFabrica operates as a specialized urban farm in Prague, focusing on the B2B gastronomy sector. The company originated as a student project in September 2018, founded by Karolína Pumprová, Michal Bílek, and Matyáš Smutný, who were students at the Czech University of Life Sciences and Czech Technical University. This method allows for year-round cultivation in a controlled indoor environment, free from pesticides. The primary farm is located in Prague's Holešovice district, repurposing industrial space to house its operations. Its product line includes microgreens, edible flowers, and exotic mushrooms, all cultivated indoors. Additionally, the company manages seasonal production of baby vegetables at an outdoor field in Jinonice, which is operated under an organic regimen. This dual-location strategy enables a diverse and consistent supply of fresh produce.HerbaFabrica's business model is centered on supplying high-quality, fresh produce directly to clients in the gastronomy industry, such as restaurants and coworking spaces. The use of hydroponics results in significant water savings—up to 95% less than conventional agriculture—and a reduced carbon footprint due to local production and delivery. Their products are known for intense flavor and high vitamin content, a direct result of the controlled growing conditions where nutrient delivery is precisely managed. In October 2018, the project won the Social Impact Award, a program for socially beneficial businesses. column5: Indicator that records continuous temperature and time and shows you how many days of shelf life remains
column6: Keep-it Technologies AS operates as a specialized developer of intelligent shelf-life indicators for temperature-sensitive products. The company's origins trace back to 2000, when four scientists from the Norwegian University of Life Sciences (NMBU) conceptualized a dynamic replacement for traditional date-stamping. This idea led to the founding of TimeTemp AS in December 2001 to commercialize the technology. The core business revolves around a time and temperature indicator (TTI) that visually represents the actual remaining shelf life of a product, a significant advancement over static 'use by' dates. The company's primary product is a self-adhesive label that monitors the cumulative temperature exposure of a product from production through to the consumer's home. This indicator features two small chambers with ingredients that react and cause a blue bar to shorten over time; the reaction accelerates at higher temperatures and slows at lower ones, accurately reflecting the product's freshness. Each indicator is specifically calibrated to the unique shelf-life profile of the product it is applied to, catering to industries such as food, pharmaceuticals, and chemicals. The business model involves selling these indicators and the necessary application machinery to producers. This technology aims to reduce food waste by providing clearer information to both retailers and consumers, and to enhance food safety. Keep-it Technologies has achieved several key milestones throughout its history. After its founding and initial lab verification in 2001, the company, then TimeTemp, secured second place in DNB's national innovation competition in 2003. Between 2003 and 2007, the technology was further developed, leading to a working lab prototype and patents in several countries, including the USA. With support from the Research Council of Norway, an industrial prototype was developed and tested between 2007 and 2009. The company raised new investment capital in 2010 and 2011, which funded the development of the first consumer version of the indicator. A major commercial breakthrough occurred in 2012 when the Keep-it indicator was launched in partnership with Norwegian retailer Rema 1000. The company has secured a total of $5.86 million in funding over three rounds, with the latest being a grant in March 2018. column5: Wireless power transfer solutions for electric mobility
column6: WPT Energy is a technology company focused on advancing wireless power transfer (WPT) for electric vehicles to accelerate the adoption of modern electromobility. The company is developing solutions designed to make EV charging more seamless, efficient, and sustainable by removing infrastructure barriers. WPT technology enables the transfer of electrical energy from a power source to a vehicle without physical connectors, using electromagnetic fields. This can be applied to both stationary charging in parking spots and dynamic charging, where vehicles are powered while in motion on electric roads. The company's journey began with research and development of WPT system components, leading to successful laboratory testing and a proof of concept. WPT Energy is now focused on increasing its technology readiness level (TRL) in preparation for pilot deployments and market entry. The technology addresses key EV challenges such as charging speed and the inconvenience of different connectors. It also offers benefits like enhanced safety by eliminating exposed high-voltage cables and the potential for automated charging processes. The team consists of three members with backgrounds in electrical and electronic engineering, prototype development, and electronic system design. Their experience also covers business operations, project management, and intellectual property protection for advanced technologies. WPT Energy aims to partner with organizations that share its vision of building the infrastructure for the next generation of electric mobility. column5: Climate-smart farming solutions for African agriculture
column6: Clargreen is an agricultural technology company focused on sustainable farming in Africa. Founded by CEO Tobe Obi, a social entrepreneur with a background in sustainability, the company aims to connect biochar science and regenerative farming with farmer prosperity. The core of Clargreen's business is turning agricultural waste into biochar, a carbon-sequestering soil enhancer, which helps regenerate soil, increase crop yields, and allows farmers to earn carbon credits. The company's primary product is CO₂ Savior, a biochar-based soil booster enriched with nutrients from Black Soldier Fly Larvae frass. This product is designed to capture carbon, improve soil health, and boost yields. Clargreen's business model involves several steps: they enroll and train smallholder farmers in regenerative practices and the use of their products at no upfront cost. The company then monitors and collects soil data with partners to verify carbon capture. These verified carbon credits are then aggregated and sold on global voluntary carbon markets like Verra (VCS) and Gold Standard. A portion of the revenue generated from these sales is distributed back to the farmers as income. Clargreen operates a specialized facility that uses clean pyrolysis technology to produce its biochar and organic inputs. The company serves a range of clients, including smallholder farmers, as well as partners, investors, and NGOs interested in sustainable agriculture and climate solutions. By converting agricultural waste into a valuable resource, Clargreen helps farmers become active participants in climate action while improving their livelihoods. column5: Seed-sharing library network promoting biodiversity and natural gardening
column6: Semínkovna is a Czech initiative established in 2015 by botanist Klára Hrdá, inspired by French 'Les Grainotheques' and American 'Seed Libraries'. It operates as a non-profit network of 'seed libraries,' which are physical locations, often in public libraries, cafes, or community centers, where individuals can freely share and exchange non-hybrid, chemically untreated seeds. The primary goal is to preserve local and heirloom plant varieties, promote biodiversity, and encourage natural gardening and seed-saving skills among the public. The initiative began as a grassroots movement and evolved into the registered association, Semínkovna, z.s., in 2016 to support the growing network. As of 2024, there are over 200 seed library locations in the Czech Republic, with the concept expanding to Slovakia, Poland, and other countries. The model functions on a principle of sharing: people take seeds for their gardens with the intention of cultivating the plants, letting some go to seed, and returning a portion of the newly harvested seeds to the library for others to use. This creates a self-sustaining, community-driven system that increases access to diverse, locally adapted seeds and reduces reliance on commercial, often hybrid, seeds that cannot be reliably replanted. In addition to the seed exchange network, Semínkovna operates an educational platform called Semínkovna EDU. This arm focuses on reviving seed-saving skills by offering online courses, workshops, lectures, and educational programs for schools and the general public. The organization's revenue is generated through these educational activities, grants, and collaborations, rather than the sale of seeds, which are always shared for free for non-commercial use. column5: Energy-from-waste services converting residual waste to energy
column6: Encyclis is an owner and operator of energy-from-waste (EfW) facilities in the United Kingdom and Ireland. The company, formerly the European branch of Covanta Corporation, became a standalone entity named Encyclis in January 2023 after being acquired by EQT Infrastructure. The company's core business involves treating non-recyclable residual waste, often called "black bag" waste, that would otherwise be sent to landfills. Through a process of combustion at its facilities, Encyclis converts this waste into baseload electricity, heat for district networks, and other reusable materials. This business model is central to its role in the waste hierarchy, which prioritizes waste reduction and recycling, followed by energy recovery. By-products of this process include ash, which can be repurposed as aggregate for the construction industry, and recovered ferrous and non-ferrous metals for recycling. Encyclis operates several advanced energy recovery facilities across the UK and Ireland, including sites in Dublin, Bedfordshire, Leicestershire, and Scotland, with more under construction. Collectively, these plants divert over 1.5 million tonnes of waste from landfills annually, generating enough electricity to power nearly 300,000 homes. The company is also focused on decarbonization and advancing the industry's goal of reaching net zero by 2040. A key initiative is the development of the UK's first full-scale carbon capture plant at an EfW facility, located at its Protos site in Cheshire, which aims to be operational by mid-2029. column5: Utility-scale battery energy storage investment trust
column6: Harmony Energy Income Trust PLC (HEIT) is an investment company that invests in a portfolio of commercial-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) in Great Britain. Founded in 2021, the trust was launched on the London Stock Exchange in November of that year, raising £186.5 million in its Initial Public Offering (IPO). The company was established to acquire, fund the construction of, and operate BESS projects developed by its parent company, Harmony Energy Limited. The trust focuses exclusively on 2-hour duration BESS projects, which it believes offers superior performance in wholesale energy markets compared to shorter-duration systems. Its business model centers on acquiring "shovel-ready" projects, overseeing their construction, and then generating revenue through their operation. Revenue is primarily generated by absorbing excess renewable power during periods of oversupply and discharging it back to the grid when demand is high, a strategy known as arbitrage. The assets also participate in ancillary services markets and the UK's Capacity Market to secure additional income streams. Upon its IPO, HEIT acquired a seed portfolio of five BESS projects and secured exclusive rights to a pipeline of future projects from Harmony Energy Limited. The portfolio grew to include eight operational projects with a total capacity of 790.8 MWh / 395.4 MW, featuring some of the largest BESS assets in Europe by MWh, such as the Pillswood and Bumpers projects. The company utilizes Tesla's Megapack systems and its Autobidder AI platform for revenue optimization. In 2025, after facing market headwinds and its shares trading at a significant discount to its Net Asset Value (NAV), HEIT's board initiated a sale process. column6: Service Enviro SCAD Inc. is a Quebec-based clean technology company specializing in the recovery and stabilization of organic waste. The company was founded by CEO Songwen Xu, who has over two decades of experience in multicultural team management and global partnership development. The company addresses a wide range of waste streams, including agricultural residues like livestock manure and straw, urban waste, and environmental contaminants such as cyanobacteria in waterways. column5: Direct lithium extraction and production from oilfield brine
column6: Volt Lithium Corp., which will be renamed LibertyStream Infrastructure Partners Inc. effective June 2025, is a mineral development and technology company focused on the extraction of lithium from oilfield brines. Alex Wylie, the President and CEO, has a background in economics and a track record of building businesses in the resource sector. By retrofitting this infrastructure, Volt avoids the costs associated with exploration, drilling new wells, and extensive construction. The company's revenue model involves sharing revenue with its oil producer partners. Volt has developed a proprietary, three-stage Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) technology. The first stage involves purifying the brine to remove up to 99% of contaminants. The second stage uses the company's core DLE technology, which has demonstrated up to 99% lithium extraction rates. The final stage processes the extracted lithium chloride into battery-grade lithium carbonate (99.5% pure) and lithium hydroxide. This in-house processing capability allows Volt to produce a suite of saleable lithium products. The company has proven its technology can achieve these results with all-in operating costs below US$2,900 per tonne of lithium carbonate equivalent (LCE), even with low lithium concentrations. Volt Lithium achieved its first lithium production in September 2024 at a field unit in the Permian Basin, Texas, in partnership with a major operator. The company operates a permanent field simulation and demonstration plant in Calgary, Alberta, and is expanding its operations into North Dakota's Bakken region. The company's shares are listed on the TSX Venture Exchange, the OTCQB, and the Frankfurt Stock Exchange. column5: Valorizing phosphate byproducts into strategic fluorine materials
column6: Fluoralpha S.A., founded in 2023, is a Moroccan-based company developed by INNOVX S.A. to valorize fluorine derived from the country's extensive phosphate rock reserves. The company's CEO is Jalil Skali. Fluoralpha is focused on transforming hexafluorosilicic acid (FSA), a byproduct of phosphate fertilizer production, into high-value, strategic materials essential for future-facing industries. This business model is central to a circular economy approach, converting industrial byproducts into critical resources. The company is constructing a large-scale industrial project in Jorf Lasfar with a total investment of MAD 2.5 billion ($280 million). This project includes two main production units: one for anhydrous hydrofluoric acid (AHF) with a planned annual capacity of 20,000 tons, and another for aluminum fluoride (AlF₃) with a 28,000-ton annual capacity. In September 2025, Fluoralpha secured over MAD 1 billion ($110 million) in financing from Bank of Africa to advance this development. Fluoralpha's products serve as critical inputs for several global value chains. Anhydrous hydrofluoric acid is a key material for producing semiconductors, battery electrolytes (specifically LiPF₆ salt for lithium-ion batteries), and specialty chemicals. Aluminum fluoride is used in primary aluminum electrolysis. The company is also developing synthetic calcium fluoride (CaF₂) to help diversify the global fluorine supply. Through these activities, Fluoralpha aims to position Morocco as a global hub for fluorine products, supporting sectors like electric mobility, energy storage, advanced electronics, and aluminum production. A significant milestone is the strategic partnership with Falcon Energy Materials, announced in May 2025, to support the development of a pilot and large-scale anode plant for coated spherical purified graphite (CSPG) in Jorf Lasfar. AHF is a critical reagent for purifying graphite, and this collaboration provides Falcon with a local, reliable supply, de-risking their operations. As part of the agreement, Fluoralpha will provide land for the pilot plant within its industrial zone. Construction of the pilot plant was anticipated to begin in Q2 2025. column6: GL Biocontrol specializes in environmental risk management, providing advanced tools for monitoring the biological quality of water and surfaces. Founded over a decade ago, GL Biocontrol has focused on developing solutions for sanitary engineering and biological surveillance. The company's business model combines the sale of diagnostic products with comprehensive client support, including user-friendly software, technical consulting, training, and risk assessment services. The core product line is the DENDRIDIAG® range of ATP-metry kits, which are designed for on-site use by field operators to quickly detect sanitary risks. In addition to its commercial products, the company's R&D department actively engages in developing new tools and customized protocols, often in partnership with academic and private institutions. column5: AI software for real-time food recipe carbon footprint analysis
column6: Forkprint is an AI-driven software tool designed to calculate the carbon footprint of food recipes in real-time. It was developed through a collaboration between the University of Manchester's Natural Language Processing (NLP) team, led by Dr. Riza Batista-Navarro, and E. Mission Innovation Ltd. The project was initially funded by Nesta, the UK's innovation agency for social good. The core of Forkprint's technology utilizes advanced NLP and AI to automatically analyze ingredients listed in recipes, assess their CO2 emissions, and suggest alternative, lower-carbon substitutions. This process involves 'reading' a recipe to extract the ingredients and then using a comprehensive database to calculate the meal's total carbon footprint, measured in kg carbon dioxide equivalent (kg CO2e). The system can analyze individual ingredients or entire menus, with the goal of making it easier for individuals and organizations to make sustainable food choices. According to the company, its intelligent substitution suggestions can help users reduce their food-related carbon emissions by up to 11%. Forkprint's business model is centered on licensing opportunities and partnerships. The company is targeting a diverse market, including recipe websites, the food service industry (restaurants and caterers), food management systems, and individual home cooks. The tool is available as a Chrome plugin and a mobile application, allowing users to analyze the environmental impact of any online recipe. For businesses, it can be integrated into existing systems to enhance sustainability features or used to develop eco-friendly menu options.
