column5: Biorefinery producing textile pulp and bioenergy from wood
column6: AustroCel Hallein GmbH is an integrated biorefinery based in Hallein, Austria, that specializes in the sustainable processing of wood into high-purity dissolving pulp for textile fibers and bioenergy. The company has a long history, founded in 1890 by Austrian chemist Dr. Carl Kellner and industrialist Edward Partington as “The Kellner Partington Paper Co. Ltd”. Throughout its existence, it has undergone numerous ownership and name changes, including periods as part of Borregaard, Schweighofer Fiber, and since 2017, it has been owned by TowerBrook Capital Partners. In September 2025, Oji Holdings announced an agreement to acquire all shares of the company. The company's core business model is centered on a zero-waste, circular economy. It processes PEFC-certified spruce wood, primarily sawmill residues, to produce up to 160,000 tons of viscose pulp annually, serving the textile industry, particularly as a market leader in China. By-products from the pulp production process are utilized to generate significant amounts of bioenergy. This includes approximately 100 GWh of green electricity, enough to power up to 28,000 households, and 100 GWh of district heating for 13,000 homes in the region. Since late 2020, AustroCel has operated the world's largest wood-based bioethanol plant, producing up to 35 million liters of second-generation bioethanol per year from wood sugars. This advanced biofuel is supplied to the Austrian oil and gas company OMV, contributing to a reduction of up to 50,000 tons of CO2 emissions annually. The biorefinery employs approximately 330 people and has an annual turnover of over €150 million. AustroCel is expanding its product portfolio, with plans to begin industrial production of a lignin-based hydrogel granulate called Retentis® in early 2025 in collaboration with the startup Agrobiogel GmbH. This biodegradable product is designed to increase the water storage capacity of soil, aiding agriculture in dry conditions. The leadership team includes CEO Dr. Wolfram Kalt, who took over from Jörg Harbring in July 2025, and CFO Bernhard Krill. column6: Fusion Fuel Cycles Inc. (FFC) is a joint venture established in May 2024 by Canadian Nuclear Laboratories (CNL) and Kyoto Fusioneering (KF), a Japanese fusion technology startup founded in 2019. The company is headquartered at CNL's Chalk River Laboratories in Ontario, Canada. FFC was created to develop and deploy deuterium-tritium (D-T) fusion fuel cycle technologies on a commercial scale for the global fusion market. The venture combines CNL's over 70 years of expertise in tritium research, handling, and management with Kyoto Fusioneering's proficiency in fusion plant engineering and technology integration. FFC provides comprehensive, end-to-end solutions for fusion developers, including design, engineering consultancy, manufacturing, installation, and commissioning of fuel cycle systems. The company's business model is centered on offering these products and services to a growing market of private and public fusion development programs. FFC operates with a novel co-CEO governance model, led by Dr. Ian Castillo from CNL and Yuhei Nozoe from KF, reflecting its collaborative international foundation. FFC's primary offering is a performance-driven fuel cycle designed to enhance fuel efficiency, minimize tritium inventory, and maximize heat transfer for power conversion. The company's flagship project is the Unique Integrated Testing Facility (UNITY-2), which is set to be the world's first fully-integrated fusion fuel cycle test facility. Scheduled for full operation by mid-2026, UNITY-2 will serve as an open platform for fusion innovators to test components, de-risk technologies, and close scientific gaps related to tritium processing systems. This facility is crucial for developing the reliable and efficient fuel cycles necessary for commercial fusion power plants, which involves breeding, capturing, extracting, and recycling tritium fuel. In August 2025, FFC secured a US$20 million, ten-year strategic investment from General Atomics for the UNITY-2 project. column5: Public energy procurement for Italy's protected market
column6: Acquirente Unico S.p.A. is a publicly-owned company within the Gestore dei Servizi Energetici (GSE) group, which is wholly owned by the Italian Ministry of Economy and Finance. Established in 1999 following the liberalization of the Italian energy market through the Bersani Decree, its primary mandate is to guarantee the supply of electricity to customers in the protected market. This includes households and small businesses that have not switched to a provider in the free market. The company purchases electricity on the wholesale market, including the Italian Power Exchange (IPEX) and through bilateral contracts, under the most favorable conditions and then sells it to retail operators serving the protected market. The price is set to cover operational costs, ensuring transparency. Over the years, Acquirente Unico's responsibilities have expanded significantly beyond its initial procurement role to enhance consumer protection and support the functioning of the energy markets. Since 2009, it has managed several key services. The 'Sportello per il Consumatore di Energia e Ambiente' (Energy and Environment Consumer Help Desk) provides information and a free conciliation service to resolve disputes between consumers and suppliers. Another critical function is the management of the 'Sistema Informativo Integrato' (SII), a centralized data hub that manages information flows for the electricity and gas markets, streamlining processes like supplier switching. The company also operates the 'Portale Offerte,' a comparison tool for consumers to evaluate electricity and gas offers, and the 'Portale Consumi,' which allows users to access their own consumption data. Furthermore, Acquirente Unico manages last-resort supply services to ensure continuity of service for customers who find themselves without a provider. It is also the designated Central Stockholding Entity (OCSIT) for Italy, responsible for maintaining national strategic oil reserves for energy security. The company is a key institutional player, operating under the directives of the Regulatory Authority for Energy, Networks and Environment (ARERA) to ensure a secure, efficient, and equitable energy supply for protected customers as the market transitions. Bei ihren Pflanzaktionen entsteht ein Gemeinschaftsgefühl, das weit über den einzelnen Tag hinaus wirkt. Teilnehmer erleben unmittelbar, wie sie Teil einer positiven Veränderung werden, und nehmen dieses Bewusstsein in ihren Alltag und ihre Organisationen mit. So entsteht ein Kreislauf aus Engagement, Bildung und Motivation.Für Unternehmen bieten die Waldfreunde speziell entwickelte Teambuilding-Formate an, bei denen Mitarbeitende nicht nur gemeinsam Bäume pflanzen, sondern auch Nachhaltigkeit praktisch erleben. Die Waldfreunde möchten die junge Generation inspirieren, selbst aktiv zu werden und zu verstehen, dass Klimaschutz im Kleinen beginnt. Mit der Entwicklung einer eigenen technologischen Plattform gehen die Waldfreunde neue Wege im Natur- und Klimaschutz. Langfristig wollen sie ein Netzwerk schaffen, das Aufforstungsinitiativen in ganz Deutschland vernetzt und Wissen, Ressourcen und Menschen zusammenführt. Ziel ist es, Wälder nicht nur als Kohlenstoffspeicher, sondern als Lebensräume und Orte der Begegnung zu begreifen.Die Waldfreunde gGmbH steht für eine Haltung, die verbindet: Wissenschaft und Herz, Fortschritt und Tradition, Engagement und Freude am Tun. Ihr Wirken ist ein Beispiel dafür, wie nachhaltiger Wandel von unten entsteht – durch Menschen, die Verantwortung übernehmen und Zuversicht in die Welt pflanzen.

column5: High-power gyrotron systems for industrial and research applications
column6: MWB Gyrotron Industries develops high-power gyrotron systems, which are advanced vacuum electronic devices that generate millimeter-wave electromagnetic waves. Pagonakis has a research history in simulating electron beams within gyrotron geometry, while Thumm is a distinguished fellow at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT) with decades of experience in high-power gyrotron development for nuclear fusion and industrial material processing. The core business revolves around manufacturing these high-power microwave sources and related components. Gyrotrons operate by using the cyclotron resonance of electrons in a strong magnetic field to produce high-frequency, high-power radiation. This technology is a critical component for various high-tech sectors. Primary clients include nuclear fusion research experiments, such as tokamaks and stellarators, where gyrotrons are essential for plasma heating and current drive (ECRH and ECCD). Beyond fusion, the company serves the industrial manufacturing sector, providing solutions for rapid material processing, including the heating and sintering of ceramics, composites, and glass. Additional applications exist in spectroscopy, particle acceleration, and advanced communications research. A gyrotron consists of an electron gun, a resonant cavity within a superconducting magnet, and a collector. The electron gun emits a beam of electrons that are accelerated and caused to move helically by the magnetic field, generating powerful microwave radiation. These systems can be engineered for either pulsed or continuous wave operation, achieving power levels up to several megawatts. MWB's business model likely involves the direct sale of these complex systems, along with integration services, staff training, and ongoing support for its specialized client base. column6: Birds&Co is a Swiss startup focused on fostering coexistence between boat owners and lakeside birds. column6: A Matter of Fruit is a material design company operating within the circular economy, focused on transforming food industry byproducts into sustainable materials. column6: ECO Shrimp Garden, founded in 2015 by Jean Claude Frajmund, operated as an indoor, sustainable shrimp farm in Newburgh, New York. The business was established to counter the environmental and social issues associated with imported shrimp, such as chemical use, slave labor, and high carbon footprints. The founder, Jean Claude Frajmund, a Brazilian transplant, was inspired 35 years prior to the company's launch after tasting shrimp fresh from the ocean in Brazil. His experience working in high-end New York City restaurants, where the origin of seafood was often unknown, further solidified his mission. Frajmund's varied background includes computer programming, documentary filmmaking, and educational consulting. This diverse experience influenced his approach, aiming to create an "open source" system for sustainable shrimp farming. The company utilized a closed-loop, zero-water-exchange system (IZHEA) with biofloc technology. This method uses a mix of beneficial bacteria, algae, and protozoans to mimic a natural oceanic environment, process waste, and provide a supplementary protein source for the shrimp. The farm was located in the basement of a former mattress factory, housing 24 tanks and four nurseries for raising Pacific White Shrimp. This system allowed for the production of fresh, never-frozen shrimp free of chemicals, antibiotics, and hormones, delivered to customers within hours of harvest. ECO Shrimp Garden served both retail and restaurant clients in the greater New York City area, including sales at the Union Square Greenmarket and to high-profile restaurants like Blue Hill at Stone Barns. The business model focused on providing a local, sustainable, and fresh product directly to consumers and chefs. The company received $175,000 in funding from the Hudson Valley Startup Fund. column5: Futura Industries designs and manufactures a wide range of extruded aluminum products for a number of industries and end markets
column6: The story of Futura Industries begins not with aluminum, but with a product called colfonite in the 1930s. In the mid-1940s, founder Frank Hobbs started a company named Colotyle. As demand for moldings grew, a new entity called the Colotrym Company was formed. By 1946 and 1947, the company expanded its product line, but a new material, extruded aluminum, was emerging as a less expensive competitor to stainless steel. Recognizing this shift, Colotrym installed its own extrusion presses in the mid-1950s after moving operations to Seattle. A significant chapter opened in 1964 when Bob Hansberger acquired the company and renamed it "Futura," envisioning it as an operator of businesses. Under this new leadership, sales doubled between 1964 and 1970. To improve distribution to California and the Midwest, a warehouse was established in Clearfield, Utah. The Utah location proved so successful that by 1979, all manufacturing was moved from Seattle to Clearfield, where it remains today. The company continued to focus on aluminum extrusions, manufacturing a wide array of products from flooring transitions to components for truck grills and solar panels. The final major event in its journey came in February 2017, when Futura Industries was acquired by Tredegar Corporation's subsidiary, The William L. Bonnell Company, for approximately $92 million. Following the acquisition, Futura became an operating division of Bonnell Aluminum, integrating its West Coast strength with Bonnell's broader market presence.

column5: Pozzolanic material for low-carbon green concrete production
column6: Universal Pozzolanic Silica Alumina (UPSA) is a private company, incorporated in England and Wales in May 2023, that controls the rights to a major pozzolanic silica alumina (PSA) resource. The company's core business revolves around marketing this resource, a key ingredient for producing 'green concrete', to the global construction industry. This material, a supplementary cementitious material (SCM), can substitute up to 40% of cement in concrete, leading to significant reductions in carbon emissions, as cement production accounts for approximately 8% of global CO₂ emissions. UPSA holds the commercialization rights to one of the world's largest PSA reserves, located at the Yammacoona Sand Quarry near Warialda, New South Wales, Australia. The company acquired these rights from Claystone International Pty Ltd, a company owned by William Clift, for a 99-year period starting in June 2023. Initial resource modeling estimates an inferred resource of 160.68 million tonnes, with a potential Net Present Value (NPV) of approximately A$3.3 billion over 25 years if the resource is proven. The business model is centered on supplying this PSA to major cement and concrete producers for use in large-scale private and government infrastructure projects worldwide. The company is actively engaging with potential off-takers in the UK, US, Africa, and Australia. In September 2025, Atlas Metals Group plc signed a conditional share purchase agreement to acquire UPSA for £1 billion in an all-share deal that would constitute a reverse takeover. The transaction, if completed, is expected to result in existing Atlas shareholders holding a 3% interest in the newly enlarged company, which would be repositioned as a significant player in the sustainable construction materials market. The deal highlights the growing market interest in materials that can decarbonize the construction sector. column5: Digital twin for wind turbine performance optimization
column6: Tipspeed provides software and services to wind energy asset managers and performance experts, focusing on enhancing wind turbine efficiency. The company has developed a digital twin that integrates existing data with physics-based models to create a comprehensive view of performance, from resource to production. This technology generates reference time series for wind and power that are independent of SCADA data, which can often be biased or miss changes over time. The core of Tipspeed's offering is its ability to deliver continuous performance insights. By comparing the digital twin's output with actual production data, asset managers can identify performance deviations, diagnose issues like yaw misalignment, and uncover optimization opportunities at scale without needing to install additional hardware. This allows for the continuous screening of all turbines simultaneously, helping to detect performance degradation or changes caused by factors like new neighboring wind farms. The software and its insights are accessible through an online application or can be integrated into clients' existing monitoring and reporting workflows. The problem Tipspeed addresses is the difficulty in untangling resource availability from asset underperformance using traditional tools. Standard monitoring based on nacelle anemometers has limitations in accuracy, and while more precise instruments exist, they are often too expensive to deploy across an entire asset's lifespan. Tipspeed's model-based solution provides a consistent and accurate reference for a site's true potential, enabling more effective performance assessments and optimizations. column5: Flexible, soft robotics-based wave energy converters
column6: EBB-FLOW Energy Ltd, incorporated on March 20, 2025, is a UK-based company developing a novel type of wave energy converter (WEC). The company was founded by Andrew Thomas Hall and Benjamin Jo Wilson. EBB-FLOW aims to address the commercial viability challenges that have hindered traditional WECs, which typically rely on large, rigid steel structures and monolithic power systems that are expensive to build and scale. The company’s approach is fundamentally different, utilizing a modular, flexible structure composed of thousands of lightweight, active generating cells inspired by soft robotics. This design distributes loads across the structure, maximizing the active power-generating material while minimizing the need for bulky, expensive components. EBB-FLOW intends for these cells to be mass-manufacturable using existing roll-to-roll industrial processes, similar to those used for flexible electronics and batteries, which is projected to significantly reduce the capital expenditure (CAPEX) compared to legacy WEC designs. The technology is designed to be highly tunable, allowing for optimization across a wide range of sea states to deliver consistent energy output, which is particularly valuable when wind and solar generation is low. By avoiding concentrated stress points and enabling scalable production, EBB-FLOW's system is positioned to be a more affordable and resilient solution in the renewable energy market. The initial concept was developed through a project sponsored by Wave Energy Scotland, which brought together expertise in wave energy and direct power generation. column5: AI-powered predictive maintenance for rotating water equipment
column6: Aquatis is a climate-focused technology company founded in Israel in 2023, specializing in predictive and prescriptive maintenance for critical rotating equipment. The company operates in the water, energy, and industrial sectors, serving clients such as water utilities, desalination plants, wastewater treatment facilities, and renewable energy operations. The core of Aquatis' offering is an AI-driven solution that utilizes proprietary wireless sensors to monitor the health of machinery like pumps, blowers, and decanters. These sensors, which can be easily attached to equipment, detect three-axis vibrations and temperature, transmitting data several times a day. This data is then analyzed by machine learning and rule-based algorithms, which leverage a database of over 40 million tagged data points to identify anomalies and potential failures. Based on this analysis, Aquatis provides prescriptive insights and actionable recommendations to address specific issues such as bearing wear or misalignment, enabling operators to perform maintenance proactively. The company's business model is service-based, generating revenue through treatment fees. column6: Lamb Space Tec GmbH is a German aerospace company focused on challenging the conventional manufacturing methods within the small satellite industry. The firm's core business revolves around the mass production of low-cost, sustainable, and reliable CubeSat structures. Instead of using aluminum, which requires time-consuming CNC milling and manual assembly, Lamb Space Tec employs plastic injection molding with the high-performance polymer PEEK (Polyether ether ketone). To further its sustainability goals, the company is also researching the integration of biopolymers and recycled PEEK into its manufacturing processes. Beyond satellite structures, Lamb Space Tec develops and manufactures compact, lightweight actuators based on shape memory alloys (SMAs). These unlocking systems, like the "FG-ONE" actuator, are designed for various space-related applications such as deploying antenna modules. The company serves clients requiring customized satellite components, offering services that span from material selection and design to prototype production and full-scale manufacturing. Through its participation in the ESA Business Incubation Centre North Rhine-Westphalia, the company is positioned to further develop and commercialize its products for the space technology market. column5: Accredited structural testing for wind turbine blades
column6: Blaest A/S is a specialized independent laboratory that provides full-scale structural testing services for wind turbine blades. The company's operations are a mandatory part of the type certification process for wind turbines, ensuring their strength and structural integrity before market entry. Blaest's client base primarily consists of European wind turbine manufacturers. The business model is purely commercial, operating without public funding, and generates revenue by providing accredited testing services. The company's history is deeply connected to the evolution of the wind energy industry. It was officially founded as Blade Test Centre A/S on May 1, 2005, as a spin-off from the RISØ National Laboratory, with RISØ, Force Technology, and Det Norske Veritas as initial shareholders. This separation occurred because the commercial nature of the blade testing activities no longer aligned with RISØ's basic research focus. In 2023, the company formally changed its name to Blaest A/S. The journey began much earlier, with the first static tests of blades occurring in 1981 and fatigue tests in 1984 at Risø. A key figure, Erik Grove-Nielsen, established the Sparkær Blade Test Centre in 1986, which was later taken over by RISØ in 1990 to accommodate the rapidly growing size of turbine blades. Blaest offers a comprehensive suite of accredited services, including static load tests, fatigue load tests, modal analysis, and determination of natural frequencies. They also provide non-accredited services like thermographic investigation and mechanical stiffness tests. With two test halls and eight test rigs, Blaest has the capacity to test up to six blades in parallel, accommodating lengths of up to 120 meters. The company continuously invests in advanced equipment to meet the demands of ever-larger offshore wind turbines, recently completing a new rig capable of testing blades over 100 meters long for clients like Siemens Gamesa. column5: Real-time corrosion monitoring for closed-loop water systems
column6: Hevasure, launched in 2014, provides patented technology for monitoring corrosion in the closed-circuit water systems of commercial buildings. The company was founded by Steve Munn, who drew upon his background in materials science and experience from Midland Corrosion Services to address the costly and damaging failures in HVAC systems. The firm's core offering is a fully integrated monitoring station that uses high-quality sensors to track water conditions and corrosion rates 24/7. This technology provides real-time data on key parameters that cause corrosion, such as dissolved oxygen, pH, pressure, and inhibitor levels. Data is typically captured every 15 minutes and sent to a cloud-based platform, where it can be accessed via a dashboard on laptops or mobile devices. The system is designed to send instant alerts via email or SMS when water conditions change, allowing building managers and engineers to take preventative action before significant corrosion damage occurs. Hevasure's business model is centered on providing this monitoring technology to a range of clients, including building owners, facilities managers, M&E contractors, and specifiers. Its product line includes the 'Aquila' range for full-spectrum water monitoring and the 'Condor' range, which focuses specifically on detecting corrosion. Variants exist for different security needs, such as the Aquila-S, which integrates directly with a building's management system (BMS) for high-security sites where data cannot leave the premises. The company's technology helps clients reduce the risk of system failure, cut down on site visits and sampling, ensure operational efficiency, and avoid expensive repairs. column5: Cooperative producing sustainably grown fresh Greek almonds
column6: Karpologio is an agricultural cooperative comprised of young farmers cultivating almond groves in the Thessalian plain of Greece, near the foothills of Mount Olympus. The initiative was co-founded by Eirini Christina Spanouli and her father, Kostas Spanoulis. The family transitioned from primarily grain and cotton farming to almond production in 2016 in response to rising global demand. Kostas Spanoulis was the first in Greece to implement a high-density planting method for almond trees, a technique that increases yield per hectare by a third compared to conventional methods. The cooperative focuses on environmentally friendly and innovative cultivation practices. They share facilities and mechanical equipment, including their own nutcracker, which allows them to shell the almonds just before sale to ensure maximum freshness and preserve their nutritional value. The group employs sustainable methods, such as using bees for pollination instead of spraying pesticides and enriching the soil with pruned branches. Karpologio sells its almonds directly to the market, managing the processing and packaging collectively. In 2023, Eirini Christina Spanouli won first prize in the EWA (Empowering Women in Agrifood) competition, an award intended to support the development of a packaging facility and product promotion. The cooperative, consisting of 14 young farmers, has faced significant challenges, including the complete loss of their crop in the devastating floods of September 2023. column5: Dynamic in-motion charging rail for mining vehicles
column6: BluVein is a Brisbane-based company, founded in 2021, that provides dynamic charging technology for heavy-duty electric vehicles in the mining sector. The company emerged from a joint venture between Olitek, an Australian firm with 25 years of experience in mining machinery and robotics, and EVIAS, a Swedish company with over a decade of research in electrified highways. This partnership adapts proven e-highway technology for the harsh conditions of both underground and open-pit mining. The core of BluVein's offering is a patented rail-and-hammer system that allows mining vehicles to connect to a power grid and charge while in motion. This "dynamic charging" powers the vehicle's motors directly while simultaneously charging its onboard batteries, which eliminates the need for stationary charging or battery swapping and reduces operational downtime. The technology is OEM-agnostic, meaning it can be integrated with vehicles from various manufacturers. By enabling the use of smaller, lighter batteries, the system allows for increased payload and faster haulage speeds. BluVein offers two main product lines. BluVein1 is designed for underground applications, supporting vehicles up to 60 tonnes and delivering approximately 1MW of power. BluVeinXL targets open-pit surface mines, providing up to 8MW of power for haul trucks with payloads of up to 400 tonnes. The enclosed, IP-rated slotted rail design is a key safety feature, mitigating the risks associated with conventional overhead trolley lines. The company operates on a consortium model, collaborating with major mining companies and vehicle manufacturers to accelerate development and adoption. Partners have included BHP, Rio Tinto, Vale, Glencore, and Newcrest Mining, who have helped fund the development and pilot testing of the technology. This collaborative approach aims to establish an industry standard for safe and flexible dynamic charging infrastructure. column5: Caribbean's largest combined-cycle gas-fired power plant
column6: Trinidad Generation Unlimited (TGU) owns and operates a 720-megawatt, combined-cycle power plant in La Brea, Trinidad, which is the largest and most efficient of its kind in the Caribbean. The company supplies approximately 50% of Trinidad and Tobago's electricity. Established on December 13, 2006, TGU began as a joint venture between the state-owned Union Estate Electricity Generation Company Limited (UEEGCL) and the AES Corporation from the United States. Construction of the plant commenced in January 2009, with the facility beginning phased commercial operations on August 1, 2011, and reaching full capacity in December 2012. In a significant milestone, UEEGCL acquired all of AES Corporation's shares on July 10, 2013, rendering TGU a 100% state-owned entity. Subsequently, in May 2018, TGU was integrated into the National Investment Fund Holding Company Limited (NIF), a holding company created by the Government of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago (GORTT). TGU's business model is structured around a 30-year power purchase agreement (PPA) with the Trinidad and Tobago Electricity Commission (T&TEC), which commenced in August 2011. Under this tolling agreement, T&TEC is the sole off-taker of the energy and supplies the natural gas fuel at no cost to TGU, which ensures stable revenue streams based on capacity payments rather than exposure to fuel price volatility. This structure positions TGU as a critical strategic asset for maintaining low energy prices in the country. The plant's technology is highly efficient; it features six GE gas turbines that generate 450 MW, and the waste heat is captured by heat recovery steam generators to power two additional steam turbines, producing another 270 MW without consuming more fuel. column5: Large-scale underground hydrogen and compressed air energy storage
column6: Triple Point Resources Ltd. is a Canadian company focused on developing large-scale, underground clean energy storage solutions. A 2023 assessment confirmed the dome's significant potential, with space to store over 180,000 tonnes of hydrogen across multiple caverns. The project aims to function as a dual-storage facility for both compressed air energy storage (CAES) to manage grid imbalances and hydrogen storage to support the export market. Triple Point Resources was established in 2022 as a spinout from Atlas Salt. The company is led by CEO Julie Lemieux, who has extensive experience in strategic business development and financial restructuring. The leadership team also includes founder and Chairman of the Board John Anderson, who brings nearly three decades of experience in corporate and capital markets. column5: Bio-electricity generation from living plants' natural processes
column6: Plant-e BV is a Dutch company established in 2009 as a spin-off from Wageningen University, specializing in technology that generates electricity from living plants without harming them. The company was co-founded by Marjolein Helder (CEO) and David Strik, who developed the technology based on an idea from Dr. ir. Bert Hamelers at the university. The technology was patented in 2007, and Plant-e is the patent holder. The core technology leverages the natural process of photosynthesis. Plants produce organic matter, and a portion of this is excreted into the soil via the roots. Naturally occurring microorganisms break down these organic compounds, releasing electrons as a waste product. Plant-e's system uses inert electrodes placed near the roots to capture these electrons, creating a continuous, 24/7 electrical current while the plant continues to grow undisturbed. This process has a positive climate impact by storing CO2 and reducing methane formation in the soil by 50%. Plant-e has developed several products based on this technology. Its main offerings are modular systems and a tubular system. The modular systems consist of trays or containers with plants and integrated electrodes, which can be used to create electricity-generating green roofs or other installations. These systems are designed to power low-energy applications such as LED mood lighting and remote sensors, eliminating the need for batteries. The company also offers a tubular system designed for large-scale application in existing wetlands, rice paddies, and mangrove forests, which enables dual land use for conservation or agriculture alongside power generation. For educational and consumer markets, Plant-e provides DIY kits to build small-scale plant batteries. The company's business model involves selling these systems for various applications, including powering sensors to monitor groundwater levels and providing lighting in parks. Plant-e has received notable recognition, being named a World Economic Forum Technology Pioneer in 2015. It has also secured significant funding, including a €2.5 million grant from the European Innovation Council (EIC) in 2021 to further develop its plant-powered sensor applications and scale up production. column5: Geothermal heat recovery from end-of-life oil wells
column6: Algar Geothermal, incorporated in 2015, is a clean technology company based in Calgary, Alberta, focused on converting end-of-life oil and gas wells into sources of geothermal heat. The company was co-founded by Blair Shunk and Peter Graham. The idea originated during a trail run, inspired by Graham's experience in coal geology and exploration where he observed heat coming from deeper wells. Shunk brings expertise in project management, business development, and digital marketing to the venture. The company's core technology is a closed-loop system designed to repurpose existing well infrastructure. This process involves inserting an inner pipe into a single, plugged wellbore, which is isolated from the surrounding geology. Fluid is circulated down the outer annulus, where it is heated by geothermal energy at the bottom of the well. The heated fluid then returns to the surface through the inner tube and transfers its thermal energy via a heat exchanger before being reinjected, completing the loop. Initially, standard circulation proved commercially unviable, which led to the development of the proprietary "Algar's Integrated Cycle," a set of four innovations that significantly increase recoverable heat and temperature. Algar Geothermal's business model is centered on licensing its technology to clients. The company also provides ongoing support to ensure successful operations and manages data on behalf of its clients. Revenue is generated through licensing fees, which vary by market size, management fees based on the number of wells, and charges for heat usage on a per-gigajoule basis. The technology targets a variety of high-heat load applications, including greenhouses, warehouses, manufacturing facilities, district energy systems, and hospitals. By giving a second, greener life to defunct oil and gas wells, Algar's solution addresses the environmental liability of inactive wells while providing a baseload, low-carbon energy source. column6: Sensoryx AG is a Swiss company specializing in high-precision motion tracking technology for spatial computing, including virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) applications. Founded in 2015 by Dr. Rolf Adelsberger and Fabian Wenner, the company originated from Dr. Adelsberger's master's thesis research at MIT and his subsequent doctoral work at ETH Zurich on mobile motion capture. The company's core business revolves around licensing its patented tracking technology to hardware manufacturers and developers. By partnering with hardware makers, such as Qualcomm and Pimax, Sensoryx's software can be integrated with minimal to no hardware modifications on the partner's side. Sensoryx's proprietary technology achieves sub-millimeter accuracy by fusing data from optical, ultrasonic, and inertial sensors. This hybrid approach is designed to be power-efficient and avoids common issues like drift and occlusion found in other systems. The technology is platform-agnostic, ensuring compatibility with a wide range of head-mounted displays (HMDs). The company provides software development kits (SDKs) for platforms like Unity and Unreal to facilitate integration for developers. Its product line has included the VRfree® gloves for precise hand and finger tracking, the SpatialTag object tracker, and the MALIANG Magic Pencil, a stylus for XR interactions. While some earlier products like the VRfree gloves have been discontinued for general sale, they remain available for specific projects. The company also offers custom development of motion tracking solutions for specific industry needs. Since its inception, Sensoryx has secured patent protection for its technology in key markets including Europe, the USA, Japan, and China. column5: Enzyme-based gene-editing technology for fungal-resistant crops
column6: Healthycrop, established in 2018, is a plant biotechnology spin-out from Aarhus University that develops crops with natural resistance to fungal infections like Fusarium and Aspergillus. The company was founded by Professor Henrik Brinch-Pedersen and is currently led by co-founder and CEO Pernille Ollendorff Hede, who has a background in molecular plant biology and business. The core of their patented technology is enhancing a naturally occurring plant enzyme, Nepenthesin, through gene-editing techniques. This enzyme degrades the essential enzymes of fungi, effectively starving them and inhibiting their growth, which in turn prevents the contamination of crops with harmful mycotoxins. The company's primary focus has been on cereals such as barley, maize, and wheat, and it is expanding to other crops, including potatoes, through strategic collaborations. Healthycrop's business model is centered on developing these fungal-resistant traits and then licensing this technology to large, global seed producers. These producers integrate the traits into their own elite crop lines. This approach aims to reduce the global reliance on chemical fungicides, leading to significant cost savings for farmers, a lower environmental impact, increased biodiversity, and enhanced food safety by preventing toxins from entering the food chain. Healthycrop's innovation has received industry recognition, including the InnovAction Award at Euroseeds 2024. The company's work is backed by over a decade of university research and it holds patents in the EU, USA, Canada, Brazil, and Australia. column6: EverScan emerges as a specialized operator in the high-precision 3D scanning sector, a venture born from the practical experience of its parent company, Lemon Construction. Founded by Yaroslav Pokotilo, EverScan's trajectory is deeply rooted in the construction and office design industry of Ukraine, where Lemon Construction established its reputation. This heritage provides EverScan with a distinct perspective and a ready-made market understanding, particularly within the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) sectors. The transition from traditional construction project management to high-tech 3D scanning appears to be a strategic move to leverage deep industry knowledge and address the growing demand for digitalization in established industries. The company's core business revolves around providing highly accurate digital models of physical assets, a service it delivers through a suite of advanced technologies. This includes LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging), utilized in both aerial (UAV-based) and terrestrial applications for large-scale scanning of factories, power lines, and urban areas. For more detailed and precise measurements of smaller, complex objects like engine parts or mechanisms, EverScan employs metrology. A significant part of their offering is Building Information Modeling (BIM), which creates a comprehensive digital twin of a building or structure, allowing for the management of its entire lifecycle. The business model is project-based, with revenue generated by delivering these scanning and modeling services on a per-project basis to a diverse client base that includes giants in the energy, industrial, and mining sectors. Projects have included preventive inspections of solar power plants, engineering and geodesic works for industrial modernization, and the restoration of documentation for modeling and upgrades. EverScan's services are not limited to industrial applications; the company has also found a niche in the preservation of cultural heritage. By using LiDAR, they can capture detailed models of historical sites and artifacts, even those obscured by vegetation, providing a valuable tool for archaeological research and conservation. This diversification into the heritage sector demonstrates a broader vision for the application of their core competencies. Furthermore, the company has developed "Everscan 3D," a unique software platform for 3D scanners. This platform is designed to be accessible for various levels of users, from DIY enthusiasts to industrial clients, and allows companies to manufacture their own 3D scanners without heavy investment in research and development. This offering represents a distinct and scalable revenue stream, moving beyond service-based income to include a software and technology-licensing component. column5: Mobile carbon capture and decarbonization technology solutions
column6: Optimabiome develops decarbonization solutions aimed at mitigating emissions from the energy and transportation sectors. The company, founded in 2019 by Dr. Malcolm Fabiyi, is headquartered in Germantown, MD. Dr. Fabiyi, who holds a PhD in Chemical Engineering from Cambridge University and an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business, has over two decades of experience in the water and wastewater industry and previously served as the COO & VP Operations at Drylet LLC. The company's core technology is a mobile carbon capture system that utilizes a unique matrix approach. This process integrates various materials with an affinity for CO2, such as sorbents, solvents, and ionic liquids, to form a stable solid matrix. This matrix can capture, sequester, and transport carbon dioxide from exhaust gases on vehicles like trucks and trains without the need for energy-intensive purification, compression, or liquefaction. The captured CO2 can then be desorbed at a storage site, and the matrix is regenerated for reuse. One application involves converting the captured CO2 into carbonate salt, which then provides carbon for the growth of nitrifier biomass, a type of microbe. This biomass can be converted into biochar for long-term carbon storage. This approach positions wastewater treatment plants as potential carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) locations. Optimabiome's business model is centered on providing a bridge solution for mobile carbon capture as industries transition toward a net-zero future. The technology serves as a "virtual pipeline" for CO2 transport, offering flexibility in how and where carbon is moved and stored. Dr. Fabiyi's vision focuses on the circular economy and transforming wastewater from a liability into a nutrient-rich resource. column6: Global Battery Materials Corp. (GB Materials) is a vertically integrated critical minerals and technology company launched in November 2025. column5: Worm humus-based solutions for organic agriculture
column6: Naturfera is a family-led project that manufactures and sells organic fertilizers, with its flagship product being worm humus, also known as vermicompost. Founded by Raquel Camarero, the company is located in the Ribera del Duero region of Burgos, Spain. The business emerged from a desire to provide sustainable and respectful alternatives to chemical products in agriculture. The company's core product, worm humus, is created through a process of vermicomposting, where Californian red worms (Eisenia foetida) digest composted organic matter, primarily from local semi-extensive livestock farming. This process transforms the waste into a nutrient-rich, microbially active soil amendment. The resulting vermicompost is designed to regenerate soil health, improve its structure, increase water retention, and provide essential macro and micronutrients for plant growth. Unlike some chemical fertilizers, it is harmless to plants even in large quantities. Naturfera serves both large-scale agriculture (Naturfera AGRO) and the urban gardening market (Naturfera GARDEN), offering products for various applications, including ornamental plants, lawns, vegetables, and fruit trees. The business operates on a direct sales model through its website, shipping products across Spain. In addition to its products, the company also offers talks and courses on sustainability, lombriculture, and regenerative cultivation models. The project has gained recognition, being selected by the EIT Food consortium as a noteworthy project in Spain and participating in the Empowering Women in Agrifood (EWA) program. By utilizing industrial and municipal rooftops, Stadtgemüse aims to create new arable land, shorten food supply chains, and contribute to sustainable urban development. Stadtgemüse targets commercial horticultural businesses, pharmaceutical companies, municipalities, and operators of vertical and aquaponic farms. The business model includes the sale of the cultivation system, its components, and related services such as planning, installation, maintenance, and training. The company has received public funding from the city of Wiesbaden and the state of Hesse and is now seeking further investment to scale its operations. column6: Myers Motors, LLC, an automotive company based in Tallmadge, Ohio, is focused on the manufacturing of environmentally sound, electric-powered alternative transportation. The company's origins trace back to August 2004, when founder Dana Myers acquired the assets of the bankrupt Corbin Motors, including a number of partially built three-wheeled electric vehicles known as the Sparrow. Prior to establishing Myers Motors, Dana Myers served as the president of S.D. Myers, Inc., a company specializing in transformer and substation maintenance for electric utilities, and was recognized as Ernst & Young's Entrepreneur of the Year for Northeast Ohio in 1992. After the acquisition, Myers and his engineering team undertook a significant redesign of the original Sparrow, addressing numerous mechanical and electrical issues. This revamped, single-passenger, three-wheeled vehicle was launched in 2006 as the Myers Motors NmG, which stands for "No More Gas". The NmG was designed specifically for city commuting, featuring a distinctive rounded body, and was powered by a 156-volt DC electric motor. Initially using lead-acid batteries, the company later upgraded to lithium-ion batteries in 2009, which reportedly doubled the vehicle's range to approximately 60 miles on a single charge and extended the battery pack's life. The business model centered on direct-to-consumer sales, with vehicles made to order. The target market consists of environmentally conscious urban commuters seeking an alternative to traditional gasoline-powered cars for short trips. Building on the NmG, Myers Motors announced plans for a two-passenger model, the Duo (short for "Doesn't Use Oil"), in 2009. The company initiated a pre-order campaign with a variable pricing structure intended to lower the cost as more orders were placed. In 2018, the company rebranded to Myers EV and began developing a new four-wheeled, two-person vehicle with tandem seating called the Point5, signaling a shift in product strategy. column5: Vertically-integrated company focused on scientific development and manufacture of products used to generate solar energy
column6: Nitol Solar was a Russian-based company positioned as a vertically integrated producer of materials for the solar energy sector. The firm was founded in 1998 by Dmitry Kotenko and a group of partners. Kotenko, a former student at the Baumann Technical Institute in Moscow, had transitioned from science to business in the 1990s, gaining experience in banking and metallurgy before aiming to apply his business knowledge back in the scientific field. The company's trajectory into solar materials was somewhat opportunistic. Initially a chemical trading company, Nitol acquired an old chemical factory near Irkutsk, Siberia. This plant had a unit producing trichlorosilane, a key ingredient for polysilicon used in solar panels. Recognizing the potential in the growing renewable energy market, the founders pivoted the factory's focus from industrial chemicals to the higher-value solar industry. The business model centered on producing and supplying solar-grade polycrystalline silicon. Nitol's operations were split into two integrated divisions: a Chemical Division producing chlorine, caustic soda, and trichlorosilane, and a Polysilicon Division focused on manufacturing the primary raw material for photovoltaic wafers. The company's main clients were to be global manufacturers of solar panels. Nitol Solar secured significant funding from international and domestic entities, including a partnership with the International Finance Corporation (IFC) in 2008 for a $50 million equity stake, and investments from Suntech Power Holdings, Sberbank, and Rusnano. Despite raising hundreds of millions and signing long-term supply contracts valued at over $1.6 billion, the company faced a dramatic downturn. A sharp global decrease in polysilicon prices, from approximately $400/kg to below $40/kg between 2008 and 2011, severely impacted its financial viability. The company halted all production activities in 2012, eventually filing for bankruptcy and officially closing in 2019. column6: Écoboeuf is an agritech company specializing in the production and sale of carbon-neutral, 100% grass-fed beef. Founded in 2019 by agronomists Simon Lafontaine and Frédérique Lavallée, the company operates from a fourth-generation family farm in Dupuy, in the Abitibi-Témiscamingue region of Quebec. The founders met while studying agronomy at Laval University, where they began questioning conventional agricultural production methods and sought to develop more sustainable practices. Lafontaine, part of the farm's fourth generation and a Ph.D. student in animal sciences, and Lavallée, who is pursuing a doctorate in agroforestry, combined their expertise to establish Écoboeuf. The company's mission is to reduce the environmental footprint of cattle farming and ensure the long-term viability of agriculture in northern regions. Écoboeuf employs regenerative agriculture techniques such as adaptive rotational grazing, agroforestry (integrating trees and shrubs into pastures), and maintaining permanent grasslands to achieve carbon neutrality. These practices not only allow for the complete reabsorption of greenhouse gases emitted by their production but also enhance soil health and biodiversity. The company has planted thousands of trees to capture carbon and improve animal welfare. Their approach also serves as a research and development platform to create a transferable model for other cattle farms. Écoboeuf's business model is direct-to-consumer and business-to-business. It sells its beef online in various formats, including discovery boxes, quarters, halves, and whole beef, which are delivered to customers or can be picked up at partner butchers. The company also supplies its products to several retail stores and eco-responsible groceries in Quebec. In addition to meat production, Écoboeuf is developing a consulting service to help other farmers transition to sustainable and agroforestry practices. column6: VEIU Tech provides a Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platform for managing the charging of electric vehicle (EV) fleets. The company’s solution is designed to integrate electric fleets into the power grid, optimizing the charging process to benefit both fleet operators and grid operators. The founders, Philippe Degen, Valentin Wyss, and Giacomo Pareschi, bring together expertise in electric mobility, energy systems, power grid usage, and IoT solutions. Degen has a background in electrical engineering and experience with load management systems. Wyss specialized in smart grid technology and has worked on projects involving battery storage and grid control. Pareschi holds a PhD focused on the integration of electric mobility into Switzerland's energy landscape. The company's business model targets two primary clients: EV fleet operators and grid or energy providers. For fleet operators, the platform aims to reduce operational costs by lowering electricity bills through peak load shaving and maximizing the use of self-generated renewable energy. For grid and energy actors, VEIU Tech offers access to the load flexibility stored in EV fleets, which can be used to manage load, stabilize voltage, and provide ancillary services like frequency control. This turns EV fleets into dynamic energy assets that can support grid stability and integrate renewable energy sources more effectively. The core of VEIU Tech's solution is a system that controls the charging process on the vehicle's side. This is achieved through a proprietary charge controller, which is installed between the charging station and the EV, and an on-board unit within the vehicle that acts as a data and signal hub. This setup allows for real-time, dynamic control over each vehicle's charging process, independent of the specific charging station being used. A cloud-based web application collects data from all connected vehicles, such as state of charge and drive schedules, and uses it along with external data like energy costs to create an optimized charging plan for the entire fleet. This automated system works in the background to maximize charging flexibility while ensuring the operational readiness of the fleet. column5: Wireless, self-powered sensors for energy consumption monitoring.
column6: Based in Grenoble, France, Enkel Sensors designs and manufactures a flexible, connected solution for collecting, remotely reading, and monitoring electricity consumption. The company's core offering consists of wireless, non-intrusive, and self-powered current sensors that utilize a patented energy-harvesting technology. This allows the sensors, called 'E-Cubes', to be clipped around electrical cables without the need for batteries or complex wiring. The system is designed for ease of use, enabling rapid deployment for energy audits, environmental certifications like ISO 50001, and permanent energy monitoring. Data collected by the sensors is transmitted to a gateway, which can be a mobile unit housed in a portable 'E-Case' for temporary audits or a fixed installation integrated into an electrical cabinet for long-term use. From the gateway, data is sent to the 'Save it Yourself' monitoring platform, where it can be analyzed to map energy consumption, identify significant energy uses, and detect anomalies. The data can also be downloaded or transferred via API or FTP to other platforms or local servers. Enkel Sensors serves a global client base across various sectors, including industrial manufacturing, helping them achieve energy savings and advance their decarbonization strategies. The company's client roster includes notable names such as Danone, Yves Rocher, Fenwick-Linde, and Bridor. By providing detailed consumption data, Enkel's solution enables clients to pinpoint energy-intensive equipment, optimize processes, justify energy-saving investments, and verify the impact of efficiency measures. The products are available for both sale and rental. column5: IoT middleware platform unifying devices and protocols.
column6: MobiusFlow provides a middleware platform that enables new and legacy systems to connect, control, and communicate with each other and the cloud. The company’s origins trace back to Interior Automation, a control solutions provider founded in 2004. The middleware journey began as an in-house commissioning solution to help engineers execute projects more efficiently. The concept for MobiusFlow as an advanced software package was formed in 2016, and it was established as a separate company in 2022 to offer its solutions to a broader market. The core team includes CEO Shawn Pedersen and CTO Chris Moorhouse, who have decades of experience in system integration and device commissioning.The firm's flagship product is a protocol-agnostic IoT edge platform. It is designed to normalize data from any source—such as sensors, actuators, and controllers—into standardized objects. This allows for interoperability between disparate devices and protocols, including BACnet, MQTT, Modbus, LoRaWAN, and EnOcean. The platform is built on a microservice-based architecture using the MQTT protocol, which allows services to be written in any language and run on any device with TCP/IP capabilities. This architecture allows for local control without a constant network connection, and nodes can be interconnected to form complex systems. The platform consists of four main products: Engine, Toolbox, View, and Manager. The Engine processes and normalizes data; the Toolbox is an engineering tool for creating workflows and automation; View allows for the creation of custom real-time dashboards; and Manager is used to organize multiple instances of MobiusFlow.MobiusFlow operates on a subscription-based business model, where customers pay for what they use. This consumption-based pricing allows clients to scale their usage and control monthly spending. The company targets system integrators, OEM platform developers, and data consultants, providing them with a white-label solution to integrate into their own offerings and open new revenue streams. It can be hosted on-premise, in the cloud, or in a hybrid model, offering flexibility and security. The company does not execute projects directly but rather passes inquiries to its network of partners. column6: Lamitex, founded in Italy in 2001, specializes in producing innovative decorative laminates for the furniture and interior architecture sectors. The company started as a research and development firm for resins and coatings and, by 2004, developed its proprietary and exclusive CLPL® (Continuous Low Pressure Laminate) technology. This technology allows for the creation of decorative laminates with a hyper-realistic and natural appearance. The company's core products are based on the CLPL® technology, which is noted for its flexibility, making it suitable for curved surfaces and 3D applications. These laminates are used on vertical interior surfaces like doors, furniture, and wall paneling. Lamitex offers its products in various formats, including rolls, sheets, and pre-applied on panels such as MDF, HDF, and chipboard. A key feature of Lamitex's products is their environmental consideration; they are produced without added formaldehyde, PVC, phenols, or melamine resins and are made from recyclable materials. Lamitex serves clients in the interior design, furnishing, and architecture industries, exporting to over 40 countries. The business model centers on manufacturing and supplying these decorative surfaces. Following its technological success, the company expanded its operations, opening a location in Pinzano al Tagliamento in 2004 and another in Spilimbergo in 2016. In November 2025, Neodecortech S.p.A. signed a binding agreement to acquire 100% of Lamitex for EUR 8.4 million, though Lamitex will remain a separate legal entity within the group. For the fiscal year 2024, Lamitex reported revenues of EUR 12.8 million and an EBITDA of EUR 1.8 million. column5: Uranium exploration and development in Zambia
column6: Atomic Eagle Limited (ASX: AEU) is a mineral resource company focused on the exploration and development of uranium assets in Africa. The firm was established in November 2025 through a reverse takeover that merged Canadian-based GoviEx Uranium Inc. and Tombador Iron Limited, a well-capitalized ASX-listed entity that had previously divested its iron ore business. This strategic combination created an ASX-listed company with a primary focus on advancing its core asset, the 100%-owned Muntanga Uranium Project in Zambia. The merger provided a new capital structure, a refreshed board, and a strengthened balance sheet, with an initial cash position of approximately $20 million following a $10 million re-compliance raise. The company's board is led by Chairman Govind Friedland, previously of GoviEx, and includes Non-Executive Directors Stephen Quantrill, Eric Krafft, and Keith Bowes, former Managing Director of Lotus Resources. Strategic advice is provided by Grant Davey of Matador Capital, a firm that played a key role in the merger and has experience with other uranium developers like Boss Energy and Lotus Resources. Daniel Major, the former CEO of GoviEx, continues to lead the new entity. The formation of Atomic Eagle consolidated GoviEx's market presence in Australia, a significant hub for uranium investment. Atomic Eagle's principal asset, the Muntanga Uranium Project, is located in southeastern Zambia and spans four mining licenses and two exploration licenses over a 1,136km² area. The project benefits from its proximity to established infrastructure, including sealed roads and access to export routes. A feasibility study completed in early 2025 outlined a robust, shallow open-pit, heap leach operation with a projected 12-year mine life, forecasting an average annual production of 2.2 million pounds of U₃O₈. The project has an after-tax net present value of $243 million and an internal rate of return of 20.8%. Following its ASX listing on November 24, 2025, Atomic Eagle completed a maiden drill program and is planning an aggressive exploration campaign for 2026 to expand the current resource. column5: Soil carbon sequestration for regenerative agriculture
column6: Carboneg is a carbon removal project established in the Czech Republic in 2021 by founder Václav Kurel. The company operates as a bridge between farmers and corporations, promoting the transition to regenerative agriculture to improve soil health and sequester atmospheric carbon. The business model is centered on the voluntary carbon market. Carboneg provides farmers with training, soil analysis, and methodological guidance to implement regenerative practices such as no-till farming and the use of cover crops. The company then measures the amount of carbon sequestered in the soil through soil sampling and satellite data, and issues verified carbon removal credits. These credits are sold to companies that want to offset their residual emissions and meet their environmental, social, and governance (ESG) goals. A significant portion of the revenue from the sale of these carbon credits is paid to the farmers as a financial reward for each ton of CO2 stored in their soil. This model provides an additional income stream for farmers, helping to mitigate potential profit dips during the 3-5 year transition period from conventional to regenerative methods. The company has expanded its operations to four continents with the goal of removing one billion tonnes of CO2 from the atmosphere by 2030. column6: Polder Guyot Energies is a joint venture established by Guyot Environnement (49%) and Idex (51%) to develop and operate a low-carbon industrial boiler plant in Brest, France. column5: Gear-based CVT transmission systems for multiple applications
column6: Varionova srl, officially incorporated in San Marino in June 2025, develops next-generation, AI-ready transmission systems. Christoph Kempermann, a professional with over 30 years in the transmission industry, joined the company in July 2025. The company's flagship technology is the RatioZero, the first commercially viable gear-based Continuously Variable Transmission (CVT). This system addresses a key trade-off in the industry: traditional geared transmissions offer high efficiency but have fixed gears, while conventional CVTs provide stepless ratio variation but suffer from low efficiency due to friction. The RatioZero technology, based on a "split rotation" principle conceived by Edyson Pavilcu around 2016, combines the efficiency of gears with the continuous control of a CVT. This approach led to the granting of two international patents. The system works by splitting the rotation into portions and using a satellite for each portion, which is disengaged by a freewheel in other portions, transferring torque efficiently through gears, freewheels, and a four-bar mechanism to create a variable ratio. Varionova's business model focuses on licensing its technology through various models, including technology transfer, joint development, and OEM integration partnerships. The company also offers custom development services to adapt the technology for specific partner applications. Their target markets include e-mobility, robotics, industrial automation, and micromobility. The company has developed different versions of the RatioZero, such as the '/Chain' for low to medium speeds and the '/Rod' for high-speed, high-torque applications. Another product in their portfolio is the Crown Drive, a reversible, self-adapting transmission designed for robotics and mobility. column5: Advancing smart EV charging and vehicle-grid integration
column6: The Vehicle-Grid Integration Council (VGIC) is a national 501(c)(6) nonprofit trade association dedicated to advancing the role of electric vehicles (EVs) and smart charging in the decarbonization of the transportation and electricity sectors. The organization was reportedly spooled up in 2019 with help from members like Enel X North America. VGIC operates as a membership-based advocacy group, bringing together major auto original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), EV service providers, technology companies, and other stakeholders. Its board includes representatives from companies such as American Honda Motor Co. and General Motors, with Zach Woogen serving as the Executive Director. The council's primary mission is to ensure that the value derived from flexible EV charging and discharging—known as vehicle-grid integration (VGI)—is recognized and compensated to support a more reliable, affordable, and efficient power grid. VGI encompasses technologies and strategies that manage when, where, and how EVs charge to mitigate grid impacts and reduce costs. This includes both unidirectional smart charging (V1G), which optimizes charging times, and bidirectional vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology, which allows EVs to send power back to the grid. By acting as distributed energy resources, EVs can provide valuable grid services like demand response, frequency control, and backup power during outages. VGIC's business model is centered on membership dues, with different tiers such as Leadership Circle, General, and Associate members, offering varying levels of influence and access to resources. Revenue is used to fund its advocacy efforts, which involve policy development, educational outreach, and research. column5: Multi-designer platform for sustainable and ethical fashion
column6: Toile operates as a multi-designer platform and eco-fashion house dedicated to sustainable and ethical fashion. column5: Cybersecurity for distributed energy resources and EV charging
column6: DER Security Corp, founded in 2022, is a spin-off of the SunSpec Alliance, a trade group of participants in the solar and storage distributed energy industry. The company's leadership team has origins in the SunSpec Alliance, Sandia National Laboratories, and the cybersecurity industry. The CEO, Thomas Tansy, is also the Chairman of the SunSpec Alliance and previously founded companies that were acquired by Microsoft, Cisco, and F5 Corporation. The company provides what it describes as the first Power-Informed Cybersecurity Protection, Detection, and Response software solution for interoperable solar, storage, and EV charging systems. The technology is designed to protect Distributed Energy Resources (DER) and the energy grid from cyber threats. The company targets its solutions toward fleet operators and equipment manufacturers of solar and storage systems, electric vehicles, and EV charging systems. Its core products, DERSec Sentry and DERSec Detective, work in tandem to secure these assets. DERSec Sentry is installed within DER and EV charging systems to monitor, detect, and protect against threats, while DERSec Detective operates in network operating centers to monitor traffic and mitigate suspicious activity. The system utilizes energy-protocol deep packet inspection, power-signal anomaly detection, and machine learning to identify threats like malicious firmware updates and falsified data injection. column5: Patented plasma pyrolysis for converting end-of-life tires
column6: Global Enviro Technology (S) Pte. Ltd. is a Singapore-based environmental services company specializing in sustainable tire recycling. Incorporated on May 7, 2019, the company addresses the environmental challenge of scrap tire disposal. The leadership team includes CEO Thomas Lim, Chief Scientist Dr. George Paskalov, and President Wendy Chew. Dr. Paskalov, a plasma physics expert, is the key creator of the company's patented waste-to-energy technology. The company's core service revolves around a patented, radio frequency (RF) induced plasma pyrolysis technology. This advanced thermal process uses extremely high temperatures in an oxygen-free environment to break down scrap tires into valuable materials, distinguishing it from traditional incineration or lower-grade pyrolysis methods. The primary outputs of this process are high-quality recovered Carbon Black (rCB), syngas, and steel. The rCB serves as a sustainable alternative to virgin carbon black in manufacturing new tires, rubber products, and plastics. The syngas can be used to generate electricity, potentially with a future pathway to hydrogen production, while the recovered steel is repurposed for construction and metal fabrication. Global Enviro Technology operates on a B2B and B2C model. It processes tires for various clients and has established partnerships, such as the 'Recycle My Tyres' initiative with Allianz Insurance Singapore, which allows the public to drop off used tires at authorized workshops for recycling. The company guarantees that 100% of the scrap tires it processes are recycled in its facility and not exported for use as fuel, positioning itself as a key player in creating a circular economy. Its facility in Loyang, Singapore, is designed with a modular system, enabling scalability for global expansion to address the worldwide issue of tire waste. column5: Affordable EV charging solution with integrated rebilling
column6: Yoink, a UK-based company founded in 2024, is focused on making electric vehicle (EV) charging more accessible and affordable. column5: A collaboration between the Flemish research partners in the field of sustainable energy and intelligent energy systems
column6: EnergyVille is a research collaboration, not a traditional startup, focused on sustainable energy and intelligent energy systems. It was formed as a partnership between several prominent Belgian research institutions: KU Leuven, VITO, imec, and UHasselt. The story began in 2009 with a collaboration between a KU Leuven research group and VITO, driven by the need for new technologies to meet climate objectives. This led to the official founding of Campus EnergyVille NV in 2010. The first building, EnergyVille 1, was inaugurated in September 2016, designed to be a highly energy-efficient structure itself. A second building, EnergyVille 2, opened in May 2018 to expand research capabilities, particularly in thin-film solar cells and battery systems. Located at Thor Park in Genk, a former coal mining site, EnergyVille represents a strategic shift from fossil fuels to renewable energy research. The campus serves as an R&D hub that unites research, development, and training, fostering collaboration with industrial and public sector partners. The organization's funding comes from its core research partners as well as public entities including the city of Genk, the Province of Limburg, and European structural funds. While it had a turnover of approximately €4.7 million according to its most recent financial statements, its primary objective is not commercial profit but to accelerate the energy transition. The business of EnergyVille is to develop technology and knowledge for public and private stakeholders. This involves integrating the entire energy system value chain, from materials and components to complete energy systems, business models, and strategies. With around 700 researchers, the collaboration's activities are organized into eight main domains: solar energy, battery storage, power electronics, power-to-molecules, thermal systems, electrical networks, energy for buildings and districts, and energy strategies and markets. Specific research areas include making PV systems more efficient, developing new battery materials, creating smart grids, and advancing district heating and cooling. The campus itself functions as a living lab, featuring state-of-the-art facilities like a pre-pilot line for thin-film solar cell production and a specialized dry room for battery material processing. column5: Laser-based inertial confinement fusion research facility.
column6: The National Ignition Facility (NIF), located at the Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) in Livermore, California, is a premier laser-based inertial confinement fusion (ICF) research facility. Its primary mission is to achieve fusion ignition with high energy gain, support the U.S. Stockpile Stewardship Program by ensuring the safety and reliability of the nation's nuclear deterrent without full-scale testing, and advance scientific discovery in areas like high energy density science and astrophysics. The facility houses the world's largest and most energetic laser system. The concept for the NIF grew out of decades of research into inertial confinement fusion, which began in the 1960s with pioneering scientists at LLNL, including John Nuckolls, who hypothesized that lasers could induce fusion ignition. The formal proposal for NIF emerged in the early 1990s as a cornerstone of the Stockpile Stewardship Program, established after the U.S. stopped underground nuclear testing. Construction officially began on May 29, 1997, and after overcoming significant technical and logistical challenges, the U.S. Department of Energy certified its completion on March 31, 2009. The NIF's operational principle involves focusing 192 powerful laser beams onto a tiny target, typically a pellet of deuterium and tritium fuel housed within a small gold cylinder called a hohlraum. The lasers heat the hohlraum's interior, generating an intense bath of X-rays that cause the fuel capsule to implode, reaching temperatures and pressures comparable to those in the cores of stars and exploding nuclear weapons. This process is designed to trigger a controlled fusion reaction. On December 5, 2022, the NIF made history by conducting the first controlled fusion experiment to achieve scientific energy breakeven, producing more energy from the fusion reaction (3.15 megajoules) than the laser energy delivered to the target (2.05 megajoules). This milestone, known as ignition, has since been repeated multiple times with even higher energy gains. As a user facility, the NIF serves a broad community of scientists from national laboratories, universities, and international partners, conducting hundreds of experiments each year. These experiments not only support national security missions but also provide critical data for understanding planetary science, stellar physics, and materials science under extreme conditions. The achievement of ignition has opened new frontiers and provides invaluable insights into the prospects of developing inertial fusion energy (IFE) as a safe, clean, and sustainable power source for the future. column6: Firebird Metals Ltd (ASX:FRB) is a Western Australian mineral exploration and development company, founded in 2016, focused on becoming a key supplier of high-purity manganese for the electric vehicle (EV) battery market. A primary focus is its lithium manganese iron phosphate (LMFP) battery strategy, aimed at making Firebird a near-term producer of battery-grade manganese sulphate (MnSO4), a critical cathode material for these next-generation batteries. The LMFP chemistry offers higher energy density than traditional LFP batteries while retaining safety and cost advantages. The company's leadership includes Managing Director Peter Allen, a mining executive with over two decades of experience in manganese marketing, and Finance Director Wei Li, a Chartered Accountant with extensive experience in the resources sector. Their strategy involves a dual-location approach, with mining operations in Australia and processing facilities in China to tap into the world's largest manganese sulphate market. In March 2025, Firebird announced it had produced its first LMFP batteries through a strategic collaboration with China's Central South University, marking a significant milestone as the first Australian company to do so. The company is also developing Lithium Manganese Rich (LMR) cathode materials for solid-state batteries. Firebird's portfolio is located in the East Pilbara manganese province of Western Australia and includes a total resource of 234Mt. Its flagship asset is the 100% owned Oakover Project, located 85km east of Newman, which holds a Mineral Resource Estimate of 176.7 Mt at 9.9% Mn. A scoping study confirmed Oakover as a long-life, tier-one operation with an 18-year mine life. In March 2025, the company was granted the Mining Lease for the project, a critical step in its vertical integration strategy. Firebird plans to establish a processing plant in China with a proposed capacity of 50,000 tonnes of MnSO4, leveraging a low CAPEX of US$83.5 million. column5: Upcycled, controlled-release fertilizers for tropical agriculture
column6: Innovaciones Circulares addresses phosphorus loss in agriculture by converting agricultural waste into valuable resources. Innovaciones Circulares partners with livestock farms to recover phosphorus from their waste, making sustainable phosphorus management more accessible and affordable for small to medium-sized farms.
