column5: Sustainable, cricket-based alternative protein food products
column6: Gryllus Inc. was a Japanese food-tech venture that specialized in producing and selling edible crickets and cricket-based food products. The company was established in May 2019 by Takahito Watanabe, who was an assistant professor at Tokushima University. The venture was founded to commercialize the results of the university's decades-long research on crickets, focusing on the two-spotted cricket, *Gryllus bimaculatus*, from which the company derived its name. The company's mission was to address future food security and sustainability challenges by providing a high-protein, nutritious alternative food source with a low environmental impact. Crickets were presented as a solution due to their rapid growth cycle of about one month, and their efficient use of feed and water compared to traditional livestock. Gryllus developed techniques for mass-producing crickets, utilizing food waste and agricultural by-products as feed. The crickets were dried and pulverized into a powder, which was then used as an ingredient in a variety of food products, including cookies, curry, crackers, and croquettes. Gryllus launched its own brand, "C. TRIA," in 2021, selling products through an online store. The company also engaged in notable collaborations. A partnership with Muji led to the release of "Cricket Crackers" in 2020, which quickly gained media attention. Another collaboration with the airline Zipair resulted in cricket-powder-infused in-flight meals starting in July 2022. The company also worked with schools to introduce cricket-based meals into school lunches to raise awareness about sustainable food sources. Despite initial success and sales reportedly tripling each year, the company faced significant challenges. A negative public reaction, fueled by misinformation and conspiracy theories on social media regarding the safety and nutritional aspects of insect consumption, led to a sharp decline in sales. An attempt to pivot the business toward producing cricket-based feed for livestock and aquaculture failed after a bid for government subsidies was denied. Faced with mounting debt and excess inventory, Gryllus Inc. ceased operations in the spring of 2024 and filed for bankruptcy in November 2024. column5: Ozone and active oxygen sanitation equipment.
column6: Oxy3 Ozongeräte Produktion GmbH specializes in the development and production of high-end equipment for eliminating odors and breaking down pollutants. The company originated in 2008 as a spin-off from the Montanuniversität Leoben. In 2013, pro aqua GmbH acquired a stake in Oxy3 GmbH, contributing over two decades of expertise in organic material degradation and bacterial elimination, which led to a significant reengineering and redesign of the existing product. Oxy3's core product is a modular sanitation system that utilizes a unique, combined process of ozone, active oxygen, and water vapor. Unlike conventional ozone generators that use ambient air (which is mostly nitrogen and can create harmful nitrogen oxides), the Oxy3 device generates ozone from pure oxygen. This ozone is then combined with water vapor to create active oxygen, which settles on surfaces as a fine condensate to break down organic odors and contaminants. After the treatment cycle, any residual ozone is converted back into oxygen, ensuring the space is safe for use. The system is offered in both mobile and stationary configurations. The mobile solution pairs the Oxy3 generator with a roll cart, designed for treating the interiors of vehicles, including cars, emergency vehicles, and rental fleets. The stationary application combines the generator with a decontamination cabinet for treating personal protective equipment (PPE) and other gear for clients such as fire departments, emergency medical services, and civil protection units. The process effectively removes harmful substances like polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and odors from smoke or sweat in protective gear. The treatment cycles are fully automatic and last between 35 and 90 minutes. column5: Nutritious freeze-dried meals and vegetable mixes
column6: Lyoca is a Montreal-based company founded in October 2020 by Anne Moorehouse with a mission to reduce food waste using freeze-drying technology. This method preserves the food's flavor, color, and up to 97% of its nutritional properties without requiring preservatives. Unlike other dehydration techniques, freeze-drying keeps the cellular structure intact, allowing for quick rehydration and a natural texture. The product lineup includes freeze-dried vegetable mixes, fruits, snacks, and complete meals, designed for ease of preparation for people with active lifestyles, at home, or on the go. The offerings are presented as a healthy alternative to fast food. The founder, Anne Moorehouse, was inspired by her love for local, healthy food and the challenge of eating well while traveling, drawing from her background in aviation. Co-founder Heiura Poroi, originally from Tahiti, contributes a vision for sustainable production and fair trade, influenced by her experience founding a vanilla producers' cooperative. column6: ZAZI is a luxury fashion label that champions social and economic independence for women through the creation of clothing from vintage and organic materials. Founded in 2016 by Jeanne de Kroon, the company was born from her desire to create a brand that celebrates women's collectives, artisanal craft, and a connection to the earth. De Kroon, who studied philosophy and had a background in modeling, was inspired to create ZAZI after witnessing the harsh realities of the fast-fashion industry during her travels. A key moment was her meeting with Madhu Vaishnav, founder of the Saheli Women, a social enterprise in rural India that empowers women through sewing and craft. This partnership formed the foundation of ZAZI, which started in de Kroon's student bedroom with just 500 euros and seven ikat dresses. ZAZI designs and produces handcrafted coats, dresses, bags, and other items, focusing on traditional and ancestral techniques. The collections are often based on the availability of recycled fabrics and the production capacity of their partner NGOs and social enterprises, reflecting a supply chain-driven model. This approach allows the brand to weave cultural narratives into its garments while ensuring fair wages and supporting local craftspeople. ZAZI positions itself as a luxury brand with a conscience, selling directly to consumers through its website, a showroom in Amsterdam, and various pop-up shops globally. While operating as a for-profit company, its core mission is deeply rooted in social impact, aiming to provide livelihoods and support the communities behind the products. The business model prioritizes ethical production and storytelling over high-profit margins, seeking to change consumers' relationship with clothing by offering pieces that are meant to be cherished for a lifetime. column6: Go Charge is a service developed by Motability Operations in partnership with the tech company Paua to simplify public electric vehicle (EV) charging for disabled drivers in the UK who are part of the Motability Scheme. Users pay a standard 'pay as you go' tariff set by the charge point operator, with payments managed directly through the app. The service is included as part of the all-inclusive vehicle lease package for new electric car customers on the Motability Scheme. The Go Charge app and card consolidate access to over 58,000 charge points from more than 40 operators, including major networks like GRIDSERVE, Source London, Shell Recharge, and Osprey. This covers over half of all charge points in the UK and 70% of all rapid chargers. The application allows users to find available chargers in real-time, filter them by connector type and speed, navigate to locations, track charging history and costs, and control charging sessions remotely. column5: Robust epoxy membranes for harsh industrial separations
column6: eXo membranes is a KU Leuven spin-off that engineers and produces highly robust filtration membranes using epoxy chemistry. This technology allows their membranes to withstand harsh industrial conditions, including extreme pH levels from 0 to 14, oxidizing environments, and solvent streams, without degradation or loss of performance. The company's products range from ultrafiltration (UF) to tight nanofiltration (NF) membranes, which are designed for challenging separation tasks where conventional membranes fail.The journey of eXo membranes began with Rhea De Wit's PhD research on chlorine-resistant membranes at the KU Leuven's Membrane Technology Group (MTG), under the guidance of Professor Ivo Vankelecom, between 2016 and 2020. Her work, which included a research stay at Yale University, led to the discovery that epoxy chemistry could be used to create exceptionally stable and high-performing membranes. Recognizing the technology's potential to make a real-world impact, Rhea, now a postdoc, teamed up with Laurent Hubert, whom she knew from high school. Laurent holds a BSc in aerospace engineering from TU Delft and an MSc in Management, Technology, and Economics from ETH Zürich. Together, they decided to commercialize the technology, leading to the establishment of eXo membranes as a KU Leuven spin-off in 2025.eXo membranes serves industries facing difficult separation challenges, such as metallurgy, where wastewaters contain complex mixtures of acids and oils, and lithium extraction from harsh brines. The company's business model involves designing, producing, and selling these specialized membranes to clients with demanding purification needs. A key feature of their membranes is a positive surface charge, which facilitates the treatment of positively charged substances without intensive cleaning. The technology is also highly tunable, allowing performance to be customized for specific applications.Significantly, eXo membranes is structured as a steward-owned company. This governance model ensures that voting rights remain with individuals actively involved in the company's mission and that profits are primarily reinvested to further the company's purpose rather than maximizing shareholder returns. For investors, this structure guarantees the company's mission will not be compromised or sold off. column5: Tokenized solar infrastructure creating a liquid energy market
column6: SolarNext is a Decentralized Physical Infrastructure Network (DePIN) protocol operating on the Solana blockchain. column5: Lithium and mineral recovery from industrial brine waste
column6: BluCore Minerals is a clean technology company that extracts high-purity lithium and other valuable minerals from industrial brine wastewater. The company was founded in San Bernardino by Raymond Moorehead Jr. and Jacob Estrada, evolving from a class project into a venture that has attracted national recognition from the U.S. Department of Energy and the Department of Defense. Moorehead, the CEO, and Estrada, the COO, both graduated from California State University, San Bernardino's Master of Science in Entrepreneurship and Innovation program and have family backgrounds in military service that influence their mission to enhance national resilience. The company's core technology is a patented liquid-to-liquid extraction system that uses a proprietary organic solvent to selectively bind with lithium ions in brine water. This mine-free process is designed to be integrated directly into existing industrial facilities, such as desalination plants, oil and gas fields, and geothermal plants. By recovering minerals from what is typically a discarded waste stream, BluCore's clients can turn a disposal liability into a potential revenue source. The process operates as a closed-loop system where the solvent is reused, making it a more sustainable and cost-effective alternative to traditional methods like mining or evaporation ponds. column5: Space-based solar power transmitted wirelessly to Earth
column6: Xorbital is developing a space-based solar power (SBSP) system to transmit clean energy from orbit to Earth. The company's technology aims to collect solar energy using advanced photovoltaic arrays on satellites in geostationary orbit, which it states are up to eight times more efficient than terrestrial systems due to the absence of atmospheric filtering and the ability to operate continuously. This energy is then converted into precise microwave or laser beams for wireless transmission to ground-based receiving stations, known as rectennas. These stations convert the transmitted energy back into electrical power for integration with existing power grids. The core mission is to provide a continuous, 24/7 power supply that is independent of weather conditions and daylight hours, targeting global energy access. Key markets include remote and disaster-affected areas lacking consistent electricity, defense sites, and supplementing traditional power grids. column6: Pristill, founded in 2024 by Simon Newman and Steve Bitterly, develops advanced water purification systems. The company's core technology is a patented Centrifugal Vapor Distillation (CVD) platform, an advanced version of a rotational vacuum distiller initially created for NASA's International Space Station. This technology is designed to treat challenging wastewater—such as dirty, variable, and scale-prone feedwater—that traditional systems struggle with. The co-founders bring together entrepreneurial and technical expertise. Pristill's CVD technology, or "Pristillization," offers several advantages over conventional methods like vapor compression distillation (VCD). It aims to be more energy-efficient, achieve higher purity levels of up to 99.99%, and features a self-cleaning mechanism that reduces scaling and allows for the processing of high-salinity water. The system creates exceptionally thin films on boiler and condenser surfaces to maximize heat transfer efficiency. It is engineered to remove a wide range of non-volatile contaminants, including bacteria, radiological materials, heavy metals, PFAS, and microplastics. The company targets several niche markets with high-pain points. These include the treatment of landfill leachate and industrial waste, wastewater recovery for the semiconductor industry, industrial de-ionized water production, and pre-treatment for hemodialysis systems. By focusing on these areas, Pristill aims to establish its CVD technology as a leading method for water purification and reuse. column5: Clean energy generators utilizing water-bio-alcohol fuel blend
column6: Coulomb Energy Solutions provides clean, decentralized energy generation by distributing generators that use MayMaan's patented internal combustion technology. column5: AI power grid orchestration middleware for residential assets
column6: BeeBob.ai is a Belgian climate-tech company developing power grid orchestration software to create Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) from decentralized residential energy resources. Founded in 2023 by serial cleantech entrepreneurs Jan-Willem Rombouts, Sandra Trittin, and Bert Claessens, the company is headquartered in Antwerp, Belgium, with an office in New York. The founding team possesses significant experience in the power grid flexibility market; Rombouts previously founded and scaled VPP pioneer REstore NV (acquired by Centrica), Trittin founded and scaled energy aggregator Tiko Energy Solutions (acquired by ENGIE), and Claessens is a former REstore NV executive. BeeBob's core offering is a software platform that acts as an abstraction layer, integrating with consumer devices such as solar panels, home batteries, EV chargers, and heat pumps. Using AI-driven orchestration, the software aggregates the flexibility of these devices, turning them into reliable, tradable assets for the power grid. This allows utilities, grid operators, traders, and Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) to manage the complexity of controlling large fleets of residential assets. The platform enables these partners to participate in various energy markets, including day-ahead, intraday, and real-time markets, as well as for grid operations like congestion management. By leveraging this idle capacity, BeeBob aims to enhance grid stability, reduce carbon emissions, and lower energy bills for consumers by up to 50%. The company operates on a B2B model, providing its middleware to partners rather than directly to consumers. In September 2024, BeeBob announced it had raised a $5.5 million (€4.9 million) seed funding round led by Angular Ventures with support from Contrarian Ventures. At the time of the funding, the company was already working with utilities and manufacturers across Europe, the UK, and the Middle East, and projected it would manage over 100,000 residential assets in the coming year. column6: Grounded Lithium Corp. (GLC) is a Canadian exploration and development company focused on producing battery-grade lithium from subsurface brines in Southwest Saskatchewan. Founded in late 2020 by President & CEO Gregg Smith and SVP Corporate Development & CFO Greg Phaneuf, the company leverages the management team's extensive background in the oil and gas resource industry. GLC's business model is centered on the exploration, consolidation, and development of its mineral rights holdings, with the flagship Kindersley Lithium Project (KLP) as its primary asset. The business strategy avoids the high capital and time costs of developing proprietary technology by licensing a proven Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) process. This method extracts lithium from brine brought to the surface, offering a more environmentally responsible alternative to traditional hard rock mining or large-scale evaporation ponds by reducing surface disturbance and freshwater consumption. In January 2024, Grounded Lithium entered a significant strategic partnership with Denison Mines Corp., a major Canadian uranium developer. Through the agreement, Denison has the option to earn up to a 75% working interest in the Kindersley Lithium Project by funding up to $15.15 million in project expenditures and cash payments, with Denison also becoming the project operator. This partnership aims to de-risk the project and leverage Denison's operational expertise and lower cost of capital to advance the KLP towards commercial production. Revenue generation will commence upon the successful commercialization and sale of battery-grade lithium products to the electric vehicle and battery manufacturing markets. column6: Orazul Energy Perú S.A. is an energy company focused on power generation within Peru. It was established on October 10, 2016, following the acquisition of Duke Energy's Latin American assets by the global infrastructure investment fund, I Squared Capital. This strategic acquisition positioned Orazul as a new major player in the Peruvian electricity sector under the ownership of I Squared Capital through its subsidiary, Inkia Energy. The company's core business revolves around the generation and commercialization of electricity, primarily through a portfolio of hydroelectric and, more recently, solar assets. Orazul operates two main run-of-river hydroelectric power plants: Cañón del Pato, with a capacity of 266 MW, and Carhuaquero, with 110 MW. In 2023, the company expanded into renewables by building a 1 MW solar plant adjacent to its Carhuaquero facility. Historically, the company also held assets in thermal power generation and natural gas, operating through its Aguaytía Energy del Perú subsidiary which included the Termoselva plant and hydrocarbon exploitation concessions. However, as part of a strategic shift, Orazul initiated the sale of its thermal and hydrocarbon businesses in 2021 to focus on its renewable generation platform. Orazul's business model involves selling electricity to both regulated distribution companies and non-regulated clients through Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs), as well as on the spot market. This hybrid approach provides a balance between the stability of long-term contracts and the flexibility of market prices. The company has engaged in proactive debt management, including issuing international bonds to refinance existing debt and manage its financial structure. After its formation, Orazul underwent a reorganization, which included selling assets in Chile, Guatemala, and El Salvador to concentrate on the Peruvian market. The company also sold its electricity transmission assets, comprising 746 kilometers of lines, to Colombia's Grupo ISA in 2020. column5: Agrivoltaic systems balancing agriculture and power generation
column6: Notus Solar Japan Co., Ltd., established in April 2022 with headquarters in Osaka, provides solutions that combine agriculture and energy generation. The company was founded by Ryuzo Takahashi, who also serves as CEO, and was initiated by Notus Research Institute Co., Ltd., an agricultural corporation specializing in brand rice cultivation. Takahashi, an English graduate, entered the agriculture sector in 2009, starting a large-scale rice paddy ownership system and later acquiring the domestic license for an advanced agrivoltaic technology from the Italian company REM TEC in 2019. Notus Solar Japan focuses on 'solar sharing' or agrivoltaics, which involves installing solar power generation systems on agricultural land to produce energy while continuing to grow crops. This model addresses the decreasing availability of suitable land for new solar installations in Japan by utilizing the country's extensive agricultural areas. The company offers planning, consulting, and sales of its proprietary mounting system, the "Notus Solar System." This system is based on REM TEC's internationally patented 3D solar tracking technology, "Agrovoltaico," which has been adapted for Japanese agricultural conditions. Key features of the system include movable panels to control shadows and minimize impact on crops, a 3D solar tracking program for efficient power generation, and automated adjustments for weather events like strong winds or snow. The company's business model involves developing agrivoltaic power plants and coordinating the entire project, from land development to system design, installation, and maintenance. It supplies the generated renewable energy to local governments, private companies, and new energy businesses through various models, including onsite and offsite Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) and private power models. This provides farmers with a new source of income from electricity sales, enhancing the economic stability and sustainability of agriculture. Notus Solar Japan has formed strategic capital and business partnerships with companies like Sinanen Holdings, Toda Corporation, and Sun Frontier Fudousan to jointly develop and construct agrivoltaic plants across Japan. For instance, its partnership with Sinanen Holdings involves a collaborative framework where a subsidiary handles the engineering, procurement, construction (EPC), and operation and maintenance (O&M) of the power plants. By 2030, the company aims to install 200 MW of its system across 400 hectares of farmland, generating over 300 million kWh annually. column6: Vilnius CHP (Vilniaus kogeneracinė jėgainė) is a modern cogeneration plant in Vilnius, Lithuania, that simultaneously generates heat and electricity from non-recyclable municipal waste and biomass. The company is a subsidiary of Ignitis Group, a state-owned energy holding company. In March 2026, Ignitis Group completed a transaction to sell a 49% stake in Vilnius CHP to the infrastructure fund Quaero European Infrastructure Fund III. The development of the plant was a strategic energy project for Lithuania, receiving its green light from the European Commission in August 2017. Construction began in February 2018 with a total estimated investment of around EUR 350 million, supported by funding from the European Union's Cohesion Fund and a loan from the European Investment Bank (EIB). The facility's waste-to-energy unit became operational in 2021, with the biomass unit starting operations in 2023 and reaching full capacity in May 2024. The project was driven by the need to reduce Lithuania's reliance on imported natural gas and to address inefficient municipal waste management. Vilnius CHP operates two main units: a waste-to-energy (WtE) unit and a biomass unit. The WtE unit processes up to 200,000 tonnes of non-recyclable municipal waste annually. The biomass unit uses locally sourced biomass, such as wood chips. The plant has a total electrical capacity of up to 100 MW and a thermal capacity of approximately 240 MW. This allows it to supply about 50% of Vilnius's annual district heating demand and generate enough electricity to power around 230,000 households. Heat is supplied to the Vilnius district heating network, while electricity is supplied to the national grid operator, LITGRID. The facility is equipped with advanced flue gas cleaning technologies to meet EU environmental standards. column5: Waste-to-biofuel production for maritime transport decarbonization
column6: SEAFAIRER is an innovation project funded by the European Union's Horizon Europe program with a budget of approximately €10 million. Coordinated by the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), the project began in September 2024 and is scheduled to run for 48 months until August 2028. The core objective is to demonstrate the production of advanced intermediate biofuels from biogenic waste to help decarbonize the maritime shipping industry. The project utilizes a thermochemical conversion process developed by the Fraunhofer Institute UMSICHT called »VINTER« (Vertical Intermediate Thermochemical Conversion). This single-stage intermediate pyrolysis and post-reforming process converts residual biomass into three main products: biochar, raw oil (intermediate biofuel), and syngas. The feedstocks are strategically sourced from non-food, residual materials to avoid land use conflicts, and include rice husks from Spain, biowaste sieving material from Germany, and agave bagasse from Mexico. SEAFAIRER is designed with two market-entry pathways for its biofuel. The first pathway addresses immediate industry needs by creating direct blends (B10 to B30) of the intermediate biofuel with Very Low Sulphur Fuel Oil (VLSFO) for use in existing ship engines without modification. The second, longer-term pathway involves upgrading the biofuel through hydrodeoxygenation to achieve a higher quality (B50 to B100), comparable to marine gasoil. column5: Porous 3D electrodes for high-performance energy storage
column6: OXYT ENERGY is a deep-tech startup spun out of the French National Centre for Scientific Research (LAAS-CNRS), capitalizing on over a decade of research and development. OXYT ENERGY serves the broader energy sector, targeting clients and partners who require more efficient and sustainable energy storage solutions. This process helps to reduce algae blooms, improve water clarity, and increase dissolved oxygen levels. column5: Magnetic liquid solution for removing waterborne microplastics
column6: Fionn & Co. LLC is a company focused on solving the issue of microplastic pollution in water. It was founded in 2020 by Fionn Ferreira, an Irish inventor and environmental scientist. Ferreira's journey began during his teenage years in West Cork, Ireland, where his passion for kayaking and the environment led him to observe the growing problem of plastic waste on the coastlines. This inspired him to develop a method for quantifying and removing microplastics from water. The core of the company's offering is a novel technology that uses a magnetic liquid, or ferrofluid, to extract microplastics from water. This non-toxic method involves mixing the ferrofluid with contaminated water, which causes the liquid to bind to the nonpolar microplastic particles. Magnets are then used to remove the ferrofluid-plastic agglomeration, leaving the water cleaner. This process is highly efficient, with prototypes removing over 85% of microplastics in a single pass, and it does not require filters or produce additional waste, as the ferrofluid can be reused. The technology is also considered safe for potential use in drinking water. Ferreira's invention gained significant recognition after he won the grand prize at the 2019 Google Science Fair. This success attracted support, notably from Robert Downey Jr.'s Footprint Coalition, and led to the establishment of Fionn & Co. to commercialize the technology. The company is working to scale the invention from a successful prototype to a full-scale commercial model, collaborating with institutions like the University of Texas. The primary market includes municipal wastewater facilities and coastal remediation projects, with the goal of deploying the technology globally. Fionn & Co. is also associated with the Green Journey Coalition Inc., another entity founded by Ferreira to advance his environmental mission. column5: Unlocking passive income through electricity market participation
column6: Flexivolt Ltd is a licensed UK Virtual Trading Party (VTP) that enables businesses with high energy consumption to generate passive income from their existing electricity usage. The company's core service involves using smart meter data to analyze a business's electricity consumption patterns. With permission, Flexivolt registers the client's meter to participate in the UK's wholesale electricity market and flexibility markets. This process turns a company's energy flexibility—minor deviations from expected power usage—into a tradable asset that helps stabilize the national grid without altering the client's day-to-day operations. The business model is centered on acting as a Virtual Trading Party, a role introduced by the UK's energy market regulator to increase competition and flexibility. As a VTP, Flexivolt aggregates the small adjustments in power usage from its clients and trades these discrepancies on the national electricity system. When these adjustments help the grid avoid deploying additional power generation, Flexivolt and its clients are financially rewarded by the grid operator and market participants. This allows businesses to monetize their inherent energy flexibility without needing to be a licensed supplier themselves. The company acceded to the Balancing and Settlement Code (BSC) with the intent to register as a Virtual Lead Party and Asset Metering Virtual Lead Party. Keywords: energy flexibility, virtual trading party, passive income, grid services, smart meter data, wholesale electricity market, demand response, energy monetization, grid stability, energy tech

column5: Traceable nettle fiber for sustainable textiles and materials
column6: Nettle Circle AG, founded in 2020 by Cornelia Bamert, is a Swiss startup focused on establishing nettle as a sustainable raw material for the textile and materials industry. Bamert, a product manager with a background in the Italian fashion industry, was driven to find sustainable material alternatives to cotton, which led her to the potential of nettle fibers. The company is developing and re-introducing one of the oldest known natural fibers into the modern textile market.Nettle Circle’s business model is built on two primary fiber products. The first is HILAYA®, a fiber derived from the Himalayan nettle species, *Girardinia diversifolia*. This product is already on the market and is produced through socially responsible supply chains in Nepal, providing an additional income source for local mountain communities, particularly during the off-season for farming. A key feature of HILAYA® is its traceability; the fiber is marked with DNA tracers from the ETH Zurich spin-off Haelixa, allowing the end product to be traced back to its origin.The second part of their strategy involves establishing the European nettle, *Urtica dioica*, as a locally cultivated fiber plant in Switzerland and Europe, with a target production start date of 2028. Nettle Circle is working to utilize the entire plant to create a scalable, circular value chain with minimal waste. Beyond textiles, the company is exploring applications for nettle fibers in technical textiles, insulation, nonwoven materials, acoustic damping material, and biomass products. Fabrics with a 30% nettle fiber content are noted for being breathable and moisture-regulating, making them suitable for applications like sportswear.The company has developed its own proprietary processing method, which is currently undergoing patenting, to become independent of traditional retting methods used for linen or hemp. Nettle is presented as a more ecological alternative to cotton, requiring significantly less water and no pesticides or chemical fertilizers, while also contributing to soil health. column5: Single-rider autonomous golf carts for individual play
column6: Mate Mobility, established in 2023 by former Callaway Golf Korea CEO Lee Sang-hyun, is a South Korean startup specializing in single-rider, autonomous golf carts. The SINGLE is a lightweight, electric mobility vehicle designed to allow individual golfers to move directly to their ball, promoting a personal tempo of play. It features an AI-based driving correction system that analyzes course conditions like slope and turf in real-time to ensure safe, autonomous navigation. Furthermore, the cart utilizes Geofencing technology to automatically recognize and avoid restricted areas, helping to maintain course conditions. Weighing 280kg and equipped with wide tires, the design minimizes impact on the fairway while providing a smooth ride. The system also offers course guidance and distance information, making it particularly useful for 'no caddie' rounds. Golfers can book and learn how to use the carts through a dedicated mobile application, which integrates with the golf course's reservation system. The company supplies its carts to golf courses and has established a strong presence in the professional golf scene. Mate Mobility has secured a five-year exclusive contract with the KPGA (Korean Professional Golf Association) and has supplied its carts for official use in various tournaments, including the LIV Golf Korea, the European DP World Tour, and the Genesis Championship. This exposure has validated its technology on a global stage. The company's business model appears to be centered on supplying these smart carts to golf clubs, enhancing operational efficiency and offering a modernized experience for players. Financially, Mate Mobility has shown significant growth. After a Series A funding round of 12.2 billion KRW in June of the previous year at a 45 billion KRW pre-money valuation, the company recently secured another 10 billion KRW from LB Private Equity. This latest investment was part of a Series B round, valuing the company at 120 billion KRW pre-money, nearly tripling its valuation in just over a year. column5: Electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft manufacturer

column5: Turnkey geodesic domes for automated vanilla cultivation
column6: Australian Vanilla Plantations (AVP) is an AgriTech company focused on enabling widespread vanilla cultivation in non-tropical climates through its proprietary technology. The company was incorporated in 2016 by IT entrepreneur David Soo, who was inspired to find a way to grow vanilla at scale in Australia after a dinner conversation in 2013. This led to the development of the "Vanilla Dome," a turnkey geodesic greenhouse solution designed to make commercial vanilla production viable outside of its traditional tropical environment. AVP's core product is an 11-meter wide, 5.5-meter high geodesic dome greenhouse. This structure is engineered for agricultural efficiency, with its shape promoting superior air circulation and temperature consistency compared to traditional rectangular greenhouses. The domes feature automated climate control systems that regulate temperature and humidity, IoT integration for remote monitoring, and a unique rotational trellis system designed specifically for vanilla vines. These features significantly reduce labor, mitigate risks from weather, and have been shown to increase yields by up to 3-5 times compared to open-field farming. The business model serves multiple client types. AVP operates its own plantations, with a significant site planned within Western Sydney University's Hawkesbury Agri-Tech Hub in partnership with the university and CSIRO. The company also offers its Vanilla Domes as a product for other growers, providing an offtake agreement to buy back the beans for processing. This approach aims to lower the barrier to entry for new vanilla farmers and create a decentralized network of producers. Furthermore, since 2020, AVP has established international buying programs in Papua New Guinea and Indonesia to secure a stable supply chain, ensure fair wages for farmers, and improve community living standards. column5: Modular technology converting biogas into renewable methanol
column6: BioReFuel ApS is a Danish clean technology company specializing in converting waste biogas into renewable methanol. The firm's core technology involves capturing CO₂ from biogas and, through advanced catalytic reactions and separation techniques, transforming it into e-methanol. This process combines steam and dry reforming of biogas in a single step, known as bio-reforming, to produce syngas (CO and H2), which is then catalytically converted into methanol. The company's system is engineered as a portable, modular plug-and-play solution housed within a standard IBC container, designed for easy integration and deployment. This approach provides a scalable and mobile method for producing a sustainable alternative to fossil fuels suitable for transportation and industrial applications. The technology aims to fully convert biogas and hydrogen into methanol, positioning it as a solution for renewable energy storage and sustainable fuel production. Founded as a project with initial funding in 2017 and a project period from 2018-2019, BioReFuel has focused on moving its technology from the conceptual stage to a higher Technology Readiness Level (TRL). The team includes CEO Jan Boye Rasmussen and CTO Rohit Vilas Gaikwad. BioReFuel targets entities seeking to decarbonize, inviting collaboration from investors and companies looking to implement green fuel technologies. column5: Organic waste processing using specialty beetle farming
column6: TOMUSHI is a Japanese insect biotechnology startup founded in 2019 by twin brothers Yosuke and Kensuke Ishida. The company's creation stems from the founders' lifelong passion for beetles, which began with the arcade game 'Mushiking' and culminated in purchasing a Hercules beetle, leading them to discover the beetles' ability to consume waste from mushroom cultivation. Before TOMUSHI, Yosuke Ishida had prior entrepreneurial experience, having founded a web and SNS marketing company which he left to return to his hometown of Odate in Akita Prefecture. The company's business model centers on converting organic waste into valuable resources through beetle farming, addressing both waste management and resource scarcity. TOMUSHI processes various organic wastes, such as spent mushroom substrate (waste from mushroom cultivation), livestock manure, and food waste, by using them as feed for specially bred beetles. These beetles exhibit rapid growth and can endure harsh conditions. The resulting products from this circular model are multifaceted. The beetles themselves are sold as pets and for educational events, their larvae are processed into protein for animal and fish feed, and their frass (excrement) is commercialized as a nutrient-rich organic fertilizer that improves soil and contributes to decarbonization. TOMUSHI is also researching the development of alternative proteins for human consumption. TOMUSHI operates on a franchise model, partnering with farmers, corporations, and local governments to establish decentralized beetle farming operations. This system allows partners to reduce their organic waste disposal costs while creating a new revenue stream. The company provides consulting and operational support to its franchisees and buys back the cultivated beetles for processing and sale. Additionally, TOMUSHI runs several e-commerce platforms, including an insect information website and an online store for beetle-related products, and its beetles have been featured as a return gift in Akita Prefecture's hometown tax donation program. column6: Victory Advanced Technologies (VAT) is a Saint John, New Brunswick-based company founded in November 2021 that designs and manufactures integrated, high-performance electric powertrain systems. VAT’s business model involves working with original equipment manufacturers, distributors, and installers to bring its sustainable powertrains to market. The company was founded by Steve Belyea (CEO), Isaac Barkhouse (CTO), and Greg Hemmings (CMO). The founding was inspired by Belyea's personal challenge in electrifying a classic car and Hemmings's difficulty in finding a durable electric motor for his sailboat. Belyea previously founded BASE Engineering Inc., where he patented electronic control systems for fuel transfer. Barkhouse is an electric powertrain specialist who co-founded Potential Motors Inc. and worked at Bosch GmbH in Germany. Hemmings is an entrepreneur and filmmaker with a focus on corporate social and environmental impact. Victory Advanced Technologies produces an integrated drive system that includes the electric motor, battery module, and control software. A key differentiator is that its motors are built without using rare-earth minerals, addressing environmental and ethical concerns associated with their mining. The company's powertrains are designed to be modular and scalable; for instance, two 150-horsepower motors can be combined to create a 300-horsepower unit, catering to bespoke client needs. The products are engineered to be durable and robust for harsh environments like the Canadian climate. Their industrial motors are explosion-proof, submersible, and feature smart controls with internet connectivity. In March 2024, Victory Advanced Technologies received $400,223 in funding from the Atlantic Canada Opportunities Agency (ACOA). This investment is intended to help the company commercialize its products, acquire new equipment like a CNC machining unit, and expand its team in Saint John. column6: Envitec Biogas Iberia SL is the Spanish and Portuguese subsidiary of the German multinational EnviTec Biogas AG, a global provider of solutions for the production of energy from biomass. The parent company, EnviTec Biogas AG, was founded in 2002 by Olaf von Lehmden, Kunibert Ruhe, and Tobias Schulz. Since its listing on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in 2007, the company has expanded its global presence, operating in 18 countries. The company's business model is structured around three core segments: Plant Construction, Own Plant Operation, and Service. The company also provides energy management solutions for marketing the produced biogas and biomethane, as well as heating concepts. A key development is the production of Bio-LNG (liquefied biomethane) as a CO2-neutral fuel for the transport sector and food-grade liquid carbon dioxide (LCO2). column5: Locally produced biochar for regenerative soil amendment
column6: Black Gold BioChar produces and supplies biochar, a charcoal-like substance used as a soil amendment to improve agricultural productivity and soil health. The company's core product is created through pyrolysis, a process of heating biomass like wood from local sawmills in a low-oxygen environment. This method creates a stable, carbon-rich material that regenerates the soil. The primary function of Black Gold BioChar's product is to enhance soil structure, whether by opening up compacted soil or adding structure to sandy soil. Its porous nature allows it to increase water retention, improve aeration, and provide a habitat for beneficial microorganisms. By improving the soil's capacity to hold nutrients, it can reduce the need for fertilizers and lessen nutrient leaching into waterways. The application of biochar is recognized for its role in long-term carbon sequestration, as the carbon is locked into the soil for extended periods, which helps mitigate climate change. Black Gold BioChar's product is sold in flake form and must be "charged" or inoculated with nutrients and microbes from sources like compost tea or worm castings before use. The company targets home gardeners and farmers seeking to improve plant health and yields through sustainable practices. Beyond soil amendment, the biochar can be used in chicken coops to control odor or as an additive in animal feed. The business model appears to be direct sales to consumers and agricultural clients, leveraging partnerships with local retailers like the Grateful Harvest Seed Company. column5: Chemical-free electronic water treatment for descaling.
column6: Sinelabs provides chemical-free water treatment solutions for residential, commercial, and industrial applications. The company's core technology is a non-intrusive electronic system that clamps onto existing pipes of any material, such as PVC or metal. This system emits a unique electronic signal that travels throughout the plumbing. The signal causes dissolved minerals like calcium and magnesium to flocculate, or crystallize, which prevents them from forming hard scale on surfaces. This process not only prevents new scale buildup but also helps to remove existing scale over time. The technology aims to deliver significant operational and financial benefits. By preventing scale, it enhances heat transfer efficiency in systems like water heaters, boilers, and HVAC cooling towers, which can lead to energy savings of up to 20%. The system also reduces the need for frequent maintenance and cleaning of water-based equipment. Furthermore, Sinelabs' solution eliminates the necessity for chemical-based treatments, reducing operational costs and environmental impact. The company states that this approach also controls biofilm and kills waterborne pathogens like Legionella by bursting their cell walls, improving water safety. Sinelabs targets a broad market, including hospitality, manufacturing, medical facilities, municipalities, agriculture, and data centers. The business model involves selling different sizes of its water treatment units to fit various needs, from small residential units to large industrial systems. The company emphasizes a quick return on investment for its clients, citing a typical breakeven time of 10 months and significant long-term savings on energy, water, and chemical usage. Residential units are designed for simple self-installation, while industrial and commercial setups are installed by authorized technicians. column5: Fouling-resistant zwitterionic membranes for industrial wastewater treatment
column6: ZwitterCo provides advanced membrane technology for treating challenging industrial wastewater, enabling water reuse and resource recovery. This patented zwitterionic chemistry makes the membranes highly resistant to irreversible fouling from organic compounds like fats, oils, greases, and proteins, a common problem that degrades traditional membranes. Unlike conventional options, ZwitterCo's membranes maintain performance after cleaning cycles, offering a longer lifecycle and reduced operating costs. The company's products are designed to be retrofitted into existing treatment systems. ZwitterCo serves a range of industrial clients in sectors such as food and beverage, dairy processing, bioprocessing, grain processing, and landfill leachate treatment. Its technology allows these industries to treat highly contaminated water streams that were previously considered untreatable, facilitating water reuse, ensuring regulatory compliance, and enabling the recovery of valuable byproducts from the waste stream, such as fertilizers or biofuel feedstocks. The business model includes the sale of its membrane products and engineered filtration systems, which are available as purpose-built installations or rentals. The company has achieved significant financial milestones, including a $33 million Series A funding round in 2022, noted as the largest ever for a water technology company at the time, and a $58.4 million Series B round in 2024. column5: Fault-managed power distribution using Digital Electricity™ technology
column6: VoltFMP is a key solutions provider for VoltServer's patented Digital Electricity™ technology, focusing on revolutionizing power distribution. A key safety feature is the rapid verification process, where the circuit is checked up to 600 times per second, and power is shut off within milliseconds if a fault is detected.  VoltFMP operates by forming strategic partnerships to deliver scalable and resilient power systems. column5: Earthen thermal batteries for inexpensive solar energy storage.
column6: Standard Thermal is a developer of thermal energy storage solutions designed to make solar photovoltaic (PV) energy available 24/7 at a price competitive with natural gas. The company was founded in 2021 and is based in Oklahoma City, with a presence in Woodinville, WA. The leadership team includes CEO Austin Vernon, COO Brian Pal, and CTO Jimmy Williams, who developed the technology for approximately two years before launching the startup. The core of Standard Thermal's technology is a system that stores energy as heat in large mounds of dirt or earth, which functions as a thermal battery. This approach utilizes co-located solar PV arrays to provide electricity, which is then converted to heat via resistive heating elements embedded in the earthen piles. The system is designed to heat the dirt to over 600°C. When energy is needed, a fluid runs through pipes within the mound to absorb the heat, which can then be used directly for industrial processes or to create steam for electricity generation. The company emphasizes that its design avoids the need for grid interconnection and long-lead-time components, reducing capital expenditures by 30% to 50% compared to grid-oriented solar farms. Standard Thermal’s earthen thermal battery offers a significant cost advantage, with a capital cost projected to be under $0.10 per kilowatt-hour thermal, which is substantially cheaper than conventional battery storage. The technology is particularly suited for seasonal energy shifting, allowing solar energy harvested during the summer to be stored for winter heating needs. The system is scalable, from the size of a house for a small factory to the area of multiple football fields for large power plants. The company has a 100-kilowatt test site in Oklahoma powering a 6-megawatt-hour thermal storage unit where it has been prototyping designs. The business model targets several customer archetypes. In the near term, the focus is on industrial clients who require 24/7 high-quality heat, such as those in food processing, manufacturing, and chemical plants. Another key market is isolated energy users who currently rely on expensive fuels like propane or fuel oil, including industries like mining and agriculture. A medium-term goal is to repower old coal power plants, using the stored thermal energy to generate steam for existing turbines, thereby feeding electricity back into the grid. column5: Consumer co-created food brand ensuring fair farmer prices
column6: Du bist hier der Chef! (You are the boss here!) is a German consumer initiative founded in June 2019 by Nicolas Barthelmé and eight other consumers. The venture is the German replication of the successful French movement "C'est qui le Patron?!", which was launched in 2016 by Nicolas Chabanne in response to a milk price crisis. Barthelmé, a former marketing executive, discovered the French concept in late 2018 and decided to bring its model of consumer participation and price transparency to the German market. The business model centers on empowering consumers to co-create food products, deciding on specifications such as production methods, animal welfare standards, and origin, which in turn determines a fair price for both the consumer and the producer. The process is facilitated through online questionnaires where the community votes on product attributes. This transparent approach aims to guarantee fair and predictable revenue for farmers. The first product launched in Germany in July 2020 was milk, produced in partnership with the Upländer Bauernmolkerei and sold initially in about 400 REWE supermarkets. The product line later expanded to include eggs and potatoes for a limited time. Despite selling 2.8 million products and demonstrating consumer willingness to pay higher prices for fairness and transparency, the initiative faced significant challenges. A key struggle was the reluctance of major German retail chains to grant nationwide listings, which limited the brand's availability and growth potential. As a result, "Du bist hier der Chef!" announced it would cease its main operational activities at the end of 2025. Founder Nicolas Barthelmé is set to return to a voluntary role, and the initiative's knowledge will be made available as an open-source resource. The flagship consumer-created milk will continue to be sold in currently supplied stores. The company is headquartered in Leoben, Austria, and is owned by Gernot Beutle. It receives support from the Center for Applied Technology of the Montanuniversität Leoben and the municipality of Leoben. GM Remediation Systems focuses on in-situ thermal methods, which involve heating the soil and groundwater to evaporate pollutants. These contaminants are then removed through soil vapor extraction and subsequent exhaust gas treatment. This process is an alternative to traditional soil excavation and disposal, eliminating the need for excavation and typically completing the remediation within three to four months. The primary energy source for the systems is electricity, though gas can be used in special cases. The technology is effective for various contaminants, including chlorinated hydrocarbons (CHCs), and is particularly advantageous in groundwater-saturated soils as it doesn't require water extraction. The company's business model involves offering its systems as kits for both purchase and rent. These kits include heating elements, data loggers, and control panels. A monthly service contract is also available, providing automatic regulation of the temperature field and operational optimization to reduce energy consumption and achieve faster results. Data loggers measure field temperatures, extracted contaminant mass, and heater temperatures, sending the data to the company's server for analysis. GM Remediation Systems provides planning services, evaluation, and piloting for their clients' projects at contaminated sites. The company serves clients in the remediation business who are focused on revitalizing brownfields in urban areas. It sells its systems worldwide through partners and is actively seeking new trading partners to expand its technology's reach. column5: All about fun
column6: Surf REC is a Lisbon-based startup aiming to enhance the surfing experience through a blend of technology and community. The company provides an ecosystem for surfers that integrates automated wave recording with online coaching. This service is designed to unite the surfing community, which has seen fragmentation as the sport grows and diversifies. By offering accessible surf footage and coaching, Surf REC intends to help surfers improve their skills while fostering a more connected and positive environment in the water. The core of Surf REC's offering is its automated recording system. At participating surf spots, users can create an account at a kiosk, equip themselves with a tracking bracelet, and have their entire session filmed by an auto-tracking camera. This technology ensures full coverage of every wave ridden without the surfer feeling the pressure of being watched. Afterward, the footage is automatically delivered to the user's account, where it can be reviewed, analyzed, or shared with the community. The business model is a pay-per-minute service, charging €0.25 per minute of use, facilitated through Stripe for secure transactions. Beyond simple recording, Surf REC is developing a platform for personalized online coaching. Surfers will be able to use their video clips for one-on-one sessions with certified coaches, who must have a minimum of five years of experience. This feature allows users to receive tailored feedback and set specific goals for improvement, bridging the gap between recreational surfing and professional-level analysis. The platform aims to serve wave riders of all skill levels, democratizing access to tools that were once only available to elite athletes. The company was founded by Afonso Maya. column5: Our sulfur resistant next generation catalyst converts your CO2 emission costs into added value from methanol
column6: Based in Vöcklabruck, Austria, CO2ol catalyst is a spin-off from the Vienna University of Technology (TU Wien) focused on carbon capture and utilization. The company was founded by Dr. Karin Föttinger and Dr. Christian Weilach to commercialize a novel process for converting industrial carbon dioxide emissions into methanol. Dr. Föttinger serves as the scientific lead, bringing over two decades of experience in catalyst research and is a Professor at TU Wien, where the core technology was developed. Dr. Weilach acts as the project's strategist, holding a PhD in Physical Chemistry and possessing more than 10 years of industrial experience in scaling disruptive technologies. The core of the business is a proprietary catalyst technology that recycles CO2 from industrial flue gas into methanol, a crucial platform chemical for the chemical industry. The technology leverages a new catalyst material based on Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2), which converts CO2 into methanol with high selectivity. A key feature of this catalyst is its exceptional tolerance to impurities, particularly sulfur compounds, which are often present in industrial exhaust streams. This resistance eliminates the need for extensive and costly purification of the CO2 feed gas, which simplifies the overall process, making it more cost-effective and efficient compared to existing technologies. CO2ol catalyst targets industrial emitters such as chemical, steel, and cement manufacturers as its primary clients. The business model centers on providing a technology that transforms a waste product and emission cost (CO2) into a valuable commodity (methanol), which can be used as a fuel additive or for producing materials like polyolefins. By using green hydrogen and renewable energy in the process, the resulting methanol has a significantly reduced carbon footprint, contributing to the defossilization of chemical value chains. The catalyst operates under mild conditions, starting at temperatures below 200°C, and is based on abundant materials, avoiding the use of noble metals. The company has gained support from investors and programs like Greenstart, VERBUND, and the TU Wien Innovation Incubation Center, and has been recognized as a finalist in competitions such as the ACHEMA Start-up Award. column6: Wefight was a digital health company founded in Montpellier, France, in 2017 by Benoît Brouard and Pierre Nectoux. The firm ceased operations, entering into liquidation in December 2023. The founding of Wefight was inspired by Brouard's experiences as a hospital pharmacist, where he identified a need for accessible and reliable information for patients with chronic conditions. Brouard, who served as CEO, combined his healthcare background with Nectoux's technical expertise as CTO to create the company's core product. Over its operational years, Wefight secured $13.8 million in funding over two rounds, with a significant Series A round of $11.8 million in September 2021 led by Digital Health Ventures and Impact Partners.The company developed Vik, an AI-powered virtual companion designed to support patients with cancer and chronic diseases. Available as a mobile and web-based chatbot, Vik provided patients and their relatives with 24/7 answers to their questions, offering scientifically backed information to alleviate anxiety and isolation. The content for each condition-specific Vik application was co-created with patient advocacy groups, patients, and scientific committees to ensure relevance and accuracy. Vik's functionalities included educating patients about their diagnosis and treatment, helping them manage their condition, and providing reminders for medication adherence. The platform supported over 15 pathologies and was available in several countries, including the US, Canada, Brazil, and nations across Europe and the Middle East.Wefight's business model targeted several stakeholders within the healthcare ecosystem. For patients, the Vik app was free to use. Revenue was generated through partnerships with pharmaceutical companies, which utilized the platform for patient engagement and to gather real-world data. The company offered several solutions, including 'Vik Studies' to conduct tailored research, 'Vik PROM' to capture patient-reported outcome measures, and 'MedVik', a platform for healthcare professionals to monitor their patients remotely. column6: Waixo Fashion & Digital Solutions, S.L. operates as a digital textile printing company, positioning itself to transform the fabric manufacturing sector by producing on-demand rather than selling from pre-existing stock. Waixo's core business revolves around an online platform that enables fashion brands, designers, and hobbyists to design and print their own fabrics without minimum quantity requirements. The company's business model is primarily B2B, although it also serves individual creators. It generates revenue through the sale of custom-printed fabrics and finished textile products, including both patterned and solid-color materials. The client base is diverse, ranging from small businesses and independent professionals who market their products on social media and third-party platforms to institutions like the Thyssen-Bornemisza museum. Waixo has integrated its entire manufacturing process to ensure quick turnaround times, offering delivery within a week, with expedited options available for a surcharge. Waixo's service is built upon a digital printing process that provides a broad catalog of over 40 fabric types, including sustainable options like organic and recycled materials. The company emphasizes sustainability by using ecological inks and sourcing materials from a trusted group of suppliers. It further minimizes environmental impact by donating fabric remnants to training workshops and repurposing used paper from the printing process as packaging. By leveraging technology to enable localized, unitary, and personalized production, Waixo aims to be a leading force in shifting textile manufacturing towards a more sustainable and on-demand model. column5: Online auctions of judicial and financial assets
column6: Clicpublic.be is a Belgian e-commerce portal specializing in the online auction of assets from judicial and financial origins. Founded in 2011 and headquartered in Nivelles, Belgium, the company provides a digital platform for assets sourced from bankruptcies, liquidations, seizures, corporate destocking, and unclaimed estates. Clicpublic operates as a broker for clients such as court-appointed administrators, receivers, banks, bailiffs, and trustees, managing the entire asset recovery process from inventory and assessment to the final online auction. The business model is centered on conducting auctions exclusively online, aiming to offer greater transparency, accessibility, and reach compared to traditional public auctions. This digital approach attracts a broad base of buyers, including both companies and private individuals, from across Belgium and Luxembourg. The platform handles a wide variety of goods, ranging from vehicles and construction equipment to office furniture, IT hardware, and assets from the Horeca (hotel/restaurant/café) sector. For sellers, the company offers a fully integrated service that covers all sales and logistics steps. Buyers can register for free and bid on items, with the option to inspect lots during scheduled viewing days. In June 2024, Clicpublic was acquired by Agorastore, a French leader in B2B digital auctions. This acquisition is part of Agorastore's strategy to expand its European footprint and enhance its expertise in judicial and bank auctions. The integration strengthens Agorastore's presence in the Benelux region, a dynamic market for digital auctions. At the time of the acquisition, Clicpublic had partnerships with over 300 court-appointed agents, nearly 100,000 registered buyers, and an annual sales volume exceeding €15 million. column5: HeartKinetics AI solutions empower motion and ECG wearable sensors to intercept heart failure and cancer cardiotoxicity
column6: HeartKinetics is a pioneering startup focused on revolutionizing the management of heart failure through innovative technology. The company offers a unique, non-invasive medical device that enables patients to monitor their heart's energy signature, which is the specific amount of energy released with each cardiac contraction. This regular monitoring helps in the early detection of potential deterioration in cardiac function, allowing for timely intervention.HeartKinetics primarily serves cardiologists and their patients who suffer from heart failure. The device is designed to be user-friendly, allowing patients to measure their heart's energy signature at home or anywhere else, in less than 45 seconds. This ease of use helps patients to relax, better manage their condition, and prevent severe episodes of decompensation, which is a worsening of heart failure symptoms.The company operates in the healthcare and medical technology market, specifically targeting the niche of heart failure management. Its business model revolves around selling the medical device to healthcare providers and patients, as well as offering a subscription-based service for continuous monitoring and data analysis. The data collected by the device is sent to a network of artificial neurons, which are advanced algorithms capable of evaluating changes in the heart's systolic ejection function. This function measures how well the heart pumps blood with each beat, and the system can deduce a measure of cardiac contractility, which is the heart's ability to contract.HeartKinetics generates revenue through the sale of its devices and subscription fees for ongoing monitoring and data analysis services. This dual revenue stream ensures a steady income while providing valuable, life-saving insights to its users.Keywords: heart failure, non-invasive, medical device, cardiology, energy signature, early detection, patient monitoring, artificial neurons, cardiac contractility, healthcare technology.

column6: Established in 2004 as a spin-off from the Catholic University of Louvain (UCLouvain), GreenWatt is a Belgian firm that engineers, constructs, and operates integrated biomethanization plants. The company's core business revolves around providing turnkey biogas installations for the food and beverage industry, as well as for agricultural players. This business model is built upon proprietary technology for multi-stage anaerobic digestion, a process that breaks down organic waste to produce biogas. GreenWatt's system is designed for robustness and flexibility, capable of processing a variety of organic wastes without the need for animal manure, which makes it particularly suitable for industrial food processing sites. The biogas generated can be utilized in several ways: as fuel for combined heat and power (CHP) cogeneration units or upgraded to biomethane for injection into the natural gas grid. This approach allows clients to transform their organic waste streams into a source of renewable energy, potentially reducing operational costs. Beyond energy production, the process yields a residual digestate that can be valorized as a bio-fertilizer. The company's clientele includes farms, food and beverage producers, food service companies, and food retailers. While its primary operational footprint is in the Benelux region and France, GreenWatt has ambitions for further international expansion. In 2012, the company secured a EUR 6 million funding round led by Gimv-Agri+ to support its growth. Subsequently, in 2016, GreenWatt was acquired by the Sol Invictus Group. column5: Developing medical devices to promote patient safety and reduce healthcare associated infections
column6: Mantra Medical was a UK-based medical device manufacturer founded by Dr. Paul Hercock, an Accident and Emergency physician, to develop innovative infection control equipment for healthcare settings. Established in 2009 and based in Rotherham, the company created specialized cleaning systems designed to disinfect high-touch patient care devices—particularly blood pressure cuffs and pulse oximeters—within seconds at the patient bedside, addressing a critical gap in standard infection control protocols.The company’s products were engineered around the principle of workflow integration rather than workflow disruption. Recognizing that healthcare staff were already resource-constrained, Mantra Medical developed systems that required minimal additional effort to operate. The blood pressure cuff cleaner utilized UV light technology, while the pulse oximeter cleaning system employed replaceable cartridges combining chemical and mechanical cleaning mechanisms. Both devices were designed for rapid, point-of-care disinfection to help reduce healthcare-associated infections such as Clostridioides difficile and norovirus transmission between patients.Mantra Medical operated within the B2B healthcare sector, primarily targeting NHS trusts and hospital institutions. The company received support from regional economic development initiatives, including Creative Sheffield and the South Yorkshire Sector Growth Enhancement Programme, which facilitated access to design consultancy services through Sheffield Hallam University’s Advanced Manufacturing Research Centre. The founder also explored additional innovation opportunities, including sharps disposal cost reduction initiatives. Despite its innovative approach to a genuine healthcare challenge, the company was dissolved via voluntary strike-off on 30 January 2024. Paul Hercock subsequently founded Mantra Systems Ltd in 2019, transitioning to medical device regulatory consulting services.Keywords: infection control, medical devices, hospital hygiene, healthcare-associated infections, bedside cleaning, patient safety, NHS, disinfection equipment, UV light technology, healthcare innovation.

The core service is delivered through a platform that facilitates the posting of short-term jobs, termed "workbits." These can range from a few hours to several months. column6: A&J Vacworx Inc. is a family-owned and operated industrial services company specializing in hydro excavation. In addition to hydro excavation, A&J Vacworx provides keyhole cutting, which allows for precise cuts and removal of hard surfaces to access utilities in roadways, and the delivery of vacuum-sealed debris bins for slurry containment. A&J Vacworx operates a large, modern fleet of hydrovac trucks and support vehicles from its yards in Mount Albert and Innisfil, Ontario. The company emphasizes a strong health and safety culture, with a dedicated internal team ensuring staff are well-trained and all equipment is maintained for safe operation. column5: Pyrolysis-based recycling of end-of-life tires.
column6: Green Rubber Energy is a Thai-based company specializing in the pyrolysis recycling of end-of-life tires (ELT). Founded in 2007, the company has developed technology to address the environmental problem of tire waste. Globally, about 30 million tons of tires are discarded each year, with many being landfilled or incinerated, creating a significant environmental burden.The company operates in the waste management and recycling sector, focusing on converting waste tires into valuable materials through thermal decomposition. This process, known as pyrolysis, heats tires in an oxygen-free environment to break them down into recovered carbon black (rCB) and tire pyrolysis oil (TPO). Green Rubber Energy has spent over a decade refining this technology to produce a stable, high-quality rCB suitable for use as a raw material in new tire manufacturing, a technical challenge that had previously hindered its adoption due to impurities. The company's plant in Samut Prakan, Thailand, processes 10,000 tons of ELTs annually.In September 2024, Marubeni Corporation, a major Japanese trading company, made a significant investment in Green Rubber Energy, acquiring a 32% stake. This partnership aims to establish a comprehensive tire recycling supply chain in Thailand. The collaboration involves Marubeni's subsidiary, B-Quik Co., Thailand's largest car maintenance company, supplying ELTs to Green Rubber Energy's facility. Marubeni also plans to enhance the purity of the recovered carbon black using technology from RCB Nanotechnologies GmbH, a German company in which it has also invested, and manage the sales of rCB and TPO through another subsidiary, Marubeni Techno Rubber Co. The goal is to expand this recycling model to Japan, Southeast Asia, and other global markets.Keywords: end-of-life tire recycling, pyrolysis, recovered carbon black, rCB, tire pyrolysis oil, TPO, waste to energy, circular economy, sustainable materials, rubber recycling, waste management, cleantech, green technology, tire-to-oil, thermal decomposition, environmental services, industrial recycling

column5: Cement-based lining and maintenance for water tanks.
column6: HydraStone Inc. is a Canadian company specializing in the maintenance, repair, and relining of large-scale domestic and commercial water tanks. This is achieved through on-site inspections, preventative maintenance programs, and the application of proprietary cementitious linings, which offer a durable alternative to factory-installed glass or epoxy linings. The company's origins trace back nearly three decades, born from the need to address a market gap in repairing and relining industrial-sized domestic hot water tanks with factory-installed cement liners. In 2005, a significant milestone was the acquisition of the Alkrete liner formula, a material with a 40-year history that became HydraStone's primary product after it was certified to CSA and NSF-61 standards for potable water. More recently, in April 2026, HydraStone was acquired by Originate Developments through its operating platform, Originate Partners. The founder, Jamie Russell, and the General Manager, Paul Duell, have continued with the business post-acquisition. HydraStone's business model is centered on service and product supply. The company not only performs on-site relining services but also manufactures and distributes its cement-based products, Alkrete and Hydrakrete, to other certified lining companies and major tank manufacturers in Canada and the United States. These products are formulated to protect against corrosion and contamination in both hot and cold water applications. The service process includes thorough inspections to identify issues, followed by repairs and relining, often completed within a 24-30 hour shutdown period. column5: High-performance marine and motorsports racing engines.
column6: Ilmor Engineering, Inc. is a globally recognized provider of high-performance engines for motorsports and recreational marine applications. The company was founded in November 1983 by two engineers from Cosworth, Mario Illien and Paul Morgan, who secured financial backing from American motorsport entrepreneur Roger Penske. Their initial goal was to design and build turbocharged engines for the IndyCar series, challenging the then-dominant Cosworth engines. The company's journey began with the Ilmor-Chevrolet 265-A Indy V-8 engine, which debuted at the 1986 Indianapolis 500. Success came quickly, with Mario Andretti securing the engine's first victory in 1987. This was followed by an Indianapolis 500 win in 1988 with Rick Mears and a CART championship with Danny Sullivan. The 1990s saw significant expansion, including the establishment of Ilmor Engineering, Inc. in Plymouth, Michigan, to support its U.S. customers. A pivotal partnership with Mercedes-Benz began in 1993, leading to the creation of the powerful Mercedes-Benz 500I engine that won the 1994 Indy 500. This collaboration extended to Formula One, where Ilmor-designed engines powered the McLaren team to back-to-back world championships in 1998 and 1999. Following the tragic death of co-founder Paul Morgan in 2001, DaimlerChrysler increased its stake, eventually owning the F1 division and renaming it Mercedes-Benz High Performance Engines. In 2005, Mario Illien and Roger Penske repurchased the Special Projects part of the company, re-establishing Ilmor Engineering as an independent entity focused on various racing series and diversification. Ilmor operates a business-to-business model, supplying engines, components, and engineering consultancy to major automotive manufacturers and professional racing teams in series like IndyCar, NASCAR, and ARCA. The company also entered the high-performance marine sector in 2002, building race engines for offshore powerboat racing. This division has grown into a significant part of the business, becoming the exclusive engine supplier to MasterCraft Boat Company and developing a range of inboard and sterndrive engines for the recreational market. Ilmor's revenue is generated through the design, development, manufacturing, and servicing of these advanced powertrain systems. More recently, the company has expanded into electric propulsion systems, partnering with other firms to develop electric outboard motors. To support its growth, Ilmor is investing in a new technology and manufacturing facility in Michigan, expected to open in 2025. The company's core offerings include a range of high-performance engines for both racing and marine use. In motorsports, Ilmor provides the ARCA Ilmor 396 and the NASCAR NT1 engines, and acts as a partner for Chevrolet in the IndyCar Series. column6: The California Plug Load Research Center (CalPlug) was established in 2011 within the California Institute for Telecommunications and Information Technology (Calit2) at the University of California, Irvine. The center's business model revolves around collaborative research, funded through grants, and membership fees.
