column5: Natural gas-fired combined-cycle power generation facility
column6: The Caithness Long Island Energy Center (CLIEC) is a 350 MW natural gas-fired power plant in Yaphank, New York, that began commercial operation on August 1, 2009. It was the first major baseload power plant constructed on Long Island in over three decades. The plant is operated by Caithness Energy, a privately-held independent power producer specializing in the development, acquisition, and management of energy projects. In September 2025, it was announced that Lotus Infrastructure Partners had agreed to acquire the facility. The development of CLIEC was initiated in response to a 2003 request for proposal from the Long Island Power Authority (LIPA) for new on-island generation, following the Northeast blackout of 2003. The facility utilizes combined-cycle technology, incorporating a Siemens SGT6-5000F gas turbine and an SST-900 RH steam turbine, to generate power with high efficiency. This process recycles heat that would otherwise be lost to generate additional power, reducing fuel consumption by approximately one-third compared to older plants. Primarily fueled by natural gas, the plant can also run on fuel oil as a backup. The electricity produced is sold to LIPA under a power purchase agreement and distributed through its transmission network. By 2020, CLIEC was the second-largest power generator on Long Island based on net energy produced. A key feature of the plant is its use of a closed-cycle, air-cooled condenser, which reduces water consumption by 95% compared to plants with evaporative cooling systems. This technology helps to conserve billions of gallons of water from Long Island's aquifers annually. The plant's design and technology make it one of the cleanest and most efficient on Long Island, producing significantly fewer emissions than older facilities in the region. column5: Data-driven price comparison for protein powders
column6: PricePerProtein.com is a data-centric comparison platform designed to analyze the protein powder market. Launched in September 2025 by a creator identified as BatuhanU, the tool was developed to solve a personal challenge: finding the most cost-effective protein powders by tracking their prices in a spreadsheet. The website provides users with key information in a table format, allowing for quick comparisons based on price, protein type, calorie count, and more. column5: Run-of-the-river hydroelectric power generation plant operator
column6: Malana Power Company Limited (MPCL) is a public limited company that develops and operates run-of-the-river hydroelectric power plants in India. Incorporated on May 20, 1997, the company is a subsidiary of Bhilwara Energy Limited, which is part of the LNJ Bhilwara Group. The company's flagship project is the 86 MW Malana Hydroelectric Plant, located on the Malana river in the Kullu district of Himachal Pradesh. Construction began in January 1999, and the plant was commissioned in a record time of 30 months in July 2001, significantly ahead of schedule and at a lower cost than typical for such projects. This project was developed to help address power shortages in India's northern region. The plant operates as a peaking station from November to May and as a baseload plant for the rest of the year. Initially, MPCL was a joint venture between the LNJ Bhilwara Group (51%) and Norwegian state-owned Statkraft (49%), Europe's largest renewable energy producer, starting in 2004. This partnership facilitated the exchange of technical and financial expertise, leading to operational improvements such as advanced sediment removal technology and turbine coatings to reduce erosion. In September 2025, Bhilwara Energy Limited, an associate of HEG Limited, acquired Statkraft's 49% stake, making LNJ Bhilwara Group the sole owner of the company. This acquisition included stakes in both the Malana (86 MW) and the Allain Duhangan (192 MW) hydropower plants. MPCL generates revenue by selling the power it produces. For the fiscal year ending March 31, 2024, the company's operating revenue was in the range of INR 100 cr - 500 cr. The power generated is sold to PTC India under a power purchase agreement. The company also earns additional income from other hydro plants that use its transmission lines. column6: The Food Project is a non-profit organization founded in 1991 by farmer and educator Ward Cheney. column6: Project Hestia is a financial initiative by Sunnova Energy International Inc. to broaden the accessibility of distributed energy resources (DERs) for American homeowners. This structure was intended to make clean energy more affordable and accessible. The first asset-backed securitization, Hestia I, was priced in October 2023. column5: Organic, fair-trade coffee roaster and cafe operator
column6: Bongo Java Roasting Co. operates as a coffee roasting company and a chain of cafes based in Nashville, Tennessee. Founded in 1993 by former journalist Bob Bernstein, the company began as Nashville's oldest coffeehouse. Bernstein, who had moved to Nashville for a journalism career, transitioned into the coffee business and opened the first Bongo Java cafe just before his 30th birthday. The company has since expanded to include multiple cafes and two wholesale businesses, establishing itself as the only certified organic coffee roaster in Nashville. The business model is centered on ethically sourced, high-quality coffee. Bongo Java exclusively sources 100% organic, Fair Trade coffee beans directly from small-scale producers in regions like Indonesia, Central and South America, and Africa, often paying prices above the Fair Trade minimum. This direct-trade practice is facilitated through Cooperative Coffees, a coffee-buying cooperative of small roasters that Bernstein helped establish to foster long-term, sustainable relationships with farmer groups. Revenue is generated through retail sales at its cafes—which include Bongo Java, Fido, and Grins Vegetarian Café—and wholesale distribution of its roasted coffee beans to other coffee shops and grocery stores. The company also engages in local collaborations, supplying its beans for products like chocolate bars and craft cider. The company gained significant attention in 1996 for the "Nun Bun," a cinnamon bun that bore a resemblance to Mother Teresa, which brought worldwide media coverage. Over the years, the Bongo family of businesses has grown to encompass several distinct cafe concepts, including Fido, which is noted for being a large buyer of local ingredients, and Grins, Nashville's oldest vegetarian cafe. The roasting operation, which started in the back of a sister cafe, eventually moved to a larger, dedicated facility to support its wholesale growth. column5: Patented frequency inverters for energy-efficient motor control
column6: NFO Drives AB is a Swedish cleantech company founded in 1996 that develops, manufactures, and markets frequency inverters for controlling electric motors. The company is publicly traded on the Spotlight Stock Market and has been listed since 1999. Based in Karlshamn, Sweden, the firm's core business revolves around its patented NFO Sinus frequency inverters, designed to optimize the speed of electric motors in applications such as pumps, fans, and industrial machinery. The company's technology is rooted in research that began in the mid-1980s by civil engineer Ragnar Jönsson, which led to inventions for controlling motors with a pure sine wave output. This technology distinguishes NFO Drives' products from conventional PWM (pulse width modulation) inverters. Key benefits of the NFO Sinus technology include the elimination of electromagnetic interference, which allows the inverters to be used in sensitive environments like hospitals and residential buildings without requiring expensive shielded cables or EMC filters. This design also prevents bearing currents that can damage motors and eliminates irritating switching noises, contributing to a longer motor lifespan and quieter operation. NFO Drives serves a range of clients across industrial, agricultural, and residential sectors, with a primary focus on the Nordic market and plans for European expansion. By enabling motor speed to be adjusted to current demand, the inverters can achieve energy savings of up to 70%, often resulting in a return on investment within a year. The company's products are sold directly and through distributors, with ZTF Lāsma being the official distributor in the Baltic states. The company's management includes CEO Johan Braun and Chairman of the Board Nicklas Johansson. column6: Agri-Cycle is an organics management company that provides collection, processing, and disposal services for commercial food waste. The process of anaerobic digestion breaks down the organic matter, capturing biogas that is used to generate renewable electricity sold back to the power grid. The remaining solids and liquids are processed into organic fertilizer and animal bedding for use on the farm. Agri-Cycle was a pioneer in the Northeast for implementing a depackaging machine in 2015, which mechanically separates food from its packaging, allowing them to process packaged and expired goods from clients like grocery chains. This service helps clients meet state-level organic waste diversion mandates and reduce landfill disposal fees. Agri-Cycle has expanded its operations from its initial base in Maine to service over 2,400 locations for 850 clients across 14 states in the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic. Its growth has been supported by acquisitions, including the New Hampshire-based company "WholeCycle" and "Food Grease Trappers," which added fats and oils processing to its capabilities. In August 2025, Agri-Cycle was acquired by Closed Loop Partners, a private equity firm focused on the circular economy, to accelerate its national expansion. column5: Commercial-scale sustainable aviation fuel production from biowaste
column6: Lighthouse Green Fuels is developing the United Kingdom's first commercial-scale facility for producing advanced Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) on Teesside. column6: X-ROTOR is a research and innovation project funded by the European Union's Horizon 2020 program, running from 2020 to 2024 with a budget of €3.5 million. The project consortium consists of 12 partners from 7 different European countries, coordinated by the Technical University of Munich. Key areas of development include innovative blade technologies, such as passive and active flow control devices, and advanced control strategies for the entire turbine system. These technologies aim to reduce the levelized cost of energy (LCOE) by mitigating aerodynamic and structural loads on the turbine blades, thereby improving energy yield and extending the turbine's lifespan. The project validates its findings through a comprehensive testing campaign, which includes experiments in wind tunnels and field tests on a research turbine. By integrating these advanced rotor technologies, X-ROTOR aims to contribute to the next generation of more efficient and cost-effective wind energy systems, supporting the EU's renewable energy targets. column6: Solid'Africa is a Rwandan social enterprise established in 2010 to address critical gaps in the country's healthcare system. What started with providing meals to a few dozen patients has grown into a major operation.  The organization's primary mission is to provide support to low-income, vulnerable patients in public hospitals. Its business model is centered on a comprehensive "farm-to-fork" approach. Solid'Africa operates its own farms to grow produce, prepares medically-tailored, nutritious meals in industrial kitchens, and delivers them directly to patients. One of its major milestones was the construction of the Mike Stenbock Gemura Kitchen, an industrial facility with the capacity to cook up to 15,000 meals daily. As of early 2025, the organization serves nearly 20,000 meals a day in six district hospitals. Beyond meals, its programs also provide hygiene products, financial aid for hospital bills, and transportation subsidies.  Solid'Africa has evolved from a non-profit to a social enterprise with a Community Benefit Company (CBC) arm to ensure sustainability and scalability. This has led to a public-private partnership with the Rwandan government to expand its meal services to 47 hospitals nationwide. The model is also being extended to the education sector, with a pilot program in collaboration with the Ministry of Education to provide nutritious meals to students. The organization's impact is significant, having delivered over 11 million meals to more than 700,000 patients and students. Founder Isabelle Kamariza has received numerous accolades for her work, including the Forbes Woman Africa Social Impact Award and the Elevate Prize. column5: Patented copper-silver ionization technology for legionella control
column6: Holland Water provides technology for combating Legionella bacteria and biofilm in water systems. The company was founded by Leo de Zeeuw in the Netherlands around 2003, following the deadly legionellosis outbreak in Boven-Karspel in 1999. The company's primary product is the HW Bifipro®, a system that utilizes this patented copper and silver ionization (CSI) technology. It works by releasing precise amounts of copper and silver ions into the water, which kills Legionella bacteria and removes the biofilm that serves as its breeding ground. This method is positioned as a sustainable and cost-effective alternative to chemical treatments. The system is designed for buildings with complex water networks, such as hospitals, hotels, nursing homes, apartment buildings, and industrial cooling towers. Holland Water's business model includes the sale and installation of its Bifipro® systems, as well as related services and maintenance. The company also operates through a distributorship model, inviting building water management service providers globally to become partners and distribute its technology. Since 2020, following an investment from private equity firm OxGreenfield, the company has been undergoing rapid expansion in Europe and the Middle East, with Rogier van den Brink appointed as CEO to lead this growth. Founder Leo de Zeeuw has transitioned to a role focusing on strategic partnerships and acquisitions. column5: Lithium and critical materials extraction from wastewater
column6: Element3 Resources is a critical material extraction company founded in 2021 by Hood Whitson, who also serves as its CEO. Headquartered in Fort Worth, Texas, the firm was established to address the shortfall in U.S. critical mineral production by creating a domestic supply chain. The company's core business involves extracting lithium and other essential materials from the vast quantities of wastewater, or brine, generated by oil and gas production. Element3 has developed a patent-pending Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) technology designed to recover these materials efficiently. This process works on wastewater with low lithium concentrations (below 40 parts per million) without needing pre-concentration, a key differentiator from other methods. Field tests in the Permian Basin have demonstrated lithium recovery rates of over 85%, and the company has successfully produced battery-grade lithium carbonate from this process. Element3's business model is designed to integrate with existing oil and gas operations, leveraging their infrastructure to process the high volumes of produced brine and turning an industrial byproduct into a valuable commodity. The company is positioned to serve the growing demand for materials required for the energy transition and advanced manufacturing, particularly for electric vehicle (EV) batteries. By tapping into the estimated one trillion gallons of wastewater produced annually by U.S. oil and gas operations, Element3 aims to provide a scalable and more capital-efficient domestic lithium source than traditional mining projects. The company has secured multiple rounds of funding, including a seed round in December 2023 and a Series A round in September 2025. Key investors include EIC Rose Rock, Cubit Capital, and TO VC. These funds are aimed at accelerating the deployment of its first commercial extraction plants, with the goal of shipping its first commercial tons of lithium by the end of 2025. column6: Althexis provides a data-driven sales optimization platform for the skincare retail market, specifically targeting brick-and-mortar pharmacies. Based on this data, the customer's profile, and the pharmacy's current product inventory, the platform's recommendation engine instantly generates a personalized skincare routine. This process is designed to transform pharmacy staff into trusted advisors, enhance customer trust, and improve in-store conversion rates, helping physical stores compete with e-commerce. Althexis operates on a business-to-business model, generating revenue through several streams. The primary source is a subscription-based model for the Althexis Skincare Suite provided to pharmacies. Additionally, the company offers a Market & Business Analytics Platform, which provides subscription access to anonymized demographic and behavioral data collected from in-store analyses, offering market insights to both pharmacies and skincare brands. Skincare brands can also pay for 'Sponsored Slots' for targeted product placements within the recommendation engine. In February 2026, Althexis announced it had secured €400,000 ($476K USD) in a seed funding round. column6: Hypermine, a spinout from the VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland, is an Espoo-based company focused on enhancing efficiency and sustainability within the mining sector. The company was co-founded by CEO Markku Makkonen, CTO Mikhail Mekhrengin (PhD), and CPO Andrei Rupasov (PhD). Mekhrengin brings over 15 years of experience in developing and commercializing advanced measurement systems, while Rupasov has a 15-year industrial career in heavy-duty optics and electronics. This venture emerged to address the mining industry's challenges of declining ore grades and increasing environmental pressures, driven by the rising global demand for critical minerals for the clean energy transition and urbanisation. The core of Hypermine's business is a mineral sensing solution designed to provide real-time mineralogy characterization directly at the point of extraction. The technology integrates proprietary broadband laser illumination, hyperspectral sensing, and machine-learning algorithms. This system is uniquely capable of operating reliably under all environmental conditions, including bright sunlight, complete darkness, rain, and dust, from a distance of up to 50 meters. The business model targets mining operators globally, offering a significant improvement in decision-making accuracy. By shifting ore grade analysis from traditional 3,000-10,000-tonne block models to a truckload resolution of 100-400 tonnes, Hypermine increases decision precision by a hundredfold. The primary service offers tangible benefits to mining clients, enabling them to sort valuable minerals from waste rock at the earliest possible stage. This process leads to an increase in mine profitability by an estimated 3-10%, a reduction in energy consumption by 10%, and a 15% decrease in the use of water and ore flotation acids. Application scenarios include scanning muck piles, shovel loads, and truck loads, feeding real-time data into fleet management systems for selective loading and optimised ore control. Following a successful seed funding round in June 2025, supported by investors like Stephen Industries, Sage Enterprises, and VTT, Hypermine is expanding its team and commercial operations. The technology has been validated with a major mining company and is undergoing pilot programs in the UK, South Africa, Brazil, and Canada. column6: HiPoint Agro Bedding Corp. is a cleantech company operating within the equestrian and agricultural sectors, founded in 2017. The firm is positioned as a provider of sustainable waste management services, specifically targeting the environmental challenges posed by horse stall waste. HiPoint has developed a patented, zero-waste recycling process that transforms equine stall residuals—a mix of used bedding and manure—into valuable commercial products without the use of chemicals. This agri-technology involves a multi-step system of separation, drying, pasteurization, and bagging to create its signature products. The company's primary offering is a premium, recycled wood shaving bedding marketed under the brand Fuzed Gold. This bedding is promoted as hypoallergenic, antibacterial, antiviral, antifungal, and virtually dust-free, created through a proprietary infusion of tree and plant cellulose oils. Beyond the animal health benefits, the business model addresses significant environmental concerns. The global horse population produces millions of tons of manure annually, leading to land and water pollution through nutrient leaching and the release of methane gas. HiPoint's process mitigates these issues by converting a polluting waste stream into multiple revenue streams. Revenue is generated through the sale of its Fuzed Gold bedding to clients such as high-end stables, racetracks, and showgrounds. A secondary revenue source comes from the creation of byproducts from the separated manure, including a high-yield organic biofertilizer and biofuel for energy production. This circular economy approach allows the company to offer its premium bedding at competitive prices. Headquartered in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada, the company has also established a US presence with entities in Florida and Delaware. HiPoint has gained recognition through its participation in the SVG Ventures|THRIVE II Canada Accelerator Program and received an invitation to the 2021 Global Investment Summit hosted by the Royal Family. column6: Founded in 2008, ComBio Energia specializes in developing renewable thermal energy projects for industrial clients, facilitating the transition from fossil fuels to sustainable biomass. ComBio overcame this by offering an aggressive business model where it covers all initial investment (CAPEX) and operational costs in exchange for long-term contracts. The company manages the entire biomass supply chain, from sourcing agricultural and forestry waste to ensuring its sustainable origin and tracking the carbon footprint. ComBio's core service is generating thermal energy in the form of steam, hot water, or hot gases by replacing clients' existing fossil fuel boilers with modern biomass boilers. column6: Ramsay Agriculture is a vertical farm that has been integrated with a renewable energy process. This cycle is reminiscent of the cycles we see in Nature such as the carbon, nitrogen and water cycles. In addition, by diverting waste from landfills and capturing methane produced from the use of anaerobic digestion the operation helps to prevent further contaminant material to be buried in the earth and reduces greenhouse gas emissions. column6: ReUse Action is a for-profit social enterprise based in Buffalo, New York, that specializes in the deconstruction of buildings and the sale of salvaged and surplus building materials. Founded in 2011 by the original founders of the non-profit Buffalo ReUse, the company emerged after a deterioration in board and staff relations at the former organization led to their departure. Co-founders include Michael Gainer and Kevin Hayes. The founders' history began with organizing Buffalo ReUse in 2006, which started operations in 2007, focusing on community-minded business, deconstruction techniques, and neighborhood regeneration. When Buffalo ReUse ceased its retail operations on December 1, 2022, ReUse Action took over its material sales and donations by mutual agreement. The company operates a 30,000-square-foot retail store on Buffalo's East Side in a factory building known as “The Guild @980”. The business model is centered on the circular economy, acquiring materials through deconstruction services, salvage operations, gutting, cleanouts, and donations, and then selling them to the public. Its clients include homeowners, landlords, contractors, developers, artists, and craftsmen. ReUse Action's inventory features a wide array of items such as board lumber, barn wood (hemlock, pine, oak), doors, windows, kitchen cabinets, radiators, and rigid foam insulation. As a full-service contractor, the company offers specialty demolition for residential and commercial clients, with a focus on interior demolition and restoration projects that adhere to historic preservation standards. Additionally, ReUse Action provides consulting services on material reuse, recycling, deconstruction, and sourcing for various stakeholders, including homeowners, builders, and municipalities. column6: Citiot is a multi-faceted retail and community space located in Catskill, New York, that combines a retail shop, a café, and a co-working area under one roof. He embraced the term "citiot"—a slang term for a city dweller in a rural setting—and established the business at 404 Main Street in Catskill. The business operates on a blended model, generating revenue from several streams. The retail component offers a diverse and frequently changing selection of products, including local and European goods, gifts, books, art, clothing, and pantry items. The café serves locally roasted coffee, among other beverages and food items. Additionally, Citiot provides co-working space with desks available for rent on a drop-in basis, as well as soundproof rooms for calls. The clientele is a mix of locals, tourists, and weekend visitors. The company also maintains an online store, allowing customers to shop its collection digitally. Citiot aims to be an inclusive community hub that supports local artists by exhibiting and selling their work. The founder's vision was to create a welcoming place that fosters creativity and community engagement. The shop's eclectic nature is a deliberate choice, blending local charm with a European flair to offer a unique experience for shopping, working, or socializing. column6: Addfield Environmental Systems Ltd. designs and manufactures thermal treatment systems for waste disposal. The company serves a diverse client base across agricultural, medical, aquacultural, and municipal sectors, in addition to providing solutions for pet cremation and specialized hazardous waste. Its business model revolves around the in-house production and global sale of incinerators, which range from compact 50kg units to large-scale, 2000kg/hr systems.The company was founded in 1982 by Richard Sherratt, who initially designed an incinerator to help the UK agricultural industry manage a Foot and Mouth disease outbreak. For over two decades, the company established itself as a reliable manufacturer of agricultural incinerators. In 2008, entrepreneur Steven Lloyd acquired the company, rebranding it as Addfield Environmental Systems Ltd. and expanding its focus to international markets and a wider range of waste streams. This led to significant growth, expanding from a three-person UK-focused operation to a global enterprise with over 50 employees supplying machines to more than 150 countries. A major milestone occurred in April 2023 when the company was acquired by an investment fund advised by Darwin Alternatives, a move intended to fuel further expansion and the development of greener technologies. The leadership team, including Managing Director Derek Carr, remained in place to ensure continuity.Addfield's product portfolio is extensive, featuring incinerators specifically designed for various waste types, including fallen livestock, medical and hazardous materials, aquaculture, and municipal waste. They also offer mobile and containerized solutions, high-capacity systems, and equipment for pet cremation. A key feature of their products is the robust build quality, utilizing thick gauge steel and advanced thermal refractory materials instead of cast concrete, which contributes to their longevity and efficiency. The company uses Computational Fluid Dynamics software for design and employs skilled craftsmen for production, ensuring all machines meet regulations such as the EU Animal By-Products Regulation. column6: Fuji Spring Corporation, founded in 1960, is a manufacturer specializing in precision metal components. Initially a spring manufacturer, the company has evolved its offerings to include precision press and deep drawing processing, precision molds and jigs, and nickel plating. A key milestone includes a capital and business alliance with Toyota Tsusho Corporation in May 2025 to strengthen the automotive battery supply chain. This partnership followed the establishment of a joint venture in the U.S. in July 2023, FUJIHATSU & TOYOTSU Battery Components, North Carolina LLC. Fuji Spring operates on a business model of integrated in-house production, from die and mold design and manufacturing to press processing, surface treatment, and assembly of automatic machines. This one-stop service allows the company to provide customized solutions from development and prototyping to mass production. The company serves major consumer electronics and heavy electrical appliance manufacturers, with a significant focus on the automotive industry, including components for airbags and next-generation vehicle batteries. Recent expansions include new plants in Kameyama, Mie Prefecture (2020), and the establishment of subsidiaries in the USA (2022) and India (2023). column6: East African Power (EAP) is an integrated renewable energy development and engineering company that delivers clean energy solutions across East Africa. Founded in 2012 by Dan Klinck, the company functions as a social-impact-oriented Independent Power Producer (IPP), specializing in the development, design, construction, and operation of hydro and solar power plants. Klinck, the company's CEO, has a background in finance and has worked as an entrepreneur and business executive across Asia, North America, and Africa. EAP develops projects from the ground up, serving clients such as developers, public institutions, and private stakeholders through every phase, from project identification to operations and maintenance. The company's business model includes providing turnkey Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) services for hydro and solar projects, including utility-scale, commercial, industrial, and mini-grid applications. It also offers comprehensive advisory services, covering project development support like feasibility studies, permitting, and contract negotiation, as well as financial services such as structuring investments and fundraising. Revenue is generated through these development, EPC, and ongoing operations and maintenance services. By 2022, the company had deployed $60 million in capital expenditures across 18 renewable energy projects. A core component of EAP's strategy is integrating social development with its energy projects. This led to the creation of Empowering Villages (EV) in 2020, a non-profit organization that collaborates with EAP to accelerate electricity access and foster local enterprise in conjunction with utility-scale projects. EAP aims to bring 1 GW of renewable energy online by 2030, working with its team of over 130 staff members. column6: The Millboard Company Ltd. is a family-run British manufacturer of premium composite decking and cladding solutions, headquartered in Warwickshire. The company was founded by James Douglass, who previously established Stonemarket, a business focused on creating concrete paving with the appearance of natural stone. After selling Stonemarket, the Douglass family applied a similar philosophy to timber, aiming to develop a decking material that captured the aesthetic of wood without its inherent weaknesses like rotting, warping, and splintering. Following years of development, The Millboard Company Ltd. was incorporated on January 23, 2007, and launched its first products. Millboard's core product is a wood-free outdoor flooring hand-moulded from real oak timbers to ensure an authentic appearance. The boards are made from a unique polyurethane and mineral stone blend, making them resistant to moisture, insects, algae, and UV light. The material composition includes a fibre-reinforced cellular core for strength and a Lastane surface layer that provides high slip resistance, even when wet. This composition makes the product durable and low-maintenance, as it does not require regular staining, sealing, or painting. The company's business model is centered on manufacturing and distributing these high-performance products for both residential and commercial applications, such as gardens, patios, pool areas, and walkways. Serving both homeowners and professionals like architects and designers, Millboard distributes its products throughout the UK and internationally, with a presence in Europe, Asia, and Oceania. Sustainability is a significant focus for the company. Millboard decking is manufactured using a low-energy process, and over a third of the raw materials in the core are recycled, including minerals diverted from landfills. The products are entirely wood-free, preserving natural forests. The company's carbon footprint has been independently verified to the ISO 14064-1 standard. In 2023, Millboard was recognized as one of the UK's top 100 fastest-growing businesses for international growth and expanded its European presence by acquiring its leading French distributor, Ansyears SAS. column6: BancoSol operates as a commercial microfinance bank in Bolivia, dedicated to providing financial services to micro and small entrepreneurs. Its history dates back to 1986 when it began as the PRODEM foundation, an NGO established by Bolivian entrepreneurs and supported by the U.S. non-profit ACCION International. This initiative was a response to high unemployment and a burgeoning informal economy in Bolivia during the national crisis of the 1980s. On February 10, 1992, the foundation transitioned to become the world's first regulated commercial bank specializing in microfinance, officially named Banco Solidario S.A. (BancoSol). The bank's business model was revolutionary for its time, as it demonstrated that lending to low-income sectors, previously considered too risky, could be a sustainable and profitable market. BancoSol primarily serves clients in the informal economy, such as street vendors, carpenters, and artisans, many of whom had never received credit from a formal institution before. Initially focused on group lending, the bank has since shifted to predominantly individual loans. Its client base exceeds one million, with women comprising a significant portion, representing about 50% of its customers. Revenue is generated from a comprehensive portfolio of financial products including loans, savings accounts, microinsurance, debit cards, and remittances. BancoSol offers a range of access channels to enhance customer proximity and convenience. These include a physical network of agencies, 'SolAmigo' agents, ATMs, and mobile agencies that travel to rural areas. Embracing digital transformation, the bank launched digital banking platforms like SolNet (internet banking) and AppSol (mobile banking). The mobile app, AppSol, allows users to check balances, make transfers, pay for services using QR codes, and manage their loans and cards. To further drive digital adoption, BancoSol introduced GanaSol, a gamified tool within the app that rewards customers for saving and using digital services. This digital push is supported by an innovation hub, CIBSOL, created in partnership with Accion and Mastercard to develop new financial products for Bolivia's micro-merchants. column6: Proton AG operates as a Swiss technology firm centered on delivering privacy-focused digital services. The company originated in 2014 from the collaboration of scientists at CERN, including founder and CEO Andy Yen, who envisioned an internet where privacy is the default setting. Inspired by this vision and motivated by revelations of widespread online surveillance, the founders launched their first product, Proton Mail, following a successful public crowdfunding campaign that raised over $500,000 from more than 10,000 individuals. The company's financial structure is deliberately independent of venture capital, relying instead on a freemium business model. Free versions of its services are supported by paid subscriptions from users who require advanced features and greater storage, ensuring the company's primary obligation remains with its user community rather than investors. This model allows Proton to maintain its focus on privacy without the pressure for data monetization that characterizes many ad-supported tech companies. In a significant move to solidify its mission, the company transitioned in June 2024 to a structure where the non-profit Proton Foundation is the majority shareholder, legally binding the company to prioritize its mission over profits and protecting it from takeovers. Headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, Proton leverages the country's stringent privacy laws to protect user data. Its infrastructure includes secure data centers in Switzerland and Germany, with one located in a former military bunker beneath 1,000 meters of granite, ensuring physical security for its servers. The company serves a global user base, including individuals and businesses, who are concerned about data privacy and wish to control their digital footprint. Proton has expanded from its initial email service into a comprehensive, integrated ecosystem of privacy-by-default applications. All products are built on a foundation of end-to-end and zero-access encryption, meaning not even Proton can access user data. The suite includes: Proton Mail, an encrypted email service; Proton VPN, which secures internet connections; Proton Drive for encrypted cloud storage; Proton Calendar for private scheduling; and Proton Pass, an encrypted password manager. The company has also grown through acquisitions, such as SimpleLogin for email aliases and Standard Notes for encrypted note-taking, further broadening its privacy ecosystem. column6: Incorporated on December 21, 2018, Caribbean Goods Ltd. operates as a Scotland-based importer and distributor focused on green coffee from Guatemala. The firm was established by Javier Gutiérrez Abril, who brings a unique blend of experience to the venture. Originally from Guatemala, Gutiérrez Abril's upbringing exposed him to the social and economic challenges faced by local communities, which cultivated a desire to create a positive impact. He pursued a bachelor's degree in Engineering in Guatemala before moving to Scotland in 2017 to obtain a Master of Science in Finance from the University of Strathclyde, which supported him in setting up the company. Caribbean Goods functions as a small-scale, ethical coffee importer, supplying specialty green coffee beans directly from farmers in Guatemala to roasters across the United Kingdom. The company's business model is built on establishing a transparent and direct trade relationship that circumvents traditional intermediaries. This approach is designed to provide farmers with fairer pay, often paid upfront, and more control than they would have in the commodity market. The company serves over 30 roasters, catering specifically to small and medium-sized coffee businesses that may face challenges in sourcing high-quality beans due to the large order quantities typically required by larger importers. Caribbean Goods addresses this by offering coffee beans in quantities that are half the standard industry unit, making premium Guatemalan coffee more accessible. The core service revolves around the sourcing and provision of high-quality, handpicked, and sun-dried green coffee beans. The product's quality is attributed to Guatemala's ideal climate and volcanic soil. Beyond the product itself, the company's operating ethos emphasizes empowerment and positive social impact. Caribbean Goods builds personal relationships with its partner farmers, visiting farms to ensure ethical practices. The firm also engages in social initiatives, including planting a tree in the Scottish highlands for every 30kg bag of a specific coffee sold and supporting the MAIA Impact School in Guatemala, which empowers young women through education. column6: Great British Sports Cars (GBS) is a manufacturer of component-form and factory-built sports cars based in Nottinghamshire, UK. The company was founded on May 5, 2006, after Richard Hall acquired the assets of Robin Hood Engineering. Hall, who had joined Robin Hood shortly after university, saw an opportunity when the company went into administration and put in a successful bid for its assets, which marked the beginning of GBS. The firm's flagship product is the GBS Zero, a lightweight sports car inspired by the classic Lotus Seven, which was launched in 2007. GBS operates on a business model that serves both do-it-yourself enthusiasts and clients seeking fully assembled vehicles. The company prides itself on manufacturing over 80% of its car components in-house, ensuring a managed supply chain and high-quality standards. This vertical integration allows GBS to offer a wide range of parts and spares, which are available through its factory showroom and online store, Kitspares.co.uk. Beyond its core business of producing the Zero, GBS undertakes other engineering projects, including reverse engineering old parts and restoring classic vehicles, such as a 1991 Lamborghini F1 car. The company also serves a global market, with exports to the USA, Australia, and Europe. The GBS Zero is designed to be highly customizable, available as a road car or a track-focused vehicle. GBS has continuously developed the Zero, with a 'Gen 2' version launched around 2019, and ensures that many new modifications are backward-compatible with older models. In recent years, GBS has expanded into the electric vehicle (EV) market, offering an EV package for the Zero that utilizes a Tesla motor. This package allows for flexibility in battery choice, catering to different performance needs, from road use with a range of over 200 miles to lightweight track applications. The company also engages with its customer base through social events and factory tours. column6: Zytek Automotive was a British engineering company specializing in powertrain and vehicle engineering, with a focus on engine management systems and, more recently, electric and hybrid vehicle systems. Founded in 1981 by Bill Gibson as part of the Zytek Group, the company initially focused on providing advanced engine management systems for motorsport, including developing the first fully electronic engine management system in Formula One for Ayrton Senna's car. The company was split into two divisions: Zytek Automotive and Zytek Engineering. While Zytek Engineering focused on motorsport, Zytek Automotive leveraged its expertise for road cars. The company's success in motorsport led to collaborations with prominent automotive manufacturers such as Jaguar, Aston Martin, Rolls-Royce, and Bentley. This move established the company as a key player in vehicle electrification, leading to a partnership with General Motors in 1999 for a hybrid truck development program and the conversion of 100 Smart Fortwo cars to fully electric vehicles in 2006 for UK market trials. In 2000, Motorola acquired a 19% stake in Zytek Automotive, which was later transferred to Continental AG in 2006. Continental increased its share to 50% and eventually acquired full ownership of Zytek Automotive on February 3, 2014, integrating it into its Continental Engineering Services (CES) division. This acquisition was aimed at meeting the growing demand for specialized engineering services for small-scale production and niche vehicles. Following the acquisition, Zytek Automotive continued to operate from its base in Fradley, Staffordshire, as a UK arm of CES, providing engineering services for chassis, interior, and powertrain systems. The motorsport-focused division, Zytek Engineering, was rebranded as Gibson Technology in October 2014 and remained under the ownership of founder Bill Gibson. column6: Clayton Equipment is a UK-based locomotive manufacturer specializing in the design, build, and maintenance of bespoke shunting, mainline, metro, and tunnelling locomotives. Devlin, the former Chief Draughtsman, initially ran the business as a single-person operation. After World War II, the company expanded significantly, producing agricultural equipment and industrial conveyors, which led to the acquisition of new premises in Hatton, Derbyshire, in 1946. In 1957, International Combustion Holdings acquired Clayton, a period during which Clayton secured a major contract to supply 88 diesel-electric locomotives for British Railways as part of its modernization scheme. The company became a market leader in underground rail haulage after developing locomotives for the National Coal Board in the 1960s to replace pit ponies. Ownership changed hands several times, including becoming part of Rolls-Royce's Industrial Power Group in 1989. In March 2005, Clayton Equipment became an independent company again following a management buyout and relocated to Burton upon Trent. The company's primary business is the production of custom-built locomotives, with a strong focus on low and zero-emission technologies such as battery-electric, battery-hybrid, and overhead trolley power systems. It serves a global market across the mining, tunnelling, construction, and mainline rail industries, exporting to over 60 countries. Clayton offers a wide range of locomotives, from 1.75 to 150 tonnes, and also provides turnkey haulage systems, conversions of existing diesel fleets to battery power, and after-sales support. Notable projects include developing the world's largest steel-tyred flameproof locomotive in 2007, creating a fleet of Stage IV Diesel tunnelling locomotives in 2016, and supplying hybrid shunting locomotives to clients like Tata Steel and GB Railfreight. column5: Innovative hydration backed by over 20 years of medical research. Performance & Recovery 💦
column6: Prepd Hydration, operated by the Australian company Preserve Health Pty Ltd, markets a specialized sports hydration system. The company was founded in 2017 as a spinout from Flinders University, but its scientific foundation rests on over two decades of medical research collaboration between Flinders and Yale Universities. This research was initially focused on a humanitarian goal: developing a more effective oral rehydration solution to combat life-threatening dehydration from diseases like cholera in developing nations. The scientific team, including Professor Graeme Young, Professor Henry Binder, B.S. Ramakrishna, and Dr. Ian Brown, identified a unique resistant starch that enhances the body's ability to absorb fluid. Their research showed that this formulation could improve hydration by 39% compared to the standard World Health Organisation solution by tapping into the large intestine's absorption capacity. The commercial application for sports performance was identified through a joint venture between Flinders University and the Adelaide Football Club. Following a successful clinical trial with the club's elite players in 2014, the technology was adapted into a consumer product for athletes. Prepd Hydration officially launched in Australia on November 7, 2018. The company's business model is direct-to-consumer, selling its products online. It targets endurance athletes and individuals engaged in intense physical activity, such as runners, cyclists, triathletes, and AFL players, who need to optimize their hydration to improve performance and recovery. The core offering is a two-step hydration system designed to work alongside water and traditional sports drinks, not replace them. The system features a unique resistant starch (or 'sustained fibre') to boost the body's hydration efficiency. The first step, 'Prepd Prime', is a pre-exercise drink consumed 10-18 hours before activity. It prepares the digestive system to absorb more fluid, helping athletes start their activity better hydrated. The second step, 'Prepd Recover', is for immediate post-exercise consumption. It aims to rapidly replenish fluids and electrolytes lost during exertion. The Recover formula also contains Whey Protein Isolate and Branched-Chain Amino Acids (BCAAs) to aid muscle repair. This system claims to reduce dehydration-related fatigue, minimize cramping, and aid in faster recovery. In November 2024, it was reported that the parent company, Preserve Health Pty Ltd, appointed liquidators due to challenges in raising the capital needed for growth in a difficult financial climate. column6: Aqsorption Ltd is a Nottingham-based engineering and research company founded in 2017, operating as the dedicated research arm of the AqGas Group. The firm specializes in developing bespoke engineering solutions for the zero-carbon hydrogen production and fusion energy sectors. A core focus is its patented, membrane-free electrolysis technology. This 'flow-through' design uses porous electrodes to inherently separate hydrogen and oxygen gases, which eliminates the need for a traditional membrane. The benefits of this approach include enhanced robustness, the ability to handle intermittent power from renewable sources, and suitability for high-pressure operation, potentially removing the need for downstream gas compression. The company's technology is designed to be more efficient and operate at higher pressures than conventional systems, with the goal of reducing maintenance costs and reliance on expensive rare earth minerals. Aqsorption is also developing systems to recover kinetic energy from the high-pressure oxygen output to further boost efficiency. Beyond hydrogen production, the firm applies its electrolysis and isotopic separation techniques to the fusion energy sector. This includes developing systems for handling tritiated water and separating hydrogen isotopes like deuterium and tritium, using innovations like 2D graphene-based isotopic sieves. The company has engaged in research collaborations with the University of Nottingham and the Graphene Engineering and Innovation Centre at the University of Manchester. It has received funding from entities such as the Net Zero Technology Centre and the UK Atomic Energy Authority's Fusion Industry Programme to accelerate technology development. column6: TicketSwap operates an online marketplace for the secondary exchange of tickets for concerts, festivals, and sporting events. The company was founded in 2012 by Hans Ober, Ruud Kamphuis, and Frank Roor in Amsterdam, Netherlands. A key feature is "SecureSwap," a technology developed through partnerships with event organizers and ticketing companies. The company's journey began with its three founders, an Excel sheet, and early adoption by friends and family before gaining wider traction. It won the Amsterdam Student Entrepreneurs Prize in 2014. column5: Belgian non-profit promoting high energy-efficiency construction
column6: Plate-forme Maison Passive (PMP) is a non-profit organization in French-speaking Belgium dedicated to promoting the construction of very low-energy buildings based on the passive house concept. PMP plays a central role in this ecosystem by raising awareness, providing training, offering technical guidance, and certifying buildings that meet the strict passive criteria. The organization's target audience is broad, encompassing the general public, students, professionals like architects and engineers, and public authorities. For individuals and developers, PMP provides guidance and answers questions about passive construction or renovation projects. For professionals, the team offers solutions to daily practice challenges, including performing Passive House Planning Package (PHPP) encoding for certification or energy optimization. PMP also assists public authorities in drafting technical clauses for passive projects and provides training for project performance evaluation. PMP's services are structured around several key activities. They sensitize the public through information dissemination, conferences, and events. They train professionals through comprehensive courses on passive design and construction, including specific software like PHPP. The organization facilitates projects by offering technical guidance and practical tools. A core function is the certification of residential and tertiary buildings to "passive building" and "zero-energy building" standards, a process that includes a mandatory pre-certification step before work begins and a final certification after completion. This certification validates that the building's heating needs are below 15 kWh/m² per year and meets stringent airtightness requirements, among other criteria. column6: BlueBella Ltd is a British lingerie and nightwear brand founded in 2005 by Emily Bendell. The company operates as an internet-first brand, selling its products through its e-commerce website and a network of wholesale partners including ASOS, Selfridges, and Nordstrom. BlueBella has established operations in the UK, US, Australia, France, and Italy. Founder Emily Bendell, an Oxford University graduate, worked as a journalist before starting BlueBella from her bedroom. Her vision was to create lingerie that was not just for special occasions but could be a form of personal self-expression and indulgence. Bendell identified a gap in the market for fashion-led, contemporary, and affordable lingerie, moving beyond the traditional categories of purely functional or sexy. The business initially utilized a direct home-selling model with a network of consultants before transitioning to its current e-commerce and wholesale structure. The company has secured funding through several rounds, raising a total of $1.23 million. Early investors included the female investor club Addidi Business Angels and online retailer Lovehoney. In 2016, BlueBella raised over £1 million through a crowdfunding campaign on Crowdcube to finance its expansion into the US market. This expansion led to its products being stocked in major US department stores like Bloomingdale’s and Nordstrom. The brand has gained significant media coverage, with celebrities such as Nicki Minaj and Maggie Gyllenhaal wearing its designs. In 2019, the company formed a wholesale partnership with Victoria's Secret. BlueBella has received numerous accolades, including being named Lingerie Brand of the Year by Drapers multiple times and receiving the King's Award for Enterprise for International Trade in 2024 for its significant overseas sales growth. The brand is also known for its marketing campaigns, such as the #BeStrongBeBeautiful campaign with GB Olympic athletes to promote body confidence among young girls and the "Dare To Bare" outdoor catwalk at Oxford Circus, which won Marketing Campaign of the Year. column5: Containerized, large-scale solar thermal systems for industries
column6: Sunoptimo S.A. is a Belgian manufacturer specializing in large-scale solar thermal systems for the collective and industrial markets. Founded in 2011, the company aims to replace fossil fuel energy with clean, renewable solar heat. The three founders brought over 20 years of combined experience in the solar heating industry to the venture. Sunoptimo's headquarters are located in Naninne, Belgium, a strategic position for exporting to neighboring European countries. The company's flagship product is the Opticube, a pre-assembled, all-in-one solar thermal kit housed in a 20-foot shipping container. Launched in 2015, the Opticube was designed to overcome the primary barriers to solar thermal adoption: complexity, installation time, and cost. The system includes solar collectors, a water storage tank, and all hydraulic components, which are pre-mounted and integrated before shipping. This design can reduce total installation costs by up to 40% compared to traditional systems and allows a 100 m² system to be assembled in a single day. The Opticube operates on a 'drainback' principle, which prevents the system from overheating and simplifies maintenance. Sunoptimo targets high-volume hot water consumers across various sectors, including industry (laundries, food processing), agriculture, hotels, collective housing, swimming pools, and sports facilities. The business model focuses on providing these clients with a cost-effective renewable energy source, delivering green energy for under €20 per MWh. The company also offers the Opticube Field, a solution designed for even larger solar fields of up to 30,000m², catering to district heating networks and large industrial sites. column5: Regional public water supply and distribution utility
column6: The Monroe County Water Authority (MCWA) is a public benefit corporation established in 1950 under the New York State Public Authorities Law. It commenced full-scale operations in 1959 after acquiring the Monroe County assets of a private water company. The authority's primary purpose is to provide quality water and reliable service at reasonable prices to its customers. MCWA serves over 749,000 people across Monroe County and parts of Genesee, Livingston, Ontario, Orleans, and Wayne Counties. Its customer base includes approximately 186,000 direct retail accounts and 20,000 wholesale accounts. The business model involves two main service types: retail and wholesale. In retail areas, MCWA manages the entire water supply chain, from distribution system maintenance to direct customer billing. In wholesale areas, it sells water to municipalities or water districts, which then handle their own distribution and billing. The authority sets its rates annually to cover operational and maintenance expenses, debt service on outstanding bonds, and capital expenses. MCWA's primary water source is Lake Ontario, treated at the Shoremont and Webster Water Treatment Plants. It also purchases water from the City of Rochester, which sources it from Hemlock and Canadice Lakes. The authority maintains a significant infrastructure, including over 130 million gallons of water storage capacity and more than 27,000 fire hydrants. Governance is overseen by a Board of Directors with several committees, including Audit, Governance, and Finance, which manage aspects like financial oversight, ethical issues, and debt issuance recommendations. The management team is led by Executive Director Nicholas A. Noce, who was appointed on December 1, 2011. column6: ZX Lidars provides Light Detection and Ranging (Lidar) systems for the wind energy and meteorological sectors. The company designs and manufactures remote wind-sensing products that are utilized in onshore, offshore, and turbine-mounted applications to inform the planning, design, and operation of wind farms. The company's history traces back to research conducted by its team, led by Director of Science Dr. Michael Harris, between 1980 and 2000. Olsen Ltd., which has been its sole shareholder since 2007. The company is headquartered in Malvern, United Kingdom. ZX Lidars' technology uses a continuous-wave laser to measure the Doppler shift of light scattered by atmospheric aerosols like dust and pollen, which allows for the remote calculation of wind speed and direction. This method offers an alternative to traditional meteorological masts, providing data from 10 meters up to 300 meters. The company's product line includes the ZX 300 for onshore vertical profiling, the ZX 300M for offshore applications (both fixed and floating), and the ZX TM, a turbine-mounted Lidar for measuring wind ahead of the turbine to optimize performance. These systems are used for wind resource assessment, operational monitoring, and turbine performance validation. The company has also demonstrated the use of its Lidar technology on a drone. column5: Farmer-owned cooperative for specialty and organic coffee
column6: Pachamama Coffee is a global coffee cooperative entirely owned by smallholder farmers in Peru, Guatemala, Nicaragua, Mexico, and Ethiopia. The company was founded in 2006 after five years of development by co-founders Thaleon Tremain and Nicholas Brown, alongside farmer representatives Raul del Aguila, Merling Preza, and Carlos Reynoso. Tremain's initial idea was influenced by his time in the Peace Corps in Bolivia, where he observed the inefficiencies of traditional development work. The cooperative was established to revolutionize the coffee industry by shifting power to the farmers, allowing them to move from being price-takers to price-setters. The business operates on a vertically integrated, direct-to-consumer model. Farmer cooperatives in the respective countries produce and harvest the coffee, which Pachamama then imports to its Sacramento, California headquarters for roasting, packaging, and distribution. This structure ensures that the farmers, who collectively own 100% of the company, retain control over the entire supply chain, from seed to cup. All profits generated from sales are returned to the farmer-owners through dividends or retained earnings. Pachamama's revenue is generated through multiple channels: direct-to-consumer online sales, a national wholesale program, and its own retail cafés. Pachamama specializes in certified organic and specialty Arabica coffee. In February 2026, the company announced that its coffees from Peru achieved Regenerative Organic Certification®, a standard that recognizes practices restoring soil health and supporting farmer livelihoods. This highlights the cooperative's long-term commitment to environmental stewardship. The business model has received significant recognition, including the Specialty Coffee Association's Sustainability Award for Business Model in 2021. column5: Insect-based protein ingredients from organic waste
column6: Magofarm is a Rwandan insect technology startup established in June 2019 by CEO Moses Katala and a team of fellow students from the African Leadership University. The founders, having grown up in smallholder agricultural families, were inspired to address the challenges of poor productivity due to the lack of affordable, high-quality farming inputs. After exploring other agricultural solutions, Katala identified the high cost and inefficiency of animal feeds as a critical issue for livestock farmers. The company bio-converts organic waste into high-value protein ingredients for animal feed by farming Black Soldier Flies (BSF). The process involves breeding the flies to produce larvae, which are then fed organic waste. These protein-rich larvae are harvested and processed into an alternative protein source for livestock, particularly targeting chicken and pig feed formulations. This waste-to-nutrient technology not only provides a more affordable and nutritionally superior protein source compared to traditional soy or fishmeal but also addresses food waste challenges. The resulting insect protein has up to a 15% higher protein composition than soy. Magofarm operates on a B2B business model, primarily targeting animal feed mills and large-scale poultry farmers in Rwanda. The company offers direct farm-to-farm deliveries and utilizes data collection to advise farmers on best practices to improve yield. Initially bootstrapped by its founders, Magofarm secured pre-seed funding of $100,000 from the GoGettaz entrepreneurship competition in October 2019. The company has a pilot production facility in Bugesera, Rwanda, and aims to become a leading insect technology firm in East and Central Africa. column5: Real-time digital simulation for power system testing
column6: The story of RTDS Technologies begins not in a garage, but in a research center. In the late 1980s, at the Manitoba HVDC Research Centre in Winnipeg, Canada, a team was working on a breakthrough: the world's first real-time digital power system simulation. Before this, testing power grid components was a cumbersome, analog process. This new digital approach offered unprecedented flexibility. Seeing the commercial potential, five members of that research effort—Rick Kuffel, Rudi Wierckx, Trevor Maguire, James Giesbrecht, and Neil Mackenzie—founded RTDS Technologies in 1994. Their mission was to commercialize the RTDS® Simulator, a system of specialized hardware and software that creates a 'digital twin' of a power grid. This allows utilities and manufacturers to test physical hardware in a simulated, real-time environment, a concept known as hardware-in-the-loop testing. This de-risks the rollout of new technologies on the actual grid. For nearly three decades, the company grew as the world's standard for this niche but critical technology. Then, in October 2022, a major event occurred: RTDS Technologies was acquired by AMETEK, a global manufacturer of electronic instruments, for approximately CAD 330 million. The acquisition placed RTDS within AMETEK's Electronic Instruments Group, validating its crucial role in modernizing the world's power infrastructure.

column5: Ergonomic backpack for safe water transport and storage
column6: PackH2O was a brand that offered a collapsible water backpack designed as a safer and cleaner alternative for transporting water in developing nations and disaster zones. The product was developed by Greif, Inc., a global industrial packaging company, and designed in partnership with the innovation firm Nottingham Spirk. The initiative was spearheaded by Greif's then-President and CEO, David Fischer, after he witnessed the challenges of water transport in Haiti following the 2010 earthquake. He challenged his company to create a better solution than the often contaminated jerry cans and buckets commonly used. The PackH2O backpack was designed to carry up to 20 liters (or 5 gallons) of water and was constructed from industrial-grade woven polypropylene, making it puncture-resistant. Key features included a removable inner plastic liner that could be sanitized by exposure to sunlight (a process known as SODIS), a wide opening for easy filling, a protected spout for dispensing water, and adjustable shoulder straps for ergonomic carrying. The design aimed to reduce the physical strain of carrying heavy water loads, particularly for women and children, and to prevent contamination by replacing repurposed containers that may have previously held harmful chemicals. The business model was structured as a self-supporting social enterprise. The backpacks were sold for around $10 to cover costs and enable distribution through partnerships with NGOs and humanitarian organizations like Habitat for Humanity, Partners for Care, USAID, and the Clinton Global Initiative. By 2018, over 225,000 units had been distributed across numerous countries, including Haiti, Kenya, and Guatemala. Despite its initial success and awards, including being named a "Best of What's New" by Popular Science in 2012, the PackH2O product was discontinued as of 2020. column5: Hotel Henry Urban Resort Conference Center in Buffalo, NY
column6: Hotel Henry Urban Resort Conference Center was a hospitality venture born from the ambitious adaptive reuse of a National Historic Landmark in Buffalo, New York. The hotel occupied a portion of the Richardson Olmsted Campus, a site originally designed in the 1870s by architect Henry Hobson Richardson, with grounds by Frederick Law Olmsted, as the Buffalo State Asylum for the Insane. Preservation efforts for the long-abandoned complex began in 2006, led by the Richardson Center Corporation, a non-profit organization. This initiative culminated in the first phase of redevelopment, which transformed one-third of the campus into the Hotel Henry. The hotel officially opened in May 2017, featuring 88 guest rooms, conference facilities, and restaurants. The business model targeted a mix of clients, including tourists, business travelers for conferences, and locals for events and dining. Its unique selling proposition was the experience of staying within a significant architectural masterpiece, blending historical character with modern amenities. The hotel quickly garnered acclaim, being named one of TIME Magazine's 'World's Greatest Places' in 2018. Despite its initial success, the enterprise faced significant financial strain due to the COVID-19 pandemic, which led to a reported 75% loss of projected revenue in 2020. Citing these impacts, Hotel Henry ceased operations in February 2021. Following the closure, developer Douglas Jemal of Douglas Development secured a long-term lease in 2021 to take over the property. After a period of redesign, the hotel reopened in March 2023 under new branding as 'The Richardson Hotel'. However, in a further development, Douglas Development returned management of the hotel to the Richardson Olmsted Campus board in mid-2025, with Buffalo Lodging Associates subsequently appointed to manage the property. column6: Proton Scientific, Inc. is a company focused on developing a commercially viable fusion power generator. Manufactured in Kiev, Ukraine, this generator can produce a power burst of 12 billion watts, concentrated on microscopic targets via an electron beam to initiate a fusion reaction. column6: GuraRide is a green e-mobility public bike-share (PBS) transport system company founded in 2017 by Tony B. Adesina and Agenor Jean-Louis. The founders, two Americans, used their personal savings to move to Rwanda and establish the company with the aim of facilitating the transition from fossil fuel-based mobility to non-polluting transport alternatives. Adesina, a Pennsylvania State University engineering alumnus, is a serial entrepreneur in the green transport sector. The company provides a dock-based bike-sharing service accessed via a mobile application that allows users to locate nearby stations and unlock bikes. Its fleet includes smart bicycles, e-bikes, and electric scooters. The e-bikes are designed to handle Rwanda's hilly terrain and have a range of up to 70 km, with charging handled by solar panels at the docking stations. GuraRide launched its service in late 2021 in partnership with the City of Kigali, initially deploying 80 smart bikes at 12 docking stations. Operations started in corridors within Kigali's Central Business District and the Remera-Kimironko area, with plans for nationwide expansion to cities like Musanze, Huye, and Rubavu. The business model has faced profitability challenges, with the low price point of Rwf300 (USD 0.22) per ride proving unsustainable. The company's president, Ike Erhabor, has stated that the service currently operates more like a Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative, as it generates little to no profit. Operations were temporarily suspended in April 2024 for bike maintenance amid these financial strains. To improve financial viability, GuraRide is exploring the introduction of higher-priced electric bikes and diversifying into electric vehicle (EV) charging stations. The company is also seeking support from NGOs or the government, similar to publicly funded models in Europe. column6: Bayou, operating as Bayou Energy, is a software company positioned at the intersection of financial technology and the clean energy sector. The firm provides a developer-focused Application Programming Interface (API) that enables businesses to seamlessly access consumer utility data. This platform addresses a significant bottleneck in the energy industry by simplifying the process of obtaining real-time and historical energy consumption information from a wide array of U.S. utility providers. Clients are primarily companies deploying clean energy products and services, such as solar panel installers who need to calculate a household's potential energy feedback to the grid, or HVAC technicians determining the appropriate size for a heat pump installation. The company was established in late 2022 by co-founders James Gordey, the CEO, and Joris Van Hecke, the CTO. Gordey, a Louisiana native and civil engineering graduate from Louisiana State University, drew inspiration for the company's name from his home state. His career path led him from a traditional oil and gas trajectory to a role as a senior technical product manager at the battery company Proterra, solidifying his commitment to working on climate solutions. Van Hecke, based in New York, brought experience from the healthcare technology field in Belgium. The pair connected through a climate-focused Slack channel, uniting their diverse technical backgrounds to tackle energy data accessibility.  In April 2024, Bayou announced a significant milestone, securing $1.2 million in a pre-seed funding round. The investment was led by a syndicate of venture firms including Surface Ventures, CoFound Partners, Leap Forward Ventures, Stepchange Ventures, and Very Serious Ventures. At the time of the funding, the platform was being used by over 40 companies and could connect to 24 utilities, representing 44% of the U.S. market. The company's core product is an API suite that allows end-users to authenticate their utility accounts with a single click, granting developers access to account information, billing history, and interval usage data in under a minute. column6: Prio SA, formerly known as PetroRio SA, is a Brazilian public company specializing in the investment, acquisition, and redevelopment of mature oil and gas fields. Founded in 2008 as HRT Participações em Petróleo S.A., the company shifted its focus from exploration to production and development, rebranding to PetroRio in 2015 and later to PRIO in 2022 to strengthen its market identity. The company is headquartered in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. PRIO's business model centers on acquiring mature, producing assets from major oil companies and applying efficient management and innovative recovery techniques to extend their lifespan and maximize output. This strategy involves significant cost optimization and operational efficiency, allowing the company to generate value even in challenging market conditions. A key operational achievement was the pioneering tieback project connecting the Polvo and Tubarão Martelo fields, which increased production and reduced costs and emissions. Revenue is primarily generated from the sale of crude oil and natural gas. In early 2025, PRIO began selling natural gas directly to the domestic market, diversifying its revenue streams. The company's asset portfolio includes several key fields in Brazil's Campos Basin, such as the Polvo, Frade, Tubarão Martelo, Albacora Leste, and the pre-salt Wahoo fields. PRIO has steadily grown through strategic acquisitions, including a 10% stake in the Manati Field via the purchase of Brasoil and the acquisition of the Albacora Leste field in 2022, which significantly increased its production capacity. The company's management, including CEO Roberto Monteiro and Chairman Nelson Queiroz Tanure, has been instrumental in its turnaround and growth since 2014-2015. PRIO also fosters a unique corporate culture by offering stock options to all employees, promoting a sense of ownership and dedication. column5: Platform for developing and implementing financial technologies
column6: The Russian FinTech Association (AFT) is a collaborative platform established in late 2016 on the initiative of the Bank of Russia and key players in the country's financial market. It serves as an inter-industry venue for interaction between banks, IT companies, telecom operators, fintech firms, and the regulator to develop and introduce new technological solutions for the Russian financial market. The association was officially registered and began operations in early 2017. The AFT focuses on several key areas, including the development of Open APIs, distributed ledger technologies, retail payment systems, and information security. A significant milestone was the development of the "Open API Concept" in 2019, followed by the publication of the first standards for Open APIs in 2020. The association also pilots various initiatives, such as projects on digital mortgages, digital auto loans, and the application of generative AI in financial organizations. Its activities involve consolidating market expertise, conducting research and analysis on technology trends, and supporting the development of domestic IT solutions to promote technological sovereignty. The organization's governance includes a Supervisory Board, chaired by Olga Skorobogatova, the Deputy Governor of the Bank of Russia. Maxim Grigoriev serves as the General Director. The association's members include major banks, insurance companies, and technology firms. The AFT's business model is based on consolidating the efforts and resources of its members to address shared business, technological, and regulatory challenges, thereby enabling cost savings and fostering market development. Key projects include the development of a "Digital Profile" service, advancements in blockchain technologies like Digital Financial Assets (DFA) and the Digital Ruble, and the creation of an AI in the Financial Industry club. column5: RTR - The New Era of Solar
column6: The story of RTR, or Rete Rinnovabile, isn't one of a garage startup, but of strategic acquisition and consolidation in the burgeoning Italian solar power market. The narrative begins not with founders, but with a major transaction. In March 2011, the private equity firm Terra Firma acquired RTR from Terna, Italy's high-voltage grid operator. At the time, RTR was a notable but smaller player with a 144 MW portfolio of solar photovoltaic (PV) assets. Under Terra Firma's ownership, RTR embarked on a significant growth phase. The strategy was clear: consolidate the fragmented Italian solar industry. Through a series of eight acquisitions, RTR more than doubled its capacity, growing to 334 MW across 134 sites throughout Italy. This aggressive expansion transformed RTR into a leading solar operator in the country and one of the largest in Europe. The company benefited from professional management, technological advancements, and government incentives for renewable energy. A new chapter began in 2018. Following a record year of power generation, Terra Firma decided to sell. An auction process led to the acquisition of RTR by F2i, an Italian infrastructure fund, in a deal valued at approximately €1.3 billion. This move was part of F2i's broader strategy to create a dominant force in European solar energy, with plans to merge RTR's assets and become one of the continent's largest producers.
